orch-apply.sh:172 builds a NON-RANDOMIZED temp filename on macOS, so concurrent writes to the fleet-mandated orch-state.json path hard-collide. | MECHANISM, reproduced not inferred: the template is `mktemp "$(dirname "$LIVE_FILE")/.orch-apply-XXXXXXXX.json"`. BSD/macOS mktemp only substitutes the X run when it is at the END of the template; with the `.json` suffix after it, mktemp creates the LITERAL file `.orch-apply-XXXXXXXX.json`. Control in the same shell: `mktemp ./ctrl-XXXXXXXX` twice -> ctrl-SMwiwaJE, ctrl-NQ9Zpalc (randomized); `mktemp ./.orch-apply-XXXXXXXX.json` twice -> first OK, second `mkstemp failed: File exists`. GNU mktemp tolerates a suffix, which is why this is macOS-specific and why it never showed up in CI. | OBSERVED LIVE this tick: dev-team 18:37Z drain, first `drain-signals.js` run aborted twice with `mkstemp failed ... File exists` while 3 subagents were running concurrently (one of them, system-auditor, writes signal rows through the same wrapper). Retry seconds later succeeded, 5 signals routed. | WHY IT HAS BEEN INVISIBLE: `trap cleanup EXIT` rm -f is the temp, so the colliding file is gone before anyone inspects. I checked docs/data/orch/ immediately after the failure - no .orch-apply-* entry, no literal-template file. The evidence deletes itself. | HONEST IMPACT BOUND: no corruption and no data loss observed. The mv is still atomic and a losing caller gets a clean non-zero exit, not a partial write. drain-signals.js has all-or-nothing tick semantics so it correctly retained all 5 signals. The cost is (a) a burned tick, and (b) any caller that does NOT retain-and-retry silently loses its write. Under 3+ concurrent agents this is probable, not theoretical. | NOT VERIFIED BY ME: which other orch-apply callers lack retain-and-retry. Fix direction: move the X run to the end of the template (check whether orch-validate.mjs requires a .json extension first) or add a bounded retry around the mktemp. Distinct from FIX-ORCHAPPLY-CAS-BASELINE-CAPTURED-AFTER-CALLER-JQ-READ (that is the CAS window; this is temp-file creation) and from the other 5 open FIX-ORCHAPPLY-* rows - none covers this.

REGRESSION FOUND IN A SHIPPED FIX — FIX-DEVTEAM-RESUME-KEY-TTL-3600-LAPSES-UNDER-LIVE-AGENT (commit faf84a6f6, agent-father, 2026-08-25). The fix is directionally right and closes a real confirmed duplicate-spawn window, but as written it introduces a PERMANENT STRAND for the most common agent death mode, and its own AC-2 ("crash recovery preserved and PROVEN") is falsified rather than merely unproven. Mechanism: the new keepalive renews resume_key on S2/ILC's claimed:false branch every tick. WF-4's stale-age reset declines to fire whenever `git log --since=claimed_at --grep=<task-id>` finds a commit — and commit-convention.md REQUIRES a `Task: <TASK-SLUG>` trailer on any fix/feat delivering a board task, so one commit from the agent before it dies satisfies that grep permanently. WF-4 therefore never resets .head; S2's outer_claim never succeeds because the keepalive keeps the lock alive; .head.resume_attempts increments only on the successful-claim branch (main.md:589) so WF-3's 3-attempt bound is never reachable. The row sits in in_progress[] forever holding a WIP slot. Pre-fix, the same scenario self-healed in 3 ticks. Note the irony worth recording: WF-4's own in-file comment names "S2's own outer_claim peer-held check" as the safety net justifying its conservative no-reset — this fix is what removes that safety net. Suggested bound (not prescriptive): increment resume_attempts on the renew branch so WF-3 stays reachable, or cap consecutive renewals, or source liveness from something other than the lock's own presence. Row moved ready[]->review[] next_agent=po with the full chain in status_note. Currently INERT (.head idle, in_progress[]=0) so there is time to fix before first exposure.

dev-team-tick-preflight.sh returns RUN for a duplicate delivery of a tick whose body is STILL IN FLIGHT, and nothing downstream can tell the two apart. Observed 2026-08-25T19:50:53Z: the 19:37Z tick body had already run (commit 39f216d2b at 19:45:48Z — drain complete, 3 agents dispatched and still live). A second delivery of the same cron prompt arrived at 19:50Z; preflight found SF-1 (dev-team-cron-singleton) and the fire-election lock (cron:dev-team:2026-08-25T19:37Z) already held by THIS SAME session, heartbeated both (claimed_at=1787687051, heartbeat_at=1787687364 on both locks — a renewal, not a re-claim after expiry), and returned {"verdict":"RUN","tick":"2026-08-25T19:37Z"} with detail "locks held — continue main.md at gcc-preflight". || WHY THIS IS NOT SIMPLY A TTL BUG (first read, corrected): the fire-election TTL is 600s against a 1800s cadence, so an expiry-then-reclaim was the obvious hypothesis. The heartbeat_at field falsifies it — the lock never lapsed. The re-entrant RUN is deliberate and has a legitimate purpose: if a tick's body crashes midway, the same-session re-fire must be able to resume rather than strand the tick. || THE ACTUAL GAP: the fire-election lock records that a tick STARTED and is released only at jump:end. It never records how far the body got, so "I hold this tick's lock" is ambiguous between (a) the body crashed, resume it and (b) the body is running fine right now, do not touch it. Both present identically to preflight, and it resolves the ambiguity toward RUN in both cases. A router that trusted the verdict here would have re-run gcc-preflight, re-drained, and re-entered Step 1 / ILC on top of three live agents — the exact duplicate dispatch the fire-election lock exists to prevent. What actually prevented it was out-of-band harness knowledge that the three subagents were still alive, which is NOT available in-flow. || UNTESTED AND IMPORTANT: whether the Phase-B intent gate would have blocked the duplicate spawn depends on whether task_claim treats a re-claim by the SAME owner_client_session as re-entrant (claimed:true) or as held (claimed:false). If re-entrant, the intent locks provide no protection here at all and this is a live duplicate-spawn vector. I did not test it, because the only way to test is to attempt the duplicate claim I am trying to avoid. Worth settling deliberately with a stubbed fixture. || SAME ROOT SHAPE as FIX-DEVTEAM-RESUME-KEY-TTL-3600 (rtr-20260825T1905): a lock's presence or absence being read as a liveness verdict it cannot actually carry. Suggested direction: stamp a completion marker (tick + jump:end reached) into the fire-election lock's payload via task_heartbeat payload_patch as the body advances, so a re-delivery can distinguish resume-after-crash from already-running.

CORRECTION + SCOPE WIDENING on the RESIDUAL flagged in review row FIX-DRS-CLAIM-TRUSTS-CACHED-DISPATCH-LANE-NOT-EFFECTIVE-NEXT-AGENT: its stated cause (board edit without an updated_at bump) is FALSIFIED, the real cause is a null detail.updated_at, the scope is 11 live rows not 3, and 73 of 105 detail items are latently in the same class
rows.detail: RELATIONSHIP TO EXISTING WORK — READ FIRST, this is deliberately NOT a duplicate. review[] row FIX-DRS-CLAIM-TRUSTS-CACHED-DISPATCH-LANE-NOT-EFFECTIVE-NEXT-AGENT (next_agent=qa, updated 2026-08-25T22:33:11Z) already carries, inside its verify_note, a RESIDUAL block naming 3 rows and routing them to 'architect/PO adjudication'. That flag is correct to exist and its instinct to escalate was right. This signal files three corrections to it and does NOT ask for the fix to be reverted. (1) CAUSE IS WRONG, AND THE WRONG CAUSE IMPLIES A FIX THAT DOES NOTHING. The verify_note says the 3 rows diverge 'because the board edit didn't bump updated_at', which implies bumping the board's updated_at would resolve them. It would not. Measured on live data: all 3 rows DO carry a board updated_at (2026-08-25T22:30:08Z on each). What is missing is the DETAIL side. scripts/lib/devteam-eligibility.jq effective_next_agent() takes the board value only inside the conjunct (($board_ts != null) and ($detail_ts != null) and ($board_ts > $detail_ts)); a null $detail_ts makes that conjunct false UNCONDITIONALLY, control falls to the else branch, and $raw_detail_na is returned no matter how fresh the board write is. No board-side bump can make a null detail_ts non-null, so the implied remedy is inert. (2) SCOPE IS 11 ROWS, NOT 3, AND 73 LATENT. Live census of orch-state.json against docs/data/orch/archive/backlog-detail.json: 105 detail items carry next_agent, only 32 carry updated_at — 73 (70%) sit in the structurally-unreachable class, so ANY future board next_agent edit on one of them is silently inert too. 15 rows currently diverge. The 4 in review[] carry BOTH timestamps and resolve CORRECTLY by recency (board_ts > detail_ts, board wins) — the comparator itself is sound and must not be 'fixed' blindly. All 11 failures are exactly the detail_ts=null rows: archive/FIX-PRICE-ANOMALY-DISH-SIGNAL-ENVELOPE: board=po IGNORED -> routes architect | backlog/FIX-AUDITOR-B11-NEWS-FRESHNESS-LAYER-SPLIT: board=agent-father IGNORED -> routes ba | backlog/FIX-AUDITOR-TASKBOARD-OVERFLOW-PREDICATE-WIP-ONLY: board=architect IGNORED -> routes ba | backlog/FIX-AUDITOR-HEALTHCHECK-FALSE-UNHEALTHY-NONHTTP-SERVICES: board=dev-mcp-server IGNORED -> routes ba | backlog/FIX-SIGNALQUEUE-DUP-ID-GUARD: board=developer IGNORED -> routes dev | backlog/FIX-AUDITOR-B05-BCTC-FRESHNESS-LAYER-SPLIT: board=agent-father IGNORED -> routes ba | backlog/FIX-ORPHAN-ADOPTION-BOARD-STATE-GUARD: board=pm IGNORED -> routes ba | ready/QA-COWORK-SLOT-SESSION-DOWN-SURVIVAL: board=po IGNORED -> routes qa | ready/FIX-COWORK-LASTFIRED-DECOUPLE-FROM-DELIVERY: board=pm IGNORED -> routes architect | ready/FIX-MACRO-TE-CHROMIUM-FETCH-BROKEN: board=developer IGNORED -> routes architect | ready/FIX-BCTC-BANK-SUMMARY-MAPPING: board=architect IGNORED -> routes ba. (3) VENUE MAKES IT UNACTIONABLE. The residual currently lives only in prose inside a verify_note on a review[] row. Dispatch gates and claim scripts read structured fields, never prose — the same class as feedback_pickers_blind_to_prose_status_note_autoclaim_contraindicated_row, where a do-NOT-build instruction in a status_note was auto-claimed straight through. Parked there it cannot reach whoever routes these rows. WHY AC-4's diff=0 IS NOT EVIDENCE OF CORRECTNESS. The row's AC-4 reports 'dispatch_lane UNCHANGED for all 8 (diff=0)' after re-resolving. That is the EXPECTED output of this defect, not a refutation of it: dispatch_lane was originally stamped from the detail side, and for null-detail_ts rows the resolver deterministically returns the detail side again. The re-resolve reproduced the same answer because the same branch fired both times. diff=0 demonstrates the resolver is deterministic, not that the routing is right. NOTE ON THE CARRIER ROW ITSELF: FIX-DRS-CLAIM-TRUSTS-CACHED-DISPATCH-LANE-NOT-EFFECTIVE-NEXT-AGENT has NO entry at all in backlog-detail.json, so it is itself a member of the unreachable class its own fix was written to address. IMPACT: resolved_dispatch_lane() chains effective_next_agent -> effective owner -> 'developer' fallback, and both claim scripts now route through it — devteam-backlog-claim-design-router-sweep.jq (DRS :138) and devteam-backlog-claim-supervised-lane-sweep.jq (SLS :138/:175). A router or PO editing .next_agent to redirect any of the 11 therefore produces NO dispatch change, silently. 4 of the 11 are in ready[] and live-dispatchable now; 3 of those carry board_ts=2026-08-25T22:30:08Z, written ~18 minutes before this tick and already inert. CANDIDATE DIRECTIONS (architect's call, explicitly not the router's): (a) treat null detail_ts as infinitely-old so a timestamped board value wins — closest to apparent intent, but flips routing on 11 rows at once and needs a blast-radius review; (b) require detail_ts and fail loudly instead of silently preferring detail; (c) backfill updated_at across the 73 detail items — data-only, leaves the comparator defect latent for the next untimestamped item. Note the 3 ready[] rows ALSO need the separate content call the verify_note already correctly identified (which side is right), and that call is independent of whichever of (a)/(b)/(c) is chosen. NOT MINTING A BOARD ROW: filing for architect triage because (a)/(b)/(c) is a routing-semantics decision with fleet-wide blast radius, and because the adjacent row is still in review[] — minting now risks the duplicate-shipping shape in feedback_po_promote_dedup_blind_to_archived_lane_reships_fixed_work. REPRODUCTION NOTE: detail items live ONLY in docs/data/orch/archive/backlog-detail.json, supplied to the claim scripts via --slurpfile detail + detail_items_from($detail). They are NOT at .task_details or .task_board.details inside orch-state.json — probing there returns null for every field and silently measures nothing.

RELATIONSHIP TO EXISTING WORK — NOT a duplicate, opposite direction. backlog row FIX-AUDIT-OUTPUT-CONTRACT-V4-V5-DEDUPSKIP-DENOMINATOR-FALSE-VIOLATION (P1, next_agent=developer, owner=po, updated 2026-08-12T15:36:33Z) covers a FALSE-POSITIVE: V4/V5 compare a NEW-only anomaly tally against an ALL-emissions signals_posted counter, so a dedup-only cycle self-reports a contract VIOLATION that is not real. THIS row is the inverse and is a FALSE-NEGATIVE: the emitted dedup_skipped counter reads 0 when dedup did occur, so a dedup-only cycle self-reports as a no-op cycle and the contract check has nothing to trip on. Same subsystem, different failure mode — merging them without preserving both directions would lose one.

EVIDENCE (all read from disk by the router after the agent returned, not from its narration):
- docs/data/db-integrity-history.json entry scan_ts=2026-08-26T02:30:33Z: findings=6; `[.findings[] | select(.dedup_check.already_open == true)] | length` = 3 (cron_job_runs -> FIX-CRON-RUNS-NULL-ERRORMSG, deep_fetch_queue -> FIX-DEEPFETCH-PIPELINE-100PCT-UNFETCHED-PRODUCER-LIVE-CONSUMER-DEAD, fred_series_daily -> FIX-MACRO-ISM-FRED-API-KEY-MISSING).
- The agent's own returned [OUTPUT-CONTRACT] line for that same run: `signals_posted=0 | telegram_sent=0 | signal_queue_rows_written=0 | dashboard_rows=0 | dedup_skipped=0`, followed by `[OUTPUT-CONTRACT-VIOLATIONS]: NONE` and `CONTRACT-CONTRADICTION: NONE` — i.e. the self-check passed while the counter disagreed with the file the same run had just written.
- The agent's own prose in the same return: '2 dedup-skipped already-open findings' and '2 findings (cron_job_runs, deep_fetch_queue, fred_series_daily) deduped' — a 2 labelling a 3-item list.
- Prior DATA entry scan_ts=2026-08-25T22:35:28Z: findings=3, already_open=true count = 2. So the nonzero-dedup condition held on both of the last two DATA runs.

SCOPE NOTE — what is NOT claimed: the other four counters on this run were checked and are HONEST. signal_queue_rows_written=0 was verified true (`[.signal_queue.rows[] | select(.created_at // .ts >= "2026-08-26T02:20")] | length` = 0). The commit it claimed, 1a0d784f4, is real and is single-file (docs/agent-memory/notebooks/system-auditor.md only) with no absorption of the 6 peer-owned dirty paths that were live at spawn time. All three cited task ids resolve to real task_board.backlog[].id rows (indices 86, 368, 101) — no phantom-id defect on this run. docs/data/db-integrity-history.json is gitignored (.gitignore:76, untracked since f102d827c), so its absence from the commit is correct, not a missed write. The defect is isolated to the dedup_skipped counter.

WHY IT MATTERS: dedup_skipped is the only field in the contract line that distinguishes 'this cycle found nothing' from 'this cycle found repeat instances of three already-open defects'. Reading 0 for both collapses a signal-bearing cycle into a silent one, and because the accompanying self-check reports VIOLATIONS: NONE and CONTRADICTION: NONE, nothing downstream flags it. Any consumer trending auditor activity off these counters will read the DATA tier as idle while it is in fact re-confirming three open production defects every run.

rows.detail:
NOT a duplicate of the existing row, and not a contradiction of it — it is a THIRD key the existing row does not mention.

THREE CLOCKS, not two:
(1) PRODUCER — cowork-team Step 4.7 (tick-snapshot.md:28) FILE_TICK=$(date -u +%H:%M), wall-clock at write, runs BEFORE spawn.
(2) SERVER PROMOTER — emitPressureStateTool derives the key from the NOMINAL tick. This is the consumer the existing row is about, and its premise is CORRECT for that consumer; that arm is what makes cycle_snapshot_promoted false (38 consecutive as of tick 02:45Z).
(3) AGENT CONSUMER — .claude/skills/cycle-bootstrap/SKILL.md:58-59 sets TICK from current UTC at the agents OWN Step -1, which runs AFTER spawn. Neither (1) nor (2).

MEASURED, 3/3 consecutive alert-commander cycles 2026-08-26 (producer key read from the dispatchers own Step 4.7 output; consumer key read from the agents own notebook, docs/agent-memory/notebooks/alert-commander.md c261-c263):
  tick 02:15Z — producer wrote cycle-snapshot-02:19.json; consumer looked for 02:20 → hit a PRIOR-DAY file, rejected on in-file created_at.
  tick 02:30Z — producer wrote cycle-snapshot-02:34.json; consumer looked for 02:35 → hit a PRIOR-DAY file, rejected on in-file created_at.
  tick 02:45Z — producer wrote cycle-snapshot-02:51.json; consumer looked for 02:52 → clean miss.
Fresh-hit rate on the file the producer actually wrote: 0 of 3. Offset is consistently +1 min, and it is structural, not jitter: the producer samples wall-clock pre-spawn and the consumer samples it post-spawn, so the gap is exactly agent-startup latency and can never be zero.

WHY THE ROUTED FIX IS INSUFFICIENT ALONE: if the producer is renamed to key by NOMINAL tick (02:45), arm (2) is fixed and cycle_snapshot_promoted goes true — but arm (3) gets WORSE. Today the agent misses by one minute and occasionally could align by luck; after a producer-only rename it would look for 02:52 against a file named 02:45 every single tick, deterministically, forever. Any fix must move the CONSUMER key in the same landing.

THE KEY IS ALREADY BEING SHIPPED AND DISCARDED: spawn-fanout.md Step 5.2 composes SCHEDULED_UTC_LINE into EVERY spawn prompt — this ticks alert-commander prompt carried the literal line scheduled_utc=2026-08-26T02:45:00.000Z. grep -rn scheduled_utc across docs/agents/alert-commander/flow/ and .claude/skills/cycle-bootstrap/ returns ZERO hits. The dispatcher already sends the nominal tick to every agent and no consumer flow reads it. Proposed fix shape: Step -1 derives TICK from the scheduled_utc line when present, falling back to wall-clock only when absent (catch-up/manual runs). That is a consumer-side edit in cycle-bootstrap/SKILL.md and costs the producer nothing.

TWO SUPPORTING DOC-TRUTH DEFECTS FOUND IN THE SAME READ (both in .claude/skills/cycle-bootstrap/SKILL.md, fix while the file is open):
  (a) Line ~75 still reads: The snapshot writer (cowork-team dispatcher) is a future task. Until it lands, Step -1 will always miss and fall through to Step 0 — zero behavior regression. The writer LANDED and writes on every non-silent tick. A reader taking that line at face value concludes the cache is intentionally inert and stops investigating — it is the likely reason SPIKE-TICK-SNAPSHOT-DEADCODE-OR-REGRESSED is still sitting at low.
  (b) Line 58 specifies round to nearest 5-min slot, but c263 looked up 02:52, which is not a 5-min slot — the consumer is not applying its own spec. Worth resolving in the same edit, because if rounding WERE applied the lookup would land on 5-min names, which is precisely the population the prior-day decoy files occupy (30 of 36 snapshot files on disk after this ticks prune are prior-day).

SCOPE NOTE — what is NOT claimed: this does not dispute the existing rows premise, its severity, or its owner, and it proposes no change to po_fold_20260825s settled newest-file-inside-7min-gate — that gate would in fact resolve BOTH arms (at 02:52 the newest file was 02:51, 49s old) and this evidence strengthens the case for it. No fallback is broken: every miss fell through to direct get_cycle_bootstrap correctly, so there is no data-integrity impact. The cost is redundant gateway calls — the dispatcher spends two calls per non-silent tick (~20KB) building a file that, for this consumer, is never read.

=== UPDATE — tick 03:00Z, cycle c264 (4th consecutive measurement; supersedes point (b) above) ===

Fresh-hit rate is now 0 of 4. Producer wrote cycle-snapshot-03:06.json; consumer looked for 03:05 AND 03:10; clean miss on both; fell through to direct get_cycle_bootstrap.

CORRECTION TO POINT (b) — the consumer is not simply ignoring its own rounding spec; it applies it INCONSISTENTLY. c263 looked up 02:52 (unrounded). c264 looked up 03:05/03:10 (rounded, and hedged across the boundary). Same skill, same agent, adjacent cycles, two different key derivations. Whatever fix lands must pin this deterministically, not just re-point it.

SHARPER STATEMENT OF THE DEFECT — it is a NAME-SPACE mismatch, not a +1-minute offset. When the consumer rounds, its key can only ever be a 5-minute multiple. The producer names by unrounded `date -u +%H:%M` (tick-snapshot.md:28), so a hit REQUIRES the producer's minute to land on a multiple of 5 by coincidence. Measured across every snapshot this producer wrote on 2026-08-26: minutes 04, 35, 04, 19, 34, 51, 06 — 1 of 7 qualifies. And the producer fires systematically ~4-6 min after each nominal tick, so its minute clusters on {04-06, 19-21, 34-36, 49-51} — a set that intersects the 5-multiples only at its edges. On the unrounded branch the offset is the +1 min already documented above. Neither branch converges. This strengthens, not weakens, the proposed fix: reading the shipped scheduled_utc line removes BOTH branches at once.

DECOY HAZARD FROM POINT (b) — FIRED THIS TICK, AND THE EXISTING GUARD HELD. c264's rounded lookup for 03:05 landed on a real file, docs/data/cycle-snapshot-03:05.json, whose in-file created_at is 2026-08-25T03:05:45Z — a genuine 24h-stale prior-day decoy. cycle-bootstrap/SKILL.md Step -1 clause 2 (file timestamp must be within the last 7 minutes of current UTC, else treat as absent) rejected it correctly and the cycle fell through to the canonical path. So the hazard I flagged in (b) is REAL and now OBSERVED, but it is already MITIGATED by an existing, working gate. Recording this explicitly so the amendment does not motivate a redundant second guard: do NOT add decoy-protection to this fix. The only thing missing is a correct key.

=== UPDATE — tick 04:45Z, cycle c272 (5th measurement; ADDS A FOURTH FAILURE MODE and refutes "a hit requires coincidence") ===

The coincidence this row says a hit REQUIRES occurred, and the consumer missed anyway.

MEASURED, tick 04:45Z: producer wrote docs/data/cycle-snapshot-04:50.json at 04:50:54Z — a 5-minute multiple, i.e. exactly the 1-in-7 winning case the NAME-SPACE-mismatch paragraph describes. Consumer (alert-commander) bootstrapped 04:53:56Z, which floors to 04:50. File present, valid JSON (jq empty passes), all four canonical keys, in-file created_at 2026-08-26T04:50:54Z (SAME DAY, not a prior-day decoy), age at lookup 181s — well inside Step -1 clause 2's 7-minute gate. Every precondition for a fresh hit held simultaneously. The consumer recorded a MISS, reason verbatim from docs/agent-memory/notebooks/alert-commander.md c272: "no tick-snapshot for current tick (all cached files stale, prior-day)". BOTH clauses are false — 181s is not stale, and all four 04:xx files on disk are dated 2026-08-26, not prior-day.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PROPOSED FIX — "the only thing missing is a correct key" is FALSIFIED. On this tick the consumer HAD the correct key (its floored wall-clock and the producer's filename were the same string, "04:50") and still discarded a valid fresh file. Reading the shipped scheduled_utc line would have derived the same key and produced the same miss. A key-only landing therefore does NOT close this defect: the consumer's own existence/freshness evaluation returns false negatives, and must be pinned in the same landing.

ALSO REFUTES the 0-of-N fresh-hit framing. c269 (2026-08-26T04:09:09Z, tick 04:00) HIT — notebook verbatim: "tick-snapshot hit cycle-snapshot-04:05.json (~4min old, <7min) -> skipped direct get_cycle_bootstrap". Today's observed sequence is therefore HIT (c269) / CORRECT-MISS (c271 — floored 04:40, no 04:40 file exists) / INCORRECT-MISS (c272). Behaviour is nondeterministic, not structurally zero. This extends this row's own c263-vs-c264 "applies it INCONSISTENTLY" correction from key DERIVATION to file EVALUATION.

DOC-TRUTH DEFECT (c) — NEW, and the likely proximate cause of that inconsistency. The rule exists in TWO copies that CONTRADICT each other, and the copy an agent reads first names the other as canonical while restating it differently:
  .claude/skills/step-0-cowork/SKILL.md:38   TICK = current UTC time as HH:MM (e.g. "02:05")                                            [NO rounding]
  .claude/skills/cycle-bootstrap/SKILL.md:57 TICK = current UTC time formatted as HH:MM (round to nearest 5-min slot, e.g. 02:05 -> "02:05")  [rounding]
step-0-cowork/SKILL.md:34 points at cycle-bootstrap/SKILL.md as "Full protocol" two lines above its own divergent restatement. The fix must DELETE one copy, not edit both. Note the rounding example is degenerate — 02:05 -> "02:05" is already a 5-multiple, so it never demonstrates floor-vs-nearest; that is why the ambiguity is not self-correcting.

SCOPE UNCHANGED: still an amendment to FIX-CYCLE-SNAPSHOT-PRODUCER-NAMES-BY-WALLCLOCK-CONSUMER-LOOKS-UP-BY-NOMINAL-TICK, still no new row, still NO decoy-protection guard (this tick's file was same-day; the 7-min gate is not implicated and behaved correctly). Fallback correct again — the miss fell through to direct get_cycle_bootstrap, so still no data-integrity impact, only redundant gateway calls.


=== BOUNDING UPDATE — tick 05:00Z, cycle c273 (6th measurement; the c272 false claim did NOT reproduce) ===

Read this together with the c272 block above, which it constrains. Deliberate replication: Step 4.7 wrote docs/data/cycle-snapshot-05:05.json (15412 B, 05:05:48Z) — a 5-multiple, same configuration that produced the c272 false-premise miss one tick earlier. Outcome DIFFERED.

c273 narration is ACCURATE, not fabricated: "no tick-snapshot exact match for current tick (nearest `cycle-snapshot-05:05.json` off-tick) -> treated absent per protocol". It named the fresh file and refused it as off-tick — the c271 shape, not the c272 shape. So the "all cached files stale, prior-day" false claim is INTERMITTENT: one occurrence in six measured cycles (c269, c270, c271, c272, c273 + the c264 baseline), not systematic. Do not scope a fix as if the freshness evaluator is persistently broken — it is not. The c272 block's sentence "the consumer's own existence/freshness evaluation returns false negatives" stands as a recorded event but must be read at that frequency.

WHAT c273 DOES ESTABLISH — it rules out floor-to-5. At its bootstrap (before its 05:10:40Z notebook write) a floored wall-clock key would have been "05:05", matching the file exactly, and it missed. c269 (04:09:09Z HIT on cycle-snapshot-04:05.json) rules out BOTH exact-wall-clock and nominal-tick for that cycle and is consistent only with floor-to-5 / nearest-file. No single derivation explains both cycles. Nondeterministic key derivation is therefore confirmed by construction, independent of any narration.

CAUTION ON ONE READING — the agent's return text (not its notebook) said "05:00-tick vs stagger", which would mean it keyed off the NOMINAL tick, i.e. the scheduled_utc line this row proposes it read. If true, the proposed consumer-side fix is partially already in effect and still misses, because the PRODUCER names by wall-clock (tick-snapshot.md:28, date -u +%H:%M -> 05:05) — the symmetric case of this row's own warning that a producer-only rename makes the consumer arm deterministically worse. Both keys must move to the SAME base in one landing; neither alone converges. Flagged as CONSISTENT WITH, explicitly NOT confirmed: the durable notebook record does not state the key, only the return text does, and return text already proved unreliable once today (c272). Verify against a cycle where the two candidate keys predict different outcomes before building on it.

rows.summary: Step 2.4 Axis C (landed 4f72c694c) promotes the Phase A.5 presence roster — a read its own SKILL.md labels "advisory; non-blocking" — into a PERMISSIVE gate: a current-period cowork-slot marker whose owner_client_session is absent from the roster is skipped as "abandoned, not live", allowing the dispatch to proceed. Presence-absence is a known-ambiguous oracle in this fleet (a live session between presence renewals reads identical to a dead one), and here the ambiguity resolves in the direction whose failure mode is a DOUBLE PUBLISH to a real channel.
rows.action_requested: Harden Step 2.4 Axis C staleness test. Do NOT revert 4f72c694c and do NOT re-open its ACs — Axis D is sound and all 6 ACs verified PASS.
rows.detail:
NOT an AC failure — all 6 ACs verified PASS by the router (fixture 6/6, negative control confirms non-vacuous). This is a new hazard created by the sanctioned design, filed so it is tracked rather than rediscovered.

WHAT LANDED (.claude/skills/dispatch-claim/SKILL.md:702-708):
  # AGE_SEC < CADENCE_SEC — marker IS within the current period (AC-2, no regression).
  if row.owner_client_session not in roster_session_ids:
    continue   # AXIS C / AC-3 — ... treat as abandoned, not live.
roster_session_ids comes from Phase A.5, whose own header (SKILL.md:554,557) reads: "Surface the live cross-team roster ... (advisory; non-blocking)" and is a single task_list_held(kind="session-presence") with NO heartbeat fallback. The diff cites "zero extra round trip" twice as the reason for reusing it — that economy is what selected the weaker oracle.

WHY PRESENCE-ABSENT IS NOT PROOF-OF-DEAD (three independent prior confirmations in this repo):
 (1) feedback_step24_cowork_collision_probe_ttl_exceeds_cadence_daily_false_positive — states the correct staleness oracle for THIS EXACT probe is max(heartbeat_at) across ALL of that session s locks, precisely because absent presence != dead.
 (2) feedback_cron_standalone_step1b1_presence_absence_false_dead_double_arm — presence-ABSENT read as dead produced a DOUBLE ARM in the cron-rearm family. Same oracle, same permissive direction, already burned once.
 (3) feedback_router_almost_rearmed_live_peer_cron_markers_20260822 — presence and heartbeat BOTH misreport for one renewal cadence around a session close; a 2-sample read was needed to disambiguate.

DIRECTION OF FAILURE IS THE POINT. Pre-fix, the bare prefix match blocked unconditionally: over-blocking, whose cost is a skipped slot (recoverable, catch-up exists). Post-fix, Axis C can under-block, whose cost is two dispatchers running the same cowork slot. The published-marker this probe guards exists specifically to stop that; feedback_chef_releases_published_marker_enables_peer_double_publish records the double-publish actually occurring once the marker stopped holding. Axis D does not share this property — it is pure arithmetic on an already-returned claimed_at, no liveness inference.

SCOPE OF EXPOSURE: only the window where a marker is BOTH within its cadence period AND its owner session is momentarily missing from presence — i.e. bounded by one presence-renewal cadence per live dispatcher, not continuous. Small, but it is the exact window a peer tick is most likely to land in, since both sessions fire on the same cron cadence.

CHEAPEST HARDENING (architect s call, not filed as a decision): require BOTH presence-absent AND AGE_SEC > one presence-renewal cadence before skipping — bounds the ambiguity without a second round trip, keeps AC-3 satisfied for genuinely abandoned markers, and costs the truly-dead case only one extra tick of delay. Alternative per (1): max(heartbeat_at) across the owner s locks, which is correct but does add a call.

DO NOT: revert the row or re-open its ACs. Axis D is sound and closes the original 100%-block defect (chef-evening blocked on every fire). Only the Axis C staleness test is in question.

rows.summary: QA-Drain is self-deadlocking. scripts/devteam-review-claim-qa-drain.jq deliberately unions .task_board.done[] into its candidate set (its own line 41), selecting status=="DONE" && effective_next_agent=="qa". scripts/orch-conservation-check.mjs derives LANE_RANK from FLAT_TASK_LANES = [backlog,ready,in_progress,review,qa,done,done_verified], so done(5)->qa(4) is rank-decreasing and scores as a BACKWARD lane move. CONSERVATION_MAX_UNDECLARED_BACKWARD_MOVES defaults to 1, so as soon as TWO done[]-origin rows are eligible the whole orch-apply write ABORTS — taking the legitimately-forward review[]-origin rows in the same batch down with it. The done[] rows can only leave done[] via this drain, so their own presence is what blocks the drain that would clear them. Once done_qa >= 2 the lane is dead until someone intervenes.
rows.action_requested: Resolve the done->qa lane-rank conflict so QA-Drain stops needing a hand-set ORCH_APPLY_DECLARED_BACKWARD_LANE_MOVES. Prefer fix shape 1 or 2; do NOT raise CONSERVATION_MAX_UNDECLARED_BACKWARD_MOVES.
rows.detail:
REPRODUCED LIVE this tick (2026-08-26T03:22Z), then worked around; the underlying conflict is untouched.

THE TWO SHIPPED COMPONENTS DISAGREE ABOUT WHAT `done` MEANS:
 - This board uses done[] = developer-complete, AWAITING QA, and done_verified[] = post-QA terminal.
   Evidence: both blocked rows carry status=DONE AND next_agent=qa. A row that still names qa as its
   next agent is by definition not terminal.
 - orch-conservation-check.mjs:216 + :378 assume the array order IS the pipeline order, so `done`
   ranks ABOVE `qa`. Under that assumption done->qa can only be a regression.
Neither component is individually wrong; the lane vocabulary is. LANE_RANK is a single flat array
reused for a board with TWO terminal lanes and a non-linear DONE->QA->DONE_VERIFIED path.

MEASURED THIS TICK:
  review[] eligible (status=REVIEW, next=qa): 2
  done[]   eligible (status=DONE,   next=qa): 2   <- exceeds the tolerance of 1 by exactly one row
  first attempt: [orch-conservation-check] ABORTED — lane-placement violation: 2 task row(s) moved
                 BACKWARD ... exceeding the tolerated 1 undeclared backward move(s)
  rows drained on that attempt: 0 (of 4 eligible, including 3 P0)
Both done[]-origin rows carry updated_at=2026-08-26T01:23:29Z — the same stamp, i.e. one batch write
earlier tonight created the deadlock. That is why this lane drained normally before today and why the
defect is only now observable.

WHY IT IS A DEADLOCK, NOT A THROTTLE: a done[]-origin row leaves done[] only by being claimed into
qa[] by THIS script. While two or more sit there, every invocation aborts, so none is ever claimed, so
the count never falls back to 1. It is stable at >=2 forever without outside intervention. The blast
radius is the whole batch: review[]-origin rows that move strictly forward are discarded along with it,
so a lane holding 27 review rows drains zero.

THIS TICK S WORKAROUND (explicitly NOT a fix): re-ran with
ORCH_APPLY_DECLARED_BACKWARD_LANE_MOVES set to exactly the two ids, the hatch the guard s own abort
message documents for "this write genuinely intends to move these rows backward on purpose". Intent is
genuine and pre-documented in the claim script, and the declaration was scoped to two named ids after
diffing candidate-vs-live across all seven lanes to confirm nothing ELSE moved non-forward. Batch of 4
then landed (3 P0 + 1 P1), review 29->27, qa 3->7, done 8->6. A router setting a safety-bypass env var
by hand every time the lane is selected is not a durable answer — the next tick, and every peer session,
hits the same wall with no memory of this analysis.

FIX DIRECTION (architect s call, three shapes, ranked):
 1. Teach the lane-placement dimension that done->qa is legitimate when the row carries
    next_agent=="qa" (i.e. exempt the transition the qa-drain script is designed to make). Narrowest,
    keeps the guard fully armed against real stale-revert writes, no vocabulary change.
 2. Have devteam-review-claim-qa-drain.jq emit the declaration itself for its own done[]-origin picks,
    so the caller never needs the env var. Localizes the knowledge in the component that has the intent.
 3. Split the lane vocabulary so the rank array stops conflating "developer done" with "verified done".
    Correct but far wider blast radius — every consumer of FLAT_TASK_LANES.
Do NOT simply raise CONSERVATION_MAX_UNDECLARED_BACKWARD_MOVES: the tolerance is what catches genuine
stale-full-doc reverts, and raising it to cover N done-origin rows disarms it for exactly the class it
exists to catch.

RELATED, NOT DUPLICATE: feedback_caller_readback_lane_narrower_than_claim_script_silently_kills_lane
records the SECONDARY drain dying on the SAME review-union-done design — there the caller s readback was
narrower than the script s selector; here the conservation guard rejects the union s done-half outright.
Same union, two different consumers, two different silent-death mechanisms. Worth fixing together.

rows.summary: alert-commander writes a WRONG tick key (notebook header + published-marker) where the spec requires the NOMINAL cron tick. ROOT CAUSE REVISED 04:00Z — the derivation is NONDETERMINISTIC, not a scope gap. CONTROLLED EVIDENCE, one tick, two instances: the 04:00Z fan-out spawned alert-commander TWICE (slots alert-commander-market and alert-commander-critical, an undeclared same-agent collision). Both received the IDENTICAL scheduled_utc=2026-08-26T04:00:00.000Z in their spawn prompt, both read the SAME tick-snapshot docs/data/cycle-snapshot-04:05.json (c269 states the hit explicitly), same agent type, same flow files, same instant. c268 wrote tick=04:05; c269 wrote tick=04:00 — CORRECT. Same inputs, different outputs. That is dispositive: a scope gap or missing wiring would be DETERMINISTIC. WITHDRAWN: the SCOPE-GAP root cause in the prior summary ('sits outside ANCHOR-3's enumerated scope, never wired to consume scheduled_utc'). c269 consumed it correctly with no wiring change, so the capability is present. Corroborating: news-scout is likewise absent from ANCHOR-3's list yet stamped c287 at exactly 2026-08-26T04:00:00Z this tick, against its own prior three cycles at +7/+8min (c284 20:08, c283 16:07, c282 12:07). ANCHOR-3's enumeration does not predict who consumes the token. OPEN QUESTION ANSWERED: 'why did c263/c264 get it right' — variance, not different wiring. Nothing distinguishes the correct runs from the incorrect ones except which candidate source the run happened to pick. FREQUENCY CORRECTED AGAIN (3rd time; it has been wrong in a different direction each time): NOT '3 of 5 consecutive'. Now 4 wrong of 7 known — c265 03:20/03:15, c266 03:35/03:30, c267 03:49/03:45, c268 04:05/04:00 wrong; c263, c264, c269 right — and the streak is BROKEN, by c269, at the same instant c268 extended it. Do not describe this as worsening or consecutive. REVISED FIX SHAPE: not 'wire alert-commander to consume scheduled_utc' (it already can). The flow offers at least three plausible tick sources — the scheduled_utc prompt token, the tick-snapshot FILENAME, and the wall clock — and names none as authoritative, so the run picks one. Fix = stage-bootstrap.md must name scheduled_utc as the SINGLE authoritative source and explicitly forbid deriving the tick from the snapshot filename or from date -u when the token is present. A nondeterministic defect will not be caught by a one-run verification, so any QA gate must sample repeatedly. Impact argument unchanged: MARKER_KEY is cross-tick dedup, so a mis-derived key silently stops the gate gating. No damage yet — every failing cycle exited silently and stage-dispatch-log.md:38-39 forbids claiming the marker then. ALSO WITHDRAWN EARLIER (unchanged, keep): floor-5, round-5, cycle-bootstrap name-collision, and header==snapshot-key mechanisms, all falsified by c267.
rows.action_requested: Fold into the SAME landing as rtr-20260826T0257-snapshotagentconsumerclock — both arms are one root cause (agent invents a tick instead of reading the scheduled_utc line the dispatcher already ships) and one consumer-side edit closes both. Do NOT reopen the FIX-CHEF-MARKER-KEY-ANCHOR-* rows; all 4 are correctly DONE_VERIFIED and alert-commander was outside ANCHOR-3s enumerated scope.
rows.detail:
SECOND consumer of "the tick" inside alert-commander derives it differently from the first, and this one is load-bearing for dedup rather than for a cache.

WHAT IS SPECIFIED: docs/agents/alert-commander/flow/stage-dispatch-log.md:96 defines the notebook header as `## c<NNN> · <ISO-timestamp> (slot=<dispatched slot>, tick=<nominal tick>)`, and :39 defines the published-marker gate key as MARKER_KEY="published:alert-commander-market:<nominal_tick>", with <nominal_tick> = "this cycle's dispatched tick". Both want the NOMINAL cron instant.

MEASURED, 3 consecutive cycles (header read from docs/agent-memory/notebooks/alert-commander.md; nominal tick read from this dispatcher's own preflight verdict for the same fire):
  c263 — wall 02:54:46Z, nominal 02:45 → header 02:45. Floored to the 15-min boundary. CORRECT.
  c264 — wall 03:09:45Z, nominal 03:00 → header 03:00. Floored. CORRECT.
  c265 — wall 03:21:45Z, nominal 03:15 → header 03:20. ROUNDED to a 5-min multiple. WRONG.
03:20 is not a cron boundary for this slot (cron is */15 2-8 * * 1-5). It is exactly the key the snapshot lookup uses. So the agent did not merely mis-floor — it appears to have written the SNAPSHOT-lookup key into the field the spec reserves for the NOMINAL tick. Two different "tick" concepts live in this flow with no naming that separates them, and this cycle they cross-contaminated.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN THE SNAPSHOT ARM: a wrong snapshot key costs a cache miss and falls through to get_cycle_bootstrap — zero data-integrity impact, which is exactly what rtr-20260826T0257-snapshotagentconsumerclock (already drained to architect) documents. A wrong MARKER_KEY is different: the published-marker gate is one of the two mechanisms slot-claim.md names as providing CROSS-TICK dedup (the other is last_fired boundary dedup in cowork-match-slots.js). A marker written under published:alert-commander-market:03:20 does not suppress a later cycle checking published:alert-commander-market:03:15, so the gate silently stops gating. Same failure class as feedback_chef_releases_published_marker_enables_peer_double_publish.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED — limits of this evidence:
  (a) NO damage observed. c265 hit the firing gate and exited silently, and stage-dispatch-log.md:38-39 forbids claiming the marker on a silent-exit cycle, so no marker was written with the bad key. The risk is latent, realised only on a FIRING cycle that mis-derives.
  (b) INTERMITTENT, 1 of 3. Do not model this as deterministic; a fix verified on one cycle proves nothing.
  (c) This is probably a SCOPE GAP, not a regression of the FIX-CHEF-MARKER-KEY-ANCHOR-* rows (all 4 DONE_VERIFIED, correctly). spawn-fanout.md's ANCHOR-3 comment enumerates the slots its SCHEDULED_UTC_LINE was meant to reach — chef-morning/eod/evening, digest-daily, digest-sunday, fb-daily, tnb-audit — and alert-commander is NOT in that list. So the producer half was never intended to serve this agent. Do not reopen the ANCHOR rows on the strength of this.

THE FIX IS ALREADY IN TRANSIT AND STILL DISCARDED: this dispatcher composes SCHEDULED_UTC_LINE into EVERY spawn prompt unconditionally, alert-commander included — the 03:15Z prompt carried the literal line scheduled_utc=2026-08-26T03:15:00.000Z. `grep -rn scheduled_utc docs/agents/alert-commander/` returns ZERO HITS (re-confirmed this tick). The agent is guessing a value it is already being handed. One consumer-side edit — derive nominal_tick from the scheduled_utc line, fall back to floor-to-cron-boundary only when absent — fixes THIS arm and the snapshot arm in rtr-20260826T0257 in the same landing, and needs no producer change.

NOT a duplicate of ARCH-CRON-THREE-TIME-BASES-UNIFY (checked): that SPIKE is about timezone/DST bases across scheduling PLANES (UTC vs Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh vs machine-local France). This is tick-KEY derivation inside a single UTC plane. Archive (docs/data/orch/archive/2026-06.json, 2026-08.json) searched by subject — no prior row.
=== AMENDED 2026-08-26T03:40Z (router, cowork 03:30Z tick) — SECOND OCCURRENCE, CONSECUTIVE. Two corrections to the text above and one new root cause. ===

CORRECTION 1 — limit (b) above UNDERSTATES the frequency. It says "INTERMITTENT, 1 of 3". Measured now over four consecutive cycles:
  c263 — wall 02:54:46Z, nominal 02:45 -> header 02:45. CORRECT (nominal).
  c264 — wall 03:09:45Z, nominal 03:00 -> header 03:00. CORRECT (nominal). Its SNAPSHOT lookup separately used 03:05 — i.e. this cycle held the two values apart correctly.
  c265 — wall 03:21:45Z, nominal 03:15 -> header 03:20. WRONG.
  c266 — wall 03:37:46Z, nominal 03:30 -> header 03:35. WRONG.
So: 2 of 4, and the two failures are CONSECUTIVE, not scattered. Limit (b) as originally written invites treating this as noise. It is not noise — the last two cycles both failed.

CORRECTION 2 — the original text calls the wrong value "ROUNDED to a 5-min multiple". That is imprecise and would send a fixer looking for the wrong arithmetic. c266's wall clock 03:37:46 rounds-to-NEAREST-5 as 03:40, but the header says 03:35. The operation is FLOOR-to-5, and more importantly it is applied to the wall clock AT BOOTSTRAP TIME, not to the notebook-write time.

NEW ROOT CAUSE — a NAME COLLISION across two skill files, which explains why the same agent gets it right some cycles and wrong others:
  .claude/skills/cycle-bootstrap/SKILL.md Step -1 defines, verbatim:
      TICK = current UTC time formatted as HH:MM (round to nearest 5-min slot, e.g. 02:05 -> "02:05")
      SNAPSHOT_PATH = docs/data/cycle-snapshot-<HH:MM>.json
  docs/agents/alert-commander/flow/stage-dispatch-log.md:39,:96 define MARKER_KEY and the notebook header in terms of <nominal_tick>.
  BOTH quantities are spelled "tick". They are not the same number and never were. On c265 and c266 the header value equals cycle-bootstrap's Step -1 TICK exactly (c265 bootstrap ~03:20 -> 03:20; c266 bootstrap ~03:35 -> 03:35, the file it reported hitting was 55s old at that moment). On c263/c264 the header value equals the nominal cron tick instead. Which of the two identically-named values reaches the header varies per cycle. That is the defect: not bad arithmetic, but two live variables sharing one name across the two files this agent reads every cycle. A fix that only corrects the arithmetic will regress.

EMPIRICAL REFUTATION OF THE OBVIOUS PRODUCER-SIDE FIX — the 03:30Z spawn prompt carried the literal line scheduled_utc=2026-08-26T03:30:00.000Z (this dispatcher composes SCHEDULED_UTC_LINE unconditionally; verified in the prompt it sent). The agent still wrote 03:35. So the value is demonstrably SUPPLIED and IGNORED — not missing. Any fix framed as "start shipping scheduled_utc to alert-commander" is already done and will change nothing. The edit must be consumer-side, inside alert-commander's flow, and should RENAME as well as re-derive so the collision cannot reappear.

INCIDENTAL, bears on the sibling row rtr-20260826T0257-snapshotagentconsumerclock: c266 reported HITTING docs/data/cycle-snapshot-03:34.json. Its own Step -1 rule can only ever compute a 5-minute-multiple path (03:35), so an exact-path lookup could not have found a file named 03:34 — the consumer is evidently not following its own documented exact-match rule either. Note this when landing that row: the consumer's lookup behaviour is itself undocumented, so "fix the name" may not be sufficient on its own. Contrast c265, which DID follow the exact-match rule and therefore missed a snapshot that was 1 minute old.

rows.detail:
E-1 EVIDENCE. jq over docs/data/db-integrity-history.json: array length 200 (at cap), newest two entries scan_ts=2026-08-26T04:59:59Z and 2026-08-26T05:00:18Z, both tables_checked=17, both findings|length=3. A structural diff of the two entries with .scan_ts deleted differs on exactly one line: context.market_prices_freshness. Every finding object — table, class, detail, verdict, severity, root_cause_hypothesis, signal_id, and the whole embedded dedup_check object including matched_task_id/matched_signal_id — is byte-identical across the pair.

E-2 CONSEQUENCE A, trail-slot burn. The array is AT the 200 cap. Each append rotates the oldest entry out. A cycle that appends twice therefore destroys TWO historical entries to record ONE scan, permanently shortening the retained window. Six observed duplicate appends means the trail has already lost ~6 entries of depth beyond its nominal 200-scan horizon.

E-3 CONSEQUENCE B, double-weighted deterministic reads. The cron prompt states the count-over-time comparison is read DETERMINISTICALLY from the history's `counts` fields by the router/dev-team, precisely so no LLM editorializes a trend. A duplicated cycle contributes two samples with identical counts for one observation, silently double-weighting that tick in any such series and damping an adjacent real move. This defeats the guard's own stated purpose rather than merely cluttering the file.

E-4 ROOT-CAUSE HYPOTHESIS (asymmetric idempotency). scripts/db-integrity-history-append.sh appends unconditionally on every invocation — correct by design for a trail whose contract is 'every scan logged, real + checked-clean'. But the SIGNAL side of the very same helper IS idempotency-guarded: line 92 passes --check-id "${table}-${CLASS_TXT}" to emit-audit-signal.sh --e3-only. So a double-run is protected against emitting duplicate signal rows and is NOT protected against writing duplicate history entries. The guard exists in the helper already; it is simply not applied to the append itself.

E-5 DETECTION GAP. Nothing reads back the trail for same-cycle duplicates, and the helper's own success assertion cannot catch this: at the 200 cap a correct append reports history_len_before=200, history_len_after=200, so a second append reports the identical success shape as the first. Length is structurally incapable of discriminating one append from two once the array is capped.

E-6 NOT COVERED. Scanned .signal_queue.rows[] and all task_board lanes (backlog/ready/review/qa/in_progress/done/done_verified/archive) for twice|duplicate entr|double.?append|append.*idempot|two entries|re-?append. Hits are unrelated (qa-drain duplicate spawn, janitor health-recheck idempotency, orch-apply mktemp). FIX-DBINTEGRITY-HISTORY-FINDINGS-MEMBERSHIP-FREE-JUDGMENT-AND-MULTITABLE-TABLE-FIELD governs WHICH findings enter findings[] and the multi-table `table` field — not how many entries one cycle writes. Do not fold into it.

REMEDY CONSTRAINT. Do NOT fix by making the append conditional on content — two genuinely distinct scans can legitimately produce identical findings[] and identical counts, and suppressing those would re-create the far worse 'cycle writes no record' defect (rtr-20260826T0435-datatiercyclewrotenorecord). Bind on the CYCLE, not on the content: have the caller pass the fire tick (the cron already knows it — the router hands the agent FIRE_TICK verbatim in the spawn prompt) and have the helper refuse a second append carrying a fire tick already present in the newest entry, exiting non-zero with a distinct code so the double-call is loud rather than silent.

SUGGESTED COMPLETION PREDICATE. After the fix, two back-to-back invocations of the helper under the same FIRE_TICK must yield exactly one new entry and a non-zero exit on the second — verifiable by `jq '[.[] | select(.fire_tick == "<T>")] | length'` returning 1.

RECURRENCE EVIDENCE ONLY — NOT re-filed, each already owned:
(a) DEDUP OVER-MATCH. This cycle's daily_ohlcv finding was suppressed as already-open:LINT-OHLCV-WRITE-BYPASS — a P1 backlog row whose summary is 'Custom ESLint rule for writer-bypass sentinel pattern', with next_agent=null. That task is not tracking the 336-row OHLC constraint residue; it matched on the token 'ohlcv'. Worse, matched_signal_id for BOTH daily_ohlcv AND financial_reports resolved to the SAME row, mdjg-20260825T055425 — the 2026-08-25 Docker-outage incident, which mentions those two table names only inside its data-safety prose ('daily_ohlcv=789926 ... financial_reports=263'). An incidental row-count mention in an unrelated incident narrative is being read as 'this table's anomaly is already tracked'. Owned by rtr-20260826T0336-dedupmatchedfeatureepic and FIX-DEDUPCHECK-MATCHEDTASKID-UNANCHORED-SUBSTRING-MISLABEL.
(b) MEMBERSHIP INSTABILITY, now with live proof of false-negative. This cycle recorded 3 findings; the immediately prior cycle (c11, 03:59:38Z) recorded 6. The four that vanished were re-read live by the router at 05:01Z via file:...?immutable=1 (market.db-wal confirmed absent) and ALL FOUR ARE STILL TRUE: deep_fetch_stats COUNT(*)=0 (c11 FAIL/HIGH); deep_fetch_queue 2579 rows with status done=0, expired=2515, pending=30, vps-failed=34 — zero rows have ever reached done (c11 STALE/HIGH, producer-live-consumer-dead); fred_series_daily max_fetched_at=2026-08-23 12:13:02, ~64.8h stale against the prompt's own >48h threshold (c11 STALE/HIGH); macro_indicators 1 row with manufacturing_pmi NULL (c11 STALE/WARN, empty columns). So absence from findings[] this cycle was not ambiguous — it was measurably wrong in all four cases. This strengthens histrec-20260825T080555Z section (A) from 'absence is ambiguous between checked-clean and checked-anomalous-not-recorded' to 'absence was demonstrated to mean checked-anomalous-not-recorded', on four tables simultaneously, three of them HIGH. Owned by histrec-20260825T080555Z (A) and FIX-DBINTEGRITY-HISTORY-FINDINGS-MEMBERSHIP-FREE-JUDGMENT-AND-MULTITABLE-TABLE-FIELD; recorded here as corroboration for whoever picks that row up, not as a new claim.
(c) NO NEW ROW FOR THE FOUR STALE TABLES THEMSELVES. Each is already open (FIX-DEEPFETCH-PIPELINE-100PCT-UNFETCHED-PRODUCER-LIVE-CONSUMER-DEAD, FIX-MACRO-ISM-FRED-API-KEY-MISSING, FIX-MACRO-INDICATORS-EMPTY-COLUMNS). fred_series_daily crossing the 48h threshold is a magnitude move on an already-open table and the GROWTH-DELTA EXCEPTION forbids re-signalling on that basis alone.

WHAT WENT RIGHT THIS CYCLE, for the record: the trail entry WAS written and the completion predicate held (newest scan_ts 2026-08-26T05:00:18Z >= FIRE_TICK 2026-08-26T04:56:05Z), and the agent emitted the RAW-COUNTS-STDOUT and RAW-APPEND-STDOUT transcription blocks for the first time across four cycles. This row was filed at 05:05Z off the 04:59:59Z/05:00:18Z pair. For the very next cycle (FIRE_TICK 2026-08-26T05:26:05Z) the router put the countermeasure directly in the spawn prompt, verbatim and prominent, as two numbered clauses: R-3(a) "call scripts/db-integrity-history-append.sh EXACTLY ONCE this cycle... if you are unsure whether an earlier invocation landed, READ the file for scan_ts >= FIRE_TICK rather than re-running", and R-3(b) "at the 200 cap, {history_len_before:200, history_len_after:200} IS success — the helper's grew-by-one assertion cannot fire there; judge by exit code and newest scan_ts, NEVER by a length delta." The defect recurred anyway, with the identical signature: two entries 33s apart (05:29:49Z, 05:30:22Z), tables_checked=17 on both, findings|length=4 on both, and a structural diff with .scan_ts deleted differing on exactly ONE line — context.market_prices_freshness (05:29:41.443Z vs 05:30:03.277Z). Every finding object is byte-identical across the pair, embedded dedup_check included. This is the 7th and 8th duplicate entry in the current array.

WHY E-7 CHANGES THE FIX CLASS, NOT JUST THE COUNT. Before this cycle the row's remedy was arguably contestable — a reader could reasonably have proposed "tighten the prompt" as the cheap fix and deferred the helper change. That option is now measured and dead: the tightest available prompt-level instruction, naming the exact script, the exact count, the exact misleading success shape, and the exact correct recovery action, was delivered and did not suppress the behaviour. The REMEDY CONSTRAINT above (bind the append on the CYCLE via a caller-supplied fire tick, refuse a second append carrying a fire tick already present, exit non-zero and loud) is therefore not one option among several — it is the only remaining one. Severity raised MED -> HIGH on that basis: not because the blast radius grew, but because the cheap mitigation was eliminated while the trail keeps losing two capped slots per affected cycle.

E-8 THE SELF-REPORT BLIND SPOT IS ALSO REPRODUCIBLE, AND THE TERMINAL-SHAPE CONTRACT DOES NOT CLOSE IT. The same spawn prompt mandated a three-block verbatim terminal shape ([RAW-COUNTS-STDOUT], [RAW-APPEND-STDOUT] incl. exit code, [RAW-SIGNAL-IDS]) specifically so a double-call would be visible in the agent's own return. The agent complied with the format and still reported exactly ONE append — the 05:30:22Z call, {"ok":true,...,"history_len_before":200,"history_len_after":200,...}, exit 0. The 05:29:49Z call appears nowhere in the return. So a correctly-formatted, contract-compliant self-report is consistent with both one append and two, and the duplicate is again discoverable ONLY by reading the file afterwards. Any acceptance test for the fix must therefore assert on the FILE, never on the agent's transcript.

RECURRENCE EVIDENCE ONLY — NOT re-filed, owned elsewhere:
(d) NOTEBOOK HISTORY-ENTRY CROSS-REFERENCE POINTS AT AN UNRELATED CYCLE. docs/agent-memory/notebooks/system-auditor.md section c12 (committed 3c41f8710) states 'Recorded to docs/data/db-integrity-history.json entry #200 (at cap). Scan timestamp: 2026-08-26T03:00:24Z.' Neither of this cycle's two appends carries that scan_ts. 03:00:24Z is a real entry, but it belongs to a cycle ~2.5h earlier; this cycle wrote 05:29:49Z and 05:30:22Z. So the durable human-readable record cross-references the wrong trail entry — a hand-authored identifier standing in for a measured one, which is precisely the failure mode and the fix shape of FIX-AUDITOR-DATATIER-DURABLE-TRAIL-NARRATED-NUMBERS-CONTRADICT-OWN-EVIDENCE AC-(1) ('every numeric field in a DATA-tier durable record is COMPUTED from the raw timestamp/count it cites, never authored in prose'). Recorded here as corroboration for whoever picks that row up; not a new claim and not a new row.
(e) MEMBERSHIP INSTABILITY, third consecutive cycle. c11 recorded 6 findings, c12(05:00:18Z) 3, this cycle 4. deep_fetch_queue, fred_series_daily and macro_indicators are absent from findings[] again, all three confirmed still-true by direct read at 05:01Z last cycle. Notably the agent DID observe deep_fetch_queue this cycle — 'deep_fetch_queue has 2583 rows (mostly expired|2518, vps-failed|34)' — but folded it into the deep_fetch_stats finding's detail prose instead of emitting it as its own finding, so it is unqueryable as a finding. Owned by histrec-20260825T080555Z (A) and FIX-DBINTEGRITY-HISTORY-FINDINGS-MEMBERSHIP-FREE-JUDGMENT-AND-MULTITABLE-TABLE-FIELD.
(f) NO RE-SIGNAL FOR THE FOUR STALE TABLES. deep_fetch_queue moved 2579->2583 rows (expired 2515->2518) since last cycle. That is a magnitude delta on an already-open table; the GROWTH-DELTA EXCEPTION forbids re-signalling on that basis alone. Each remains owned by its existing row.

WHAT WENT RIGHT THIS CYCLE, for the record: the trail entry WAS written (the 'cycle writes no record' defect rtr-20260826T0435-datatiercyclewrotenorecord did not recur, 2nd consecutive clean cycle), the three mandated raw-stdout blocks were emitted, zero new signal rows were minted, and the one REAL finding was correctly suppressed as already-open against FIX-DEEPFETCH-PIPELINE-100PCT-UNFETCHED-PRODUCER-LIVE-CONSUMER-DEAD — a genuine, correctly-matched dedup hit this time, not a token collision.
E-9 -- 2026-08-26T05:56:04Z CYCLE: DID NOT RECUR. Exactly ONE entry at-or-after the fire tick (scan_ts 2026-08-26T06:00:10Z), confirmed by independent router readback of the file, not from the agent self-report. This cycle carried R-3(a)+(b) -- the clauses that FAILED last cycle -- PLUS a NEW (c): a mandatory post-append readback the agent must run and report verbatim. The agent reported 1 and disk agrees.

What (c) buys durably, independent of whether the duplicate ever recurs, is that a duplicate can no longer be INVISIBLE in the agent's own return -- that is the E-8 blind spot, and it is closed for this cycle.
--- E-10 (router, 2026-08-26T06:35Z, cycle fire 06:26:04Z): R-3(c) HELD A SECOND CONSECUTIVE CYCLE. Disk-verified: exactly 1 entry with scan_ts >= 06:26:04Z (scan_ts=06:28:19Z); pre-spawn baseline at-or-after the fire tick was 0. Structural implication for the fix: a readback that counts rows/matches is a necessary but insufficient guard — the next arm must assert on the SHAPE of what was written (tables_checked non-null, findings key present), which is a helper-side assertion, not a promptable instruction.
E-11 (router, 2026-08-26T07:05Z) — OCCURRENCE 3, and the first one whose harm reaches a TRACKED artifact. Fire 06:56:04Z. Verified by jq on docs/data/db-integrity-history.json, not from the agent's return: TWO records at-or-after the fire tick, scan_ts 2026-08-26T06:58:59Z and 2026-08-26T07:00:10Z. rows.summary: Recurring unactionable push-block condition has no notify-once/backoff contract: 3 adjacent alert-commander cycles on the IDENTICAL pre-existing block sent/declined/sent bug-channel telegrams. No mechanism exists (the only dedup guard is MARKET-scoped), so it floods the bug channel ~every 15min all session.
rows.action_requested: Triage: define a shared notify-once/backoff contract for recurring known operational conditions across cowork committers. Do NOT close by fixing the push block itself — that is separately owned.
rows.detail:
Three consecutive alert-commander cycles hit the IDENTICAL pre-existing condition — the repo-wide pre-push size-lint block on six offender files none of them touched — and made OPPOSITE decisions about notifying the bug channel.

c272 (2026-08-26T04:53:56Z, tick 04:45) SENT a bug-channel telegram.
c273 (2026-08-26T05:10:40Z, tick 05:00) DECLINED, citing the prior send as a duplicate.
c274 (2026-08-26T05:25:26Z, tick 05:15) SENT again, message_id 5735.

Same agent, same flow, adjacent 15-minute cycles, unchanged upstream condition. The
discriminator is not the condition, so it is agent discretion rather than a gate.

CONFIRMED ABSENCE OF A MECHANISM (checked before filing, not assumed): the only telegram
dedup guard in this agent flow tree is docs/agents/alert-commander/flow/stage-dispatch-log.md:77,
and it is scoped to MARKET alerts via write_alert_verdict duplicate:true for a (ticker,
alertSource) pair. Nothing governs bug-channel operational notices. c273 declining was
therefore unreproducible judgment, not a rule firing — which is why c274 reverted.

WHY IT MATTERS. alert-commander-market runs `*/15 2-8 * * 1-5`, so at the sending rate this
emits roughly one bug-channel telegram every 15 minutes across the whole VN session for a
blockage that (a) is already documented, (b) has two board rows open against it
(FIX-PREPUSH-SIZELINT-BCTCSCALARAGGREGATOR-1206L-STRANDS-117-COMMITS and
FIX-SIZELINT-PREPUSH-SCANS-WORKING-TREE-NOT-PUSH-RANGE, both dispatch_lane:null), and (c)
no cowork agent has the zone or standing to fix. The cost is signal-to-noise on the one
channel real incidents arrive through. This is a noise/observability defect, not a
correctness one — the commits themselves land locally and correctly every cycle.

SCOPE NOTE — do NOT let this be closed by "fix the push block". The push block is separately
owned by the two rows above. The defect here is that a recurring, unactionable, already-known
condition has no notify-once/backoff contract, so any future recurring condition of the same
shape will flood the same way. The fix belongs wherever a shared operational-notice guard
would live, not inside alert-commander alone — every cowork agent that commits hits this same
pre-push hook.

Observed and verified by the router across three cowork ticks; the c274 sample landed in the
05:15Z tick return (dispatcher commit 45f0f7542, agent commit 7c33afa61).

rows.summary: kinh-dich reading_composer test suite cannot detect Vietnamese text corruption: every .Vi localized field is unpinned while .En fields are snapshot-tested. A real regression stripping diacritics from all 64 MarketTrendLabel entries passed the full suite green.
rows.action_requested: Mint a row to add content-fidelity assertions over the Vietnamese half of localized fields in apps/kinh-dich-service/pkg/module/reading_composer. Consider whether the same .En-only snapshot asymmetry exists in other localized services.
rows.detail:
VERIFIED STRUCTURALLY BY ROUTER, not merely reported by qa.

During the go:embed prose extraction, intermediate commit 928557a66 stripped Vietnamese diacritics from all 64 MarketTrendLabel entries (THUAN LOI for THUẬN LỢI etc). Fixed in 88e93338f, so HEAD is correct and this is NOT an open data defect. The defect is in the DETECTOR.

The full suite passed green on the broken commit. Root cause is structural, not a near-miss:

1. TestQueReferenceHexagram1Snapshot (hexagram_invariant_test.go:296) is the only content-fidelity test in the package. It pins exactly two fields, CoreMeaning.En and Phases[0].Gloss.En, on hexagram 1 only. Both are ENGLISH. It is blind to Vietnamese corruption on every hexagram including the one it covers.

2. All 7 invariant tests assert emptiness and cardinality only (is empty / got %d want 64). Diacritic stripping preserves non-emptiness and preserves count 64, so every assertion holds.

3. grep for any accented literal or MarketTrendLabel across all *_test.go in the package returns ZERO hits. No test anywhere pins an accented string.

Generalization worth checking: the suite snapshot-tests the .En half of localized fields and leaves the .Vi half entirely unasserted. METHOD, reusable: probe the running binary for the package path, then DISCRIMINATE against a stripped-binary explanation before trusting a zero.

A bare 0 is ambiguous (Go builds are often linked with -s -w). The discriminator settles it:

METHOD AND ITS LIMITS — the useful part, because the naive version is wrong twice over.

TRAP 1, timezone. docker image inspect .Created is UTC; git log %cI is local (+0200 on this host). Comparing them raw manufactured five phantom STALE rows at +0d. Force git to UTC before any comparison. Cf. feedback_hand_typed_iso_timestamps_drift_into_the_future — same +2h family, different surface.

TRAP 2, probe granularity. Probing the binary for a PACKAGE PATH only discriminates when an ENTIRE package became newly-linked. stock-price qualified: nothing imported vndirect-quote-mapper until 912a4bf79, so Go dead-code elimination had dropped it, and strings gave a clean 0 against a non-stripped binary (discriminator: stock-price/pkg 77 hits, two sibling primitives linked by name). technical-analysis did NOT qualify: 969b5d96b merely extracted a handler into the EXISTING pkg/interface/http, which was already linked (45 hits). A package probe there is vacuous, not negative.

Also vacuous: probing for symbols that predate the build. RouterConfig (2026-06-14) and FetchBudgetSec (2026-06-14) both predate their images. The only genuinely-new symbols in e10e2a500 (HangingOMOProvider, BoundedByFetchBudget) are test doubles and never enter a production binary. Verify a probe symbol first appeared AFTER the image build before trusting its absence.

FINDINGS.

1. stock-price — CONFIRMED UNDEPLOYED (structural). Image 2026-08-06T15:58:56Z, source HEAD 2026-08-26T05:21:22Z, drift 469h. vndirect-quote-mapper absent from /app/stock-price against a non-stripped binary. Live impact: JSON null change still collapses to 0, so unavailable is served as a genuine flat day. Detail in sibling signal rtr-20260826T0628-stockpricefixabsentfrombinary.

2. macro-indicators — CONFIRMED UNDEPLOYED (behavioral). Image 2026-07-29T23:58:16Z, source 2026-08-11T17:41:28Z, drift 305h. e10e2a500 wraps the combined current+fallback fetch in context.WithTimeout(ctx, FetchBudgetSec) where domain.FetchBudgetSec = 8 (ports.go:24), specifically so two hangs cannot stack. Timed POST /liquidity-state on 127.0.0.1:5004: 12.50s, 12.23s, then 2.09s. The first two exceed the 8s bound by ~4.3s, i.e. the bound is not being enforced; the 2.09s run is a cache hit that does not exercise the fetch path. Live impact: the handler runs ~12.3s against a 15s cron deadline, ~2.5s margin, which is the exact failure e10e2a500 was written to prevent. NOTE this was confirmed by a DIFFERENT method than stock-price — no string probe can see an added context.WithTimeout built from pre-existing symbols.

3. technical-analysis — DRIFT ONLY, NOT CONFIRMED. Image 2026-07-15T15:07:07Z, source 2026-07-31T23:15:44Z, drift 392h. Post-build commits are a /health handler extraction, a dedup refactor and dead-code removal. No valid probe exists: the package was already linked, and the new symbols are not distinctive. EVIDENCE.

  docker logs <pdfx> | grep -c ocr_pages_worker or _rasterize_and_ocr_page_worker or infrastructure.ocr_worker  -> 0
  docker logs <pdfx> | wc -l   -> 3895

  container started 2026-08-26T00:33:39Z

Logging works in the container generally (3895 lines). This ONE module emits nothing. Among the silent calls is logger.info at ocr_worker.py:199 on the main OCR entry path, which should fire on every invocation, so this is not a rare-branch artifact.

WHAT IT BLOCKS. The standing goal is to replace tesseract with PaddleOCR to IMPROVE BCTC extraction quality. Quality improvement is a measured claim. With this module dark there is no denominator: we cannot count how often the rescue fires, cannot compare per-page char yield tesseract vs paddle, and cannot detect the budget-exhaustion warning at :509 that the code itself added precisely so a page silently reverting to a weak read would be VISIBLE. That warning cannot be seen either.

CORRECTS AN EARLIER ROUTER CLAIM. Router previously recorded that mechanism B (ocr_worker page-rescue, PaddleOCR lang=vi, ungated) RUNS in production today. Code-reachability remains true: grep -c OCR_TEXT_BACKEND ocr_worker.py = 0, so nothing gates it. But there is NO execution evidence, and this defect means there CANNOT be. The honest state is reachable and ungated, firing rate UNKNOWN and currently unknowable. Distinguish reachable from observed. The code-in-image is not branch-executes lesson applies to the router own earlier conclusion here.

NOTE the 4 paddle hits that DO appear in docker logs are all pek_engine_adapter (PP-StructureV2 table mode, mechanism A, PID 1). Mechanism A is observable; mechanism B is not. Do NOT read mechanism A log lines as evidence about mechanism B. That exact conflation invalidated an earlier analysis.

LIKELY ROOT CAUSE, UNVERIFIED: the rescue runs in a multiprocessing pool child (_paddle_ocr_worker_instance) while PEK runs in PID 1. Pool-child stdout/stderr capture or logging-handler propagation is the first place to look. Verify before fixing.

Dedup was run against the whole board by subject before filing. Three adjacent rows exist; none covers this:

1. FIX-NOTBEFORE-DEFERRAL-GATE-ENFORCED-BY-ONE-OF-FOUR-DISPATCH-PICKERS (ready, P1) says the not-before gate is decorative on 3 of 4 pickers because only the QA-drain calls is_gated_not_before(). The drain is the one picker that gets not-before RIGHT, which is exactly why this second gap was invisible.

2. FIX-DEVTEAM-SECONDARY-DRAIN-CANDIDATE-SET-NO-NOT-ACTIONABLE-PREDICATE (backlog, P1, architect) is the same CLASS -- candidate set lacks an actionability filter -- but scoped to the SECONDARY drain lane, with a secondary-specific premise (throttle-by-design is false for held rows). Different lane, different script.

3. FIX-DEVTEAM-REVIEW-LANE-QA-DRAIN (backlog) is PLAN-ONLY and superseded: it argues the drain does not exist. It does, and it ran.

THE MECHANISM. FACTORY-STOCK-extract-vndirect-mapper carries a populated blocked_by field naming OPS-FLEET-REDEPLOY-STOCKPRICE-MACROINDICATORS-CONFIRMED-BINARY-DRIFT, which is still status=READY / next_agent=ops in ready[]. PO had already adjudicated (po_adjudication_20260826T0650Z) that the row's one outstanding QA clause is discharged only when that ops row's AC-2 lands. The dependency was therefore recorded correctly, in a structured field, on the row itself. The drain simply never read it.

The qa_not_before stamp was set by the router at 07:54Z as a wall-clock churn-brake after an earlier revert of this same claim, and its own note at the time flagged that the gate does not track the real dependency. That note was correct and is now confirmed empirically: a time-based proxy standing in for a dependency check does not defer, it merely delays -- it converts a permanent block into a recurring one.

EVIDENCE THE BLOCK IS REAL, re-derived by qa rather than assumed from the gate: the live stock-price container is still image sha256:663e258b50de created 2026-08-06T15:59:04Z, identical to the prior QA cycle, so no rebuild occurred; and git log 912a4bf79..main -- fetchers.go mapper.go is empty, so nothing changed since the last QA cycle. Re-running the suite could only reproduce the already-recorded PASS and could not touch the one unmet clause.

COST AND RECURRENCE. One full QA dispatch consumed (~136k subagent tokens, 45 tool calls, 9m30s) to reach a conclusion already recorded on the row. qa correctly declined to charge a redispatch and bumped qa_not_before 09:30Z -> 14:00Z, which re-arms the identical waste for 14:00Z unless the predicate is fixed. rows.summary: Decision-journal cap-roll is a lost-update race. When a journal breaches its byte cap, every concurrent agent independently computes the SAME next continuation filename and creates it with Write() (whole-file), so the later writer silently clobbers the earlier one's entry. Two qa sessions hit this within 60 seconds today on sprint-COWORK-GUARANTEED-SLOT-CATCHUP-qa-31.md. Data was recovered only because the second agent happened to notice.
rows.action_requested: Mint a row to make the cap-roll safe under concurrency. The existing fleet rule 'notebooks must be appended with plain printf >>, never Edit/Write' already encodes the correct discipline but is scoped to NOTEBOOKS; decision journals under docs/agent-memory/decisions/ are governed by a separate cap-roll procedure that mandates creating a new file, which is precisely the unsafe operation. Options for the implementer: append-only creation (printf >> against the continuation path, which is safe because it merges rather than replaces), or a session-unique continuation suffix, or taking the git commit-mutex across the roll.
rows.detail:
ROUTER-VERIFIED ON DISK AND IN GIT, not merely reported by the agent.

WHAT HAPPENED. sprint-COWORK-GUARANTEED-SLOT-CATCHUP-qa-30.md breached its 36000B byte cap (final 37591B / 146L). Two qa sessions from the same 4-row drain batch reached their cap check within about a minute of each other. Both computed the next continuation name as ...-qa-31.md. The vndirect session created it and wrote STEP qa-S242. The DRS session then created the same path with Write(), which is whole-file and does not merge, clobbering qa-S242.

WHY IT WAS CAUGHT. The DRS agent noticed the collision, recovered the peer's entry verbatim from that peer's still-intact notebook (a second, independent copy of the same content), and reinserted it chronologically ahead of its own. Router confirmed the final state: qa-31.md now holds STEP qa-S242 (10:58Z, vndirect) at line 9 and STEP qa-S243 (10:59Z, DRS) at line 20, correct order, and both strings present.

WHY THIS IS STILL HIGH SEVERITY DESPITE THE CLEAN OUTCOME. The recovery depended on two pieces of luck, not on any mechanism. First, the clobbered content happened to be duplicated in the peer's notebook, so a source existed to recover FROM; a journal-only entry would have been unrecoverable. Second, the clobbering agent happened to look. Nothing in the roll procedure detects the collision, and git did not catch it either -- the peer had already committed 18d1f2717 before the clobber, so the working-tree loss would have surfaced as a silent content deletion inside the next commit, not as a conflict. Explicit pathspec would not have helped: this is one file, one path, two writers.

BLAST RADIUS. Any capped shared journal under a multi-agent batch. Today's 4-row qa-drain fan-out is exactly the shape that produces it: N agents, one sprint, one shared journal, one shared cap. It is more likely, not less, as batch sizes grow -- the QA-drain take budget is currently capped at 10.

NOTE ON THE ADJACENT RULE. The fleet already knows this failure mode: notebooks are required to be appended with printf >> precisely to avoid whole-file replacement under concurrency. The decision-journal roll path appears to have been written without inheriting that constraint, so the lesson is enforced on one artifact class and not on the neighbouring one.
