entries.root_cause: PROVEN on two planes. (1) The host —France/CEST— lost its caffeinate wake-lock at ~05:00-05:13Z (pmset: multiple `caffeinate ClientDied`) when the interactive CLI session holding the */15 CronCreate cowork dispatcher ended; the host then entered standby/darkwake. (2) The launchd StartInterval guaranteed-slot firer provably did NOT execute for ~11.5h (05:58Z->17:34Z): the firer logs a line whenever it MATCHES a guaranteed slot, and chef-eod(08:45Z)+fb-daily(09:15Z) had last_fired=07-21 which does NOT suppress them, so had launchd run the firer in-window it WOULD have logged+fired them — their total absence from the 07-22 log proves StartInterval never ran (host not rebooted: uptime 11d; job not unloaded: resumed same-day 17:34Z). Both coverage planes were dark. On resume at 17:34Z the matcher only offers slots within +/-2min of the CURRENT nominal tick — the 08:45/09:00/09:15/11:00/14:00Z windows were hours gone and NEVER re-offered. `guaranteed:true` is therefore a false promise across any host-standby/session-down window: neither plane has look-back/catch-up.
entries.vision: Make cowork `guaranteed:true` an HONORED contract, not a false promise. A guaranteed slot whose firing window elapsed while the host was in standby or the session was down must, on the next live tick/startup, either be recovered exactly once within a bounded freshness-safe catch-up window, OR record a structured (non-silent) miss when the VN trading day has already rolled past its window — and the `guaranteed` label must be corrected wherever it overstates real coverage.
entries.scope_in: TRACK A (PRIMARY, dev-team chain): add look-back/catch-up to the guaranteed-slot firing path shared by all 3 callers (scripts/agents-flow/cowork-match-slots.js matcher, scripts/agents-flow/cowork-guaranteed-slot-firer.sh launchd firer, and the live */15 dispatcher startup). On each tick/startup, in addition to the +/-2min current-tick match, detect guaranteed slots DUE earlier in the current VN trading day but never fired (last_fired < today scheduled-fire epoch) and re-offer them IF now is within a bounded, per-dish-type catch-up window that keeps the deliverable meaningful (tight for market/FB posts, looser for chef/digest). Dedup STRICTLY via the existing published:<slot_id>:<VN-work-date> task_claim marker so a late catch-up never double-posts and never labels stale data as fresh. VN-date rollover is explicit: if the VN day rolled past the slot window, DO NOT retro-post under a new date — skip + record miss. CONSOLIDATES the existing cluster (subsume together, do NOT re-litigate): SPIKE-DEAD-WINDOW-20260722-EIGHT-HOUR-SILENCE (root-caused by this triage — its `already_ruled_out: machine sleep` note is INCORRECT, corrected here), SPIKE-COWORK-GUARANTEED-SLOT-SUPERSEDE-WIRING (root-caused), FIX-GUARANTEED-SLOT-FIRER-FANOUT-TRUNCATION (the 07-22 chef-morning exit_code=143 SIGTERM at the 1800s bound / 600s subagent kill truncates guaranteed dishes — catch-up re-firing must complete, not re-truncate), FIX-GUARANTEED-SLOT-DUAL-PLANE-DOUBLE-FIRE (catch-up adds a 3rd fire path — published-marker arbitration must be verified airtight), FIX-COWORK-LASTFIRED-DECOUPLE-FROM-DELIVERY (catch-up detects a miss via last_fired, so last_fired MUST reflect DELIVERY not just spawn-dispatch). DOC-HONESTY: update cowork-schedule.json `guaranteed` semantics + docs/agents/cowork-team/flow/*.md + docs/architecture-briefs/2026-07-07-cowork-guaranteed-slot-durability.md + docs/protocols/cowork-master-cron-runbook.md to state the true coverage envelope.

entries.vision: When any frontend data surface goes stale AT REST, the system automatically DECIDES the root cause and ROUTES a remediation: mint a dev FIX task if the fetch/writer CODE is broken, OR call the responsible refresh agent (market-watcher / news-scout / the cron fetchers) to re-run if the data merely wasn't refreshed — with NO alert spam. This is the auto-REMEDIATE layer (conceptually FFT-L6) sitting ON TOP of L4 detection. Detection already exists and emits SLA-breach signals, but today they DEAD-END: alert-commander suppresses freshness-sla-monitor urgent_news every cycle as infra noise (DS-OBS-01-FIX note in freshnessSlaMonitorJob.ts lines 538-548), so a genuine stale-page breach never mints a fix and never re-runs a fetcher — the user's 'many frontend pages show non-updated data' persists because the signal has no remediation consumer.
entries.scope_in: THREE genuinely-new pieces ON TOP of L4: (1) REMEDIATION-TRIAGE decision-layer — for each breaching surface, read its coverage-map .writer + .cadence, probe the writer's live runtime (generalize queryBctcPipelineRuntimeState's queueDepth+serviceActive idle-vs-crash reader across ALL coverage-map surfaces, not just bctc), and CLASSIFY broken-code (writer service down / erroring / never-scheduled) vs not-refreshed (writer healthy+idle, just didn't run) → route to dev FIX vs refresh-agent re-invoke. (2) ANTI-SPAM gating — REUSE apps/alert-engine dedup-key-builder + cooldown-gate primitives (Go) plus the existing sla_breach_audit 60-min cooldown table; key dedup by (surface, breach-class); SUPPRESS repeat signals while a remediation task/signal is already OPEN for that surface; keep the isVnMarketHours() market-hours gate. (3) ORCHESTRATION integration — REDIRECT the breach signal OFF the dead-end alert-commander addressee ONTO the po/dev-team signal_queue drain (the existing anomaly→BACKLOG bridge: emit-audit-signal.sh + po-s* drain-mint jq library) so remediation is AUTO-picked-up, not a dead alert. Detection-completeness input: coverageMapFreshnessChecker.ts currently maps only 5 of 50 surfaces to DB queries (ENDPOINT_DB_QUERY) — the other 45 are silently skipped, so 'many pages' cannot even be detected yet; widening endpoint→DB coverage is an input the architect must scope for the triage layer to be effective.

entries.vision: Replace the ENGINEERING ESTIMATE of silent-tick cost with a MEASURED number. The cron preflight scripts shipped by TOKEN-ECONOMY-TICK-PREFLIGHT (2026-07-02) each emit one compact JSON verdict on stdout and then exit — on ~80% of ticks that verdict is SILENT/SKIP and no LLM work follows. Nothing anywhere records that those invocations happened, so the only available answer to 'what does the silent-tick layer cost' is an estimate derived from the script's I/O shape (the router quoted ~250-500 tok/silent cowork tick on 2026-08-12; the user asked for that to become a measurement). This sprint adds per-invocation, append-only, LOCAL-FILE-ONLY usage telemetry at each script's verdict choke point: what verdict, when, how many BYTES of verdict JSON the LLM actually receives, how long it took, what exit code. It records only what is measurable and deliberately does NOT compute a token number inside the script.
entries.scope_in: FOUR rows, sequenced, WU-0 gates the rest. (WU-0) NEW shared lib scripts/agents-flow/lib/tick-telemetry.sh — one log_tick_usage() helper + log destination + size-cap/tail-truncate rotation + its own regression suite; must land and be green before any wiring. (WU-1) wire into scripts/agents-flow/cowork-tick-preflight.sh at its single _emit_verdict() choke point (lines 76-82) — the user's specifically named target, ships first after WU-0. (WU-2) wire into scripts/agents-flow/dev-team-tick-preflight.sh at its single _emit_verdict() choke point (line 200-203) — structurally identical to WU-1, ~1 line after WU-0 exists. (WU-3) wire into scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh — GATED on WU-0/1/2 all green; NOT the same change, see product_decision.
entries.scope_out: BINDING. (a) NO change to any verdict token, verdict JSON field set, exit code, lock claim/release, or MCP call sequence in any of the 4 scripts — instrumentation is a pure side-effect append, and the R2/R3/R4/R7/R8 risk notes from sprint TOKEN-ECONOMY-TICK-PREFLIGHT still bind. (b) NO new tool call, MCP call, git operation, or network I/O on the silent/skip path — the entire point is to MEASURE the cost, not add to it; logging is a local file append and nothing else. (c) NO est_tokens / estimated-cost field computed inside any script — record measurable bytes, let a later analysis step convert. (d) NOT in scope, deliberately deferred and recorded here so it is not lost: the OTHER THREE members of the same preflight family that share this exact verdict-JSON-on-stdout shape and the same silent-tick economics — scripts/agents-flow/code-janitor-tick-preflight.sh (SKIP-SPAWN|SPAWN), scripts/agents-flow/db-integrity-probe.sh, scripts/agents-flow/orch-sentinel-lite-probe.sh. The brief said '3 scripts'; the real family is 6. Mint a follow-up row for those 3 AFTER this sprint proves the shared lib, do not widen this one. (e) NOT building the analysis/reporting step that reads the JSONL and produces the bytes-to-tokens rollup — separate row once real data has accumulated for >=7 days. (f) NOT logging CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID verbatim, see product_decision.
entries.success_metric: (1) After 24h of live cron operation, docs/data/telemetry/tick-usage.jsonl contains >=90 cowork rows (15-min cadence = 96/day) with verdict/verdict_bytes/elapsed_ms/exit_code populated, RAW-verified by reading the actual file, never on an agent's RETURN text. (2) All four existing regression suites green at or above their pre-sprint counts — cowork-tick-preflight.test.sh, dev-team-tick-preflight.test.sh, auditor-tier1-probe.test.sh, plus the new lib suite; QA re-establishes the true pre-sprint counts live rather than trusting the 20/37/32 figures quoted in the intake brief. (3) Negative control: a deliberately unwritable log destination produces an UNCHANGED verdict on stdout and an UNCHANGED exit code on every verdict path of every wired script. (4) Negative control: mcp_call invocation count on the SILENT path is byte-identical before and after wiring. (5) The stdout verdict line is still the FIRST and ONLY thing on stdout (feedback_tick_preflight_verdict_is_first_json_key_tail_always_drops_it) — asserted, not assumed.
entries.product_decision:
PO triage 2026-08-12T13:03Z, from a user 'yes' to a router proposal. The router asked 1 WU (cowork only) vs 3 (all preflight scripts). PO read all four scripts at source and both framings are wrong; the answer is 4 rows.

WHY NOT 1: measuring cowork alone answers 'what does a silent cowork tick cost', not 'what does the silent-tick LAYER cost', which is the actual question behind the user's yes. dev-team fires more often than cowork (7/37 min vs 15 min). And once WU-0 exists, WU-2 is approximately one line — refusing it would be false economy.

WHY NOT 3-AS-EQUALS: it is NOT 'the same change 3x'. cowork-tick-preflight.sh and dev-team-tick-preflight.sh each have a SINGLE _emit_verdict() function every verdict routes through — a genuinely mechanical hook. auditor-tier1-probe.sh has NO choke point: it builds verdict JSON inline at >=6 distinct sites (lines 757, 767, 772, 858, 894, 921) AND it is dual-mode — run_tiered_probe() (tier 2/3) internally calls run_probe() and then re-emits its own wrapper verdict with a DIFFERENT field set (checks_verdict ALL_GREEN|FAILURE inner vs verdict SKIP-SPAWN|SPAWN outer). A naive per-call-site hook therefore DOUBLE-LOGS every tier-2/3 tick with two incompatible shapes and silently corrupts the very dataset this sprint exists to produce. Correct instrumentation there requires first extracting a choke point from a 925-line script guarded by a 1323-line suite. That is a different risk class and gets its own gated row, droppable without invalidating the sprint.

WHY WU-0 FIRST: three copies of the same log helper is exactly the debt CLAUDE.md forbids. Precedent for the extraction already exists in this tree — scripts/agents-flow/lib/hook-guard.sh and scripts/agents-flow/lib/notebook-section-direction.sh.

ENGINE: jq, NOT python3. The intake brief suggested reusing a python3 json.dumps() log_json() pattern from another project. Rejected: all four scripts already hard-depend on jq and use `jq -nc --arg` as their quote-safe JSON emitter throughout. Adding a python3 dependency to four cron-critical paths is a new failure mode for zero benefit.

SESSION ID: NOT logged, even hashed, in v1. cowork-tick-preflight.sh's own header (lines 56-57) states CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID is 'never echoed/logged by this script beyond its use as a bound task_claim arg'. Writing it to a telemetry file breaks that stated contract. This sprint is about cost, not cross-session correlation.

RATIO: PO checked and the convention ALREADY EXISTS — 4 chars/token, used in docs/architecture-briefs/2026-05-21-token-toolcall-economy.md §W-1 ('At 4 chars/token') and applied in docs/architecture-briefs/2026-07-12-token-economy-lazyload-audit.md (3,162 chars ~= 790 tokens; 23,994 chars ~= 6k tokens). Do NOT invent a new one, and do NOT bake it into a script.

HONESTY CAVEAT, ACCEPTANCE-BEARING: verdict_bytes is a LOWER BOUND on true per-tick cost, not the cost. The real cost of a silent tick is the cron prompt text the LLM reads + whatever flow-doc lines it loads + the tool_result. The script can only measure the last of those three. Every artifact this sprint produces (script header, lib doc, dev-standards pointer, any later rollup) MUST state that explicitly, so the resulting number is never mis-sold as 'a silent tick costs N tokens'. Shipping a precise-looking number with an unstated denominator would be worse than the estimate it replaces.

entries.vision: The prediction engine LEARNS from being wrong. Today it does not: it computes empirical likelihood ratios from realized outcomes daily, scores its own Brier weekly, and applies NEITHER — so a 95%-confidence call has a 0% actual hit rate and avg Brier 0.4743 is worse than a coin flip (0.25). Close the loop so published confidence is an honest probability and accuracy compounds automatically as outcomes accumulate.
entries.scope_in: apps/mcp-server/ prediction engine. (D1) Wire evidence_likelihood_ratios into the score that produces a prediction — evidenceAccumulatorJob's `score = sum(magnitude*confidence)/count` currently ignores it entirely. (D2) Build the recurring path calibration_snapshots -> future prediction behavior; calibrationReportJob is measurement-only (zero 'likelihood' references) and its weekly Brier feeds nothing. (D3) Shrink published confidence toward the base rate by evidence sample size / LR strength, replacing the agent-prompt flat `computed * 0.90` haircut in docs/agents/digest-predict/flow/daily-predict.md:30 with code-side correction. (D4) Freshness bound on evidence_scores — fold in the 37-day-old SPIKE-EVIDENCE-SCORE-CACHE-FRAGMENT-DECOUPLE rather than re-triaging it.
entries.scope_out: NO per-ticker or per-evidence-type coefficient refit on the current n=17/n=25 sample, and NO hard-coded sign flip for foreign_flow_institutional or the bearish channel — the VPB 95% triple is one stale cache row read three times (D4), not three independent observations. BCTC OCR total_assets=0 corruption stays with the existing FIX-BCTC-VALIDATION-GATE-NONBANK-ZERO-SCALE row. No frontend/API/route change. Sibling rows FIX-FB-PREDICTION-CALIBRATION-LOOP, ALPHA-S5-TRUTH-LEDGER-BACKTEST, FEAT-PREDCLAIM-UPDATED-AT to be reconciled by BA, not absorbed.
entries.success_metric: PRIMARY (structural, verifiable now and independent of sample size): (1) the likelihood ratio provably participates in the score arithmetic — the live identity Bullish 0.3012 == (0.4224+0.1800)/2 on ACB, which today holds despite BOTH fragments carrying TRUSTED sub-1.0 LRs (n=91, n=195), must no longer hold; (2) a scheduled job consumes calibration_snapshots and alters subsequent prediction confidence, with a recorded cron_job_runs history proving it recurs; (3) no evidence score is served as current past a defined freshness bound — get_evidence_summary('VPB') can never again return a 13-day-stale 0.95 bearish conviction with '(no fragments found)'. SECONDARY (directional only, NOT a certification gate — n=17 cannot certify a Brier delta): the monotone anti-calibration 65%->50%, 75%->33%, 85%->0%, 95%->0% flattens toward the diagonal on the LIVE forward curve as resolved outcomes accumulate over subsequent weeks.

archive.po_cancel_ruling_20260721: PO RULING 2026-07-21T18:42Z — PREMISE DISPROVEN AT SOURCE. The claim 'price_anomaly_*.json reach no consumer / are market-facing data loss' is FALSE. Verified by reading source, not inferring: (A) WRITER = docs/agents/market-watcher/flow/eod.md:29 (Step B 'SIGNAL FILE'), schema literal at :33, output contract declared at :13. (B) CONSUMER = docs/agents/unified-agent/flow/chef.md:116 — 'Collect file groups: price_anomaly_* — from market-watcher'. Chef reads by DIRECT PATH GLOB over docs/signals/ top-level, NOT via the drain. (C) The by-path contract is already written down in THREE places: eod.md:15 ('Chef (unified-agent) reads the signal file at 08:37 UTC EOD dish'), eod.md:61 ('File written atomically; chef reads at 08:37 UTC (24min settle window)'), and docs/agents/market-watcher/init.md:119-121 (sends_to unified-agent, note 'Chef reads price_anomaly_*.json at 05:23/08:37/19:37 UTC'). WHY EVERY PRIOR REPORT MISSED IT: greps were restricted to .js/.ts/.sh and treated .md as 'documentation'. In this system flow docs ARE the executable source for LLM agents — excluding .md from a writer search structurally cannot find any cowork writer. TWO PLANES SHARE THE NAME: the DB/MCP plane (market-watcher/flow/cycle.md:179 post_agent_signal signal_type=price_anomaly -> alert-commander via get_agent_signals; this is what docs/standards/mcp-tools.md:175 documents) is the INTRADAY path; the FILE plane (eod.md -> Chef) is the EOD path and deliberately does NOT call post_agent_signal. Alert-commander was therefore never an intended recipient of the EOD file, and its silence on the 07-20/07-21 selloff is NOT explained by envelope shape. CONSEQUENCE — THE PROPOSED FIX WAS A REGRESSION: adding a from/type envelope would make drain-signals.js MATCH these files and MOVE them to docs/signals/processed/. Chef's price_anomaly_* glob reads top-level ONLY — the dual-read AUTO-CURE (top-level + processed/) was added exclusively for bctc_signal_* and fundamental_* (chef.md ~100-118). Enveloping price_anomaly would have silently broken the one consumer that currently works. The drain's 'SKIP non-signal shape ... leaving in inbox' behaviour is precisely what KEEPS the EOD dish fed. ANSWER TO 'where is this analysis supposed to go': already decided, and it is option B of the signal's own framing — a Chef/dish input read directly by path. It is NOT undelivered; it only LOOKS undelivered to a drain that was never its transport.

archive.title: PUBLISHED-MARKER KEY AGREEMENT — derive the dedup key from the scheduled UTC fire-window, never from a wall-clock date read (P0: chef-evening double-published 2026-07-22 19:56Z + 20:00Z on keys :2026-07-22 vs :2026-07-23 derived from ONE instant; the same defect will FALSELY SUPPRESS the 2026-07-23 19:45Z dish)
archive.note:
ROOT CAUSE (RAW-verified 2026-07-22T20:00-20:10Z, router + po). chef-evening cron is `45 19 * * *` = 19:45 UTC = 02:45 VN of D+1 — cowork-schedule.json chef-evening.vn_description literally reads '02:45 VN next day (GMT+7)'. chef.md Step 0.5 L48 computes WORK_DATE = TZ="Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh" date +%Y-%m-%d and L70 builds MARKER_KEY = published:<slot>:<WORK_DATE>. Because this slot fires AFTER VN midnight, the key straddles a date boundary: two peers reading the SAME wall-clock instant derive DIFFERENT keys. EVIDENCE — task_list_held(task_kind=cowork-slot) shows BOTH published:chef-evening:2026-07-22 (owner_client_session 9f4a6bfc-b001-4349-8a44-545f24c1b0ac, claimed_at 1784750141 = 19:55:41Z) AND published:chef-evening:2026-07-23 (owner_client_session ab870ed6-0502-4e49-811a-8e7c90aff1ef, claimed_at 1784750490 = 20:01:30Z) HELD SIMULTANEOUSLY, ttl_seconds 100800 each. Both runs therefore claimed successfully, both passed the gate, both published. Artifacts on disk, both dish_type=evening + quality_verdict=degraded, overlapping conviction VHM+VIC: docs/data/unified-agent-synthesis-2026-07-22-evening.json (date_vn 2026-07-22, timestamp_utc 19:56:15Z, EIB/VIC/VHM/VJC, regime risk-off) and docs/data/unified-agent-synthesis-2026-07-23-evening.json (date_vn 2026-07-23, timestamp_utc 20:00:37Z, VHM/VIC/VCB, regime carry-unwind-risk-off). NOTE the historical convention was the UTC/trading-day label — published:chef-evening:2026-07-21 was claimed 2026-07-21T19:51:10Z i.e. VN 07-22 — so the 19:55Z run followed PRECEDENT while the 20:01Z run followed the SPEC AS WRITTEN. Neither agent misbehaved. The spec is ambiguous exactly at the boundary it is supposed to defend.

WHY THIS IS **NOT** UC-CCA-P3 — DO NOT FOLD AND CLOSE. UC-CCA-P3 fixes marker LIFECYCLE (claim timing + release immunity). Its design recommendation (early read-only probe + late task_claim immediately before send_telegram + never release) would NOT have prevented this incident: both peers would still compute DIFFERENT keys, both probes would read free, both late claims would succeed, both would publish. Key AGREEMENT is orthogonal to key LIFECYCLE. A mutex whose key depends on which timezone the reader happens to consult is not a mutex. If UC-CCA-P3 ships alone, this defect survives and the umbrella closes green — the recurring-detection-vs-recurring-FAILED-FIX class (feedback_recurring_detection_vs_recurring_failed_fix).

PO RULING (product decision, po-owned, decided 2026-07-22 — DO NOT re-litigate; architect/ba own the HOW, not the WHAT). The dedup key and the human-readable date label are TWO DIFFERENT VALUES and MUST NOT be derived from one expression. chef.md L654 (CYCLE_DATE = WORK_DATE verbatim) deliberately couples them; that coupling IS the defect, not the fix — it was introduced by GAP-CHEF-SYNTHESIS-A-FLOW-PERSIST to make the FILENAME deterministic and it silently made the MUTEX KEY timezone-dependent. (1) MUTEX KEY = window-anchored and timezone-free: derived from the scheduled cron fire-window expressed in UTC (shape e.g. published:<slot_id>:2026-07-22T19:45Z), NOT from any `date` call made by the executing agent. Two peers executing the same scheduled window MUST derive byte-identical keys with zero shared state beyond the cron expression. This is invariant to timezone, to VN/UTC midnight straddle, to DST, to host clock skew, and to run-start jitter within the window (19:55 vs 20:01). It needs NO trading-calendar lookup. NEVER put a trading-calendar / holiday lookup on the mutex path. (2) DISPLAY LABEL (metadata.date_vn, synthesis filename, prose) = the VN trading session the dish INFORMS. chef-evening fires after the prior VN close (08:00Z) and before the next VN open (02:00Z of D+1) and gates on macroIndicatorRefreshJob US macro data — it is a FORWARD preview; the slot's own dish_type is literally `evening_preview`. Therefore the correct label for a 19:45Z fire is the NEXT VN session = the VN wall date at fire time. Tonight's correct label is 2026-07-23; the 19:55Z run's date_vn=2026-07-22 is WRONG. Weekend/holiday note for ba: the cron is daily including weekends, so 'next VN session' is not the next calendar day on Fri/Sat/Sun fires — the LABEL MAY remain the plain VN wall date (simple, calendar-free); if a true session label is ever wanted it belongs in a SEPARATE display-only field and never in the key.

CAUTION for architect/ba: metadata.cycle_id is NOT a ready-made substitute — today's two runs emitted cycle_id evening-2026-07-22T19:56:00Z and evening-2026-07-22T20:00:37Z, i.e. cycle_id is keyed to RUN-START and diverges exactly like WORK_DATE does. RECOMMENDED PLUMBING (non-binding): the cowork dispatcher ALREADY holds the canonical window value — the fire-election lock cron:cowork:2026-07-22T20:00Z carries payload.tick — so pass the tick DOWN to the spawned agent instead of having the agent re-derive it; DESIGN-COWORK-FANOUT-T1-TICK-SNAPSHOT-WON-SLOTS (tick-snapshot.md Step 4.7, already in ready[]) is the natural carrier. Deriving-at-the-leaf is what created this bug class.

LIVE FORWARD HAZARD (self-healing — do NOT 'fix' it with lock surgery): published:chef-evening:2026-07-23 expires 2026-07-24T00:01:30Z, which is AFTER tomorrow's 2026-07-23T19:45Z fire. If tomorrow's run uses the UTC-date convention it derives :2026-07-23, finds it HELD, and SILENTLY SKIPS — a MISSED evening dish. If it uses the VN convention it derives :2026-07-24 and publishes. Tomorrow's outcome is a coin flip on which convention the spawned agent picks. So this ONE defect produces BOTH double-publish AND missed-publish. Both markers are deliberately LEFT IN PLACE: they are the evidence, and releasing published: markers is the known-wrong direction (feedback_chef_releases_published_marker_enables_peer_double_publish). Hazard self-clears 2026-07-24T00:01:30Z.

AC: (1) two peers spawned for the SAME scheduled window derive byte-identical MARKER_KEY regardless of host timezone, of VN-vs-UTC midnight straddle, and of run-start offset within the window; (2) the key contains NO value obtained from a `date` call made by the executing agent; (3) mutex key and display label are SEPARATE named values with separate derivations, and no later step re-derives either; (4) chef-evening's synthesis date_vn + filename carry the NEXT-VN-session label per the PO ruling above; (5) the fix applies to ALL cowork published: gates (chef-morning/intraday/eod/evening, digest-daily, digest-sunday, fb, market-watcher, news-scout, tnb-audit) — not chef-evening alone; the same straddle hits ANY slot whose UTC fire hour maps across VN midnight, and single-fire slots carry a 100800s TTL that outlives the next window; (6) RAW-verify by executing two same-window runs: exactly ONE claim succeeds, exactly ONE synthesis artifact exists for the window, exactly ONE MARKET post is emitted.

SEQUENCING: ships WITH UC-CCA-P3, not before and not after — lifecycle-without-key-agreement is defeated by divergent keys, key-agreement-without-lifecycle is defeated by leaked or released markers. architect should treat UC-CCA-P3 + this row as ONE design.

RECURRENCE 2026-08-06 (PO triage, 3rd+ confirmed instance of this key-derivation class). This row's own 2026-07-22 title predicted today verbatim: "the same defect will FALSELY SUPPRESS the [next day's] 19:45Z dish". It did, 15 days later, while the row sat in BACKLOG.

SEQUENCE (every step RAW-verified, not agent self-report):
(1) 2026-08-05T19:51:57Z the scheduled chef-evening fired (cowork-schedule.json .slots[chef-evening].last_fired) and the session died mid-composition AFTER claiming published:chef-evening:2026-08-05 and BEFORE send_telegram. Router released that marker and re-dispatched a retry at ~19:52Z.
(2) The retry did not begin executing until 2026-08-06T06:34Z. THE 10h42m GAP IS NOT AN AUTH OUTAGE AND NOT A SCHEDULER STALL -- that was the initial triage hypothesis and it is wrong. It is macOS host sleep: `pmset -g log` shows a MAGICWAKE at 2026-08-06 08:34 CEST = 06:34Z, matching the retry's start instant exactly, and the agent's own runtime was only 175909ms (~2m56s). Do not design against a phantom auth/scheduler bug.
(3) On wake, chef.md Step 0.5 recomputed CYCLE_DATE_UTC = `date -u +%Y-%m-%d` = 2026-08-06, so the retry keyed published:chef-evening:2026-08-06 and published a degraded dish to MARKET at 06:37:25Z (msg id 1129, headline "Thi truong 5-6 thang 8"). docs/data/unified-agent-synthesis-2026-08-06-evening.json records quality_verdict="degraded", 0 clusters, gaps [gap:L2_US_macro_absent_no_gap_token] [gap:L3_VN_macro_incomplete] [gap:business_context_unavailable]. It landed 13h before its real 19:45Z window and while the VN session was still OPEN (06:37Z = 13:37 ICT, close is 15:00 ICT) -- an "evening" dish published mid-session.
(4) That marker then tombstoned tonight's legitimate 19:45Z fire (28h TTL, expiry 2026-08-07T10:37:25Z). PO manually released published:chef-evening:2026-08-06 at 2026-08-06T06:53Z to unblock it, RAW-verified absent from task_list_held afterwards. THAT MANUAL RELEASE IS THE THING THIS ROW MUST MAKE UNNECESSARY.

DECISIVE DESIGN INPUT -- THE CORRECT KEY IS ALREADY COMPUTED AND SITTING UNUSED. scripts/agents-flow/cowork-catchup-predicate.js (shipped under TASK-COWORK-CATCHUP-1/-2) already emits per slot exactly the fields this row needs: scheduled_utc_time, scheduled_key_part, expected_publish_task_id. Executed live 2026-08-06T06:52Z it returned for chef-evening: scheduled_utc_time=2026-08-05T19:45:00.000Z, expected_publish_task_id=published:chef-evening:2026-08-05 -- i.e. the predicate ALREADY identifies the missed window as 08-05, which is precisely the key the retry should have used and did not. So the fix is not new date logic. It is:
  (a) propagate the nominal scheduled tick into the slot trigger_prompt (e.g. `slot=<id> scheduled_utc=<ISO8601>`), sourced from the values the predicate already produces;
  (b) make chef.md Step 0.5 derive CYCLE_DATE_UTC from that scheduled_utc when present, falling back to wall-clock ONLY for genuine ad-hoc runs. Because CYCLE_DATE_UTC is already the single canonical date-derivation point (chef.md:73 -- pinned once, reused verbatim at Step 7.6 synthesis filepath + metadata.date_vn and Step 8b notebook header), this lands in ONE place and simultaneously fixes the marker key, the synthesis filename and the dish's own date label;
  (c) add a lateness guard: when now - scheduled_utc exceeds the slot's freshness window, the run must publish under an explicit backfill label or abort -- never silently retarget to the current day. The predicate ALREADY implements this notion (catchup_eligible:false with reason "rolled_past_vn_date" / "freshness_window_exceeded"); reuse it, do not reinvent it.

GENERALITY -- DO NOT SCOPE THIS TO CHEF. Every guaranteed slot derives its published-marker key the same wall-clock way, so any delayed, retried or post-sleep execution of digest-daily, tnb-audit, fb-daily, digest-sunday has the identical failure. On this host (laptop, France) sleep is a routine nightly condition, so "execution delayed hours past the nominal tick" is the NORMAL case, not an edge case. Any fix that assumes prompt execution is already wrong.

archive.title: Every subagent shares ONE git working directory + ONE HEAD: any agent that honours a `branch:` field (e.g. a PM handoff) checks out that branch in the shared checkout, and every concurrent peer's commits silently land on it. 4 independent hits on 2026-07-31 alone; zero board rows existed.
archive.root_cause: STRUCTURAL, not behavioural. There is no worktree/checkout isolation between agents — all agents (router, dev-team, pm, po, developer, architect, agents-architect, qa) operate on the same `$PROJECT_ROOT` and therefore the same `.git/HEAD`. `git checkout <branch>` is a process-global mutation of shared state with no lock, no claim and no TTL, so it is not serialisable against peers the way the index is (the index at least has `index.lock` + the Layer-0 sweep guard). CLAUDE.md's `NO branches — all work stays on main` invariant is the only thing holding the system together, and it is enforced by prose alone: nothing structurally prevents a `branch:` field from appearing in a PM handoff / task row and being obeyed. Note this is the SIBLING hazard to the shared-INDEX sweep (FIX-COMMIT-PATH-PEER-INDEX-SWEEP-GUARD family, 6 rows, Layer-0 hook shipped): same shared-working-dir root, different shared resource (HEAD vs index), and the sweep-guard hook is structurally blind to it because it only inspects $GIT_INDEX_FILE shape, never HEAD.
archive.evidence: dev-team signal `dev-20260731T020908` (signal_queue, status READ, minted by commit 3b20fc8c9): '4x today: subagents share dev-team's git checkout (no worktree isolation); a branch checkout (e.g. PM handoff's branch: field) hijacks peer commits.' The 4 named incidents that tick: dev-team's own stray commit, agents-architect's stray commit, the FIX-COWORK-FIRE-ELECTION-TICK-TOMBSTONE developer originating the branch, and the head-stamp developer's stash-pop failure. Independently corroborated by project memory `feedback_subagent_branch_checkout_hijacks_shared_working_dir` ('dev-team's own commits land on a subagent's branch; recover via isolated worktree, never checkout main mid-subagent-edit') — the hazard has been KNOWN and carried as tribal memory + ad-hoc recovery, never as a board row. 4 occurrences in one day clears the recurring-bug bar (>=2) by a factor of 2.
archive.ac: (AC-1) Name the enforcement layer and make it STRUCTURAL, not prose. The prose invariant already exists in CLAUDE.md and did not prevent 4 hits — a 5th doc sentence is a rejection. Candidate layers to evaluate explicitly, choosing and justifying one: (a) a `pre-checkout`-equivalent guard (git has no pre-checkout hook — say so if rejecting, do not silently assume one exists) e.g. a wrapper/alias or a `post-checkout` hook that hard-reverts + fail-louds any move off `main`; (b) real per-agent `git worktree` isolation; (c) a schema-level ban on the `branch:` field in task rows / PM handoffs so the trigger can never be authored. (AC-2) Whatever layer is chosen MUST be reachable by agents that have no MCP grant — the same reason the sweep guard was pushed down to a git hook (`docs/policies/dev-standards.md` CANONICAL sweep-guard entry): a skill-level or flow-doc-level fix can be improvised around, and 4/4 of these incidents were improvised behaviour, not doc-following. (AC-3) DEDUP/RECONCILE — do NOT mint a 3rd overlapping row. Two adjacent rows already exist and this row must explicitly state its boundary against both, in writing, before implementing: `UC-RDL-P7` (BACKLOG, next=po — 'Reconcile branch policy across the FULL branch lifecycle with the main-only invariant') owns the POLICY; `SPIKE-C44-PARALLEL-PROOF` (BACKLOG — 'two developer agents in worktrees on disjoint zones, no shared-index race -> lift sequential mandate') is the permission-WIDENING spike and shares the worktree mechanism this row may want to use as its fix. If the chosen fix is (b) worktree isolation, SPIKE-C44 becomes a hard dependency, not a sibling — say so and sequence it. (AC-4) Live positive control, two concurrent agents in the real repo (or a byte-clone of it): agent A checks out a branch, agent B commits its own files, assert B's commit landed on `main` and is not reachable only from A's branch. Asserting from hook/wrapper source prose is a rejection.

[architect 2026-07-31T02:40:37Z DESIGN COMPLETE — plan-only, no code shipped this cycle] Verified git has NO pre-checkout hook (git help githooks, git 2.49.0 — only post-checkout exists, contractually cannot block the checkout itself, only revert-after + force the calling command exit code). CHOSE AC-1(a): new scripts/git-hooks/post-checkout hard-reverts any non-main checkout in the PRIMARY working dir back to main (MODE=enforce default, diverges deliberately from the sweep-guard hooks WARN default — justified in brief SS3: zero legitimate off-main state exists live today per UC-RDL-P7s own 2026-07-17 ground truth, and revert is self-healing not blocking). REJECTED (c) schema-level ban as this rows OWN primary layer: the branch: field lives in free-form markdown handoffs, not a Zod-validated shape (grepped orchStateSchema.ts — no branch field exists to ban) — a schema-ban has nothing to bind to there.
CRITICAL COORDINATION FINDING (not in the original triage): grep-confirmed 5 flow docs still ACTIVELY author/verify/honor a task/NNN-* branch-checkout convention TODAY, post-dating UC-RDL-P7 STEP1s ruling by 2 weeks — pm/flow/main.md:75 (branch: template, fired literally hours before this brief on docs/handoffs/FIX-COWORK-FIRE-ELECTION-TICK-TOMBSTONE-dev.md, one of this rows own 4 cited incidents), developer/flow/main.md:51-54+158 (VERIFY: git branch --show-current must equal task/NNN-kebab-description — a HARD precondition before touching any file), developer/flow/microservice-main.md:53-57+161 (identical), qa/flow/main.md:37,42,114-124,219-224 (pipeline JUMP-TOs first line is git checkout task/NNN-*), fixer/flow/*.md:34,36,60,110. This means shipping the hook with ZERO coordination will make developer/microservice-main.mds own VERIFY line fail for every M/L task (the hook will have already reverted HEAD to main before that line runs) — this is UC-RDL-P7s own cited "wedges QA merge if only one half edited" hazard, reproduced via a different mechanism (a hook, not mixed doc state), same remedy needed either way. UC-RDL-P7 STEP2 (BACKLOG, next_agent=ba, unstarted) already owns rewriting exactly these 5 files — this row does NOT duplicate or implement that edit; the 5-file/line-number target list above is handed to whoever eventually works STEP2 (agent-father commit_zone per its own init.md — docs/agents/ is explicitly in its allowed list), found live via grep, not assumed.
AC-4 LIVE PROOF: 5 scenarios reproduced in a disposable scratch repo (never the live repo) — control (reproduces the hijack exactly as reported), guarded (hijack prevented, peer commit lands on main, not reachable only from the checked-out branch), non-destructive-conflict edge case (git refuses the revert rather than discard uncommitted work, fails loud), linked-worktree exemption (fleet-worktree-push-style worktrees unaffected), re-entrancy (single pass, 0.39s, no recursion). Full design + transcripts: docs/architecture-briefs/2026-07-31-fix-subagent-branch-checkout-hijacks-shared-working-dir.md.

po 2026-07-25T16:25:39Z — EVIDENCE FOLDED IN, NO NEW ROW MINTED. This annotation changes what "done" means for this row; read it before implementing.

THIS ROW'S OWN IMPACT ASSESSMENT IS NOW OBSOLETE AND MUST NOT BE ACTED ON AS WRITTEN. The note above says "at the live rate 26110 all three currently agree on direction, which is exactly why this has stayed invisible — the divergence only bites between 25000 and 26500." That framing treats the defect as a LATENT disagreement. It is no longer latent, and the more serious problem is not the disagreement at all.

MEASURED THIS TICK, AT SOURCE: apps/macro-indicators/pkg/primitive/macro_usdvnd_direction_classifier/macro_usdvnd_direction_classifier.go:34 BearishThreshold = 25000.0, line 37 BullishThreshold = 23000.0, so the NEUTRAL band is 23000-25000 and BULLISH requires < 23000. Live rate 26130. The rate has not been under 25000 in a long time and is not trending back. BEARISH IS THEREFORE THE ONLY REACHABLE OUTPUT OF THIS CLASSIFIER — it is SATURATED, not merely divergent. A three-valued direction classifier has silently become a constant that still reports a verdict on every call, and consumers cannot distinguish "the model assessed the rate and found it bearish" from "the model can only say bearish". news-scout emitted "USDVND 26130 bearish >25000 threshold" from it in both c199 and c200 today.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ROW'S ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA — THE STATED GOAL IS NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT. "Pick one SSOT" does not fix saturation if the value picked is 25000, and 25000 is the most likely pick precisely because it is the one with a named exported constant in Go. Shipping a single-SSOT refactor on 25000 would close this row while leaving the classifier constant — and would additionally propagate the saturated threshold to the two planes (25500 in macroTools.ts / macroAdjustments.ts) that are currently, by accident, slightly less wrong. AC ADDITION, mandatory: whatever value is chosen, add a test asserting that BOTH the bullish and bearish branches remain reachable at the CURRENT live rate, not at a fixture rate. A classifier whose test suite only exercises synthetic inputs cannot detect that its live input has left the discriminating range.

THE DURABLE FIX IS A DIFFERENT SHAPE OF THRESHOLD, AND THAT DECISION BELONGS TO WHOEVER WORKS THIS ROW. A fixed absolute threshold on a drifting nominal exchange rate saturates eventually by construction — this is not a mis-set constant, it is a design that has a shelf life. Honest options: [a] make the threshold relative (z-score or percent deviation against a trailing window, so the discriminating range travels with the series); [b] keep absolute levels but bind them to a real policy anchor (e.g. the SBV reference-rate band) that is itself revised, and add a staleness alarm on the anchor; [c] keep 25000 as a deliberate permanent red-line and DELETE the NEUTRAL/BULLISH branches plus the "direction classifier" framing, so the output honestly reads as a single boolean threshold breach rather than an assessment. What is NOT acceptable is shipping one SSOT and leaving three branches of which two are unreachable. po did not choose among these.

archive.title: PO RULING: flip the pdf-extractor default OCR_TEXT_BACKEND from unset (tesseract-vie) to `auto` — set it in docker-compose.yml, NOT as a code default, behind four named gates
archive.po_ruling_20260825T1700Z: RULING: YES, FLIP TO `auto`. The dev-pdf-extractor specialist declined to make this call and said so; PO owns it and makes it here. FOUR REASONS, all from measured evidence on commit e9144ea75, none re-derived from the retracted first benchmark. (1) IT IS THE ONLY SURVIVING PATH TO THE USER'S STANDING DIRECTIVE ('replace ocr tesseract to PaddleOCR using support vietnamese langage for improve quality of extraction BCTC'). The wholesale swap is CLOSED and is not re-litigated here: paddleocr 2.10.0 maps lang='vi' into a shared 30+-language 'latin' rec bucket with no dedicated Vietnamese model (a library limitation, not a config bug), ran 414.5s against tesseract's 174.5s = 2.4x, and pinned at cgroup memory.max with 1444 hard-limit hits against tesseract-vie's 0. `auto` keeps tesseract-vie as the engine on every region and invokes PaddleOCR ONLY where the recall-aware confidence says the page was essentially missed. (2) IT CLEARS BOTH BARS THE SWAP FAILED, same session, table-phase measurements: 117.26s vs 112.97s = +3.8% wall clock, and cgroup memory.peak 1,336,745,984 B = 1274.9 MiB = 49.8% of the 2,684,354,560 B cap, memory.events.max = 0 hard-limit hits, oom = 0. That is BETTER headroom than tesseract-vie's own corrected 63.7% baseline. (3) THE NEGATIVE CONTROL IS STRONG, on two independent bases: the rescue fired exactly 1x across 51 table regions (page 9 only), captured structurally from the backend's own INFO line rather than scraped off stderr; and per-unit sha256 of stitched_markdown across a tesseract-vie run and an auto run of the SAME commit left 29 of 30 table units BYTE-IDENTICAL. The second basis matters more than the first because it also catches a rescue that fires and then silently loses, which a fire counter alone misses. A 1-in-51 rescue cannot spread the diacritic problem fleet-wide. (4) THE UPSIDE IS NOT MARGINAL. Page 9 went 122 -> 452 chars with 9 of 9 income-statement figures recovered (doanh thu thuan 20.225.450 Q4 / 70.112.826 LK, LNTT 3.498.405 / 13.038.869, LNST 2.988.149 / 11.225.523 / 9.427.423). Pre-fix that cell held headers plus a garbled 'NB— rr 178%' and zero figures. archive.status_note: REJECTED AND CANCELLED 2026-08-25T17:52Z. The 17:00Z po_ruling on this row ('RULING: YES, FLIP TO auto') is WITHDRAWN IN FULL — do not quote it. Auto-mode does NOT become the production default. (1) DISPOSITIVE ON ITS OWN: this row's own rollback triggers are ALREADY BREACHED, pre-deployment, on the second document ever measured. Trigger (a) was 'rescue fire rate above 10% of table regions on any single document' — DBC measured 46%. Trigger (b) was 'any cgroup hard-limit hit or oom, baseline 0' — DBC measured 494 memory.max events with memory.peak == memory.max EXACTLY. A change its own criteria would roll back on day one must not ship. (2) The premise is falsified STRUCTURALLY: ink coverage divides by ALL crop foreground, so it conflates missed text with non-text ink the engine correctly skipped (rule lines, shading, seals, speckle) — an issuer-styling variable orthogonal to read quality. No threshold repairs that, and at n=2 the broken and legitimate bands already overlap. (3) MEMORY IS SUPERLINEAR IN FIRE COUNT, which means it is NOT bounded by the discriminator at all: FPT 1 fire = +111.8 MiB / 0 events, DBC 6 fires = +1493 MiB / 494 events — 6x fires, ~13x delta. Model residency cannot explain it (PaddleOCR is constructed unconditionally in _load_pek_models() in BOTH arms, so it cancels). If this is retention across calls, then even a PERFECT discriminator OOMs on a document with enough genuinely-broken pages. (4) Criterion 3 of the rollback ladder ('table-phase wall >15% over baseline') is WITHDRAWN as unmeasurable rather than declared green: dev's +3.8% and qa's +54.9% are both SINGLE-FIRE measurements of a fire-count-dependent cost, and dev's is additionally unreproduced and mechanically implausible (it implies one PaddleOCR page cost 4.3s total against ~8s/region from the valid lang=vi benchmark). AC-0 comes back FLAT, AND some recall proxy achieves min(legitimate) > max(broken) with ONE fixed constant across a frozen, hash-deduplicated n>=8 sample with FPT held out. backlog.title: A-29 cron-fire-gap has no total-outage-window discriminator — it emitted 6 MISSED + 23 STALE of which 26 are ONE host-suspension artifact, and the auditor's compensating 'recovering normally' prose then MASKED the 2 genuinely dead crons
backlog.note:
PO RAW-MEASURED 2026-08-23T08:05-08:10Z from cron_job_runs inside vn-market-intelligence-mcp-mcp-server-1 (/app/data/market.db) — NOT inferred from signal text. TOTAL-SILENCE WINDOW: daily run counts 08-13=3146/74 jobs, 08-14=3147/71, 08-15=1584/45, 08-16=18/12, 08-17=42/24, 08-18=154/35, 08-19/20/21=ZERO ROWS, 08-22=1215/42, 08-23=889/36. intelligenceCycle (every 15m) last fired 2026-08-18 09:xx then NOTHING until 2026-08-22 12:40, then exactly 4/hour every hour since. Whole scheduler stopped and whole scheduler resumed => host/Docker suspension, NOT a partial scheduler defect (mcp-server RestartCount=0, StartedAt 2026-08-15T08:44:09Z, never restarted across the gap). 3rd confirmed occurrence of project_host_suspension_causes_multiday_cron_silence_backlog_flush. THE DEFECT THIS ROW TRACKS IS THE DETECTOR, NOT THE OUTAGE (outage folded onto FIX-CRON-NONRECOVERY-POST-HOST-SUSPENSION-...): A-29 reads GET /api/cron-status per-cron and cannot tell 'silent because every peer was also silent' from 'dead cron'. Result 1 = CRITICAL noise: 26 of 28 STALE/MISSED are weekday/weekly/monthly crons that simply had no eligible fire slot after the 08-22T12:40Z resume (today is Sunday). Result 2 = the sharper harm: because the finding was un-triageable, the cycle hand-waved 'post-recovery backlog / recovering normally', which MASKED the 2 rows that are NOT outage artifacts — monthlySignalQualityAudit (0 0 1 * *, last 2026-06-01, missed 07-01 AND 08-01 on days the scheduler was demonstrably alive at 3146 runs/day; tracked separately on FIX-MONTHLYSIGNALQUALITYAUDITJOB-MISSED-JULY-RECOVER-GUARD) and ragFtsRebuildCron (15 20 * * *, last 2026-07-20, deploy-pending BY DESIGN per RAG-FTS-BUILD-MEMORY-BOUND — correctly dead, must be suppressed not reported). AC-1: A-29 computes a fleet-wide fire-density timeline from cron_job_runs and derives total-silence windows before evaluating any individual cron; a cron whose every missed fire slot falls inside a total-silence window is reported at INFO/suppressed with the window named, never CRITICAL. AC-2: a cron that missed a scheduled fire while peer crons WERE firing is still reported at full severity — prove with monthlySignalQualityAudit, which MUST survive the new discriminator as a real finding. AC-3: crons intentionally deploy-pending (ragFtsRebuildCron) are suppressed via an explicit ack with a tracked_by, not by threshold luck. AC-4: persist the discriminator as scripts/audits/cron-gap-discriminator.sh (reusable — this same host-suspension-vs-dead-cron question has now been hand-answered 3x); PO ran the probe ad hoc this tick and deliberately did NOT author the script (out of PO role). AC-5: NEVER_FIRED set (marketOpen/marketClose/foreignFlowFetch/dataAuditDaily/summaryWeekly/Monthly/Quarterly/Yearly/publicContractsRefresh = 9) stays on the existing A-29b unresolved-join path, unchanged by this row.

[PO SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-08-23T08:16Z — read before working this row] A pre-existing row already owns the DOMINANT cause of today's noise and this row must NOT duplicate it: FIX-CRON-STATUS-LAYERA-SCHEDULE-BLIND-FALSE-CRITICAL (backlog) — "GET /api/cron-status Layer-A misreports 23 healthy crons as MISSED/STALE every weekend: classifyCronLiveness() ignores the expected_last_fire it already computes and ladders on raw age vs cadence". That row predicts today EXACTLY: 23 STALE observed on a Sunday. Priority dropped P1->P2 accordingly. THE RESIDUAL THIS ROW STILL OWNS, which the Layer-A fix does NOT cover: after classifyCronLiveness() is corrected, a cron that missed REAL weekday fires because the whole host was suspended is still genuinely overdue by the corrected logic, so A-29 will still emit CRITICAL and a reader still cannot separate it from a dead cron. That is the outage-window discriminator (AC-1/AC-2) and it lives at the AUDITOR/consumer layer, not in the endpoint. Sequence: land FIX-CRON-STATUS-LAYERA-SCHEDULE-BLIND-FALSE-CRITICAL first, re-measure, then size this — building the discriminator on top of a miscounting classifier would tune the defect, not the detector. | FOLDED-IN from bespoke key po_ruling_20260824T1405 (unreachable to conventional readers, standing rule) by po 2026-08-24T14:31:26Z: PO 2026-08-24T14:05Z - CORROBORATING EVIDENCE THAT WIDENS THIS ROW'S SPEC.

The escalation into this row proposed that the 2026-08-24 five-cron ~5h cluster (vpsProxyWatchdog, priceUpdateWatchdog, vnIndexRefresh, alertScanParallel, taAlertNotifier) was a single outage/suspension window - reasoning that five independent crons cannot fail simultaneously to within 0.1h, and that this host has a confirmed multi-day-suspension history.

I TESTED THAT HYPOTHESIS AGAINST cron_job_runs AND REJECTED IT. The four resolvable jobs each completed their FULL normal daily run count on 2026-08-24 (vnIndexRefreshJob 84, vpsProxyWatchdogJob 42, alertScanParallelJob 28, taAlertNotifierJob 28 - identical to 2026-08-12/13/14) and stopped at their designed session-close times 08:45/08:50/08:55 UTC. Nothing was missed. There was no outage on 2026-08-24.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ROW - THIS IS THE POINT: a TWO-class discriminator (outage-window vs genuinely-dead-cron) is NOT sufficient. It would still misclassify this cluster, because the cluster is a THIRD class: a market-hours-scoped schedule whose long quiet window is by design. Any discriminator built under this row must separate at least three classes:
  (1) total-outage window - fleet-wide, ALL jobs, zero rows (the 2026-08-19/20/21 shape: no cron rows at all, 08-17/08-18 truncated to 42 and 154 runs vs ~3150 normal);
  (2) genuinely dead cron - one job silent while its peers stay healthy (the ragFtsRebuildCron shape);
  (3) schedule-envelope quiet period - full daily complement completed, then a designed stand-down (the 2026-08-24 shape).

WHY CLASSES 1 AND 3 ARE THE HARD PAIR: both produce a SYNCHRONISED multi-cron gap, which is exactly the signature that makes '5 crons at once' look alarming. Age-since-last-fire cannot separate them - it is identical in both. The separator that actually worked here was 'did each job complete its NORMAL DAILY RUN COUNT before going quiet' - a completed-complement test, not an age test. Recommend that as the discriminator primitive: compare today's per-job run count against that job's own recent full-day baseline; complement met => class 3 (benign), complement truncated fleet-wide => class 1, complement truncated for one job while peers are complete => class 2.

Class 3 is owned by FIX-CRON-STATUS-LAYERA-SCHEDULE-BLIND-FALSE-CRITICAL (task_board.backlog[328], P1) - coordinate, do not duplicate. The full measurement backing this ruling is in that row's COLD detail entry: docs/data/orch/archive/backlog-detail.json#FIX-CRON-STATUS-LAYERA-SCHEDULE-BLIND-FALSE-CRITICAL, field po_ruling_20260824T1405 (it is in cold, not inline, because that row is over the row-prose ceiling).

FIFTH NAME IS NOT A CRON AT ALL: priceUpdateWatchdog has ZERO rows under any %priceUpdate% match in cron_job_runs - the A-29b unresolved-join class owned by FIX-CRONSTATUS-STATICMAP-MISSING-9-PAIRS (task_board.backlog[436]).

Their last runs (08:45-08:55 UTC on 2026-08-25) are the LAST SCHEDULED FIRE OF THE DAY, and the next legitimate fire is 2026-08-26T02:00Z. At the 22:37Z measurement instant not one of them was overdue by a single second. THE AXIS THIS ADDS TO THIS ROW: the discriminator you are building must handle TWO kinds of legitimate silence, not one. This row was minted for a total-outage window (host suspension). This batch is the other kind -- silence INSIDE a cron's own declared off-window -- and 'overdue' computed as now-minus-last_run is structurally wrong for any schedule that is not continuous. Compute against the expected NEXT fire derived from the cron expression instead. SIBLING, DO NOT DUPLICATE THE FIX: FIX-CRON-STATUS-LAYERA-SCHEDULE-BLIND-FALSE-CRITICAL owns exactly this schedule-blindness on the GET /api/cron-status Layer-A plane and already names the same 5 jobs' class. backlog.router_note_20260826T043626Z:
THIRD BENIGN-GAP CLASS, observed live 2026-08-26T04:36:26Z — distinct from host-suspension, and it has a different signature.

T1 (*/30) heartbeat went 2026-08-26T03:44:34Z -> 2026-08-26T04:35:17Z: a ~51min gap across a 30min cadence, i.e. the 04:00Z tick never fired. Cause was NOT an outage and NOT host suspension: session-scoped crons only fire while the REPL is idle, and this router was continuously busy 04:00-04:30Z verifying three returning agents. Every service was healthy throughout — the same probe returned ALL_GREEN on all 6 checks.

Why this sharpens A-29's ask: the row currently frames the artifact class as host-suspension (long, spans MANY cron families at once, machine-wide). REPL-busy gaps look different and are separable without any new instrumentation:
  - SHORT and bounded (one or two missed ticks, not hours)
  - AFFECTS ONLY session-scoped families (dev-team, detect-loop, cowork), never launchd-owned jobs, which keep firing
  - CORRELATES with router activity — commits/board writes exist INSIDE the gap window, whereas a suspension leaves the window empty
That last one is the cheap discriminator: a gap containing this session's own commits is by construction not an outage.

SECOND-ORDER, and the reason this matters beyond taxonomy: the Tier-1 passive-health-masking guard spawns a system-auditor when heartbeat age > 60min. That threshold assumes ticks fire on schedule. A router busy ~25min longer than today would have crossed 60min and spawned an auditor for router busyness, not a system fault — a self-inflicted false positive on a fully-green system. Cf. sibling FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-FRESHNESS-CHECK-RELOCATE-TO-SENTINEL, which moves that check off this path entirely; whichever lands first should account for the other.

(1) 'FIX-FLEET-PUSH-LAUNCHD-EXCONFIG-SILENT-DEAD -> ABSENT from every lane' is NOT a dangling pointer. That row resolves to status=DONE_VERIFIED in docs/data/orch/archive/2026-08.json; it is absent from orch-state.json (0 hits) because cold-evict moved it to the monthly archive file. The resolver at scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh:259-266 unions the task_board lanes INSIDE orch-state.json including a lane literally named 'archive' — that is a task_board lane, NOT the monthly archive FILE, which the resolver never opens. So 'ABSENT' here means cold-evicted. backlog.desc: scripts/agents-flow/decision-journal-archive.sh scans `find $DECISIONS_DIR -name 'sprint-*.md'` and derives each file's sprint id from the filename stem, then classifies any id with no active_sprints[]/closed_sprints[] object as `no_orch_record` and emits a `sprint_registry_unresolved_journal_ids` signal to PO (script L363-397). LIVE COUNTS at triage time: 646 files match `sprint-*.md` in docs/agent-memory/decisions/, and the signal reports 257 unresolved. The first ids in the payload are `2026-06-05`, `2026-06-06`, `2026-06-08-po`, `2026-06-10-dev-mcp-server`, `2026-06-11-dev-mcp-server`, `2026-06-12-pm` — i.e. `sprint-<DATE>[-<agent>].md`, a legacy DATED-DAILY-JOURNAL naming convention that shares the `sprint-` filename prefix but was never a sprint id and can never resolve to one. The derivation has no discriminator between the two populations, so this signal re-fires forever. Its own dedup is a sha256 of the unresolved-id SET, so adding any one new dated journal changes the hash and re-emits the whole 257-id payload.

A coordinator finding this tick proposed attaching a mislabelled-report case here on the theory that this row's "filename heuristic / pattern-guessing" IS the mechanism. PO traced it and IT IS NOT. Do not absorb that case into this row.

THE FILENAME IS NOT GUESSED FROM NOTHING — IT IS RENDERED FROM THE STORED PERIOD KEY. apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/routes/bctcVpsIngestHandler.ts:224 calls normaliseFilename(sourceUrl, actionCode, periodYear, periodQuarter), and apps/mcp-server/src/application/usecases/bctc/resolvePdfText.ts:45-61 returns canonical ACTIONCODE_YEAR_QUARTER.pdf unless the source URL's own basename both ends in .pdf and already contains the action code. So the canonical filename is a faithful projection of financial_reports.period_year/period_quarter — the two cannot disagree, and today the filename is the ONLY place a wrong period identity is visible to a human reading a directory listing.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ROW'S DELIVERABLE. "Derive the real filename from source metadata instead of pattern-guessing" is a reasonable goal on its own terms, but it decouples the filename from the stored period. If the stored period is wrong, the file would then be named correctly while the DB row remains mislabelled — the corruption becomes invisible instead of fixed. The live case that prompted this: report_id 5b0dad71-3b05-4455-9823-c2072442777d is stored as DPM_2025_Q4.pdf while its refined content is unambiguously Q1-2026 across five independent pages. The filename is what exposed it.

That row adds the period-vs-content validation the ingest boundary has never had (bctcVpsIngestHandler.ts:194-201 validates only that the year is 2000..2099 and the quarter is one of Q1..Q4 — shape, never correspondence). Once a wrong period identity cannot be stored, decoupling the filename from it is safe and this row becomes a clean improvement. Until then, this row's change would delete the tripwire.

ADD TO THIS ROW'S ACCEPTANCE when it is eventually worked: a real-filename derivation must not be able to mask a period mismatch — either it preserves a period assertion somewhere visible, or the validation row has already landed. WHY THE EXISTING VALIDATION DOES NOT CATCH IT (read the code, do not assume): orch-apply.sh's advertised "dup-key" is orch-validate.mjs findDuplicateJsonKeys(), a RAW-TEXT scan for duplicate JSON OBJECT KEYS at any nesting level ({"a":1,"a":2}) — see its header "Stage 0 (raw text, pre-parse): duplicate JSON key scan on raw bytes" and exit code 1 = "duplicate JSON keys detected in raw text". It has no notion of array-element .id uniqueness. Separately, orch-conservation-check.mjs's signal_queue.rows[] row-identity guard is an ANTI-LOSS guard: undeclaredSignalRowDrops() reports ids that VANISH, and it compares id SETS. So the guard family is asymmetric by construction — it protects rows from being deleted and is structurally blind to rows being duplicated. That asymmetry is the gap this row should close.
CONSEQUENCE IF LEFT: any lookup by `.id ==` or by grep resolves ambiguously to two rows with CONTRADICTORY status (RESOLVED vs NEW) — the same ambiguous-id-resolution hazard as feedback_auditor_dedup_citation_resolves_to_nonexistent_row_id. Note it must run on the CANDIDATE, and it must be a hard reject, not a WARN — this instance proves a WARN would have been ignored by an autonomous writer.

backlog.title: FIX-CI-GOLANGCI-CONFIG-VERIFY-NETWORK-FLAKE: golangci-lint-action v7 `config verify` live schema-fetch times out -> false CI red
backlog.note: PLAN-ONLY (anomaly->BACKLOG invariant; WIP=ready17+in_progress1=18 over cap -> NOT dispatched now). ROOT CAUSE: commit dd79f8118 (FIX-CI-LINT-STACK) bumped golangci/golangci-lint-action v6->v7 in .github/workflows/ci.yml — v7 auto-runs `golangci-lint config verify`, which does a LIVE network fetch of https://golangci-lint.run/jsonschema/golangci.v2.0.jsonschema.json to validate .golangci.yml before linting. That fetch times out intermittently (external host slow/unreachable) -> false CI red, INDEPENDENT of our code and .golangci.yml (both byte-identical + passed 6 consecutive runs 3be781412->b787e115b->12cdf685d->604909c5d->cfc62a347->b9e9877c6). SIGNATURE(RAW): `[.golangci.yml] validate: compile schema: failing loading "https://golangci-lint.run/jsonschema/golangci.v2.0.jsonschema.json": context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)`. OBS(2, identical sig): obs#1 8419b9c49 @2026-07-18T12:37Z; obs#2 d2034d456 @16:07Z (CI run 29651771448 — jobs "Stock Price Go Lint" + "Macro Indicators Go Lint" both failed at step "Run golangci-lint"; other 4 Go-lint + py-lint + bun test passed). SCOPE: ONE shared file .github/workflows/ci.yml — 6 IDENTICAL lint-step blocks (technical-analysis ~L68-73, macro-indicators ~L90-95, stock-price ~L112-117, alert-engine ~L138-143, api-gateway ~L161-166, kinh-dich ~L184-189), each `uses: golangci/golangci-lint-action@v7.0.0` with `version: v2.0`. Any of the 6 can hit it. IMPACT: non-blocking NOW (obs#2 red was a docs-only push, stranded nothing) — but WILL false-red a future CODE push -> strands a real dev change / trips false rebase-block (red-prepush-strands-fleet class). GOAL: make config-verify network-INDEPENDENT. CANDIDATE APPROACHES (ba/architect own final HOW): (a) disable/skip the config-verify step via the action's supported input (e.g. skip schema verify) or run golangci-lint without the remote-schema check; (b) VENDOR/pin golangci.v2.0.jsonschema.json locally + point verify at the local file (offline, deterministic) — RECOMMENDED; (c) wrap verify in retry/allow-failure — WEAKEST, still network-dependent, avoid. VERIFICATION_GATE: config-verify makes NO request to golangci-lint.run in CI logs (grep run logs) OR 10 consecutive Go-lint runs green with the schema host artificially unreachable. Chain: po->ba->architect->dev-team (generic developer, cross-service infra). Prior art: CLEAN (grepped golangci|config verify|jsonschema|lint flake across board/handoffs/signals — 0 existing row). Origin: router-detected recurring CI flake, 2026-07-18.

backlog.po_live_occurrence_20260814T0710Z:
[po 2026-08-14T07:07:35Z | UNBLOCK-OPS-RAG-REBUILD-DONEVERIFIED-FALSIFIED-BY-KERNEL] LIVE OCCURRENCE — I was the victim, and I self-detected only by accident.
WHAT HAPPENED: I landed two gated writes to docs/data/orch/orch-state.json (orch-apply.sh, 06:59:05Z and 07:01:03Z) plus one atomic write to docs/data/orch/archive/2026-08.json. When I entered the commit-mutex critical section at ~07:08Z and ran `git add` on my 7 explicit paths, only 5 staged — both orch files reported as already-clean. They had been absorbed into a PEER's bare commit 3220f31bc ("chore(tasks): cold-evict terminal sprints/done lanes -> archive/2026-08.json"), which is exactly this row's thesis: a clean `git status` on a path you just wrote is INDISTINGUISHABLE from "my commit landed". I only caught it because I ran `git log --oneline -- <path>` and `git log -S` to find which SHA actually carried my content. Nothing in my flow required that step.
SECOND, SHARPER FINDING — THE EXISTING AC-3 GATE WOULD HAVE FIRED A FALSE ALARM ON THIS: `docs/agents/po/flow/main.md` § AC-3 tests `git show --stat $(git rev-parse HEAD) | grep -q 'docs/data/orch/orch-state.json'` against PO'S OWN commit and, on miss, sends `send_telegram(channel="bug", "...landed on disk via orch-apply.sh but not in git HEAD")`. On this cycle that grep MISSES (my commit abfa9de90 legitimately does not contain orch-state.json — a peer's did) while the write is nonetheless fully durable in HEAD ancestry, verified by reading the content back out of `git show HEAD:docs/data/orch/orch-state.json`. The gate conflates "not in MY commit" with "not in git HEAD". Its failure direction matters: it would emit a bug report asserting a data-loss that did not occur, inviting the next actor to re-apply an already-applied write. Correct predicate is ancestry-and-content, not own-commit-membership: `git show HEAD:<path>` re-read (or `git log -S<marker> -1 --format=%H -- <path>` returning any SHA reachable from HEAD), with own-commit-membership demoted to an informational note.
NO DATA LOSS THIS TIME: I verified all 4 board assertions by reading them back out of `git show HEAD:...` — restored row BLOCKED with banner + retractions intact, UNBLOCK row REVIEW, LANCECORE cross-ref present (2621B), .head untouched. Benign sweep, correct content. That is precisely why it is worth recording: the benign case is the one that trains agents to stop checking.
backlog.status_note: EVIDENCE 2026-08-26 08:45Z tick (cowork-dispatcher): this rows premise covers only the ABSORB branch (victim staged WIP swept into a peers commit -> clean status -> false success). A second, complementary branch was observed live and the remedy as titled would MISS it. chef-eod staged both own_paths at ~08:51Z; its commit was denied; alert-commander won commit-mutex:main at 08:52:49Z and correctly RESTORED the 2 foreign staged paths (a0803e878) rather than absorbing them. The victim still reported success: chef cited "Git commit: fe93e2971" - this dispatchers own tick commit, zero chef content. fe93e2971 was HEAD only during 08:51:02-08:52:49Z, exactly while chefs own commit was being denied, because the denier IS the mutex holder and commits while holding it. So the false hash is produced SYSTEMATICALLY by the protocol, not hallucinated, and it RESOLVES under git show - which is why it survives review. REMEDY MUST BE own-path-scoped, not trail-scoped: end-of-cycle assert `git status --porcelain -- <own_paths>` empty AND the commit touching those paths is one this agent authored this cycle. Root ordering defect feeding both branches: agents run `git add` BEFORE acquiring the mutex, so a fail-closed denial leaves staging applied. Artifacts rescued in a173400b1. backlog.title: An agent-side context-budget limit is written into permanent report state as a data failure — failed_ct is indistinguishable between 'source data is bad' and 'worker could not hold a 1.2MB image'
backlog.mechanism: For the final 4 windows of POW_2026_Q1 the refine agent reported the page-28 image fetch returned ~1.2MB of base64 that 'exceeded context token budget'. That is a limit of the SUBAGENT's context window — not a property of the document and not of the pipeline. Per its error-boundary contract the agent pushed FAILED for those windows and called finalize_bctc_refine, producing refine_status=FAILED with failed_ct=28.
backlog.why_it_matters: The failure reason is now indistinguishable, in stored state, from a genuine data defect. A future remediation pass reading failed_ct=28 cannot tell that some windows failed because a transcription worker could not hold a 1.2MB image rather than because the page is unreadable. Combined with the head-of-line row this is also what makes the head row PERMANENTLY dead: the finalization is sticky.
backlog.fix_direction: Introduce a distinct terminal-ish status (e.g. DEFERRED / RESOURCE_EXCEEDED) that does NOT finalize the report and leaves the window re-attemptable by a worker with a larger budget or via an image-downscale path. Do not class it with text_fetch_failed.
backlog.scoping_caution: The agent FOLLOWED its documented graceful-degradation contract — this is NOT filed as agent misbehaviour. The defect is that the contract has no distinct terminal status for 'worker could not process within its own resource envelope' versus 'source data is bad'. Prior art (the BCTC reingest guard: 56/56 FAILED/empty-markdown, data-loss guard refused to wipe bctc_table_rows) shows the downstream cost of that ambiguity is already being paid elsewhere.

backlog.title: 'Write acceptance criteria before editing files' is structurally unverifiable for every agent whose commit zone excludes orch-state.json — move acceptance authorship to the dispatcher
backlog.po_evidence: Surfaced by the FIX-COMMIT-PATH-PEER-INDEX-SWEEP-GUARD-SKILLS supervised sign-off 2026-07-21. agent-father claimed it wrote acceptance onto the row BEFORE editing any file, and the row carries self-reported acceptance_written_at=2026-07-21T19:08:10Z. But the acceptance text's FIRST appearance in git is 304f24edd at 19:14:24Z, AFTER the skills commit 3e4f50d3a at 19:12:13Z — because agent-father's commit zone excludes docs/data/orch/orch-state.json, so a peer cold-evict swept the board and collapsed the acceptance-write and the lane-move into one indistinguishable blob. The claim is UNVERIFIABLE, not disproven. acceptance_written_by/acceptance_written_at are self-reported fields authored by the same agent whose ordering they attest — they are narration, not evidence.
backlog.po_ruling: The dispatcher's framing is correct and generalises: an agent whose commit zone excludes the board can NEVER produce evidence for an ordering claim about the board. Requiring such a claim therefore mandates an unfalsifiable self-report, which is exactly the failure class feedback_agent_selfreport_metalayer_confabulation.md warns about. The requirement is unenforceable across the whole maintenance lane, and the unsatisfiable dispatch instruction was the dispatcher's error, not agent-father's — no fault attaches to the agent. PREFERRED RESOLUTION: acceptance is authored by the DISPATCHER (or PO) at dispatch time, before spawn. The dispatcher's commit zone already includes the board, so ordering becomes provable by construction across two disjoint zones: dispatcher commits acceptance, implementer commits code, and git ordering across the two zones is independently checkable. Rejected alternatives: (a) letting maintenance agents commit the board row themselves — breaks zone separation and re-introduces the peer-sweep class this very sprint just fixed; (b) silently dropping the requirement — loses the real benefit that acceptance predates implementation.
backlog.question: Should acceptance-criteria authorship move from the implementing agent to the dispatcher for all supervised maintenance-lane rows, and what is the migration path for flow docs that currently instruct the implementer to self-write acceptance?

backlog.title: Session-scoped CronCreate loops are invisible and unpersisted across 5 CLI sessions — build the launchd-hosted liveness watchdog that turns 'a session died and its whole loop vanished' from silent into a BUG-channel alert
backlog.status_note: PO SEQUENCE RANK 4 — gated on UC-SDF-P6 (cron-registry.json) landing first; this row is that registry's first consumer. See po_design_ruling below: the design call was made, this row implements one third of it.
backlog.problem: CronList in the router session returns 'No scheduled jobs.' Crons live inside 5 separate CLI sessions (dev-team, cowork, system-audit, claude-heler, workflows-fix). No session can see or repair another's crons. When a session dies its whole loop vanishes with zero trace. CronCreate additionally only fires while the REPL is idle, so a session stuck mid-query fires nothing. PO verified there is NO on-disk cron persistence under ~/.claude (no crons dir; ~/.claude/jobs/ holds two stale June background-job state dirs, unrelated).
backlog.po_design_ruling: OPTION (a) BROADER LAUNCHD COVERAGE — SCOPED, plus (c) MONITORING. Option (b), a persistence/registry layer for CronCreate, is REJECTED as a new scheduler. Reasoning: (1) building persistence for CronCreate means re-implementing a scheduler we do not own, inside a surface (the CLI REPL) whose contract can change under us; we already own two durable planes (launchd, and the containerized mcp-server node-cron scheduler with 85 jobs) and a third home-grown one is exactly the 'duplicating cron hosts' that UC-CDC-P5 already names as the thing to avoid. (2) launchd is the ONLY plane that survives session death and it demonstrably works (firer: 815 runs). (3) But WHOLESALE migration to launchd is equally wrong — `claude -p` per tick is expensive and, per FIX-GUARANTEED-SLOT-FIRER-FANOUT-TRUNCATION, structurally truncates fan-out work. So launchd hosts loop RE-ARM and LIVENESS, not every loop. (4) The REPL-idle constraint is unfixable from our side; that is a second independent argument for making session-plane failures VISIBLE rather than trying to make the session plane reliable. (5) Monitoring alone (option c as a terminal answer) is also rejected: without a registry there is nothing to monitor against.
backlog.three_part_sequence: PART 1 (registry of record) — FOLDED INTO EXISTING UC-SDF-P6, not re-minted: the 5 session-scoped loops must be DECLARED in a repo file so absence becomes detectable. Not a new scheduler; an inventory. PART 2 (this row) — one launchd-hosted watchdog that reads that registry and alerts when a declared loop has produced no evidence-of-life within its cadence. PART 3 (re-arm automation) — EXISTING UC-CDC-P5, sequenced LAST, only after 1+2: re-arming blind is how you get double-hosted crons.
backlog.hard_constraint_evidence_of_life: Evidence-of-life MUST be the loop's own external artifact — its commits, its notebook mtime, its telemetry row — NEVER a self-report or a heartbeat the loop writes about itself. A loop that can assert its own liveness is a loop whose watchdog is self-satisfying (see FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-FRESHNESS-CHECK-RELOCATE-TO-SENTINEL in ready[], same defect class, already ruled).
backlog.acceptance: Kill any one of the 5 sessions and, within one cadence period, a BUG-channel message names the dead loop. Today that event is completely silent.
backlog.note:
PO 2026-08-14 (incident-driven update, triage session 632721c2). (C1) docs/data/cowork-schedule.json .slots[].last_fired IS NOT A LIVENESS ORACLE. There are two independent firing planes and only one writes it back. backlog.title: Three time bases coexist in one scheduling system: server jobs mix timezone UTC and Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh, CronCreate fires at MACHINE-LOCAL France time (CEST/CET, DST-sensitive), and the market it serves is fixed UTC+7 — no single place states what any job's real wall-clock is
backlog.status_note: PO SEQUENCE RANK 7 — gated on UC-SDF-P6 cron-registry.json. A registry that records each job's declared time base is most of this answer; doing it before the registry means writing the same table twice.
backlog.problem: (1) mcp-server scheduler jobs individually declare timezone:'UTC' or timezone:'Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh'. (2) CronCreate jobs fire at machine-local France time (CEST=UTC+2 summer / CET=UTC+1 winter) and therefore SHIFT BY AN HOUR twice a year against the market. (3) Vietnam is fixed UTC+7 with no DST. A job authored as '15:00' has three different meanings depending on which plane it lands on, and nothing declares which.
backlog.dst_is_the_sharp_edge: The France planes silently re-time relative to the VN trading session at each DST transition. docs/standards/cron-jobs.md:292 already documents this reasoning for the guaranteed-slot firer (StartInterval chosen over StartCalendarInterval precisely because the latter is DST-sensitive) — the insight exists but is applied in exactly one place. backlog.title: cowork-team parallel fan-out has no producer/consumer ordering — alert-commander read the signal bus before its co-dispatched producers wrote to it, and went silent on a session with real >5% drops
backlog.mechanism: BGFAN-1 mandates run_in_background=true for every dispatcher spawn and spawn-fanout.md issues all matched slots in ONE parallel block, with no dependency ordering. When a tick matches both a PRODUCER (market-watcher -> price_anomaly; news-scout -> urgent_news/chain_catalyst) and a CONSUMER (alert-commander -> gates on those exact signal types), the consumer can complete its bus read before the producers have posted.

po_clause_d_20260808.headline: (d) effective_next_agent()/effective_owner() DETAIL-FIRST precedence lets a COLD mint-time value silently outrank a lifecycle-flipped HOT board row.
po_clause_d_20260808.mechanism: docs/data/orch/archive/backlog-detail.json is a COLD mint-time store. Its ONLY writer (scripts/orch-backlog-stub.sh) runs on new-backlog-item write and documents 'existing cold wins' merge semantics — it NEVER re-syncs a cold entry after the hot row is later flipped by the implementing agent. So for EVERY row that moves past BACKLOG, cold .next_agent/.status are systematically stale, and detail-first makes that stale value authoritative over the live hot SSOT.
po_clause_d_20260808.harm_two_sided: Measured live 2026-08-08 (jq via scripts/lib/devteam-eligibility.jq against the live board): 6 review[] rows carried hot next_agent=='qa' but resolved to a stale cold agent. (i) FALSE-NEGATIVE, the bigger harm: scripts/devteam-review-claim-qa-drain.jq selects effective_next_agent=='qa', so all 6 were PERMANENTLY invisible to PRIMARY QA-Drain and could never be signed off — accreting in review[] forever, actively defeating the throughput goal of docs/architecture-briefs/2026-08-01-review-lane-drain-throughput-and-secondary-sweep.md. (ii) FALSE-POSITIVE: the same 6 sat in the SECONDARY-Drain pool (selects != 'qa'), which never lane-moves a claimed row, so it re-dispatches the WRONG agent every tick the row is oldest. Materialised twice: FIX-NOTEBOOK-AUTOPRUNE-REGEX-HEADING-MISMATCH -> 'developer' (2026-08-05T08:15:09Z) and FIX-COWORK-SPAWN-IDENTITY-PREAMBLE-OFFFLOW -> 'agent-father' (2026-08-08T17:26:17Z; agent-father returned 'already implemented, 9/9 tests, correctly parked for QA' — a full wasted dispatch).

Predicate-driven, idempotent, gate-verified. That is a DATA patch for one lane — this clause is the actual fix.
po_clause_d_20260808.do_not_blanket_flip: A blanket board-first flip is a SAFETY REGRESSION and must NOT be shipped. 10 live backlog[] rows also carry a board-vs-cold next_agent conflict (board architect/agent-father/dev-mcp-server/pm/developer vs cold ba/architect) — e.g. FIX-AUDITOR-C06-OFFMARKET-RECALIBRATE, FIX-ORPHAN-ADOPTION-BOARD-STATE-GUARD. Those are NOT lifecycle flips (still status BACKLOG), and there cold-first is the CONSERVATIVE direction: is_non_dev_next_agent_unrouted() currently gates them OUT of BOUNDED-1 unattended pickup. Board-first would make them auto-dispatchable, reopening exactly the class the 2026-07-09..07-16 gate fixes closed.
