backlog.title: Add a real updated_at audit column to prediction_claims, maintained on every write, surfaced per-row on the Du bao AI page so a reader can tell at a glance whether a prediction was actually refreshed
backlog.root_cause: Direct user demand: 'each prediction need add update at time for easy recheck is update or not'. VERIFIED ABSENT end-to-end. The store row type PredictionClaimRow (predictionClaimStore.ts:60, mapRow ~:110) exposes exactly: id, stock, agent_id, claim_text, direction, target_price, resolution_date, confidence, resolution_outcome, actual_price, brier_score, creation_price, is_excluded, created_at, resolved_at — no updated_at. The serve DTO (predictionClaimsHandler.ts) and the page type (dashboard.prediction-claims.tsx:82-83) carry only createdAt and resolvedAt. PO DECISION — ADD A REAL COLUMN, do not repurpose an existing timestamp. Reasoning: (1) resolvedAt is the closest existing candidate but it is NULL for all 5 pending rows in live data, which is exactly the population the user wants to recheck — surfacing it would answer 'was this updated?' with a blank for every row the question is actually about; (2) createdAt answers a different question (when minted) and by construction never moves; (3) FIX-PREDCLAIM-CREATIONPRICE-UNGATE-ZOD-CONTRACT deliverable (c) and FIX-PREDCLAIM-BACKFILL-NULL-CREATIONPRICE both introduce a genuine THIRD mutation class — post-creation edits to a claim that are neither creation nor resolution — after which no existing timestamp can represent 'last touched' at all; (4) the backfill will rewrite historical rows, and without an audit column there is no way for a reader to distinguish a backfilled row from an untouched one, which is precisely the recheck affordance being asked for.
backlog.deliverable: (a) mcp-server: add updated_at to prediction_claims using the ESTABLISHED idempotent pattern already in schema-system.ts:209-212 (try { db.exec('ALTER TABLE prediction_claims ADD COLUMN updated_at TEXT') } catch {}) — same shape as the creation_price and is_excluded columns added before it. Do not introduce a new migration mechanism for one column. (b) Maintain it on EVERY write path with no exceptions: insertPredictionClaim sets updated_at = created_at; resolveClaim and excludeClaim set it to now; the backfill script sets it; any future partial-update helper sets it. Stamping must live inside the store functions, not at call sites — a call-site convention is exactly the kind of thing the next new call site skips. Use real UTC from the runtime, never a hand-formed string (feedback_hand_typed_iso_timestamps_drift_into_the_future.md). (c) Backfill existing rows: updated_at = COALESCE(resolved_at, created_at), which is truthful for every row under the current two-event lifecycle. (d) Extend the serve DTO in predictionClaimsHandler.ts with updatedAt, passing through as null where genuinely unset — never coerced, matching the existing 'all nullable columns pass through as null' rule in mapClaimRow. (e) frontend: render it per claim on dashboard.prediction-claims.tsx as 'Cap nhat luc', clearly distinct from the creation date, and legible for pending rows. (f) Fold updated_at into the Zod contract from FIX-PREDCLAIM-CREATIONPRICE-UNGATE-ZOD-CONTRACT as a REQUIRED field on write once the column exists.
backlog.acceptance: Every one of the 17 live claims returns a non-null updatedAt through the LIVE served endpoint after backfill. A claim mutated by the backfill script shows an updatedAt strictly later than its createdAt; an untouched historical claim shows updatedAt equal to its resolved_at or created_at. Resolving a pending claim advances its updatedAt within the same tick. The value is visible per row on the rendered page. All timestamps are runtime-generated UTC — no hand-typed ISO strings anywhere in the change.
backlog.note: zone=multi because the change spans apps/mcp-server/ (column + store stamping + DTO) and apps/frontend/ (render) — architect splits per the precedent set by FIX-PRED-CLAIMS-EXCLUDED-SERVE-DISPLAY, which was minted zone=multi (commit c40f90062) and dispatched to dev-mcp-server + dev-frontend in parallel (commit b0a786690). Sequenced P2 behind the three P1 rows: an updated_at on a claim that is still structurally unscoreable would tell the user when a worthless row was last touched. Fix the scoring first, then give the reader the recheck affordance.

(a) Adding triaged/RETRACTED to TERMINAL_SIGNAL_STATUSES (scripts/orch-cold-evict.sh:87) and to the signal-dashboard PRUNE criteria WOULD EVICT ROWS WHOSE TRACKED WORK IS STILL OPEN - it contradicts handlers.md:240 (TRIAGED = active), scripts-registry po-s137 (explicitly NOT TRIAGED), and the cron-db-data-integrity dedup guard that reads TRIAGED as already-open. backlog.scope_open_question_for_architect: ARCHITECT MUST RULE on the semantics before code lands, because the two documented readings disagree and the fix differs per reading. backlog.title: system-auditor labelled `pdf-extractor at memory limit 98.87% (2.472/2.5 GiB)` as WARN (rank 2) when its own tier-1 ladder maps `peak >97%` to CRITICAL (rank 3): `--severity` is a hand-authored literal with no binding to the measured value, so the dedup layer's escalation bypass (`new_rank > stored_rank`) is structurally unreachable for magnitude-driven conditions — and three improvised dedup_keys for one condition are currently the ONLY reason the 98.87% alert was not suppressed
backlog.root_cause: PREMISE CORRECTION — THE ESCALATING REPORT'S CENTRAL CLAIM IS REFUTED, AND THE REFUTATION IS THE FINDING. The report to PO asserted: `its BUG Telegram was DEDUP-SKIPPED: dedup_key microservice_degraded:pdf-extractor:A-30-MEMORY had already been sent at 2026-07-28T14:30:09Z for the BENIGN 85% state ... the key minted while the condition was 'stable plateau, not a defect' now suppresses notification for '20 MiB from OOM and climbing' for the next 7 days.` PO checked the ledger and the signal rows instead of accepting this. It is wrong on the decisive fact. The 14:30:09Z entry did NOT carry the benign 85% state. Live signal_queue row sys-20260728T143010-6ec2, ts=2026-07-28T14:30:10Z, summary verbatim: `pdf-extractor at memory limit 98.87% (2.472/2.5 GiB) — sustained after OCR workload`. The 14:30:09Z Telegram WAS the near-cap alert, and it WAS sent. What the 14:34:57Z emit hit was a 4-minute-later re-observation of the SAME state (98.84% vs 98.87%) under the SAME key — a textbook intra-cycle duplicate, and the router itself independently classified it as one on the row: `router_dedup_note: INTRA-CYCLE DUPLICATE of sys-20260728T143010-6ec2 (same sweep, same pdf-extractor condition, 98.84 vs 98.87). Triage as ONE.` THE DEDUP GATE BEHAVED CORRECTLY. No escalation was swallowed. Filing the reported bug as reported would have `fixed` the one component in the chain that worked. LEDGER TIMELINE, read from docs/data/auditor-dedup-ledger.json at 2026-07-28T14:44Z, which is what the claim should have been checked against: `microservice_degraded:pdf-extractor:PDF-MEM-01` ts=2026-07-28T12:49:39Z sev=2 | `mem_pressure:pdf-extractor:A-30-PDF-EXTRACTOR` ts=2026-07-28T13:12:18Z sev=2 (this is the 85.54% plateau — archived signal row sys-20260728T131219-3fca, `pdf-extractor memory 85.54% of 2.5 GiB (2.138 GiB) — stable plateau`) | `microservice_degraded:pdf-extractor:A-30-MEMORY` ts=2026-07-28T14:30:09Z sev=2 (this is the 98.87%). Three keys, one condition, 101 minutes, all rank 2. DEFECT 1 — SEVERITY IS A HAND-AUTHORED LABEL, NOT A FUNCTION OF THE MEASUREMENT. scripts/emit-audit-signal.sh `_severity_rank()` collapses to `CRITICAL) echo 3 ;; HIGH|WARN) echo 2 ;; MED|INFO) echo 1 ;; *) echo 1`, ranking whatever string the calling agent typed into `--severity`. docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/tier1-probe.md clause 5 states the policy the label was supposed to follow: `verdict=="ESCALATE", reason contains "OOMKilled=true" -> CRITICAL` / `reason contains "peak >97%" -> CRITICAL` / `reason contains "no reclamation dip" (>93% baseline case) -> WARN`. 98.87% is a `peak >97%` reading; the policy says CRITICAL (rank 3); the emit said WARN (rank 2). That ladder is prose in a markdown file, enforceable only by an LLM remembering to read it, and the tier-2 sweep that produced this emit does not read it at all — there is no tier2 flow file (docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/ contains only main.md, tier1-probe.md, page-freshness.md). Nothing in the emit script can detect that `--severity WARN` contradicts a summary reading `98.87% of 2.5 GiB`. CONTROL CASE, SAME AUDITOR, SAME SWEEP, MINUTES APART — this is why the diagnosis is producer-side and not gate-side: sbv_fx DID escalate its label across the identical window, sys-20260728T142957-693e ts=14:29:57Z severity=HIGH `sbv_fx stale 43min (SLA 30min)` then sys-20260728T143455-6a8a ts=14:34:55Z severity=CRITICAL `sbv_fx stale 47min (check B-02-SBV)`. Rank 2 -> rank 3 on the same sweep, which would fire the bypass exactly as designed. One condition varied its label with the measurement; the other did not. The gate is common to both. DEFECT 2 — DEDUP-KEY NAMESPACE DRIFT, and it is currently MASKING defect 1. docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/tier1-probe.md:208 prescribes `"dedup_key":"microservice_degraded:<service_id>:<A-xx>"` with the worked example at :93 `microservice_degraded:pdf-extractor:A-20`; the canonical key here is `microservice_degraded:pdf-extractor:A-30`. The call sites instead improvised `PDF-MEM-01`, `A-30-PDF-EXTRACTOR` under a `mem_pressure:` category prefix that appears in no documented category set, and `A-30-MEMORY`. THE CONSEQUENCE IS COUNTER-INTUITIVE AND IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE IN THIS ROW: because `microservice_degraded:pdf-extractor:A-30-MEMORY` was a BRAND-NEW key at 14:30:09Z, `_ledger_prune_and_lookup` found no entry, took the `if [ -z "$LEDGER_ENTRY_TS" ]` branch, and SENT. Had the keys been correctly normalised, the 98.87% emit would have collided with the 13:12:18Z 85.54% entry under one canonical key, compared 2 > 2, evaluated false, and been SKIP-dedup'd — the exact failure the escalating report described, which has not happened yet but WOULD have. backlog.root_cause: The crash-vs-deploy discriminator classifies a startup by comparing it to its PREDECESSOR startup, but it only ever sees predecessors inside a FIXED lookback of 2x the alert window (8h), while the gap between startups is unbounded. Both implementations share it. (a) docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/tier1-probe.md:119 fetches mcpServerStartup rows >= datetime('now','-8 hours'), :120 sets the 4h alert cutoff, :122 loops `for (let i=1;i<rows.length;i++)` comparing rows[i] to rows[i-1]. The earliest fetched row has no predecessor in the set and is never evaluated. (b) apps/mcp-server/src/scheduler/system/restartCadenceAlertJob.ts is identical in effect: WINDOW_HOURS=4 (:96), fetch bound `-${WINDOW_HOURS * 2} hours` (:179), loop from i=0 (:200) with an explicit `if (i === 0) continue;` at :207 commented 'No predecessor -> cannot classify -> skip (conservative: not a crash)'. (c) The same query appears verbatim in the design brief at docs/architecture-briefs/2026-07-23-auditor-a30-reclamation-gate-a21-windowed-restart.md:178-181, so this originates in the SPEC and was ported forward, not introduced by an implementer. THE INTENT WAS EXPLICIT AND THE GUARANTEE IS FALSE: :171-173 of the TS job states the 2x lookback exists 'to capture the startup that preceded the oldest in-window startup (needed to classify the first row)'. A fixed 2x extension only guarantees that predecessor when the inter-startup gap is short. Formally: for an in-window startup T (T >= now-4h) with predecessor P, P is fetched only if P >= now-8h; if the gap T-P exceeds 8h then P < T-8h <= now-8h and P is ALWAYS dropped. So the discriminator can only classify crashes that follow LESS THAN 8h of uptime - i.e. it works during an already-established fast crash loop and fails on the first crash after any stable period. The conservative skip is not conservative: it is a silent false negative on the highest-signal event.

This row prescribes "call the real exported runRestartCadenceAlertJob via docker-exec import with an injected readonly db". That de-duplication is right, but the docker-exec TRANSPORT preserves a self-referential blind spot that a 2026-07-31 live incident exercised. THE INCIDENT: 12 mcpServerStartup rows on 2026-07-31 between 11:36 and 12:40 with ZERO mcpServerCleanShutdown sentinels in that window (verified read-only against data/live/market.db cron_job_runs; only sentinel that day = 14:44:23). The A-21 logic was therefore NOT the reason -- the windowed crash-only re-model behaved correctly on paper. THE STRUCTURAL PROBLEM: tier1-probe.md:115-116 resolves MCP_CTR via `docker ps | grep mcp-server` and then runs `docker exec "$MCP_CTR" bun -e ...` INSIDE the very container whose restart behaviour is being measured, and :148-149 maps any docker exec/query failure to "[A-21] TOOL-UNAVAILABLE -- skip (NOT an infra finding)". During a restart storm the container is intermittently absent from `docker ps` and `docker exec` intermittently fails, so probe failure is POSITIVELY CORRELATED with the condition the probe exists to detect, and the spec converts that failure into silence rather than into a finding. A detector whose transport dies with its subject, and whose failure mode is "not an infra finding", cannot page on the strongest form of its own signal. NOTE ON RIGOUR: the restart burst and the missing sentinels are directly verified; that a Tier-1 cycle actually ran during the burst and took the TOOL-UNAVAILABLE branch is INFERRED (the auditor notebook is overwrite-per-cycle so the 07-31 midday entry is gone). FEASIBLE ALTERNATIVE, VERIFIED TODAY: market.db is bind-mounted to the host (docker inspect Mounts: <root>/data/live -> /app/data), so the probe can read it host-side with NO dependency on the monitored container. Host `sqlite3 -readonly` FAILS with CANTOPEN(14) because journal_mode=wal and no -shm exists to open read-only; `sqlite3 "file:<abs>/data/live/market.db?immutable=1"` works and was cross-checked today against the in-container bun readonly query -- both returned identical counts (agent_signals 131 total, 27 in the 24h window). backlog.mechanism_correction: The row's recommended_action (add a T4 dedup guard, then flip recoverMissedExecutions:false -> true) is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT and must not be shipped alone. Confirmed at source in node-cron@3.0.3 src/scheduler.js: Scheduler.start() sets lastExecution = timeMatcher.apply(new Date()) and lastCheck = process.hrtime() at start time, and the recovery loop only walks back Math.floor(elapsedMs/1000) seconds since the previous in-process 1s tick. Therefore recoverMissedExecutions:true recovers ONLY event-loop stalls inside a living process — it can NEVER replay a fire that fell during a process restart or downtime window. Any restart spanning 1st-of-month 00:00 UTC still loses the audit with the flag set to true. Real fix must be a startup catch-up: apps/mcp-server/src/scheduler/startupHelpers.ts already ships shouldRunCatchup() (task 1430) with a DB-backed 'already ran today' guard, weekdayOnly / requiredUtcDay / utcHour window gating, and fail-safe-on-DB-error semantics. backlog.root_cause:
PO source-verified 2026-07-30T21:1xZ, BOTH planes read at source, not inferred.

PRODUCER — docs/agents/bctc-analyst/flow/main.md:118-127. guard_key = "esc-deepdive:" + ticker + ":" + quarter + ":" + trigger_id; the ONLY emission gate is task_claim(task_id=guard_key, ttl_seconds=86400). There is NO board lookup, and structurally there cannot be one in the current design — bctc-analyst has no Bash tool grant (its own notebook records 'no Bash tool this session' for cycles c078-c133), so it cannot jq the task_board. The producer is board-blind BY CONSTRUCTION; its 24h TTL is a rate-limiter, never a known-root suppressor.

CONSUMER — docs/agents/dev-team/flow/drain-esc-dispatch.md:75-95. GATE-B Tier 1 board_hit matches REFLOW-<ticker>-<quarter>, any id starting REFLOW-<ticker>-, a .related entry, or guard_key appearing in title/status_note/root_cause, over all non-TERMINAL rows. That gate is WORKING: zero deep_dive_result signals exist anywhere on disk or in git since docs/signals/processed/bctc-analyst-20260724T152500Z.json, i.e. no Opus deep-dive has been spawned for FPT ESC-5 since BEFORE the REFLOW row existed. The Opus burn is already contained; only the re-emission is not.

FALSIFIED CLAIM (this is the actual defect, and it is load-bearing on the board): REFLOW-FPT-Q1-2026's own title asserts 'minting it also stops the 24h re-escalation'. It does not, and cannot — GATE-B is downstream of the producer. Minted 2026-07-25T15:28:08Z; re-escalations observed 07-28, 07-29, 07-30 (3 file-sourced signals on disk, all byte-identical payloads: report_id e8ea3df5-3f32-413d-a3eb-c71634c0438d, same 7 low-confidence units unit-0008..unit-0014, same min_confidence 0.45, refined_at unchanged since 2026-05-31). Predecessor PO counted 11 consecutive TRUE cycles (c119..c129) at 2026-07-29T21:3xZ; bctc-analyst's own c133 entry (2026-07-30T21:12:55Z) records a LIVE recheck — get_bctc_refined, 15 units read in full — reconfirming ESC-5=TRUE on the same inputs, so the run now extends to c133.

COST, measured not assumed: 4x/day (cron 15,18,21,00 UTC) bctc-analyst re-reads all 15 refine units to re-derive a conclusion that has not changed in 60 days, plus ~1 signal file/day through drain, plus one PO dedup triage per day. This is the 5th consecutive PO tick spending triage budget on the same finding.
backlog.status_note:
AC — READ THE AMPLIFICATION CAUTION FIRST, IT INVERTS THE OBVIOUS FIX.

(0) DO NOT 'FIX' THE GUARD RELEASE. drain-esc-dispatch.md TERMINAL-EXIT (:116-117) and Step 5 (:140) both call task_release(guard_key) on EVERY exit path, including the GATE-B known-root path. Observation says that release is currently a NO-OP: bctc-analyst c133 found the guard still held at 21:09Z with expiry 21:10:43Z, i.e. it survived its full 86400s TTL from the 07-29T21:10:43Z claim, across ~8 intervening dev-team drain ticks. Candidate mechanism (UNPROVEN, do not assume): the release passes only {task_id}, no owner_agent, while the claim was made by bctc-analyst — the known released:0-orphan class in feedback_task_release_owner_agent_mismatch_orphans_lock. THE POINT: if you 'repair' that release, the guard frees on the very next drain and the loop goes from 1 re-emit/day to 4 re-emits/day. The broken release is currently the ONLY thing bounding this loop. Any fix must make suppression correct BEFORE, or in the same change as, making the release work.

(1) STATE WHICH PLANE YOU ARE FIXING. Two coherent designs, pick one explicitly and say why: (a) CONSUMER-EXTENDS — on a GATE-B Tier 1 known-root hit, re-claim/extend guard_key with a long TTL instead of releasing it, so the producer stays suppressed for as long as the owning board row is open. Cheap, needs no producer change, and works with bctc-analyst's no-Bash constraint. (b) PRODUCER-ASKS — give the producer an MCP-tool-shaped known-root query it CAN call without Bash. More correct, more surface. A third option — widening the producer's TTL — is NOT acceptable: it re-tunes a constant instead of owning the condition, the same anti-pattern called out in FIX-SIGNALQUALITYAUDIT-WRITE-GATE-UNREACHABLE-BY-EMITTER-CONTRACT.

(2) DO NOT SUPPRESS GENUINE CHANGE. Whatever suppresses must re-open when the underlying finding actually changes. Negative control, mandatory: with a known-root row open, an escalation carrying a DIFFERENT refined_at or a DIFFERENT low-confidence unit set must still emit. Suppressing on ticker+trigger_id alone would silently swallow a real regression on the same ticker.

(3) FIX THE FALSIFIED BOARD CLAIM. REFLOW-FPT-Q1-2026's title says minting it stops the 24h re-escalation. Correct it as part of this row, or the next PO re-derives this from scratch for the 6th time.

(4) BIDIRECTIONAL PROOF, on the live signal path, not a fixture. Show (i) zero new docs/signals/bctc-analyst-*.json esc-deep-dive-request for esc-deepdive:FPT:Q1-2026:ESC-5 across at least 2 consecutive bctc-analyst cycles while REFLOW-FPT-Q1-2026 stays open, AND (ii) emission still occurs once that row reaches a TERMINAL_SET status or the finding's inputs change. 'The signal stopped' alone is not proof — it is also what a dead emitter looks like.

(5) Regression test pinning the chosen design, so this cannot revert to board-blind re-emission.

backlog.title: signal_outcomes liveness guard reports 0 = healthy while ZERO rows are being produced — post-GLOB-fix the only outcome-pipeline detector is structurally blind to producer death
backlog.verification_gate: live_runtime_query_after_deploy
backlog.desc: FOUND WHILE TRIAGING telegram reports #4236/#4237 (both RESOLVED as stale pre-deploy false alarms — see status_note). checkStalledResolutionLiveness() (signalOutcomeResolutionJob.ts:80-114) is the ONLY liveness detector on the signal-outcome calibration pipeline. It asks exactly one question: 'how many rows have checked_at IS NULL and created_at older than 72h (and a 3-letter ticker code)?'. That predicate is monotone in ROW EXISTENCE — it can only be non-zero if rows are actually being created. LIVE STATE read from the running container 2026-07-31T15:5xZ (docker exec vn-market-intelligence-mcp-mcp-server-1, readonly bun:sqlite on /app/data/market.db): 105 rows total, 103 resolved, the 2 unresolved are the known-structural MACRO (2026-06-06) + MULTI (2026-06-25) pseudo-codes, MAX(checked_at) = 2026-07-26 00:17:00, and ZERO rows created in the 5 days since. So the guard now returns 0 and reports HEALTHY at the precise moment the pipeline is deadest — the classic passive-health / dead-detector shape (feedback_passive_health_masks_dead_data, feedback_composite_score_masks_dead_detector_pruned_table). Note this is a SECOND-ORDER consequence of the correct fix 314e70718 (FIX-SIGNAL-OUTCOMES-LIVENESS-GUARD-COUNTS-STRUCTURALLY-UNRESOLVABLE-ROWS, now in review[]): before it, the MACRO/MULTI rows kept the count at 2, which by accident made the guard fire daily and kept the subsystem visible. Excluding them was right, but it removed the last thing making noise, so nothing is left to notice that record_signal_outcome has stopped emitting entirely. backlog.title: docs/agents/po/flow/main.md:30 declares zone MUST be one of {apps/<service>/, multi, cross-service/} and that a missing zone gets the batch rejected — but 256/659 open board rows (38.8%) carry a zone outside that enum and 3 carry none, so the stated contract is not the one the board actually runs on
backlog.desc:
MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-01T04:36Z across the five open lanes (backlog/ready/in_progress/review/qa), not sampled: open_rows=659, conforming=400, null_zone=3, NON-CONFORMING=256 (38.8%). Conformance predicate used is main.md:30's own enum, verbatim: zone == "multi" or zone == "cross-service/" or zone matches ^apps/[a-z0-9-]+/$.

THREE DISTINCT DEFECT CLASSES INSIDE THE 256 — they need different remedies and should not be lumped:
(A) NEAR-MISS PUNCTUATION on an otherwise valid zone — `apps/mcp-server` (14 rows, no trailing slash) alongside a conforming `apps/mcp-server/` (141 rows); also `apps/technical-analysis` (5), `apps/stock-price` (4), `apps/macro-indicators` (4), `apps/pdf-extractor` (3), `apps/vps-scripts` (1), and `cross-service` (6, no slash) beside `cross-service/`. This is the dangerous class: any consumer doing string equality or a prefix test anchored on the trailing slash silently splits one zone into two populations, and the split is invisible because both spellings look right at a glance.
(B) BARE SERVICE NAME, prefix missing entirely — `mcp-server` (9), `dev-mcp-server` (7), `stock-price` (6), `alert-engine` (5), `kinh-dich-service` (4), `api-gateway` (3), `frontend` (3), `news-fetch` (3), `pdf-extractor` (3), `technical-analysis` (3), `rag-service` (2), `macro-indicators` (1).
(C) PATH-SHAPED PSEUDO-ZONES that are not services at all — `docs/agents/` (36), `docs/agents/dev-team/flow/` (14), `docs/agents/system-auditor/` (10), `scripts/` (9), `.claude/skills/` (8), plus a long tail of one-off doc paths, and sub-service pseudo-zones `mcp-server-domain`/`-infra`/`-application`/`-interface`/`-scheduler` (6/5/4/3/2). A handful are not even single values — `apps/mcp-server/ + flow-docs/`, `vps-scripts + apps/mcp-server (fetch-pipeline design)`, `docs/data/system-map.json + docs/architecture-briefs`, `agent-father / docs/data/cowork-schedule.json`.

WHY THIS IS A REAL CONTRACT PROBLEM AND NOT COSMETIC BOOKKEEPING: main.md:30 states 'dev-team Step 3 reads this field; missing zone = batch rejected back to PO'. If that were enforced as written, 259 of 659 open rows could not be dispatched. They evidently are being dispatched, so either the consumer is more permissive than the contract (the contract is wrong and should be widened + normalised) or the consumer is quietly mis-routing class (A)/(B) rows (the rows are wrong and must be normalised). Both are actionable; which one is true is the first thing to determine, and it must be determined by reading dev-team Step 3's actual zone handling, not by assuming.

CLASS (C) IS THE DESIGN QUESTION, not a typo sweep: agent-flow and skill work is a genuine, high-volume category of task on this board that the three-value enum has no slot for. 'cross-service/' is documented as 'genuine root/scripts work — routes to generic developer', which is a poor fit for docs/agents/* work whose correct next_agent is agent-father. So the enum probably needs a fourth member rather than 100+ rows being force-fitted; that is an architecture call, hence next_agent=architect.

PROVENANCE — deferred four consecutive ticks before this mint, and re-encountered live: PO's own notebook Carry-over has carried 'zone-enum conflict (docs/agents/ vs main.md:30)' as still-owed for four ticks, with the 2026-08-01T03:55Z entry explicitly resolving to 'past my own stated mint threshold, mint it next tick rather than re-noting it'. It is minted now with a measurement attached rather than re-noted a fifth time. Re-encountered concretely this tick: FIX-PO-TRIAGE-SIGNALS-TABLE-MATCHES-ZERO-LIVE-SIGNAL-TYPES, the row selected by the manual-dispatch sweep, carries zone 'docs/agents/' — so building its BATCH entry from its own fields (which manual-dispatch-sweep.md Step 3 mandates) emits a zone main.md:30 says must be rejected.
backlog.ac: AC-1: the discrepancy is RESOLVED IN ONE DIRECTION, explicitly, after reading dev-team Step 3's real zone handling — either main.md:30's enum is widened (and every other doc stating the three-value enum updated in lockstep) or the non-conforming rows are normalised; a decision that leaves both the doc and the 256 rows unchanged is not acceptance. AC-2: classes (A) and (B) are normalised regardless of the AC-1 direction — trailing-slash and missing-apps/-prefix variants are pure data errors under any enum, and the `apps/mcp-server` vs `apps/mcp-server/` split in particular must be collapsed. AC-3: a guard exists that prevents silent re-drift — a zone-shape check in scripts/orch-validate.mjs (REPORT-level is acceptable, it need not be fatal) or an equivalent audit script, so the next 256 cannot accumulate unobserved. AC-4: the multi-value zone strings (`apps/mcp-server/ + flow-docs/` and the three others listed in desc) are resolved to a single value or to `multi`. AC-5: the 3 null-zone open rows are given a zone or explicitly exempted.

Assert `apps/mcp-server` and `apps/mcp-server/` no longer coexist as distinct values. Assert the AC-3 guard actually fires on a deliberately malformed candidate row — a guard that never rejects anything is not a guard.

backlog.title: Live /api/cron-status serves a stale 4-file layer_b view — process-lifetime memo with no TTL cached the deleted-cron-docs window
backlog.source: PO triage 2026-08-05 — collateral of the cron-doc deletion window 06:20-07:06Z
backlog.root_cause: docker-compose.yml:26 bind-mounts ./.claude/commands/crons into mcp-server read-only at /app/.claude/commands/crons, and layerBCronRegistry.ts parses it to build the Layer-B half of GET /api/cron-status (the dashboard Cron Recheck Table). getLayerBCronRows() memoizes into a module-level `_cachedRows` (layerBCronRegistry.ts:137-152) that is populated once and has NO TTL and NO invalidation — only the test-only reset hook clears it. Between ~06:20Z and 07:06Z on 2026-08-05, 12 of the 16 cron docs plus .claude/commands/dev-team.md were deleted from the working tree; the memo was filled during that window. PO restored all 13 files from HEAD at 07:06Z and the container now sees 16 files (docker exec ls confirms), but the API still returns layer_b length 7 — the stale memo survives the file restore.
backlog.evidence: Before restore: docker exec ls /app/.claude/commands/crons -> 4 files; curl /api/cron-status -> layer_b length 7 (cron-cowork-team, cron-dev-team, cron-market-watcher#1..#3, cron-orch-sentinel#1..#2). After restore: docker exec ls -> 16 files; curl -> STILL 7. Cache confirmed, not a file problem. Note apps/mcp-server/src/__tests__/layerBCronRegistry.test.ts AC-12 and cronStatusHandler.test.ts AC-12 both assert '13 live files' against the real tree — those would have gone RED during the deletion window, and the hardcoded 13 is itself a NO-HARDCODE violation worth folding in.
ac: AC-1 ops: restart ONLY vn-market-intelligence-mcp-mcp-server-1 to flush the memo, then curl /api/cron-status and assert layer_b length matches the parse of all 16 files. Single-service restart per memory feedback_rebuild_after_dev_change — never `docker compose down && up`, which kills peers. Do it in a quiet window: 4 live CLI agent sessions currently route every gateway call through this container.

AC-2 Decide whether a process-lifetime memo over a bind-mounted doc dir is the right design at all. It means any cron-doc edit is invisible to the dashboard until the next container restart, which silently backdates the operator's view. A cheap mtime check or a short TTL would close it; if the memo is kept deliberately, say so in the handler doc so the next person does not read a stale table as ground truth.

AC-3 Replace the hardcoded '13 live files' expectation in both AC-12 tests with a count derived from the directory (or from system-map.json), so the suite tracks the real fleet instead of pinning a number that was already wrong twice.

backlog.title: backupDatabase() overwrites the ONLY market.db backup with an unconditional copy and zero pre-copy integrity check — one rotation over an already-corrupting file destroys the last known-good state. Add a quick_check gate + 3-generation rotation.
backlog.created_by: po (triage tick 2026-08-06T12:2xZ — routed from ops's P2 flag in the 2026-08-06 incident report)
backlog.root_cause: backupDatabase() performs an unconditional `Bun.write(dst, src)` onto a single rotating market.db.backup file, with no integrity check on the SOURCE before copying and no generational history. A rotation that happens to run while the live DB is already corrupting silently overwrites the last clean snapshot with a corrupt one. Flagged as §5.4 of the 2026-07-30 architecture brief and re-flagged by ops in the 2026-08-06 incident report; never scoped as a task until now.
backlog.evidence: Near-miss already realised once: the 2026-07-30 incident required a `.recover` salvage precisely because the only backup had already been overwritten (see market.db.impoverished-backup-2026-07-30T08:33:51Z, 16.9MB — a salvage remnant of a 400MB DB). The 2026-08-06 recovery got lucky in the other direction: market.db.backup happened to be clean (quick_check=ok) so a straight restore worked. Luck is the current control.
backlog.impact: P2 — secondary. It did not cause any of the 5 corruptions and did not block this recovery, but it is the difference between 'restore from backup' (2026-08-06, ~6.4h of regenerable telemetry lost) and 'salvage a 400MB DB down to 17MB' (2026-07-30). Given the corruption class is demonstrably recurrent, the backup path is the last line of defence and is currently ungated. PO keeps this at P2 rather than promoting it: it reduces blast radius but does not reduce recurrence, and the two P0 rows do. Deliberately NOT bundled into either P0 — different zone, different owner, and folding a defence-in-depth item into an active-incident fix is how P0s slip.
acceptance: AC-1 pre-copy gate: run a cheap integrity check (PRAGMA quick_check) on the SOURCE before any overwrite. Source fails -> ABORT the rotation, keep the existing backup, and alert the BUG channel. Never overwrite a good backup with a bad source.
AC-2 generational rotation: keep at least 3 generations (market.db.backup.0/.1/.2) instead of one, so a single bad cycle cannot erase all known-good state even if AC-1's check is somehow bypassed.

AC-3 the abort path must be loud, not silent — a backup that silently stops rotating is indistinguishable from one that is working, which is the same unarmed-observer failure as FIX-MARKETDB-JOURNALMODE-GUARD-SHIPPED-BUT-NEVER-ARMED. Emit on both success (with generation + source verdict) and abort.
AC-4 prove it: fixture test with a deliberately corrupted source proving the rotation ABORTS and the prior generation survives byte-identical.
backlog.verification_gate: Fixture run with a corrupt source: rotation aborts, prior generation byte-identical, BUG alert emitted.
backlog.note: Housekeeping observed while triaging, NOT part of this row's scope: /app/data now holds ~14 market.db.* forensic artifacts (corrupt snapshots, pre-salvage copies, impoverished-backup) totalling well over 1.5GB on the same bind mount as the live DB. Prior ENOSPC history (project_enospc_blocker) makes that worth a janitor sweep with an explicit retention policy — route separately, do not absorb here.
backlog.po_fold_20260826T0116Z: PO FOLD 2026-08-26T01:16Z — this row just had its cost demonstrated in production, and its missing datum supplied. THE SINGLE GENERATION WAS CLEAN when it mattered (quick_check ok on data/live/market.db.backup, 2026-08-25T04:30Z), so the 2026-08-26 recovery succeeded. But it was 20 hours STALE, and because it is the ONLY generation there was no fresher clean choice available: the restore therefore dropped 12,205 intraday_foreign_flow_5m rows and 54 evidence_fragments rows (measured — see FIX-MARKETDB-20260826-RESTORE-DROPPED-12205-FF5M-AND-54-EVIDENCE-ROWS-STILL-RECOVERABLE). That is the concrete price of single-generation retention, no longer a hypothetical. Two design implications for whoever builds this. (a) Rotation MUST be gated on a pre-copy integrity check — this row original point, and it remains correct: one rotation over an already-corrupt live db would have destroyed the only escape route on 2026-08-26. (b) ONE generation is not enough even when it is clean, because restore COST scales with staleness — keep N dated generations so the freshest CLEAN one can be chosen rather than merely the only one.

backlog.title: dev-team-tick-preflight.sh DEFAULT_ROOT resolution is CWD-dependent through the apps/mcp-server/{docs,scripts} symlinks — wrong invocation cwd silently redirects git commit to a nested path and fails
backlog.why_this_row_exists: Live-reproduced this tick, not theoretical. dev-team-tick-preflight.sh:170-171 computes DEFAULT_ROOT via `cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd` — bash's cd/pwd are logical (symlink-preserving) by default. apps/mcp-server/docs and apps/mcp-server/scripts are both symlinks to the repo-root docs/ and scripts/ dirs. If the script is invoked (BASH_SOURCE relative) from a cwd under apps/mcp-server, dirname-walking two levels up lands on apps/mcp-server itself instead of the true repo root. Step 5.5's _step55_git_commit_evict then built its pathspec against apps/mcp-server/docs/data/orch/orch-state.json, and git refused it: "fatal: le chemin ... est au-dela d'un lien symbolique" (path is beyond a symbolic link) — the cold-evict write succeeded on disk (both paths resolve to the same physical file) but the commit step failed, leaving 2 files uncommitted in the working tree until manually caught and committed this tick (commit 4db659e30).
backlog.trigger_this_time: This session's Bash tool keeps one persistent shell across turns; an earlier unrelated turn left cwd at apps/mcp-server (via a bare `cd apps/mcp-server && ...` with no return-to-root), and the next dev-team cron tick's preflight inherited that stale cwd. Not yet confirmed whether any non-interactive/fresh-shell cron path can independently reach the same cwd, but the underlying resolution logic is wrong regardless of trigger: it silently produces a different ROOT depending on caller cwd, which a repo-root-anchored script never should.
backlog.scope: Make SCRIPT_DIR/DEFAULT_ROOT resolution symlink- and cwd-invariant, e.g. `cd -P "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd -P` (physical) instead of logical cd/pwd, so it always resolves through the symlink to the canonical repo root regardless of invocation cwd. Audit other scripts sharing the same `$SCRIPT_DIR/../..`-style idiom under scripts/agents-flow/ for the same fragility while in the zone.
backlog.acceptance: Script invoked from repo root, from apps/mcp-server, and from apps/mcp-server/scripts/agents-flow all resolve ROOT to the same canonical repo-root path (verify via `pwd -P` comparison in a test). Existing dev-team-tick-preflight.test.sh suite still green.
backlog.evidence: git commit failure text this tick: "fatal : le chemin '/Users/admin/Documents/Hung/__works__/__PROJET/__labo/VN-Market-Intelligence-MCP/apps/mcp-server/docs/data/orch/orch-state.json' est au-dela d'un lien symbolique"; ls -la apps/mcp-server/docs -> symlink to ../../docs; realpath of both the symlinked and canonical orch-state.json paths match (no content divergence, no data loss — recovered via manual commit 4db659e30).

backlog.title: deriveOrchApplyHelpers() in drain-signals.test.js only throws when it matches ZERO helpers, so PARTIAL regex drift (3 of 4 matched) silently reproduces the exact sandbox crash it was built to prevent
backlog.source: Residual bound recorded by router on FIX-DRAIN-TEST-HARNESS-ORCH-HELPER-COPY-LIST (router_residual_partial_drift_not_caught_20260721T2022, 'ROUTER DID NOT MINT'); minted by PO at that row's DONE_VERIFIED sign-off 2026-08-06T15:46Z so the bound survives the terminal lane move.
backlog.desc: MECHANISM (re-read at source 2026-08-06T15:45Z, still present): scripts/agents-flow/drain-signals.test.js:255-265 derives the sandbox helper-copy list by regex-scanning scripts/orch-apply.sh for /\$\{REPO_ROOT\}\/scripts\/([A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.(?:sh|mjs|js))/g. Its stale-regex guard at 261-263 throws ONLY when found.size === 0. So it catches TOTAL regex rot and is blind to PARTIAL drift: if orch-apply.sh later invokes a helper via $SCRIPT_DIR/, a bare relative path, an interpolated variable, or any other idiom, the derivation returns N-1 of N, the sandbox omits that one file, and orch-apply.sh inside the sandbox crashes at makeOrchRefHarness() exactly as it did before the parent fix — killing every assertion after the first harness block. NOT CURRENTLY BROKEN, and PO verified this twice: git log shows ZERO commits to scripts/orch-apply.sh since a5d079663 (predates the parent fix), and today's ground-truth scan finds exactly 3 live invocations (orch-validate.mjs L136, orch-stamp-updated-at.mjs L159, orch-conservation-check.mjs L179), every other scripts/ mention being a comment (L3,15,17,22,34,38,62,124,146,168). This row exists because the parent's AC-4 asked for the CLASS to be closed and the derivation closes only the dominant idiom.
acceptance: AC-1 Make the guard fail on PARTIAL drift, not only on zero matches: after deriving, independently scan orch-apply.sh's NON-COMMENT lines for any scripts/<name>.<sh|mjs|js> reference and throw if any such reference is absent from the derived set. The second scan must be deliberately broader/dumber than the first (it is the cross-check, not a second copy of the same regex) — a comment-stripping pass plus a loose scripts/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.(sh|mjs|js) match is sufficient. Comment lines MUST be excluded or the guard fires permanently on the 10 documentation mentions listed in desc.

AC-2 Prove BOTH polarities against fixtures, not by inspection: (a) a fixture orch-apply.sh that invokes a 4th helper via a non-matching idiom (e.g. $SCRIPT_DIR/orch-fake.mjs) MUST make the harness throw a named, actionable error; (b) the real repo orch-apply.sh MUST still pass. Without (a) this ships as another guard nobody has seen fire — the exact defect class as FIX-MARKETDB-JOURNALMODE-GUARD-SHIPPED-BUT-NEVER-ARMED.

AC-3 Full suite must remain green and must not shrink: scripts/agents-flow/drain-signals.test.js is 36/36 PASS / exit 0 as of 2026-08-06T15:45Z. Report the post-change count explicitly; a count below 36 means an assertion was lost, not that the change was clean.

AC-4 Do NOT solve this by hardcoding a fallback list or by widening the primary regex to swallow every idiom — both re-create the hand-maintained manifest the parent fix deleted. The invariant to enforce is 'the derived set covers every helper orch-apply.sh actually invokes', and the enforcement is a LOUD THROW, never a silent top-up.

backlog.title: No detector exercises an actual data-SERVING read path — every liveness check probes container health or a DB file, so a service can serve empty/error to 100% of callers indefinitely and every board stays green (kinh-dich dark 6 days undetected; news push silent 11h, alarm fired 1 min before self-recovery)
backlog.desc:
Two independent live outages in 8 days were invisible to the entire detector fleet because NOTHING in the fleet asks a service for real data and checks that the answer is real.

OCC-1 (kinh-dich, 6 days, telegram 4459/4461): stock-price served `/price/history?code=<any>` -> [] and kinh-dich returned 503 'insufficient price data for market reading' for EVERY ticker from 2026-07-31T00:41Z until PO rebuilt the container 2026-08-06T15:59Z. During that entire window: container healthchecks PASS, `docker ps` healthy, and the market-db-journal-guard reported PASS — because it probes the DB FILE's journal_mode, not whether any read path returns rows. 4461's own closing line: 'no detector fired for 6 days. All-tickers insufficient price data is trivially detectable — needs an active read-path probe, not a DB-file probe.'

OCC-2 (news push, 663 min, FIX-NEWSVPS-OVERNIGHT-PUSH-OUTAGE-663M-SILENT): the transport hung 2026-08-05T19:38:29Z -> 2026-08-06T06:42:25Z. Tier-1 B-01 fired at 06:41:27Z — ~1 minute before self-recovery, i.e. 11h into an 11h04m outage. ops's AC-2 recon is correct that no existing detector MIS-behaved: threshold-on-staleness detectors are inherently trailing, so they alarm at threshold-expiry, not at failure onset. That is exactly the structural gap.

ROOT CAUSE (shared): the fleet has container-health probes, DB-file probes, and staleness-threshold probes. It has ZERO probes that call a public read path and assert the RESPONSE IS NON-DEGENERATE. Empty array, 503, and 'database is locked' are all indistinguishable from healthy to every current check. This is the `feedback_passive_health_masks_dead_data` class, now measured at 6-day blast radius.

backlog.verification_gate: replay_both_branches_on_fixture
backlog.desc: OBSERVED LIVE THIS TICK, not derived. docs/agents/po/flow/main.md AC-3 (added by FIX-PO-BATCH-MINT-NO-WRITE-ACTUATOR, currently review[]) instructs: SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD); git show --stat "$SHA" | grep -q docs/data/orch/orch-state.json || send_telegram(channel=bug, FAIL-LOUD: orch-state.json NOT in own commit ...). At 18:59Z this PO tick ran two orch-apply.sh pipes, both OK, then staged its own paths - and git diff --cached showed orch-state.json absent because peer commit 414da5ba2 (chore(orch-state): TE-T05 direct-dispatch to agent-father) had already swept the file into ITS commit seconds earlier. The file was therefore clean vs HEAD and unstageable. Running AC-3 as written would have emitted a bug-telegram asserting the writes had NOT landed, while all four mutations were provably present in HEAD tree: git show HEAD:docs/data/orch/orch-state.json | jq confirmed po_manual_dispatch_flagged_at=2026-08-06T18:57:46Z, occurrence_count=3 + next_agent=developer on the CLEAN row, the decision-journal evidence key, and desc_len=3145 on the filled stub.
backlog.root_cause: The predicate tests the WRONG object. AC-3 exists to prove the writes reached the persistence layer, and its own generic rule states that correctly (any step that writes an artifact AND asserts its own persistence must re-read the persistence layer (git HEAD) before claiming it). But the implementation re-reads the COMMIT AUTHORSHIP (is this path in the stat of the commit I just made) rather than the persistence layer (are my mutations in HEAD tree). Those coincide only when no peer committed the shared hot file between the orch-apply write and this agent commit. On shared main with multiple concurrent sessions that window is routinely lost - see feedback_shared_main_peer_push_sweeps_held_data_commits and feedback_coldevict_bare_commit_sweeps_worker_staged_index for the same sweep behaviour observed from the other side.
backlog.user_impact: False FAIL-LOUD on the bug channel from a routine, correct PO cycle. Two compounding costs: (1) it trains readers to discount AC-3 bug-telegrams, which defeats the gate the parent fix was built to install; (2) the inverse error is worse and also live - a PO tick whose orch-apply genuinely failed but whose commit happened to include an orch-state.json change made by a PEER would PASS the grep and be reported as confirmed. So the predicate is both false-positive and false-negative prone. Every PO tick that mutates the board is exposed.
backlog.fix_spec: Replace the authorship grep with a content assertion against HEAD tree. After the commit, re-read the persistence layer and assert the specific mutation this cycle made is present, e.g. git show HEAD:docs/data/orch/orch-state.json piped to a jq predicate over the id(s) and field(s) this cycle wrote (the same ids already named in the cycle RETURN/journal), not a filename grep. Pass when the mutation is found in HEAD tree regardless of WHICH commit carried it; FAIL-LOUD only when it is genuinely absent. Keep AC-3 mandatory and keep the generic rule prose - only the predicate changes. Note the parent row FIX-PO-BATCH-MINT-NO-WRITE-ACTUATOR is still in review[]: this is its read-side fast-follow, so land it before that row is signed off or the sign-off ratifies a predicate that does not hold.
backlog.ac: AC (replay both branches, no live writes): POSITIVE - fixture where the agent own commit does NOT contain orch-state.json but HEAD tree DOES contain the named mutation, new predicate must PASS and emit no telegram (current predicate FAILS here - this is the live 18:59Z case). NEGATIVE - fixture where the agent own commit DOES contain orch-state.json but the named mutation is absent from HEAD tree (simulating an orch-apply that silently did not land the field), new predicate must FAIL-LOUD (current predicate PASSES here - the dangerous inverse). Both required; a fix that only flips the first branch reintroduces the second.

backlog.title: VnDirect Tier1+Tier2 served path structurally cannot emit a nil Change/ChangePercent -- an unavailable change is served as 0 ("genuine flat day"), violating DSI-INV-1
backlog.desc:
PROVEN 2026-08-06 during PO sign-off of FACTORY-STOCK-vndirect-mapper-tests (ruling: docs/agent-memory/decisions/ruling-20260806T2059Z-vndirect-mapper-tests-po.md).

MECHANISM. apps/stock-price/pkg/infrastructure/fetchers.go declares its inline VnDirect payload struct with Change/PctChange as NON-pointer `float64` -- Tier1 :78-79, Tier2 :182-183. Unmarshalling JSON `null` into a non-pointer float is a documented no-op in encoding/json ("unmarshaling a JSON null into any other Go type has no effect on the value"), so the field silently keeps its zero value. The code then does `change := item.Change` (:89, :193) and returns `Change: &change` (:113-114, :214-215) -- the address of a local, which is structurally NEVER nil. An omitted field behaves identically.

The comment sitting directly above that code at :88 and :192 reads `// DSI-INV-1: use pointers so 0 is distinguishable from nil (unavailable)`. It is false with respect to its own code -- the pointer exists but can never be nil. Classic comment-not-code; do not let the comment convince a reviewer the invariant holds.

CONTRACT BREACHED. pkg/domain/models.go:22-23 -- `Change *float64` with tag json:"change" and the comment `// nil = unavailable, 0 = genuine flat day` (named invariant DSI-INV-1, org-wide, see docs/architecture-briefs/2026-06-05-carry-yield-single-signal-fixture.md). The pointer propagates untouched through pkg/application/usecases.go:76-77 into the served FetchPriceResponse, so the wire response emits `change: 0` where the contract says `change: null`. A consumer cannot distinguish "VnDirect had no change data" from "the stock genuinely closed flat".

MEASURED, not inferred (stdlib-only harness, both struct shapes copied verbatim from the two files, identical input):
  `"change":null`  -> SERVED &0  |  PRIMITIVE nil  -> DIVERGE
  field omitted    -> SERVED &0  |  PRIMITIVE nil  -> DIVERGE
  `"change":0`     -> SERVED &0  |  PRIMITIVE &0   -> agree
Reproduce by unmarshalling those three payloads into (a) the fetchers.go inline struct and (b) the mapper.go struct, then comparing nil-ness of the resulting pointers. The correct shape already exists and is already tested: apps/stock-price/pkg/primitive/vndirect-quote-mapper/mapper.go:30-31 + :116-124, guarded by mapper_test.go cases `null_change_and_pctChange_maps_to_nil_pointers`, `omitted_change_fields_treated_as_nil`, `partial_null_-_only_change_is_null` (all green).

AC-1 ESTABLISH REACHABILITY BEFORE ASSUMING SEVERITY. This row proves the code path cannot emit nil; it does NOT prove VnDirect ever actually sends null or omits the field. Capture real api-finfo.vndirect.com.vn/v4/stock_prices payloads (illiquid/halted/newly-listed tickers and pre-open are the likely shapes) and state with evidence whether null/omitted change occurs live. If it never occurs, say so plainly and downgrade to P3 -- do not quietly close, the struct shape is still wrong and the comment is still false.
AC-2 Fix the served shape so an unavailable change reaches the wire as null, not 0. Preferred: rewire Tier1/Tier2 to call the existing primitive (see FACTORY-STOCK-extract-vndirect-mapper -- ONE rewire closes BOTH rows; do not bill this twice and do not re-create mapper.go). Fallback if that refactor is not taken: change the two inline structs to *float64 and copy-when-non-nil.
AC-3 This is a BEHAVIOUR CHANGE on a served endpoint, not a pure refactor -- an unavailable change flips from `0` to `null` on the wire. Do NOT ship it as invisible. Check every consumer of FetchPriceResponse.Change / .ChangePercent for a bare dereference or a formatter that assumes non-nil, across the Go plane AND any TS/frontend consumer of the JSON, and state what you checked. rebuild_required: a served-path change to a shipped binary -- rebuild stock-price and RAW-verify sample tickers after.
AC-4 Delete or correct the false `// DSI-INV-1: use pointers so 0 is distinguishable from nil` comment at fetchers.go:88 and :192 in the same change.
AC-5 Regression guard on the SERVED path, not on a copy -- the whole point of the row that produced this finding. A test that would have failed before this fix and passes after, exercising the fetcher's own mapping.

DO NOT close by making the primitive match the served path. The primitive is the correct one; models.go documents the contract; reverting it would enshrine the violation and break 3 currently-green tests.

backlog.root_cause: Two counters with different denominators are compared as if they had the same one. scripts/audit-output-contract.sh line ~180 counts '[emit-signal] SKIP-dedup' as signals_posted++ (and signal_queue_rows_written++ and dedup_skipped++). docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/main.md:835 defines the RETURN-headline N as NEW findings only and says verbatim 'dedup-skipped known anomalies do NOT count - they are not new'. V2 and V3 are unaffected because signal_queue_rows_written and dashboard_rows also increment on SKIP-dedup, so those two comparisons are denominator-symmetric; only V4/V5 straddle the new-vs-all boundary.

backlog.title: rebuild-raw-verify-check.sh ATTEST_ERE does not match 'RAW-verified' — the hyphenated PAST-TENSE form that is this repo's dominant attestation idiom (18 of 24 occurrences in the last 400 commit messages) — so the gate false-blocks pushes whose verification genuinely happened and was genuinely attested.
backlog.root_cause: scripts/audits/rebuild-raw-verify-check.sh:115 `ATTEST_ERE='raw-verify|raw verified|realdata'`. The three alternatives cover the hyphenated INFINITIVE ('raw-verify') and the SPACED past tense ('raw verified'), but NOT the hyphenated past tense ('raw-verified'): 'raw-verified' does not contain the substring 'raw-verify' (position 10 is 'i', not 'y') and does not contain 'raw verified' (hyphen != space). `shopt -s nocasematch` is correctly set at :180 and :202, so this is NOT a case-sensitivity bug — casing is already handled; the gap is purely the missing tense/separator combination. Both escape hatches (i) commit-message attestation at :181 and (ii) docs/agent-memory/decisions/**|reports/TASK_REPORT_*.md added-line attestation at :203 share the SAME regex variable, so a single missing alternative closes BOTH escapes simultaneously.
backlog.evidence: MEASURED, not inferred. (a) Predicate replayed verbatim in bash with `shopt -s nocasematch` and the live ERE string: 'RAW-verified' NO-MATCH, 'RAW-VERIFIED' NO-MATCH, 'raw-verified GREEN' NO-MATCH; 'RAW verified' MATCH, 'RAW-verify' MATCH, 'REALDATA' MATCH. (b) CORPUS FREQUENCY over the last 400 commit messages (`git log -400 --format=%B | grep -oiE 'raw[- ]verif(y|ied)' | sort | uniq -c`): RAW-verified=16, raw-verified=2 (18 total, ALL non-matching) vs raw-verify=3, RAW-verify=1, raw verified=1, RAW verified=1 (6 total, matching). So 18/24 = 75% of the attestation phrasings this repo actually writes are invisible to the gate. (c) LIVE INCIDENT: this is the root cause of pendingSignal#3 (fleet-worktree-push auto-push-abort, 2026-08-07T02:47:17Z, ahead=21 threshold=20). The router's remediation was commit 1c26af802, which added a decision-journal line WORDED to contain 'RAW verified' (spaced) — its own commit message states the verification 'genuinely happened (documented in detail in the S76/S77/S78 entries above: docker logs, per-tool log file, DB query, wc -l line counts, test runs) but neither commit message in this range used the exact case-insensitive token the gate's ATTEST_ERE requires'. That is a per-incident WORKAROUND (rephrase until the regex matches), not a fix: the gate is unchanged and will false-block the next agent who writes the idiomatic 'RAW-verified'.
backlog.ac: (AC-1) ATTEST_ERE must match the hyphenated past tense. Prefer collapsing the tense/separator axes rather than appending a 4th literal — e.g. `raw[- ]verif(y|ied)|realdata` — and state in a code comment WHY the axes are collapsed (a literal-list ERE is what shipped the gap; adding one more literal leaves 'rawverify', 'raw-verifying' etc. equally invisible and re-opens the same class). Do NOT weaken it into matching bare 'verified' — the token must stay a deliberate attestation, not an accidental word. (AC-2) REGRESSION TEST, corpus-based not synthetic: assert the new ERE matches every distinct phrasing actually present in the repo's commit-message corpus (derive the list with the uniq -c command in `evidence` (b), do not hand-write it), and assert it still REJECTS a control body containing 'verified' / 'verify' with no raw|realdata qualifier. A fresh-fixture-only test is what let this ship (same class as project memory feedback_fleetwide_gate_validated_on_one_file_optout_allowlist). (AC-3) Prove the live incident is closed: replay the gate over the exact range that aborted (BASE..HEAD spanning the flagged confidence-threshold lines) with commit 1c26af802's journal line REMOVED from consideration, and show it now PASSES on the pre-existing 'RAW-verified' text alone. (AC-4) Grep the fleet for any OTHER gate carrying its own copy of this token list and fix or converge them in the same pass — a second divergent copy is the same defect one file over.

backlog.title: Agents verify 'memory was reclaimed' acceptance criteria by reading a resource meter during the cold-start window, before the lazily-loaded workload has ever loaded — a post-restart low reading is structurally indistinguishable from a post-idle unload unless the load event is checked first; reclamation-class ACs need a mandatory load-event precondition and a log-line (not meter) primary discriminator
backlog.trigger_this_time: OPS-RAG-SERVICE-REBUILD-STALE-IMAGE-PREDATES-IDLE-UNLOAD-FIX was flipped DONE at 2026-08-08T08:12:36Z on a false AC-3. The agent ran a REAL docker stats call against the RIGHT container and got a REAL number (39.13MiB / 3.82% at t+12s post-restart), then declared 'AC-3 RECLAMATION VERIFIED — idle-unload mechanism is now active and working'. Every element of that measurement was valid except WHEN it was taken: apps/rag-service/infrastructure/embedder.py:64-72 makes initialize() a documented no-op (GFD-13 lazy-load), so the ~400MB model had not loaded yet. 39MiB was the pre-load floor, not a reclaimed footprint. Its own FINAL VERIFICATION 55s later read 98.66% and was never reconciled against the verdict.
backlog.why_this_row_exists: MINTED because this is a NEW sub-class not covered by the existing self-verification lessons, and the distinction is what makes it worth a row. The known lessons all cover an agent that DID NOT MEASURE (feedback_agent_selfreport_metalayer_confabulation, feedback_empty_read_is_not_evidence_confirm_tool_targets_store) or that MEASURED THE WRONG OBJECT (feedback_auditor_memory_pct_denominator_falsespike wrong denominator, feedback_fix_landed_in_the_pregate_not_the_probe wrong probe, feedback_reader_writes_its_own_trigger_field vacuous check). None covers MEASURED THE RIGHT OBJECT WITH THE RIGHT TOOL AT A TIME WHEN THE READING CANNOT CARRY THE CLAIMED MEANING. Existing guards are all object-identity guards; none is a lifecycle-phase guard, so none of them fires here. Note also that the inverse error is live in the same incident: signal router-20260808T081544-falseac3 read the flat ~98% line at t+2m44s as proof the unload mechanism is broken, when the 15-minute threshold simply had not elapsed. Same defect, mirrored — which is the strongest argument that the missing guard is temporal, not directional.
backlog.scope: Design a reclamation-class AC authoring rule and land it where AC text is written and where AC verdicts are issued. Three concrete requirements the design must satisfy: (1) MANDATORY LOAD-EVENT PRECONDITION — any AC of the form 'resource X drops after event Y' must first assert the evidence that X was ever ALLOCATED in the current process lifetime; for a lazily-loaded service the admissible evidence is the load log line, not elapsed time. (2) LOG-LINE-OVER-METER — where the code emits an explicit event on the state transition (here embedder.py:144 'Embedding model unloaded after %.0fs idle'), that log line is the PRIMARY discriminator and the resource meter is secondary corroboration; a meter alone cannot separate 'transition fired but allocator kept the pages' from 'transition never fired'. (3) ELAPSED-TIME FLOOR — an AC that mandates waiting N minutes cannot be satisfied by an agent whose total runtime is under N minutes; this is mechanically checkable from the task's own AC text against the agent's start/finish stamps, and here would have caught it outright (AC-3 demanded 15 minutes, the whole task ran ~4.3 minutes). Requirement (3) is the cheapest and most general of the three and should be considered for a standalone gate even if (1)/(2) stay advisory.
backlog.acceptance: AC-1 the rule is written into the AC-authoring standard that agents actually read (architect to identify the live SSOT — docs/standards/ or the dev-team/qa flow verdict step; do NOT assume a path, verify it is loaded at verdict time). AC-2 the elapsed-time-floor check is specified precisely enough to be implemented as a script, including where the agent start/finish stamps are read from. AC-3 the rule is demonstrated against THIS incident: applying it to OPS-RAG-SERVICE-REBUILD-STALE-IMAGE-PREDATES-IDLE-UNLOAD-FIX's original AC-3 must reject the ops agent's 08:12:36Z evidence, and applying it to the corrected AC-3 protocol on that row must accept a Branch A result. AC-4 the rule must NOT reject Branch B/C outcomes as failures — it distinguishes 'mechanism did not fire' from 'mechanism fired but the meter did not move', per that row's four named branches.

The canonical grammar already EXISTS and is literal with zero free-text slots — docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/tier1-probe.md:300 mandates dedup_key = 'microservice_degraded:<service_id>:<A-xx>' for the general A-xx emit site; main.md:598 mandates 'data_stale:<source_id>:<B-xx>'; main.md:951 mandates 'db_integrity_breach:<table>:<C-xx>'. But the caller composing that JSON is an LLM, and nothing between it and the ledger enforces the template. Two independent drift axes observed, both narrative-driven: (AXIS-1) the type token is swapped for a topical synonym — mem_pressure / memory_pressure / microservice_memory_degraded all substituted for canonical microservice_degraded; (AXIS-2) a free-text severity/narrative suffix is appended INSIDE the check-id slot — A-30-floor-breach, A-30-loss-of-reclamation, A-30-recurring-ceiling, A-30-post-fix-monitoring. Every variant is a fresh key in docs/data/auditor-dedup-ledger.json, so _ledger_prune_and_lookup() finds no prior entry and DEDUP_OUTCOME is 'OK' (fresh emit + BUG Telegram) instead of 'SKIP-dedup'. THE 7-DAY DEDUP WINDOW — the entire mechanism whose job is to stop re-alerting a known finding — IS DEFEATED BY CONSTRUCTION on every drifted key. This is not a cosmetic/bookkeeping defect.

The 09:35Z cycle was directly, explicitly briefed by the router's spawn prompt to search for and converge onto an existing key before minting, and it minted variant #9 regardless. Per feedback_recurring_detection_vs_recurring_failed_fix and the project's fix-the-root-cause rule, the fix belongs at the choke point.

backlog.title: Review-Lane QA-Drain has no task_id-level claim — two live dev-team sessions each dispatched a full QA cycle for the same row (SYSREMAKE-P2-T2, ~185K tokens burned for zero new information)
backlog.status_note:
AC: two concurrent runs of the QA-Drain claim path against the same eligible review[] row result in exactly ONE qa dispatch. Regression proof required: drive scripts/devteam-review-claim-qa-drain.jq twice with two distinct owner_client_session values against one fixture row and assert the second run returns an empty batch (row skipped, not merely CAS-losing after the spawn already happened).

PREMISE VERIFIED AT SOURCE by po before minting (not accepted on the reporter's word): grep of scripts/devteam-review-claim-qa-drain.jq returns claimed_at/claimed_by board stamps ONLY (lines ~174-175, 'claimed_by: "dev-team (review-lane qa-drain)"') and ZERO task_claim call. Confirmed: the script's entire mutual exclusion is a board-field CAS that lands AFTER the dispatch decision, so it can only detect a collision retroactively, never prevent one.

EVIDENCE (live, materialized 2026-08-08): a QA-Drain batch (TAKE_BUDGET=6, claimed 18:53:13Z) selected SYSREMAKE-P2-T2-SCHEMA-ADDITIONS and dispatched qa. That agent ran a FULL independent verify-committed cycle to completion (120/120 + 8/8 + 14/14 + 29/29 + 75/75 re-runs, grandfather-set re-derivation, mock-guard, tsc) and only discovered on write-attempt that a peer QA session had already committed the identical close-out (9c6feb8f2 board move + 8c9a1d24a notebook/journal) for the same task_id and the same commit under review. Cost: 184,693 tokens / 78 tool calls / ~10.5 min for zero net new information. Zero writes were made by the loser — the waste is the duplicate CYCLE, not corruption.

ROOT CAUSE: the only locks in the path are the dispatch-wrapper's outer PRE-CLAIM (intent:dev-team:<intent>) and the per-tick fire-election lock (cron:dev-team:<TICK>). Neither is task_id-scoped, so two live dev-team dispatcher sessions both read review[] pre-claim state, both select the same row (status==REVIEW, next_agent==qa, no claimed_at), and both spawn before either orch-apply.sh CAS write becomes visible to the other.

REQUESTED FIX (from the reporter, and po concurs): take task_claim(task_id="task:<row id>", task_kind="task", owner_client_session=$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, ttl_seconds=<qa runtime ceiling, observed ~10.5min — do not set 600s blindly, see feedback_preclaim_ttl_600s_expires_under_long_agent_runs>) PER CANDIDATE ROW, BEFORE stamping claimed_at/claimed_by, and drop any row whose claim is already held by a different session. Mirrors the published:<slot>:<date> per-slot dedup gate that already protects cowork's guaranteed daily slots.

IMPLEMENTER CONSTRAINTS — read these, they are not optional: (1) a held lock is a NO-OP, not an error — use task_heartbeat on re-entry rather than re-claiming (feedback_task_claim_held_lock_noop_use_heartbeat). (2) On release, owner_agent MUST match the claiming agent or the lock orphans (feedback_task_release_owner_agent_mismatch_orphans_lock). (3) The claim must wrap the SELECTION, not just the stamp — a lock taken after the spawn decision reproduces the exact bug being fixed. (4) Do NOT serialize the whole drain behind one global lock: QA-Drain's batch throughput (QA_CAP=10/TAKE_BUDGET) exists because the review[] lane was the fleet's bottleneck (FIX-DEVTEAM-REVIEW-LANE-QA-DRAIN, review[]=185 vs qa[]=9 today) — per-ROW locks only. (5) scripts/devteam-review-claim-secondary-drain.jq shares this shape and is listed in files[] — check it for the same gap in the same pass rather than leaving a sibling hole.

SCOPE: this is the DISPATCH-side half of a two-session concurrency problem that also has a COMMIT-side half — the same two-live-session condition produced this tick's first confirmed-genuine sweep-guard SAME-FILE DIVERGENCE on orch-state.json (peer QA closeouts swept into another actor's pathspec-scoped commit; see FIX-SWEEPGUARD-ESCALATION-HAS-NO-ACTUATOR-REPEAT-OFFENDER-13-STRIKES occurrence log). Fixing this row does not fix that one; they are related, not duplicates.

OCCURRENCE: first observed instance, escalated on occurrence #1 by explicit standing guidance in memory project_peer_cowork_dispatcher_session_collision_20260801 ('if seen, escalate immediately as a HIGH signal to po given the corruption/waste potential') — this is that predicted residual risk materializing in a new subsystem. backlog.title: manual-dispatch-sweep: deliberate SKIP writes po_manual_dispatch_skipped_at but flag_reentrant only reads po_manual_dispatch_flagged_at — skipped row re-ranks #1 every tick and starves the sweep single-selection slot

backlog.status_note:
LIVE-MEASURED THIS TICK. manual-dispatch-sweep.md Step 1 excludes a candidate only via `flag_reentrant`, which reads exactly one field: `po_manual_dispatch_flagged_at`. But a PO that DELIBERATELY SKIPS a top candidate (correct behaviour — prior-art-suspect, needs AC-level verify not dispatch) writes `po_manual_dispatch_skipped_at` + `po_manual_dispatch_skipped_reason` instead. Those two fields are read by NOTHING. Consequence: the skipped row stays permanently unflagged and re-ranks #1 on every subsequent tick, monopolising Step 2 (which selects exactly ONE row per invocation) forever. PROOF: TASK-COWORK-MUTEX-001 (P0, rank 0, BACKLOG-XOR-GAP) was skipped at 2026-08-08T16:06:57Z with a full documented reason; re-running Step 1 verbatim at 2026-08-08T20:56Z — 4h50m later, past the 14400s staleness window — still returns it as candidate[0] with reflag:false. Live field census: 1 row carries skipped_at, 5 carry flagged_at; the 1 skipped row is the P0 that outranks all 5. So the sweep has produced ZERO new selections since 16:06Z. AC: after a PO records a skip, the NEXT tick Step 1 run must return a DIFFERENT top candidate. Candidate fixes: (a) widen flag_reentrant to `(.po_manual_dispatch_flagged_at // .po_manual_dispatch_skipped_at // "")`, or (b) make the documented skip path write flagged_at too. Prefer (a) — keeps the audit distinction between skipped and dispatched while making both suppress re-selection. Same `documented consumer, no documented producer` family as this sub-flows own origin row FIX-PO-NO-PRODUCER-FOR-MANUAL-DISPATCH-ESCAPE-HATCH (REVIEW), one layer down: here the producer writes a field no consumer reads.

TASK-COWORK-MUTEX-001 carries po_manual_dispatch_skipped_at=2026-08-08T16:06:57Z with reason 'prior-art-suspect: deliverable appears live in CLAUDE.md + .claude/skills/dispatch-claim/{CARD,SKILL}.md; needs AC-level verify, not dispatch'. backlog.title: GET /api/cron-status Layer-A misreports 23 healthy crons as MISSED/STALE every weekend: classifyCronLiveness() ignores the expected_last_fire it already computes and ladders on raw age vs cadence; Layer-A also enumerates the CRONS config table instead of the registered scheduler table
backlog.root_cause: apps/mcp-server/src/domain/cron/cronLivenessClassifier.ts classifyCronLiveness(nowMs, lastFireMs, cadenceMs, thresholdMultiplier) is a pure age ladder (ON_TIME<=cadence, LATE<=cadence*mult, MISSED<=cadence*3, else STALE) — FR-1.6 verbatim. cronStatusCompute.ts computes expected_last_fire / expected_next_fire per row via cron-parser and ships them in the payload, but NEVER feeds them to the classifier (line ~339 passes only cadenceMs+thresholdMultiplier). For any job whose cron restricts day-of-week or hour-of-day, real inter-fire gap != cadenceMs: '*/10 2-8 * * 1-5' has cadenceMs=10min but a Fri-08:50 -> Mon-02:00 gap of 65h, so every such job is GUARANTEED to classify STALE/MISSED every single weekend. Four further defects compound it: (b) expected_last_fire/expected_next_fire are computed in UTC ignoring each job's options.timezone, so all Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh jobs are skewed exactly 7h (morningBriefing/alertDigest/eveningSummary all show delta -25198..-25199s); (c) cron-parser applies POSIX dom/dow OR semantics while node-cron@3.0.3 TimeMatcher.match() ANDs all six fields, so brokerSanctionsSweep '0 8 25-31 * 5' gets expected_last_fire=2026-08-07 (a Friday not in 25-31) instead of its real 2026-07-31 fire; (d) Layer-A enumerates cronConfig.ts CRONS keys and name-joins <key>Job, so config keys with no registration are reported dead forever (taAlertScan/bbAlertScan last_fire 2026-04-24 — they were merged into the registered alertScanParallelJob at schedulerJobTable.ts:447-458, which itself never appears in Layer-A because it has no CRONS key of its own), and env-gated-off registrations are reported dead (ragFtsRebuildCron, CRON_RAG_FTS_REBUILD_ENABLED default-false, schedulerJobTable.ts:132-140,673-681, deliberate per ALPHA-S2-RAG-FTS-CRON-SAFETY-GATE).
backlog.evidence: LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-08-09T02:45Z against http://localhost:3000/api/cron-status (layer_a_count=90; 57 ON_TIME, 12 MISSED, 8 STALE, 4 LATE, 9 NEVER_FIRED). Per-row delta (last_fire minus the endpoint's OWN expected_last_fire) for all 24 non-ON_TIME/non-NEVER_FIRED rows: 15 rows delta in [0s,+2s] — i.e. the job fired EXACTLY on its own computed schedule and was still labelled MISSED or STALE (vpsProxyWatchdog 0s STALE, foreignFlowAlert 0s MISSED, franceSummary +2s MISSED, taAlertNotifier +1s STALE, signalOutcomeJob +1s MISSED, ohlcvDailyAggregator 0s LATE, ohlcvStalenessCheck 0s MISSED, priceUpdateWatchdog +1s STALE, vnIndexRefresh +1s STALE, marketEarningYield +1s MISSED, alertOutcomeJob +1s MISSED, vnstockTradingStatsRefresh +1s MISSED, breadthHistoryPersister 0s MISSED, ohlcvSanityCheck 0s LATE, ohlcvSanityCheckEarly +2s MISSED); 3 rows delta exactly -7h = timezone skew, fired on time in Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh (morningBriefing, alertDigest, eveningSummary); 1 row dom/dow-semantics skew (brokerSanctionsSweep, real last fire 2026-07-31 08:00:01, real next fire 2026-08-28 not the reported 2026-08-14); 2 rows merged-job name-join (taAlertScan/bbAlertScan); 1 row deliberate env-gate (ragFtsRebuildCron); 1 benign sub-cadence jitter (intelligenceCycle -898s LATE); leaving exactly ONE genuine gap in the whole set (monthlySignalQualityAudit, already tracked by FIX-MONTHLYSIGNALQUALITYAUDITJOB-MISSED-JULY-RECOVER-GUARD).
backlog.refuted_premise: This row REPLACES, not corroborates, the escalated container-crash narrative. system-auditor Tier-2 reported 23/90 crons 'stopped firing simultaneously at 2026-08-07T08:50:00Z, 41.6h overdue'; ops (docs/agent-memory/notebooks/ops.md, commit 02b456b4d) concluded HIGH CONFIDENCE that the mcp-server container died at that exact instant and that node-cron cannot replay across a restart. The node-cron claim is TRUE at source (node-cron@3.0.3 src/scheduler.js re-seeds lastExecution=timeMatcher.apply(new Date()) inside start(), so recovery only ever walks back the in-process event-loop stall since the last 1s tick — never anything before process start), but it is IRRELEVANT here because no crash occurred. Refutation from the same cron_job_runs data ops read: marketEarningYield fired 2026-08-07 09:30:01 (40 min AFTER the alleged death), alertDigest 14:00:01, ohlcvDailyAggregator 15:03:00, ohlcvSanityCheck 15:05:00, eveningSummary 15:30:01 — the process was alive and firing all Friday. 08:50 is simply the last slot of the '*/10 2-8 * * 1-5' market-hours window on a Friday; ops's own notebook states 'next scheduled fires would have been 09:00+ UTC (outside market-hours window for these jobs), so wouldn't fire anyway' and 'weekday-only jobs correctly did NOT fire on Sat/Sun', which already contradicts the crash conclusion in the same paragraph. Docker corroborates: the running container has RestartCount=0, FinishedAt=0001-01-01 (never exited), StartedAt=2026-08-08T19:06:16Z — a deliberate ops rebuild/recreate for the separate scheduler double-registration fix, not a crash-restart.
backlog.acceptance_criteria: AC-1: classification is schedule-derived — a job whose last_fire >= its own expected_last_fire (minus a documented grace, e.g. 120s) classifies ON_TIME regardless of wall-clock age; the age ladder survives ONLY as the fallback when the cron expression is unparseable, and that fallback must be labelled as such in .reason. AC-2: expected_last_fire/expected_next_fire honour each job's registered options.timezone — regression asserts morningBriefing/alertDigest/eveningSummary expected fires land at 01:00/14:00/15:30 UTC, not 08:00/21:00/22:30 UTC. AC-3: dom/dow matching mirrors node-cron TimeMatcher AND-semantics, not cron-parser POSIX OR — regression asserts brokerSanctionsSweep next fire = 2026-08-28. AC-4: Layer-A is enumerated from the REGISTERED job table (buildJobTable + registerBespokeJobs), not from CRONS keys — alertScanParallelJob appears, taAlertScan/bbAlertScan do not appear as separate dead rows, and env-gated-off registrations (ragFtsRebuildCron) report a distinct DISARMED status, never STALE. AC-5: replay the 2026-08-09T02:45Z snapshot through the fixed classifier — exactly one row (monthlySignalQualityAudit) may remain non-ON_TIME; any of the other 23 still flagged is a fail. AC-6: a weekend-clock regression test pins now=Sunday and asserts zero MISSED/STALE among the weekday-windowed jobs.
