backlog.title: orch-apply.sh advertises dup-key validation but does not check duplicate task ids in task_board lane arrays — 2 ids live, one duplicated INSIDE ready[] with divergent priority + next_agent (SSOT split, first-match consumers non-deterministic)
backlog.desc:
CLAUDE.md and docs/policies/dev-standards.md CANONICAL:SSOT-W1-ORCH-APPLY-WRAPPER both advertise that scripts/orch-apply.sh "Validates (Zod + dup-key)". Live counter-example found by PO triage 2026-08-11: the dup-key check does not cover duplicate task ids inside or across .task_board lane arrays, so two ids are currently duplicated on the hot board and every orch-apply pipe run over them (including this tick's own three) validated PASS.

EVIDENCE (jq over docs/data/orch/orch-state.json, group_by(.id) on every lane array):
  (1) FIX-ACTIVE-READPATH-LIVENESS-PROBE-NO-DETECTOR — 2 rows, CROSS-lane:
      backlog: status=BACKLOG priority=P1 next_agent=developer created_at=2026-08-06T17:39:33Z
      ready:   status=READY   priority=P1 next_agent=(absent) created_at=2026-08-06T00:00:00Z
  (2) FIX-NEWSVPS-OVERNIGHT-PUSH-OUTAGE-663M-SILENT — 2 rows, BOTH INSIDE ready[] (worse case):
      ready[a]: status=READY priority=P2 next_agent=(absent)        created_at=2026-08-06T00:00:00Z updated_at=2026-08-06T17:58:36Z
      ready[b]: status=READY priority=P1 next_agent=dev-mcp-server  created_at=2026-08-06T08:24:43Z updated_at=2026-08-06T17:39:34Z

WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC: case (2) is an SSOT split, not a harmless copy — the two rows disagree on priority AND on next_agent. Every board consumer in this repo resolves an id with a first-match idiom (`map(select(.id == $tid)) | first`, used verbatim in docs/agents/dev-team/flow/main.md WF-2, docs/agents/po/flow/supervised-goahead.md Step 1, and scripts/lib/devteam-eligibility.jq's callers), so which of the two rows a gate sees is decided by array position — i.e. by whichever writer last appended. A supervised/plan_only/po_goahead stamp written onto one copy is invisible to a reader that resolves the other, which is the exact vacuous-gate shape those flows exist to prevent. Case (1) additionally means one id is simultaneously BACKLOG and READY, so the same task can be promoted twice.

FIX DIRECTION (not a spec, the implementer decides): extend the existing validator stage in scripts/orch-apply.sh (or orchStateSchema.ts, wherever the dup-key stage lives) with a lane-row identity check — collect .task_board[<array lanes>][].id, fail loud on any id with count > 1, both within a single lane and across lanes. Precedent for the shape already exists in the same script: the conservation-check stage already prints `signal_row_identity=clean`, i.e. row-identity checking is an established pattern here for .signal_queue.rows[] but was never extended to task rows.

SEQUENCING: land the guard FIRST, then de-duplicate the 2 live ids — de-duplicating first leaves the hole open and the board will silently re-acquire duplicates.

AC: (1) a synthetic fixture with a duplicated id inside one lane is REJECTED by orch-apply.sh with a non-zero exit and a message naming the id and both lane paths; (2) same for an id duplicated across two lanes; (3) a clean board still PASSes (negative control); (4) the 2 live duplicates above are resolved to one row each, with the surviving row's priority/next_agent chosen explicitly and recorded, not silently; (5) regression test lives beside the existing orch-apply validator tests, run in the standard suite.
backlog.deliverable: Lane-row identity validation stage in the orch-apply validator (fail-loud, names the id + both lane paths), landed BEFORE de-duplicating the 2 live ids; regression fixture with in-lane dup, cross-lane dup, and a clean negative control.
backlog.source: po triage 2026-08-11T14:31Z — found by jq group_by(.id) over every task_board lane array while dup-guarding this tick own mints; three orch-apply pipes this same tick validated PASS over the existing duplicates

backlog.title: Auto-tracked indicator plane stores vnindex as 170468 (=1704.68 x100) while get_macro_snapshot serves 1773.41 tier-1 in the same tick — unit error that the [STALE] label does not disclose; 3 more indicators implausible on the same plane
backlog.desc:
Two data planes disagree by a factor of ~100 on VN-Index, and only one of them is plausibility-gated. Measured live by PO triage in a single tick (2026-08-11T14:29-14:30Z, same container, uptime 9m):

  SERVING PLANE  — get_macro_snapshot: vnIndex = 1773.41, vnIndex_is_estimate=false, vnIndex_source_tier=1, vnIndexDelta=-3.36, direction=down. Correct and honest.
  INDICATOR PLANE — get_system_status "Auto-tracked Indicators": vnindex = 170468, 236 data points, flagged [STALE].

170468 = 1704.68 x 100, i.e. the indicator-plane row is not merely stale, it is stored in the wrong UNIT (index points x100). Staleness labelling does not disclose a unit error: a consumer that correctly honours the [STALE] flag and decides to use the value anyway (or that compares it against a threshold) still gets a number that is wrong by two orders of magnitude, and nothing in the payload says so.

Corroborating evidence that the indicator plane is unhealthy more broadly (same payload, all [STALE]): interest_rate_pct=1 (VN policy rate is ~5%, and get_macro_snapshot's own carry block reports vndDepositRate=5 in the SAME response), inflation_pct=8, gdp_growth_pct=9, wti_crude_usd=95.5 vs the serving plane's oilUsd=87.76 in the same tick. gold_usd_oz=4451.2 vs serving 4446.60 is the only near-agreeing pair. So the vnindex x100 is the sharpest instance of a plane that is generally divergent, not a lone typo.

ALSO IN SCOPE (same tick, likely same plane): get_system_status "Recent System Errors" shows `[get_macro_snapshot] vnIndex plausibility gate fired` twice (14:21:26Z, 14:27:56Z) while get_macro_snapshot's OWN served vnIndex was fine. Determine what input tripped that gate — if the gate is reading the x100 indicator-plane value as a candidate, the two findings are one defect and the gate is currently the only thing standing between the x100 value and a published MARKET number (memory: feedback_usdvnd_frozen_value_labelled_tier1_not_estimate, project_dashboard_two_data_planes).

NOT A DUPLICATE OF: FIX-VNINDEX-ESTIMATE-IMPLAUSIBLE-DELTA-GATE (archive[], CANCELLED) — that row was about a tier-4 fallback ESTIMATE emitting an implausible DELTA and asked for the gate that now demonstrably exists and fires. This row is about the stored indicator VALUE's unit being wrong on a different plane, which that gate does not fix.

AC: (1) identify the writer of economic_indicators.vnindex and state, from source, whether x100 is an intentional storage convention or a bug; (2) if intentional, every read path must divide and the unit must be declared in the column/tool contract — no bare 170468 in any human- or agent-facing output; if a bug, fix the writer AND reflow existing rows (memory: feedback_derived_column_fix_needs_reflow — do not fix the writer and leave 236 corrupt points); (3) get_system_status Auto-tracked Indicators renders vnindex in the same unit get_macro_snapshot serves; (4) explain the two 2026-08-11 vnIndex plausibility-gate fires and, if they trace to this plane, cover them in the same fix; (5) add a cross-plane assertion test: |serving vnIndex - indicator vnindex| within a sane band, failing loud on a 100x divergence.

backlog.title: Guaranteed-slot catch-up is structurally unwinnable for any outage longer than the freshness window — window is measured from SCHEDULED fire time, not from when execution capability returned (0/8 recovery, 2026-08-09 -> 2026-08-11 quota outage)
backlog.evidence_verified_by_po: Live-measured 2026-08-11T18:33Z, not inferred. scripts/agents-flow/cowork-catchup-predicate.js:243-247 computes elapsedMinutes = (nowUnix - scheduledFireUnix)/60 and compares it to _dish_type_catchup_config[dish].catchup_max_lateness_minutes. That clock runs during the outage, so the window burns down while execution is IMPOSSIBLE. Anthropic weekly usage limit was exhausted 2026-08-09T13:17:17Z -> 2026-08-11T12:00:00Z (reset '2pm Europe/Paris', literal CLI stdout captured 12x in docs/agent-memory/sessions/cowork-guaranteed-slot-firer.log:1912,1919,1926,1933,1940,1947,1954,1961,1968,1975,1982,1989,1996,2003). Window-close vs quota-return, all 8 slots due in the outage: chef-morning 08:15Z, chef-eod 11:45Z, fb-daily(08-11) 11:15Z, fb-daily(08-10) 08-10T11:15Z, chef-evening 08-11T01:45Z, tnb-audit 08-11T02:13Z, fb-weekend 08-09T15:13Z, digest-sunday 08-10T13:47Z — every single one closed BEFORE 12:00Z. Recovery rate 0/8. The one slot that did recover (digest-daily, window closes 23:30Z) was never a catch-up case: it was scheduled at 17:30Z, AFTER quota returned, and fired normally. fb-daily's window closed at 11:15Z, 45 minutes before execution became possible again — yet 5 further hours of working quota remained inside the same VN date (rollover 17:00Z) during which the post was still correctly dated and fully recoverable.
backlog.note: NET EFFECT: the COWORK-GUARANTEED-SLOT-CATCHUP epic, as specified, cannot recover any outage that lasts longer than the dish's own freshness window — which is precisely the outage class it was built for (session death, host sleep, quota exhaustion are all multi-hour). It only recovers outages shorter than 2-6h. AC (proposed, architect/BA to ratify): (1) the eligibility clock must be gated on EXECUTION CAPABILITY, not wall-clock alone — track a 'capability_returned_at' (first successful claude invocation after a run of failures; the firer already has the exit-code signal it needs) and start the lateness budget from max(scheduled_fire, capability_returned_at); (2) keep the VN-date rollover rule ABSOLUTE and unchanged — it is correct and must still veto (docs/data/orch/orch-state.json .sprint_goal entry COWORK-GUARANTEED-SLOT-CATCHUP scope_in: 'if the VN day rolled past the slot window, DO NOT retro-post under a new date'), so a recovered dish is only ever published under its own true date; (3) dedup unchanged — published:<slot_id>:<key_part> task_claim marker still arbitrates; (4) regression test: simulate a 48h capability gap and assert a same-VN-date slot IS recovered while a rolled-over one is NOT. MUST land with or after TASK-COWORK-CATCHUP-3 (the consumer sub-flow catchup-check.md, still unbuilt) — until that ships, catchup_raw is computed every tick and consumed by nothing, so fixing this predicate alone changes zero behaviour. Do NOT let two agents edit cowork-catchup-predicate.js in parallel.

[po/triage 2026-08-12T15:36:32Z] ROOT CAUSE MEASURED — this row's scope is NARROWER than the live defect; widen it. Trigger: telegram 4736 (2026-08-12T09:09:16Z) 'macro-indicators /liquidity-state unreachable (deadline) — sbv_omo_daily did NOT accrue today. Check macro-indicators service / VPS.'

PO probed the live endpoint directly at 2026-08-12T15:36:32Z: GET http://localhost:5004/liquidity-state -> HTTP 405 (route IS registered, method not allowed); POST http://localhost:5004/liquidity-state -> HTTP 200, 1241 bytes, time_total = 9.66 SECONDS; GET http://localhost:5004/health -> {status: ok, service: macro-indicators, port: 5004}; container Up 13 days (healthy).

So the service is UP, the route is REGISTERED and the handler RETURNS 200 — it is simply ~10s slow. The failure mode is A DEADLINE SHORTER THAN THE ENDPOINT'S REAL LATENCY, not unreachability. Two consequences: (1) the alert's own remediation advice ('Check macro-indicators service / VPS') routes every responder to the wrong layer and has done so on every fire; (2) sbv_omo_daily genuinely does not accrue, so this is a REAL DATA GAP, not merely a message-quality nit.

Fix scope should therefore be BOTH: split the conflated error string (this row's original scope) AND raise the cron deadline above the measured ~10s handler latency (or make the handler fast). Priority raised P3 -> P2 on the strength of the accrual gap.

Secondary observation from the same 200 response, deliberately NOT ticketed: policy_rates carries source='sbv_rates DB fallback (HTML parse failed)' with is_estimate=true, and sjc_gold_gap reports sjc_price_mn_vnd=0 with note 'SJC price absent from DB (no SJC crawler row)'. backlog.title: COWORK SIGNAL/SYNTHESIS filenames are date-keyed (bctc: ticker+date+mode; chef synthesis: date_vn+dish_type; tnb notebook) not cycle_id -> intra-day cycles collide on ONE path; a between-drains write silently destroys the prior cycle's UNROUTED signal = a dropped escalation with no error anywhere. 3rd instance of one root class same day; CONFIRMED clobber today: processed/bctc_signal_FPT_20260715_routine.json signal 9240 overwritten by 8120.
backlog.note:
MINTED 2026-07-15 by po from signal cow-20260715T212838 (data-integrity, MED). ROOT CAUSE: signal/synthesis filenames carry ticker+date+mode (or date_vn+dish_type) with NO cycle discriminator; bctc-analyst runs 4x/day (cron 0 15,18,21,0 UTC) so all 4 cycles collide on the same path (39 such filenames in processed/). HARM (the real one, not the lost artifact): the drain READS these files to route signals; if cycle N writes the same filename as cycle N-1 between drains, N silently destroys N-1's UNROUTED signal and it is never triaged. Today the hourly drain interleaved so nothing was lost -- luck, not a guard; a late/missed drain loses a signal silently. 3 INSTANCES SAME CLASS SAME DAY: (1) chef synthesis date_vn+dish_type -> run2 clobbered run1 (Write, silent); (2) tnb notebook same collision, caught ONLY by the Edit tool stale-read check; (3) bctc signals ticker+date+mode -> 9240 overwritten by 8120. feedback_recurring_bug_escalation (2+ -> block) qualifies. SAME ONE-LINE FIX EACH TIME: key the filename by cycle_id (bctc already carries one; chef's is already in metadata). SCOPE (ba/architect own HOW): the docs/signals/*.json writers (bctc-analyst, chef/unified-agent, tnb) + docs/data/unified-agent-synthesis-<DATE>-<SLOT>.json + the Signal Bus naming contract docs/standards/mcp-tools.md (Naming Contract) + the drain reader that consumes filenames. DISTINCT-FROM (checked, none cover this): FU-CTG-DISCOVERY-FILENAME-FILTER (VPS HNX discovery CV_CBTT filename detection), FU-BACKFILL-REAL-FILENAMES (backfill real-filename heuristic), FIX-COWORK-SCHEDULE-STALE-BASE-CLOBBER. OBSERVATION folded (mechanism UNPROVEN -- do NOT diagnose, NOT a blocker): signal_id regressed 9240->8120 over 20h same file/tool/sequence; parsimonious candidate = SQLite INTEGER PRIMARY KEY WITHOUT AUTOINCREMENT reuses max(rowid)+1 after the drain prunes highest rows; NOT probed because the LIVE DB is a named volume, not docs/signals/signals.db (feedback_live_db_is_named_volume_not_host_data); cheap check for the implementer = does the SERVING schema use AUTOINCREMENT. If ids ARE reused, any cross-time signal_id reference can silently re-bind to an unrelated later signal (worse than an orphan FK -- looks resolved). AC: (1) two same-day cycles for the same ticker/mode never share a signal/synthesis path; (2) a between-drains double-write of the same ticker+date+mode cannot silently destroy an unrouted signal; (3) the drain-reader change (if any) preserves routing of both cycles' signals.

po_architect_signoff_20260807T0545.amendment_3_FR1_WINDOWKEY_MIDNIGHT_STRAD: BINDING CORRECTION to brief Section 2, fallback branch 2 (the ACTIVE day-one path, per the brief's own Section 1). As written, WINDOW_KEY = <date portion of live_mcp_fetched_at> + 'T' + CRON_HOUR + '00Z' unconditionally pairs the RUN's UTC calendar date with the SLOT's cron hour. That re-introduces this row's own collision class at the UTC day boundary for any fire that is not same-UTC-day as its own nominal window. Two reachable cases, both live: (a) bctc-analyst-slot-4's cron is '0 0 * * *' = exactly 00:00Z — a backstop/catch-up fire a few minutes EARLY (23:5xZ) keys to the PREVIOUS day's slot-4 window and clobbers a 24h-old file; (b) a slot-3 ('0 21 * * *') run delayed past midnight, or an ordinary operator re-run of slot-3 the following morning, keys to a FUTURE window (D+1 21:00Z) that the real D+1 fire will then collide with. Neither is exotic: FIX-GUARANTEED-SLOT-FIRER-FANOUT-TRUNCATION documents live off-nominal re-fires, and EC-1 manual re-runs are explicitly in scope. FIX (deterministic, pure, no extra I/O, does not change the function's signature): branch 2 must select the occurrence of CRON_HOUR:00Z NEAREST to live_mcp_fetched_at — evaluate the candidate set {yesterday, today, tomorrow} at CRON_HOUR:00Z and take min |delta| — rather than unconditionally concatenating today's UTC date. backlog.title: 3 notebooks are over byte-cap AND structurally unprunable (preamble + 1 section left) — auto-prune has given up on all 3; digest-predict.md is the anomaly at 41L/23477B (~573 bytes/line)
backlog.desc:
Seven inbox signals collapse to three files. All are 'action_required: manual_split_to_archive' — the auto-prune hook has already tried and reports it cannot prune further without data loss:
  - docs/agent-memory/notebooks/code-janitor.md — 213L / 12820B (cap 200L / 12000B). Over BOTH caps. Ordinary overage.
  - docs/agent-memory/notebooks/dev-rag-service.md — 95L / 15888B (byte-cap only, +3888B).
  - docs/agent-memory/notebooks/digest-predict.md — 41L / 23477B (byte-cap only, +11477B).

TREAT digest-predict.md AS A SEPARATE DEFECT, NOT JUST AN OVERAGE. 23477 bytes across 41 lines is ~573 bytes per line, and it is nearly 2x the byte cap while at 20% of the line cap. A notebook cannot reach that shape through normal cycle appends — something is writing very long single lines (most likely an un-wrapped JSON blob, a base64 payload, or a full tool response pasted inline). Splitting it to archive would relocate the bytes without stopping the producer, and it would be back over cap within days. Find and fix what is writing those lines FIRST; the split is the cleanup afterwards, not the fix. dev-rag-service.md at 167 bytes/line is mildly elevated and may share the same cause — check it while you are there.

WHY MANUAL: with only preamble + 1 section remaining there is no droppable unit left, so the automatic path is genuinely exhausted and this needs a human-judgement split into docs/agent-memory/archive/. Route per the notebook-write skill's own archive convention; do NOT full-overwrite the live files (feedback_qa_notebook_fulloverwrite_drops_concurrent_peer_entries — that failure has already happened 3x on this fleet, most recently landing on po.md).

NOTE: the 3 notebook_tiebreak_direction_defaulted signals on qa.md that arrived alongside these are explicitly 'informational_no_action_needed' per their own payload and are deliberately NOT folded here — they are the documented newest_first default working as designed, not a breach.

AC: all 3 files under both caps; digest-predict.md's byte producer identified and named in the close-out (or explicitly ruled out with evidence); no live notebook content lost — archived content must be reachable, byte-for-byte, in docs/agent-memory/archive/.

backlog.title: Requirement spec: per-invocation usage telemetry for the cron preflight scripts — turn silent-tick cost from an estimate into a measurement
backlog.desc:
USER REQUEST (verbatim 'yes' to a router proposal, 2026-08-12): add per-invocation token/usage instrumentation to the cron preflight scripts so silent-tick cost is a measured number instead of an estimate. Named target: cowork-team. Sprint goal SSOT: docs/data/orch/orch-state.json .sprint_goal.entries[] sprint_id=TICK-PREFLIGHT-USAGE-INSTRUMENTATION — READ IT FIRST, it carries the binding scope_in/scope_out/product_decision and this row does not repeat them.

WRITE docs/REQ_<n>.md. PO has already done the source read; do NOT re-derive these, they are inputs not questions:

FINDING 1 — choke points differ, and that IS the scope decision.
  scripts/agents-flow/cowork-tick-preflight.sh:76-82  _emit_verdict()  — single choke point, every verdict routes through it.
  scripts/agents-flow/dev-team-tick-preflight.sh:200-203 _emit_verdict() — single choke point, structurally identical.
  scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh — NO choke point. Inline jq -n verdict construction at lines 757, 767, 772, 858, 894, 921. Dual-mode: run_tiered_probe() (tier 2/3) calls run_probe() internally then re-emits its OWN wrapper verdict with a different field set (inner {verdict:ALL_GREEN|FAILURE, detail, last_healthy_at} vs outer {tier, checks_verdict, verdict:SKIP-SPAWN|SPAWN, detail, last_healthy_at, fresh_threshold_minutes, heartbeat_age_minutes}). A per-call-site hook double-logs every tier-2/3 tick with two incompatible shapes. WU-3 must extract a choke point FIRST; that extraction is the risk, not the logging.

FINDING 2 — the family is 6, not 3. Also present with the same verdict-JSON-on-stdout shape: scripts/agents-flow/code-janitor-tick-preflight.sh, scripts/agents-flow/db-integrity-probe.sh, scripts/agents-flow/orch-sentinel-lite-probe.sh. Explicitly OUT of this sprint (scope_out d). Do not widen. Do not silently drop either — the REQ should name them as the designated follow-up.

FINDING 3 — the ratio already exists: 4 chars/token, docs/architecture-briefs/2026-05-21-token-toolcall-economy.md §W-1, applied in docs/architecture-briefs/2026-07-12-token-economy-lazyload-audit.md. Do not invent one. Do not put it in a script.

FINDING 4 — test seam already exists and must be reused. Every suite sources the script and overrides functions after sourcing; cowork-tick-preflight.test.sh sets PREFLIGHT_ROOT to an isolated mktemp fixture and stubs mcp_call. If the log path derives from that same root, the existing suites write into the fixture automatically and never touch live data. An explicit override var is still required as a second seam.

RECORD PER INVOCATION (measurable only — no computed token field): ts (UTC ISO-8601, real wallclock via date -u, never hand-typed — memory feedback_hand_typed_iso_timestamps_drift_into_the_future), script, verdict, tick where the script has one, verdict_bytes = byte length of the exact JSON line written to stdout, elapsed_ms, exit_code. NOT session id (scope_out f).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA the REQ must formalize — each needs a named test, and each of the negative controls needs a real fault-injection case, not an assertion that the happy path still works:
  AC-1 One log line per invocation, on EVERY verdict path of every wired script (cowork SILENT/WORK/LOST_ELECTION/DEFER/ERROR/TOMBSTONED; dev-team RUN/RUN-IDLE/SKIP/SKIP-WIDENED/ERROR; auditor ALL_GREEN/FAILURE plus the tier-2/3 SKIP-SPAWN/SPAWN wrapper). Not one path may be silently uninstrumented.
  AC-2 Logged verdict string == the verdict on stdout, and logged verdict_bytes == the real byte length of that stdout line. Assert against actual captured stdout, not against a re-derivation.
  AC-3 Zero semantic change: verdict token, JSON field set, exit code, lock claim/release sequence and MCP call sequence all byte-identical before and after. The mcp_call stub already counts calls — assert the SILENT-path count is unchanged.
  AC-4 NEGATIVE CONTROL, exit code: the logger must not alter the caller's return status. _emit_verdict is frequently the last statement before an explicit return, and cowork's _step8_silent_release propagates via return $?. Inject a logger that fails and assert every verdict path's exit code is unchanged.
  AC-5 NEGATIVE CONTROL, unwritable destination: read-only / missing / full log dir produces an unchanged verdict on stdout, an unchanged exit code, and nothing on stdout from the logger. The tick must never fail because telemetry failed.
  AC-6 stdout purity: the verdict line stays the FIRST and ONLY thing on stdout. Memory feedback_tick_preflight_verdict_is_first_json_key_tail_always_drops_it — a stray logger byte on stdout breaks every downstream reader. Logger writes to the file and to nothing else.
  AC-7 No new tool call, MCP call, git operation or network I/O on the silent/skip path. Local file append only.
  AC-8 Rotation: size cap enforced, last-N lines preserved, truncate is atomic (tmp+mv, never in-place) so a concurrent appender cannot read a half-truncated file. State plainly whether an append racing a rotation can be lost, and if so that it is accepted — do not leave it unstated.
  AC-9 Concurrency: appends are single-write O_APPEND of one line, never read-modify-write. cowork (15 min) and dev-team (7/37 min) overlap, possibly from different sessions.
  AC-10 All pre-existing suites green at or above their pre-sprint counts. The intake brief quoted 20/20, 37/37, 32/32 — treat those as UNVERIFIED; QA establishes the real pre-sprint baseline by running them before any edit.
  AC-11 Every artifact states the honesty caveat: verdict_bytes is a LOWER BOUND on true per-tick cost (it excludes the cron prompt text and the flow-doc lines the LLM loads). See product_decision — this is acceptance-bearing, not a nicety.

OPEN QUESTIONS for architect, flag them, do not decide them in the REQ:
  Q1 Log destination + git-tracked vs git-ignored. PO PREFERENCE, overridable only with written rationale: docs/data/telemetry/tick-usage.jsonl, GIT-IGNORED. Rationale: ~500+ lines/day of churn on a tracked file collides with the documented commit-sweep hazards (feedback_shared_main_peer_push_sweeps_held_data_commits, feedback_coldevict_bare_commit_sweeps_worker_staged_index) and buys nothing — the analysis step reads it locally. Precedent for gitignored docs/data files exists: docs/data/cycle-snapshot-*.json. Note the existing tracked precedents (code-janitor-tick-preflight-last-verdict.json, db-integrity-probe-last-snapshot.json) are single-row SNAPSHOTS, not append-only growth — they are not precedent for this.
  Q2 One shared JSONL for all scripts, or one file per script? Affects rotation fairness — a chatty script could rotate away a quiet one's history.
  Q3 WU-3's choke-point extraction shape, and how the tier-2/3 wrapper is represented without double-counting.

Size M. Chain: BA (this row) -> PO spec approval -> architect (Q1-Q3 + WU-3 design) -> PM decomposition into WU-0..WU-3 -> developer -> QA. WU-0 gates WU-1/2; WU-3 gates on WU-0/1/2 green.

backlog.desc: scripts/audits/verify-a30-mcp-memory-reclamation.sh:311-322 is an if/elif chain. Branch 1 = STATE_CHANGED (RestartCount/StartedAt delta) -> ESCALATE 'container died/restarted'. Because branch 4 is an elif, it can ONLY be reached when branches 1-3 all evaluated FALSE — i.e. the script has already established, from docker inspect, that the container did NOT restart, was NOT OOM-killed, and shows NO death signature. It then labels the drop a 'crash cliff' and the tier1-probe.md reason-substring table (line 244, 'discontinuity' -> CRITICAL) maps it to a CRITICAL Telegram alert. A branch that fires only in the proven-no-crash case cannot correctly assert a crash.

backlog.title: PO AC-3 persistence gate tests OWN-COMMIT membership, not HEAD ancestry — fires a FALSE data-loss bug-telegram whenever a peer bare-commit legitimately absorbs the write (reproduced live 2026-08-14T07:08Z)
backlog.desc:
Minted by po 2026-08-14T07:07:35Z from a live occurrence during UNBLOCK-OPS-RAG-REBUILD-DONEVERIFIED-FALSIFIED-BY-KERNEL.
DEFECT: `docs/agents/po/flow/main.md` § "AC-3 — mandatory self-verification before RETURN may assert persistence" verifies persistence by grepping PO'S OWN commit: `SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD); git show --stat "$SHA" | grep -q 'docs/data/orch/orch-state.json'` and, on miss, fires `send_telegram(channel="bug", "[po] FAIL-LOUD: orch-state.json NOT in own commit $SHA — landed on disk via orch-apply.sh but not in git HEAD")`.
WHY IT IS WRONG: on a shared main, a peer's bare commit routinely absorbs another agent's already-written data file (the tracked FIX-COMMIT-SWEEP-VICTIM-SELF-DETECT class). When that happens the write IS durably in git HEAD but is NOT in the writing agent's own commit, so the gate reports a data-loss that did not occur. Reproduced live 2026-08-14T07:08Z: po's writes at 06:59:05Z/07:01:03Z were swept into peer commit 3220f31bc; po's own commit abfa9de90 legitimately contains no orch-state.json; content verified fully intact via `git show HEAD:docs/data/orch/orch-state.json`.
FAILURE DIRECTION IS THE SEVERITY: this is a FALSE POSITIVE that asserts loss. A bug-channel message saying "landed on disk but not in git HEAD" invites the next actor to re-apply an already-applied board write — a second write on top of a correct one, on the hot SSOT file.
AC-1: the gate's predicate is ancestry-and-content, not own-commit-membership — e.g. re-read `git show HEAD:docs/data/orch/orch-state.json` and assert the specific mutation is present, or `git log -S'<marker>' -1 --format=%H -- <path>` returns a SHA reachable from HEAD. Own-commit membership may remain as an informational log line, never as the alarm trigger.
AC-2: when the write IS in HEAD but NOT in the agent's own commit, the flow emits a distinct SWEPT-BY-PEER note (work channel, not bug) naming the absorbing SHA — this is the missing evidence trail FIX-COMMIT-SWEEP-VICTIM-SELF-DETECT asks for, produced at zero extra cost from the same probe.
AC-3: the same own-commit-membership pattern is grepped for across `docs/agents/*/flow/*.md` and every sibling instance is corrected or explicitly allowlisted — opt-IN allowlist only (feedback_fleetwide_gate_validated_on_one_file_optout_allowlist); do NOT assume po is the only carrier.
ZONE NOTE: po deliberately did NOT self-fix. `docs/agents/po/flow/main.md` is an agent definition/flow file — po's own init.md forbidden_outputs bars po from modifying it ("NEVER modify agent definition files — use agent-father for that"), hence next_agent=agent-father rather than a self-repair.

backlog.title: task_claim re-entrancy is discriminated on owner_client_session ALONE, which two sub-agents of the same router session necessarily share — the documented rule made a po sub-agent heartbeat-EXTEND a peer's lock instead of detecting a collision
backlog.source: durable-inbox signal from=dev-team type=bug-escalation 2026-08-14T09:35:00Z
backlog.dedup_checked: backlog+ready+in_progress+review+qa scanned for TASK-CLAIM / TASKCLAIM / OWNER-SESSION. Only hit is FIX-CI-TASKCLAIM-QA-FLOW-OWNER-SESSION-PAYDOWN (review/po) which is a CI lint paydown for a MISSING owner_session arg in docs/agents/qa/flow/main.md - a call-site-completeness defect, not a discriminator-soundness defect. NO dedup hit -> minted.
backlog.evidence: Discovered live 2026-08-14T09:3xZ by a po sub-agent (ac362246d1ed5d95c) triaging the rag-service incident. It hit claimed:false with current_holder.owner_client_session matching its OWN session id, but current_holder.owner_session belonging to a DIFFERENT concurrent same-session po sub-agent. Following the documented re-entrant rule (CLAUDE.md Step 2.5 / dispatch-claim SKILL: claimed:false + owner_client_session == own -> task_heartbeat and proceed) caused it to EXTEND a peer's lock. Its subsequent task_release then correctly no-op'd (released:0) because the lock was never its own - so the peer's lock was silently lengthened and the mutex was defeated in both directions.
backlog.root_cause: owner_client_session identifies the coordinating CLIENT session, not the claiming PROCESS. Every background Agent() sub-agent spawned by one router session shares it. The re-entrancy predicate therefore cannot distinguish 'me again' from 'my sibling'. Likely correct predicate: re-entrant requires BOTH owner_client_session AND owner_session to match.
backlog.acceptance: AC-1 architect design pass covering the predicate change AND every consumer of it. AC-2 enumerate the blast radius - this is CLAUDE.md's mandatory Step 2.5 PRE-CLAIM, so it is every agent type's claim path fleet-wide, plus dispatch-claim CARD.md/SKILL.md, plus each flow doc that restates the rule. AC-3 a fixture proving two sub-agents of one client session racing the same task_id produce exactly one winner and one peer-collision verdict. AC-4 decide the disposition for an existing holder whose owner_session is absent from the presence roster (stale) - interacts with FIX-COWORK-PUBLISHED-MARKER-TTL-28H-EXCEEDS-24H-DAILY-CADENCE's AC-3.
backlog.non_goals: Not a narrow single-flow fix - do not patch one call site. This is the core coordination primitive.
backlog.consumer_impact: Highest-blast-radius item in this triage pass. Every PRE-CLAIM in the fleet inherits the unsound predicate whenever two sub-agents of one session race the same task_id - which is the normal operating mode of the backgrounded-by-default dispatch policy.

backlog.title: mcp-server cannot record its own OOM deaths: read the cgroup memory.events oom_kill counter at startup and write a real crash sentinel. docker inspect OOMKilled/ExitCode are a PROVEN false negative for this kill shape.
backlog.root_cause:
Successor to OPS-MCP-RESTART-CHURN-UNCLEAN-SHUTDOWN fix direction 3, minted at its PO sign-off (2026-08-15). That row established, and this row does not re-litigate: a per-container memcg OOM-kill arrives as SIGKILL, so NO userspace shutdown handler can ever record it -- the mcpServerCleanShutdown sentinel is structurally incapable of covering the crash case, and its ABSENCE is the only signal A-21 currently has. Absence is not evidence of cause: A-21 can say a restart was unclean, never why. Worse, the one API field that should answer it lies -- docker inspect returned ExitCode=0 / OOMKilled=false for three kills the kernel recorded plainly against that exact container cgroup ID.
WHY THIS IS NOT CLOSED BY FIX-MCP-MEMORY-CODE-LEAK (DONE_VERIFIED 2026-08-08): that fix removed the trigger, confirmed at sign-off (13.83% of cap at ~31h uptime vs 77.05% at ~12h before). It did not add any way to SEE the next one. The class is demonstrably still live elsewhere in the fleet: the dmesg window retained at sign-off held 4 memcg OOM kills in ~2.5 days, all python3 -- 3 at ~1.0GB against rag-service 1g cap, 1 at 2.35GB against pdf-extractor 2.5g cap -- and docker inspect will misreport those the same way.
UNATTRIBUTED CASE THIS WOULD HAVE CLASSIFIED: the 2026-08-11 14:20:07 mcpServerStartup carries no preceding clean-shutdown sentinel and fell outside the dmesg retention window, so its cause is permanently unknowable today.

On increase, write an explicit crash-cause row (e.g. cron_job_runs job_name mcpServerOomKill) carrying the observed counter delta, so A-21 and A-30 gain a POSITIVE crash-cause discriminator instead of inferring from sentinel absence. Self-scoped only -- reading other containers cgroups needs privilege this service must not take; a fleet-wide sweep is a separate ops-lane row if ever wanted.

backlog.title: Two independent, uncoordinated SIGTERM/SIGINT shutdown handlers race on graceful shutdown (checkpoint.ts:335 registerShutdownHook vs composition-root.ts:242) -- each calls process.exit(0) on its own. Latent, currently not manifesting.
backlog.root_cause:

On a real SIGTERM both fire concurrently and whichever calls process.exit(0) first terminates the other.

Do NOT re-file it as a cause of the historical unclean-restart count -- that was the uncatchable SIGKILL, and both handlers were absent from every one of those boundaries, not racing.
backlog.deliverable: One shutdown path. Fold the WAL TRUNCATE checkpoint into composition-root.ts ordered shutdown sequence (checkpoint BEFORE the sentinel write and before process.exit) and delete the independent handler registration in checkpoint.ts, or have registerShutdownHook expose a plain async callback the single owner invokes. Exactly one process.exit(0) call site for signal-driven shutdown.

backlog.title: task_claim enum has no guard/marker category, so every persistent escalation lock is minted as sprint-task - that pollution is the sole reason D4 needs a name-prefix whitelist at all
backlog.note:
Split out of FIX-AUDITOR-D4-WHITELIST-DATA-QUALITY-ANOMALY-PREFIX by po 2026-08-15 during PLAN review. Do NOT block that row on this one — it should land its whitelist/SSOT fix as-is; this row removes the need for the whitelist to exist at all.

PROBLEM. `task_claim`'s enum (apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/tools/system/coordination/taskClaimTool.ts:60) is exactly ["cowork-slot","sprint-task","dashboard-row","commit-mutex","intent","orphan-signal","session-presence"]. It has NO member for a persistent guard/escalation/marker lock — a lock that is board-row-less and long-TTL BY DESIGN and is never adoptable work. So every agent minting one falls back to `sprint-task`. Live evidence 2026-08-15T05:54Z (task_list_held kind=sprint-task expired=false, 10 locks): `cron-registration:cowork-team`, `cron-registration:detect-loop`, `cron-registration:standalone-team`, `esc-datacov:HPG:Q1-2026:ESC-3`, `esc-datacov:FPT:Q1-2026:ESC-3`, `esc-deepdive:FPT:Q1-2026:ESC-5` — four different owner agents, all forced to `sprint-task`. bctc-analyst's `bctc-dataquality:*` locks (expired 08-14/15) are the same shape.

WHY IT MATTERS. tasksMdJanitorJob's D4 Step R-1 scans `kind:"sprint-task"`, so its scan set is structurally polluted with non-tasks. That is the ONLY reason the D4-R1b name-prefix exclusion whitelist (KNOWN_LEGIT_PREFIXES) has to exist — and a static name list provably lags every new lock kind an agent mints later (that IS the parent row: authored 2026-07-08, missed the kind introduced 2026-07-19, then missed its rename to `bctc-dataquality:` before 2026-08-06). The parent row's fix (SSOT in system-map.json) makes the list cheaper to maintain but does not remove the need to maintain it. Telling detail: `session-presence`/`commit-mutex`/`intent:*` DO have their own enum members and are therefore already excluded structurally by the kind filter — the spec keeps them in the whitelist only as defense-in-depth (spec §287/§293). The enum-based filter already works for kinds that have a member; only the memberless kinds need prefix-matching.

AC-1: add a task_kind enum member for persistent guard/escalation markers (working name `guard-marker`) in taskClaimTool.ts + the TaskKind type + the lock store, with the tool description explaining when to use it vs `sprint-task`.
AC-2: migrate the known minting call sites to it — `cron-registration:*` (.claude/skills/cron-*/register.md), `po-triage-*` (po flows), `esc-datacov:*` (docs/agents/bctc-analyst/flow/esc-coverage-guard.md:43), `esc-deepdive:*` (docs/agents/bctc-analyst/flow/main.md:119), and bctc-analyst's `bctc-dataquality:*`. Migration must be additive/back-compatible: locks already held under `sprint-task` must not be orphaned mid-TTL.
AC-3: once migrated, shrink KNOWN_LEGIT_PREFIXES to only what still needs it, and confirm D4 still trips on a genuinely orphaned `sprint-task` lock (the parent row's negative control must keep passing).
AC-4 (second, related gap — folded here rather than a third row, same "these marker locks have no owning contract" cause): bctc-analyst's data-quality marker lock-kind is UNDOCUMENTED. A repo-wide grep of docs/agents/bctc-analyst/ finds task_claim call sites only for `esc-datacov:` and `esc-deepdive:`; NO flow doc documents a `data-quality-anomaly:*` or `bctc-dataquality:*` claim, and the name silently drifted between 2026-07-19 and 2026-08-06 with nothing to catch it. Document one canonical lock-kind name in the owning bctc-analyst flow doc and stop ad-hoc renaming — an undocumented lock kind cannot be whitelisted, migrated, or reasoned about by any other agent.

ZONE NOTE: spans apps/mcp-server (enum + D4 filter) and several agent flow docs (call sites), hence zone:multi and next_agent:architect to split. Parent row's spec §7 explicitly declined this as out of dev-mcp-server's zone.

backlog.title: CONFIRMED DATA LOSS: notebook-auto-prune AC-6 detects it has no ordering evidence and drops the section ANYWAY — date-only '## YYYY-MM-DD' headings all tie at day granularity, so drop-oldest is a coin flip
backlog.status_note:
CONFIRMED LIVE DATA LOSS, verified by grep not by narration. Signal notebook_prune_dropped_newest_dated_section fired on docs/agent-memory/notebooks/dev-mcp-server.md line 3, section '2026-08-15 — SPIKE-BCTC-EXTRACTION-DORMANT-MASS-ENRICHFAIL-FLOOD supervised-hold triage → HELD, deferred to PO'. PO checked whether the content survived: `grep -c 'SPIKE-BCTC-EXTRACTION-DORMANT-MASS-ENRICHFAIL-FLOOD' docs/agent-memory/notebooks/dev-mcp-server.md` returns 0. The section is GONE. The 3 sections that remain are all unrelated (FIX-PENDING-REFINE-OUTPUT-235K-OVERFLOW x2, FACTORY-APP-split-pollNews). The dropped section was the PO-facing supervised-hold handoff — the single most load-bearing section in the file.

MECHANISM (read from source, scripts/agents-flow/notebook-auto-prune.sh + lib/notebook-section-direction.sh): dev-mcp-server.md uses the DATE-ONLY heading convention '## YYYY-MM-DD — <topic>' with no time-of-day. nso_ts_key()'s Tier-1 pattern requires a T..Z suffix and therefore finds nothing, so it falls through to the Tier-2 bare-date pattern, which yields a DAY-GRANULARITY key. Every section authored on the same day collapses to the identical key (here: all 4 sections = 20260815). MIN_KEY == MAX_NON_SENTINEL_KEY, AC-6 correctly detects it has zero within-file ordering evidence, emits emit_dropped_newest_dated_section_signal() — AND THEN PROCEEDS WITH THE DROP ANYWAY. The script's own comment concedes this: 'Non-blocking — the prune proceeds; this signal exists so the drop is never silent.'

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE BUG. AC-5 (emit_no_valid_drop_candidate_signal) faces the identical epistemic situation — no trustworthy ordering — and correctly REFUSES to prune, explicitly to avoid 'manufactur[ing] a false oldest and risk[ing] dropping the file's NEWEST content'. AC-6 faces the same situation and does the opposite. The AC-6 path is strictly the more dangerous of the two because a tie means the victim is chosen arbitrarily from real content, and it has now cashed that risk in for an actual loss.

DISTINCT FROM FIX-NOTEBOOK-AUTOPRUNE-ROLLING-SECTIONS-BYTE-COUNTED-BUT-UNDROPPABLE (READY) — that row is about SENTINEL/rolling headings absorbing byte overage and being structurally undroppable (the AC-5 branch). This row is the AC-6 branch: same-day-tie among genuinely DATED sections, proceed-anyway. Same script, different branch, opposite failure direction (that one prunes too little, this one prunes the wrong thing). Minted separately and deliberately, not folded.

FIX OPTIONS (either is acceptable, prefer B): (A) make AC-6 REFUSE like AC-5 — symmetric and safe, but leaves same-day files permanently unprunable, which is the AC-5 residue problem. (B) BREAK THE TIE WITH FILE POSITION. The script already knows each section's line number, and notebook-write's own convention is newest-first prepend (lib/notebook-section-direction.sh exists precisely to vote on direction). Position IS real, already-available ordering evidence — a same-day tie should be resolved by direction-aware position (drop the LAST section under newest-first), not declared evidence-free. Under (B) this incident inverts correctly: the dropped section was at line 3, i.e. the NEWEST under newest-first, and would have been protected.

AC: replay this exact file shape (4 sections, identical date-only headings, newest-first) through the hook on a throwaway fixture; the line-3 section must survive and a later section must be the victim. Add the fixture to scripts/agents-flow/notebook-auto-prune.test.sh.

RECOVERY (do this first, it is cheap): the lost content is NOT unrecoverable — it is preserved verbatim in telegram report 4911 and in dev-mcp-server's decision journal per that report's own text ('Recorded in decision journal + dev-mcp-server notebook'). Restore the section to the notebook before the fix ships.

[po/triage 2026-08-22T22:58:36Z - FOLD x4, occurrence_count 1 -> 5] Four notebook-auto-prune-hook envelopes reached the PO durable inbox, all on docs/agent-memory/notebooks/ba.md, forming two matched PAIRS that together are a complete, self-documenting reproduction of this row's defect: (a) `notebook_tiebreak_direction_defaulted` at 20:55:22Z and 20:58:09Z, tied_sections = `5:20260822000000000:## FIX-GHOSTZONE-P0-PAIR . 2026-08-22` and `29:20260822000000000:## SPRINT-PREDICT-ENGINE-CALIBRATION-CLOSE-LOOP . 2026-08-22` (identical normalised timestamps - the hook has NO ordering evidence between them); (b) `notebook_prune_dropped_newest_dated_section` at the SAME two timestamps, each reporting that it dropped line 29 `## SPRINT-PREDICT-ENGINE-CALIBRATION-CLOSE-LOOP . 2026-08-22` with section_count=4 / non_sentinel_section_count=2 / sentinel_section_count=2. The pairing is the finding: the hook emits `direction defaulted` (admitting it cannot order the tie) and then, in the same pass, drops a section anyway - which is verbatim this row's title (`AC-6 detects it has no ordering evidence and drops the section ANYWAY`). Neither type has a row in triage-signals.md's Pipeline-A table, so both were routed via the ROUTE-BY-`to` fallback (to=claude-manager-helper); the fallback's mandatory DEDUP GUARD matched this row on subject (file + mechanism), so per that rule they FOLD into one open artifact rather than minting four. CONFIRMED DATA LOSS, twice, on a live notebook, three minutes apart. Recommend this row be re-prioritised on that basis: the sentinel_section_count=2 / non_sentinel_section_count=2 shape means only 2 droppable sections existed and the hook chose the NEWER of two same-day-normalised sections both times, so the failure is deterministic, not a coin-flip that happened to lose.

[po/triage-2026-08-23T21:08:06Z — FOLD, occurrence 6] notebook_prune_dropped_newest_dated_section fired on docs/agent-memory/notebooks/ba.md at 2026-08-23T20:06:44Z, line 27, heading '## FEAT-BCTC-INSPECT-QUARTER-TICKER-FILTER 2026-08-23' (section_count=4, non_sentinel=2, sentinel=2). A same-tick sibling signal (notebook_tiebreak_direction_defaulted, same file, same second) records the fallback that fired: direction_applied=newest_first. That informational signal is NOT itself a defect (FIX-NOTEBOOK-AUTOPRUNE-DIRECTION-UNRESOLVABLE-ZERO-TS-NOTEBOOKS owns the design); it is corroborating evidence that the tie was real and the drop proceeded on a default rather than on evidence.

backlog.title: PO flow can read telegram reports but has no documented tool to RESOLVE them, so reports resurface every tick forever; + AC-3 self-verification false-negatives when a peer sweep lands PO's write first
backlog.status_note:
TWO defects in PO's own flow/tooling docs, both independently CONFIRMED by PO this tick, folded into one row because they share an owner (agent-father — docs/agents/** is its commit zone) and are both small doc edits.

DEFECT 1 — NO RESOLVE ACTUATOR (the higher-value half). docs/agents/tools/package/po.md lists read_telegram_reports but NOT process_telegram_report / claim_telegram_report. PO's flow is therefore structurally READ-ONLY on this queue: it can see reports and act on their content, but has no documented call to mark one resolved. CONFIRMED LIVE, not inferred: report 4911 (created 2026-08-15T07:49:20Z) and 4912 (08:19:01Z) are BOTH still status='new' with resolution='none' and claimed_by=null after multiple PO ticks, and both re-presented on this tick's read_telegram_reports(status='new'). This is the same class as feedback_limitation_may_be_structural_check_the_tool_grant — the agent's apparent 'it keeps coming back' is a missing tool grant/doc, not agent error. FIX: add process_telegram_report + claim_telegram_report to the MCP Tools table in docs/agents/tools/package/po.md, and add an explicit 'resolve the report' step to the telegram-reports triage sub-flow so the disposition is actuated, not just narrated (the narrated-not-executed failure shape).

DEFECT 2 — AC-3 FALSE NEGATIVE UNDER PEER SWEEP. docs/agents/po/flow/main.md's AC-3 self-verification block asserts persistence via `git show --stat $(git rev-parse HEAD) | grep -q 'docs/data/orch/orch-state.json'`. That check assumes PO's OWN commit is the one carrying the file. On this shared-main repo a peer sweep frequently commits orch-state.json between PO's orch-apply.sh write and PO's own commit — PO's commit then legitimately contains no orch-state.json delta (nothing left to commit), AC-3 reads that as FAILURE and fires a spurious fail-loud BUG telegram. PO has now worked around this inline on two consecutive ticks by substituting `git show HEAD:docs/data/orch/orch-state.json`, which is the correct check: it verifies the CONTENT is at HEAD regardless of WHICH commit put it there — and content-at-HEAD is what AC-3 actually claims. FIX: replace the --stat grep in main.md's AC-3 block with a content assertion against `git show HEAD:docs/data/orch/orch-state.json` (e.g. jq the specific row id PO just wrote and assert it is present). Keep the generic rule text ('re-read the persistence layer before claiming persistence') — it is correct; only the implementation is wrong.

ORIGIN: both surfaced by the router's own RAW-verification of PO's 2026-08-15T09:15Z triage run (flow_defect_report, low severity). PO independently re-confirmed both this tick before minting rather than accepting the report on trust.

backlog.title: chef.md has no backfill-target-date concept — a delayed catch-up retry publishes under today's UTC date, leaving the missed slot permanently unfilled and prematurely tombstoning today's marker
backlog.created_by: po (adjudication of FIX-CHEF-EVENING-DUP-DATE-MISLABEL-INVESTIGATE, qa CHANGES_REQUESTED item ii)
backlog.origin: signal cowork-20260806T064440Z-chef-evening-retry-date-drift (aged out of signal_queue; recovered from qa_note)
backlog.note: DESIGN ASK — architect ruling required before any implementation. chef.md pins ONE canonical CYCLE_DATE_UTC = "date -u +%Y-%m-%d" at Step 0.5 (wall-clock at execution) and reuses it verbatim at the synthesis filepath, metadata.date_vn, the notebook session header and the published:<slot>:<date> marker key. That single-derivation-point rule is the ratified AC(1) of FIX-CHEF-EVENING-DUP-DATE-MISLABEL-INVESTIGATE and is CORRECT for a live on-time fire. It has NO concept of a backfill target date, so a delayed catch-up retry publishes under TODAY instead of the slot date it was meant to fill. OBSERVED (RAW-verified via get_market_message_digest at filing time): a ~10h43m-delayed retry intended for the missed 2026-08-05 evening slot published under 2026-08-06 — permanently leaving 2026-08-05 evening unfilled AND prematurely tombstoning the 2026-08-06 marker ~13h before that day's real 19:45Z fire, so the on-time fire was then blocked as a duplicate. One miss becomes two. ORIGIN: signal cowork-20260806T064440Z-chef-evening-retry-date-drift (2026-08-06T06:44:40Z, HIGH, routed to po). That signal has since AGED OUT of .signal_queue.rows[] (rolling window) and existed on NO board row — recovered from the qa_note of FIX-CHEF-EVENING-DUP-DATE-MISLABEL-INVESTIGATE during PO adjudication 2026-08-15 and minted here so it is not lost a second time. THE TENSION TO RULE ON: introducing a backfill-target-date parameter ADDS a second date input to chef.md, which is exactly what AC(1) forbids. Architect must decide whether AC(1) means "one derivation POINT" (a target date passed in by the dispatcher, still resolved once, still never recomputed downstream — compatible) or "one date SOURCE, always wall-clock" (incompatible; then the correct fix is elsewhere, e.g. the catch-up dispatcher must not retry across a UTC day boundary at all). Do NOT let an implementer resolve this silently — reversing a ratified AC is an architect call. SCOPE BOUNDARY: this row owns the backfill/target-date question ONLY. Marker key SLOT_ID canonicalization stays on FIX-CHEF-EVENING-DUP-DATE-MISLABEL-INVESTIGATE; marker release/immunity stays on UC-CCA-P3; double-dispatch cause stays on FIX-COWORK-DISPATCH-ROUTER-INTENT-MUTEX-BYPASS. Cross-ref, not subsumed.
backlog.verification_gate: Architect writes a ruling (brief or inline architect_note) that explicitly reconciles the new behaviour with FIX-CHEF-EVENING-DUP-DATE-MISLABEL-INVESTIGATE AC(1) — either amending AC(1)'s wording on that row or rejecting the parameter and naming the alternative owner. Implementation AC once ruled: a catch-up retry for slot S targeting date D publishes under D at all four surfaces (filepath, metadata.date_vn, notebook header, published:S:D marker) and does NOT claim or tombstone the marker for any other date. RAW-VERIFY on a real delayed retry, not a simulation.

backlog.title: Re-queueing a BCTC report to pek_triggered via applyPushBctcExtractionOutcome leaves reconcile_attempts stale (14 rows already over the cap-8), so the documented post-fix recovery path gets zero effective retries

backlog.desc: There are exactly two writers of bctc_vps_queue.status='pek_triggered'. apps/mcp-server/src/scheduler/financial-reports/bctcPdfPullJob.ts:445 does it CORRECTLY: `UPDATE bctc_vps_queue SET status='pek_triggered', reconcile_attempts = 0, last_attempt = datetime('now')`. apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/routes/bctcVpsIngestHandler.ts:99 (applyPushBctcExtractionOutcome, case 'async_routed') omits the counter reset: `UPDATE bctc_vps_queue SET status='pek_triggered', last_attempt = datetime('now')`. Because bctcExtractReconcileJob.ts only ever SELECTs status='pek_triggered', and its still-pending branch tops out at reconcile_attempts=7 while its exhaust branch (nextAttempt >= MAX_RECONCILE_ATTEMPTS=8) writes at most 8, any value above 8 is arithmetically unreachable without a status reset that left the counter stale. Live DB (mcp-server container, /app/data/market.db, readonly, 2026-08-15T12:54Z) shows 14 such rows: 13 enrich_failed + 1 done. Histogram for attempts>=7: {7:5, 8:64, 9:10, 10:1, 11:3}. Examples: HUT 2025-Q3 = 11 (the row architect flagged), HUT 2025-Q2 = 10, plus KDC/GEX/DBC 2023-2024 quarters at 9. WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: the RECONCILE EXHAUSTED alert that bctcExtractReconcileJob.ts:461 itself emits tells the operator to 'consider manual /api/trigger-pek-extract re-fire once the root cause is fixed' — that IS the recovery plan for the ~58 enrich_failed queue rows once FIX-PEK-EXTRACT-SEMAPHORE-CONTENTION-BOUNDED-QUEUE ships. A row re-driven through the async_routed path while still carrying reconcile_attempts=8 hits nextAttempt=9 >= 8 on its very FIRST reconcile pass and returns to enrich_failed having consumed zero real retries. Worse, the literal route the alert names, handleTriggerPekExtract, writes NO bctc_vps_queue status at all (PO grepped the whole file: no reconcile_attempts write anywhere in bctcVpsIngestHandler.ts), so it fires the PEK request but never re-enters the reconcile lifecycle that would verify the outcome. The semaphore fix alone therefore does NOT recover the already-exhausted backlog.
acceptance: AC-1 apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/routes/bctcVpsIngestHandler.ts:99 (applyPushBctcExtractionOutcome, case 'async_routed') resets the counter on re-queue, matching the already-correct sibling at bctcPdfPullJob.ts:445: SET status='pek_triggered', reconcile_attempts = 0, last_attempt = datetime('now'). Decide and DOCUMENT whether an unconditional reset or a reset-only-when-transitioning-from-a-terminal-status is correct — an unconditional reset could in principle let a genuinely stuck row loop forever if some other caller re-pushes it every tick; state the chosen invariant in a code comment.

AC-2 Decide the ownership question for handleTriggerPekExtract (the manual /api/trigger-pek-extract route): it currently fires the PEK request without touching bctc_vps_queue, so a manually re-fired report is invisible to the reconcile lifecycle. Either make it re-queue (status='pek_triggered', reconcile_attempts=0) so reconcile verifies the outcome, or — if leaving it lifecycle-free is deliberate — say so in a comment AND fix bctcExtractReconcileJob.ts:461's alert text, which currently recommends it as the remediation. Do not leave the alert recommending a path that cannot converge.

AC-3 One-off data remediation for the 14 over-cap rows: decide whether to normalize reconcile_attempts (and whether any of the 13 enrich_failed rows should be re-queued for a fresh run once the semaphore fix is live). Record the before/after counts.

The file already has an in-memory bctc_vps_queue test harness (see its header comment at line 30/73) so this needs no HTTP simulation.

backlog.title: Shared $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID defeats the re-entrant branch in EVERY task_claim gate: two sibling CLI processes each read the other's live claim as their own re-entrant hold and BOTH proceed — genuine double-dispatch, blast radius includes the router's own Phase B hot path
backlog.desc:
Follow-up explicitly handed to PO for scoping by agents-architect (brief_complete, requires_scoping=true, envelope 19181b10, 2026-08-15T11:24:25Z) and deliberately held OUT of the bounded 2-file cowork-registration fix already shipped to agent-father.

DEFECT: the re-entrant escape hatch present in every task_claim gate on this fleet reads 'claimed:false AND current_holder.owner_client_session == $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID => this is my own lock, proceed'. That predicate assumes session UUID uniquely identifies a PROCESS. It does not — two sibling Claude CLI processes can share one session UUID, which is the same root assumption that already produced duplicate cowork-cron registrations (brief docs/architecture-briefs/2026-08-15-cowork-cron-registration-sibling-process-defer.md). Under a shared UUID the branch is not merely wasteful, it INVERTS the lock: each sibling sees the other's genuine, live, foreign claim, matches it against its own session UUID, concludes re-entrancy, and proceeds. Both run. The mutex returns the wrong answer precisely when contention is real, which is the only time it matters.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE ALREADY-SHIPPED FIX: commit 0468c2821 fixed the REGISTRATION path in .claude/skills/cron-cowork-team/SKILL.md only (2 files, sibling-process fingerprint defer). The re-entrant BRANCH is a separate call site and was left untouched by design — the architect signalled it out of scope and asked PO to scope it, because the blast radius reaches the router's own dispatch hot path and a bad edit there stops all delegation fleet-wide.

WHY IT IS TRACTABLE NOW: the discriminator already exists and is already proven in production. 0468c2821 introduced a sibling-process fingerprint that distinguishes two processes sharing a session UUID. This task is propagation of that same proven fingerprint into the remaining re-entrant call sites, plus one decision the architect must own: whether the fingerprint becomes a required field on task_claim itself (server-side, one enforcement point, correct-by-construction) or stays a caller-side check repeated at each site (no server change, but re-drifts). That decision is why this routes to architect first and is sized M rather than S.

CALL SITES (from the brief's own enumeration, to be re-verified at HEAD by architect before editing — do not trust this list blind):
  - docs/agents/cowork-team/flow/leader-lock.md
  - docs/agents/dev-team/flow/main.md, Step [3] fire-election P3 re-entrant branch
  - all 3 system-auditor tier crons
  - .claude/skills/dispatch-claim/CARD.md + SKILL.md Phase B re-entrant branch (the router's own PRE-CLAIM gate, per CLAUDE.md)

zone=multi because the set spans docs/agents/, .claude/skills/, and the system-auditor cron definitions — architect must split it into per-zone work before any edit lands.

backlog.desc:
THE REAL DEBT behind code-janitor's (wrong) '84% of scripts/ is dead' claim. The orphan framing was incorrect, but the underlying mass is real and it has a clean root cause.

COMPOSITION of scripts/ (908 files): 626 .jq, 177 .sh, 50 .ts, 17 .js, 13 .py, 9 .mjs. The .jq class is 69% of the directory and is almost entirely SINGLE-USE by construction — names are per-tick and per-decision: po-s108-idle-wip-promote-groom-terminal-backlog.jq, router-d41-fbop-liveverify-partial-queryrecon-20260615.jq, po-triage-20260808T1248Z-auditor-verdict-transcription.jq, router-hnx-ssl-claim.jq. By prefix: 265 po-, 46 qa-, 16 devteam-, 15 dev-fix-, plus a large router- family. 516 of 626 are older than 30 days and ZERO have been modified in the last 7 days.

WHY THEY EXIST: CLAUDE.md's Orch-State Hot File write contract requires every board mutation to be expressed as a jq transform piped through scripts/orch-apply.sh, and every PO/router/QA mutate sub-flow carries that pipe inline at the mutation point. Combined with the Script Persistence directive ('Any script useful for the work or reusable later MUST be saved to scripts/, NEVER left in /tmp'), agents persist their one-shot transform as a file. The policy has a SAVE rule and a location table but NO retirement rule and no reusable-vs-one-shot distinction, so the one-shots accumulate monotonically forever.

THIS IS NOT A DELETE-THEM JOB. Many are cited from decision journals and notebooks as the actuation record of a specific board decision, so blind deletion destroys audit trail. It is an ARCHIVE-BY-RULE job plus a policy amendment that stops the inflow.

WHY BA-FIRST rather than a direct FIX: it needs a real decision on the reusable/one-shot boundary, on whether one-shots should go to scratchpad instead of scripts/ (which would put the Script Persistence directive and the orch-apply write contract in tension and needs an explicit ruling), on the archive destination and retention window, and on whether journal references must be rewritten to the archived path. That is spec work, not a patch. Note code-janitor's own recommendation (a) — 'canonicalize the 41-script active list into dev-standards.md as SSOT' — is REJECTED as specified: 41 is a wrong number derived from the too-narrow caller surface (see FIX-JANITOR-DEADCODE-AUDIT-CALLER-SURFACE-TOO-NARROW-MASS-FALSE-POSITIVES), and a hand-maintained list of live scripts would drift within days. If an active-script SSOT is wanted at all it must be GENERATED from the declared corpus, never hand-listed.
backlog.status_note: AC-1: dev-standards.md § Script Persistence gains an explicit REUSABLE vs ONE-SHOT test, with the dated orch-state transform named as the canonical one-shot example and a stated destination for it. AC-2: a retirement/archive rule exists with a concrete age + non-reference predicate and a named archive destination (reuse the existing quarantine-first mechanism of scripts/audits/clean-obsolete-files.sh rather than inventing a second one). AC-3: archival preserves audit trail — any .jq cited from docs/agent-memory/decisions/** or a notebook must remain resolvable after archiving (either left in place or its citations rewritten). AC-4: the inflow actually stops — after the policy lands, a fresh mint by a PO/router tick must not add a new dated one-shot to scripts/. AC-5: measure before and after; report the .jq count. AC-6: explicitly reconcile the tension between CLAUDE.md 'Reusable scripts -> scripts/ NEVER /tmp' and one-shot transforms, so future agents get an unambiguous rule rather than defaulting to persist-everything.

backlog.status_note:
CONFIRMED LIVE, cost measured: UC-CCA-P2-MARKET-WATCHER sat in review[] for 8 days (2026-08-14 -> 2026-08-22) on an acceptance criterion that could never be satisfied. docs/handoffs/UC-CCA-P2-BA-spec.md:418-419 wrote AC-3 as 'next live market-watcher cycle's WORK ping / notebook shows exactly one [GATEWAY] probe log line, not two'. The implementation it gates (.claude/skills/gateway-availability-gate/SKILL.md:30) emits that line to the TRANSCRIPT on the success path and writes the notebook ONLY on its DEFER/BLOCKED failure branches; the WORK ping is a fixed <=80-char ULTRA template (docs/agents/market-watcher/flow/cycle.md:328) with no gateway field. So on every healthy cycle both named planes read ZERO, forever. The row was re-reviewed, re-blamed on an unrelated dispatcher outage, claimed by a dev-team secondary-drain and re-spawned to PO before anyone read the skill and noticed the plane does not exist.

CLASS, not an instance: this is the AC-authoring twin of the already-known agent-side failure in docs/protocols/fail-loud-protocol.md § Analysis-Only Exit Guard ('re-read the persistence layer before claiming it'). That rule tells the WRITER to verify the plane. Nothing tells the AC AUTHOR that the plane must exist and be written by the code under test in the first place. An AC whose evidence plane is never written is indistinguishable, to every downstream reviewer, from an AC that is failing.

PROPOSED SCOPE (small — BA to confirm/adjust, not prescriptive):
(1) BA spec-authoring rule: every AC MUST name a persistence plane (file path / DB table / signal row / commit / channel message) that the code or flow under test demonstrably writes on the PASS path, and the spec must cite where that write happens. 'Transcript log line' is NOT an acceptable AC plane — no reviewer can re-read a past transcript.
(2) A reviewer-side escape hatch, so this never strands a row again: when an AC turns out to be unfalsifiable, the reviewing agent is explicitly authorised to substitute an equivalent falsifiable criterion, record the substitution + evidence on the row, and sign off — rather than blocking indefinitely or fabricating a pass. PO exercised exactly this on UC-CCA-P2-MARKET-WATCHER 2026-08-22 without a documented mandate; the mandate should exist.
(3) OPTIONAL, flagged not proposed (avoid scope creep): a grep-based scripts/audits/ check over docs/handoffs/*-BA-spec.md for ACs whose evidence noun is 'log line'/'transcript'/'output' with no file path — opt-IN allowlist only per feedback_fleetwide_gate_validated_on_one_file_optout_allowlist.

backlog.title: Prediction engine is anti-calibrated (95% confidence -> 0% actual hit rate): the empirical likelihood-ratio table is computed but NEVER applied, and the weekly Brier measurement feeds back into NOTHING
backlog.desc:
USER REQUEST (2026-08-22, verbatim intent): user pasted the live 'Du bao AI & Ket qua' dashboard (49 predictions, 25 resolved, 24% hit rate, avg Brier 0.4743 — WORSE than the 0.25 naive-coinflip baseline) and asked to 'improve and make it more recurrent for find good to invest'. Avg Brier > 0.25 means the engine is ACTIVELY MISCALIBRATED, not merely imprecise: a constant 50% forecast would score better than what ships today.

ALL FINDINGS BELOW ARE LIVE-VERIFIED (2026-08-22T20:30-20:40Z) against the running gateway + source, NOT read off the pasted dashboard snapshot.

=== LIVE BASELINE (get_calibration_report, computed 2026-08-09T13:04:00Z) ===
Overall Brier 0.5319 over 17 resolved in the 90d window; trend 'degrading' (+0.244 WoW).
Per-direction: bearish 0.7045 | bullish 0.4380 | neutral 0.3309 — the BEARISH channel is the specifically broken one; neutral is actually acceptable.
Calibration curve (predicted -> actual hit rate) is MONOTONICALLY ANTI-CALIBRATED:
  65% -> 50.0% (n=2) | 75% -> 33.3% (n=9) | 85% -> 0.0% (n=3) | 95% -> 0.0% (n=3)
The engine is MOST WRONG exactly where it is MOST CONFIDENT. All 5 worst predictions are bank tickers: VPB bearish 95% x3 (Brier 0.9025 each), ACB bearish 88% x2 (0.7744 each).

=== D1 (PRIMARY, NEW) — the likelihood ratio is computed, displayed, and then DISCARDED ===
apps/mcp-server/src/scheduler/news-analysis/evidenceAccumulatorJob.ts computes the score that every prediction is built from as, verbatim from its own header:
    score = sum(magnitude * confidence) / count   (per direction)
It does NOT import likelihoodRatioStore at all (verified: import list is logger, getDb, recordJobRun, evidenceFragmentStore only). So `evidence_likelihood_ratios` — the ONE table in the whole system derived from REALIZED price outcomes (written daily by baseRateComputationJob at 19:07 UTC, cron key baseRateComputation '7 19 * * *') — never enters the arithmetic that produces a prediction. It is rendered as decoration in get_evidence_summary and nowhere else.
LIVE ARITHMETIC PROOF (get_evidence_summary('ACB'), 2026-08-22): the two contributing fragments are
  bctc_roe_strong [bullish] mag=0.70 conf=0.60 score=0.4224 | LR=0.54 (n=91, 5d) [TRUSTED]
  bctc_roe_ratio  [bullish] mag=0.30 conf=0.60 score=0.1800 | LR=0.86 (n=195, 5d) [TRUSTED]
and the reported Bullish score is 0.3012 = (0.4224 + 0.1800) / 2 EXACTLY — the plain unweighted mean. Both fragments carry a TRUSTED, large-sample LR BELOW 1.0, i.e. empirically ANTI-predictive (hit rate below base rate), and the score is completely unmoved by that. The system has already measured that its own bullish BCTC evidence does not work, on n=91 and n=195, and keeps weighting it at full strength.

=== D2 (PRIMARY, NEW) — the outer feedback loop does not exist; this IS the 'more recurrent' ask ===
apps/mcp-server/src/scheduler/macro/calibrationReportJob.ts (weekly Sun 13:04 UTC, cron key calibrationReport '4 13 * * 0') contains ZERO occurrences of 'likelihood' (verified by grep -c) and does not import likelihoodRatioStore. Its documented 11-step computation terminates at step 9 insertCalibrationSnapshot + step 10 sendCalibrationDigest. It measures Brier, per-direction Brier, and the full calibration curve every week, writes them to calibration_snapshots, posts a Telegram digest — and then throws the measurement away. NOTHING in the engine consumes calibration_snapshots to change future behavior.
The two loops are fully decoupled: baseRateComputationJob (daily) fits LRs from evidence-fragment -> price-move outcomes but its output is unused (D1); calibrationReportJob (weekly) scores the engine's ACTUAL published predictions but its output is unused (D2). There is no path from 'this prediction was wrong' to 'weight that evidence type less next time'.

=== D3 (NEW) — 'confidence' is a raw score passed through ~1:1, never shrunk toward the base rate ===
Live get_evidence_summary('VPB') returns Bearish: 0.9500, and the engine published 95%-confidence VPB bearish claims (ids 19/22/25) whose bucket has a 0.0% actual hit rate. There is no Bayesian shrinkage, no sample-size penalty, and no widening toward 50% anywhere between the directional score and the published probability.
The ONLY shrinkage in the entire system is a flat multiplicative haircut living in an AGENT PROMPT, not in code: docs/agents/digest-predict/flow/daily-predict.md line 30 — `final_confidence = min(0.95, max(0.05, computed * 0.90))`, armed only when the calibration report says 'degrading' AND trend_delta > 0.05 (plus an unconditional copy at line 25 when REGIME=TIGHTENING). This is the blanket '-10% dampening' the user sees quoted in nearly every prediction. It is arithmetically incapable of fixing the observed defect: 95% * 0.90 = 85.5%, and the 85% bucket ALSO has a 0.0% actual hit rate. A 10% shave cannot repair a bucket that is 95 points wrong. It is also applied off a calibration report that was 13 days stale at the time of this triage (see D4-adjacent staleness note).

=== D4 (ALREADY TRACKED — DO NOT RE-MINT, fold + escalate) ===
Stale evidence_scores cache serving fragment-less rows as if live. Root cause located this pass: getLatestEvidenceScore (apps/mcp-server/src/infrastructure/db/evidenceFragmentStore.ts) is `SELECT * FROM evidence_scores WHERE stock = ? ORDER BY score_date DESC LIMIT 1` with NO recency bound, while runEvidenceAccumulator only writes rows for stocks having fragments within the last 30d (and purgeExpiredFragments deletes expired ones first). A stock whose fragments all expire therefore keeps serving its LAST score row forever.
LIVE PROOF: get_evidence_summary('VPB') on 2026-08-22 returns `Score date: 2026-08-09` (13 days stale), `Bearish: 0.9500`, `Fragment count: 2`, and `(no fragments found)` — a 0.95 bearish conviction with zero surviving backing evidence, still served as current. Meanwhile ACB returns Score date: 2026-08-22 (fresh) — so this is PER-TICKER cache rot, NOT a dead cron. The get_evidence_summary tool description meanwhile advertises 'Data is at most 23 hours stale', which is false for VPB by 12 days.
This is EXACTLY the pre-existing row SPIKE-EVIDENCE-SCORE-CACHE-FRAGMENT-DECOUPLE (created 2026-07-16T17:50:39Z, still BACKLOG, next_agent=architect, zone=apps/mcp-server/) — unrouted for 37 days. Its measured cost is now known: VPB is the single worst-scoring ticker in the engine (Brier 0.9025) and its three worst predictions were all generated off this stale fragment-less 0.95 bearish row. BA/architect MUST treat that SPIKE as a sub-task of this sprint rather than re-triaging it independently.

=== ALSO ALREADY TRACKED — explicitly OUT of scope, do not re-mint ===
Recurring BCTC OCR corruption (total_assets=0 on DXG/VIC/VNM/VEA) that the user's dashboard narrative surfaces is FIX-BCTC-VALIDATION-GATE-NONBANK-ZERO-SCALE (BACKLOG, next_agent=architect). Router raised it as a hypothesis; confirmed here as a DUPLICATE of existing tracked work. Related but distinct existing rows, for BA to reconcile against rather than duplicate: FIX-FB-PREDICTION-CALIBRATION-LOOP (fb-poster-scoped, zone=agent), ALPHA-S5-TRUTH-LEDGER-BACKTEST (signal_outcomes/alerts, zone=multi), FEAT-PREDCLAIM-UPDATED-AT (audit column, zone=multi), FIX-CI-BUNTEST-167-PREDICTION-MARKET-JOB (READY, dev-mcp-server, CI red on a prediction-market test file — likely wants sequencing BEFORE this sprint touches the same area).

=== MANDATORY STATISTICAL DISCIPLINE (PO directive to BA + architect) ===
n is SMALL: 17 resolved in the 90d window, 25 all-time, and the extreme buckets are n=3 each. Therefore:
(a) DO NOT refit per-ticker or per-evidence-type coefficients on this sample, and DO NOT hard-code a sign flip for foreign_flow_institutional or for the bearish channel off 3x-repeated single-ticker misses (the VPB triple is ONE stale cache row read three times — D4 — not three independent observations, so it is nearer n=1 than n=3).
(b) D1, D2 and D3 are STRUCTURAL defects provable by code-reading and exact arithmetic (the 0.3012 identity above; the zero 'likelihood' references in calibrationReportJob). They do NOT depend on sample size for their justification and are safe to fix now.
(c) The honest near-term accuracy win is to WIDEN/SHRINK extreme confidence toward the base rate and to WIRE the recurring recalibration cadence, so accuracy improves automatically as resolved outcomes accumulate — that is what the user's 'make it more recurrent' actually requires. A one-shot coefficient rewrite is NOT the deliverable.

=== ACCEPTANCE (BA to refine into a REQ; architect owns the design) ===
AC-1: evidence_likelihood_ratios demonstrably participates in the score that produces a prediction (D1) — with the sample_size<10 -> LR=1.0 neutral-prior guard and the clampLikelihoodRatio(0.1, 5.0) bounds preserved.
AC-2: a RECURRING, scheduled path exists from calibration_snapshots back into future prediction behavior (D2), replacing the agent-prompt flat *0.90 haircut with a code-side, per-bucket or per-direction correction. The cadence itself is the deliverable, not a single re-fit.
AC-3: published confidence is shrunk toward the base rate as a function of evidence sample size / LR strength (D3); no bucket may ship at 95% off a 2-fragment score.
AC-4: no evidence score older than a defined freshness bound is EVER served as current (D4) — get_evidence_summary must degrade honestly instead of serving a 13-day-old fragment-less row, and its own description string must stop claiming '<=23 hours'.
AC-5: measured, not asserted — after the change, a re-run of the calibration report over the SAME 17 resolved historical claims must be reported alongside the old numbers. Note explicitly for QA: on n=17 a Brier improvement is NOT statistically certifiable, so AC-5 is a DIRECTIONAL sanity check + a no-regression gate, and the durable success metric is the LIVE forward-looking curve accumulating over subsequent weeks — do not let QA certify this sprint on a backtest alone.
AC-6: full existing suites stay green — 1121-likelihood-ratio-store, 1127-calibration-snapshot-store, 1128-calibration-report-job, 1129-calibration-tools, 1173-calibration-label-integration, 1392-calibration-report-diacritics.

CHAIN: ba -> architect -> pm -> dev-mcp-server -> qa. Zone owner apps/mcp-server/ = dev-mcp-server per docs/references/agent-roster.md.

backlog.status_note:

An undercounting roster makes a LIVE peer read as DEAD -> double-arm. That is exactly the already-CONFIRMED-2x failure in memory feedback_cron_standalone_step1b1_presence_absence_false_dead_double_arm.md.
  - Sibling of the recorded dashboard 'Chua tung chay' gap.

ROOT CAUSE IS UNKNOWN — DO NOT GUESS, DO NOT SHIP A FIX ON A HYPOTHESIS. Three candidate planes, measure each:
  (a) agents skipping Step 0a self-registration — countable: grep the flow docs for the Step 0a call, then diff against which agent ids ever appear as owner_agent on a session-presence row over a 24h window.
  (b) ttl_seconds 1800 expiring with no renewal hook on most families — countable: compare row created_at/heartbeat_at against 1800s for every family; cowork has a renewal hook (scripts/agents-flow/cowork-tick-preflight.sh Step 2), most do not.

Deliverable: name the plane WITH the measurement that proves it, then mint ONE follow-up FIX row. Do not fold the fix into this SPIKE.

BLOCKS-BY-COUPLING (not a hard dep): FIX-CRON-REARM-STEP1B1-LIVENESS-ORACLE-BLIND-WINDOW-FALSE-LIVE's architect brief needs the answer to decide whether the presence roster is repaired or removed from the cron-guard decision path entirely. Deliberately NOT wired as depends_on so the architect brief is not stalled — the architect may proceed with 'remove from decision path' and this SPIKE then only governs Phase A.5.

[po/triage 2026-08-26T03:48Z] FOLD -- BLAST-RADIUS ADDITION, no new row, and explicitly NOT a reopen of the Step 2.4 Axis C row (that row passed QA and is DONE_VERIFIED; the finding below is a hazard introduced by a sanctioned design, not an AC failure). Envelope 847066d1d (router, system-issue, WARN).
A NEW CONSUMER now depends on this broken oracle in its most dangerous direction. Step 2.4 Axis C (landed 4f72c694c) promotes the Phase A.5 presence roster -- a read its OWN SKILL.md labels 'advisory; non-blocking' -- into a PERMISSIVE dispatch gate: a current-period cowork-slot marker whose owner_client_session is ABSENT from the roster is skipped as 'abandoned, not live', allowing the dispatch to proceed. Presence-absence is exactly the ambiguity this SPIKE exists to measure (a live session between presence renewals reads identical to a dead one), and here the ambiguity resolves in the direction whose failure mode is a DOUBLE PUBLISH to a real channel.
WHY THIS RAISES THIS SPIKE'S VALUE: until now the roster's undercount produced conservative errors (a live session read as absent merely lost a claim). Axis C inverts the sign -- the same undercount now GRANTS a dispatch. The SPIKE's output must therefore include a directional statement, not just a count: for each consumer, does roster-absence fail safe or fail open. Two known fail-open consumers today: Step 2.4 Axis C, and FIX-CRON-REARM-STEP1B1-LIVENESS-ORACLE-BLIND-WINDOW-FALSE-LIVE (ready[], developer).
Cross-ref memory: feedback_step24_cowork_collision_probe_ttl_exceeds_cadence_daily_false_positive and feedback_router_almost_rearmed_live_peer_cron_markers_20260822 both record that heartbeat AND presence lie for one renewal cadence after a close.
