backlog.title: `architect_handoff` is a write-only orch-state field with ZERO readers fleet-wide — every architect brief reaches an implementer only if a human-equivalent hop happens to re-open it by hand
backlog.desc: Root cause behind today's FIX-SIGNAL-INBOX-... misroute (po ruling 2026-08-23T10:17:06Z). MEASURED: grepping `architect_handoff` across docs/agents/, scripts/ and .claude/ returns exactly one non-data hit — scripts/architect-20260823-orch-prose-ceiling-row-handoff.jq, the jq that WRITES it — plus stale .claude/worktrees/ copies of orch-state itself. No flow doc and no dispatch script READS it. Meanwhile docs/agents/developer/flow/main.md declares its Input (line 12) as `docs/handoffs/TASK_NNN.md with [Architect] Brownfield Findings`, and Step 0c + Step 3 both hard-require that exact path. So an architect can complete a design, write an 18KB brief, stamp architect_design_complete=true and architect_handoff=<path>, and the pointer reaches no consumer. The row then either (a) routes to pm, who re-derives the handoff by hand, or (b) routes to developer, who never learns the brief exists.
acceptance: AC-1: Name the single mechanism by which an architecture brief reaches an implementer, and make it real in the flow docs — either developer/flow/main.md Step 0c gains an architect_handoff fallback when docs/handoffs/TASK_NNN.md is absent, OR architect's own flow is required to emit docs/handoffs/TASK_*.md so the existing reader always finds one, OR architect_design_complete=true is made to force next_agent=pm. Pick ONE; do not ship two half-mechanisms.

AC-2: Negative control — construct a ready[] row with architect_handoff set, note=null, and no docs/handoffs/ file, then demonstrate the chosen mechanism surfaces the brief to the implementer. A design that only works when a handoff file already exists does not close this.

AC-3: If architect_handoff is retained, at least one live reader must exist and be exercised by a test. If it is retired, remove it from the writer jq and from any row that carries it, rather than leaving a field that looks meaningful and is not.
non_goals: Do NOT re-litigate zone routing. Both of today's briefs correctly name `developer` as the eventual zone owner for cross-service/ work; this row is about the HOP, not the OWNER.
Do not touch the direct-execute / self-closeout path in execute-tier.md:123 — it is legitimate for rows whose own note carries the spec.

backlog.title: A row can carry qa_verified_at + a full QA APPROVED record while its `status` stays DONE — deps_satisfied() then reads it as unsatisfied and silently dams every dependent chain behind it
backlog.desc: GENERALISED FROM A CONFIRMED 26-DAY OUTAGE. deps_satisfied() (scripts/lib/devteam-eligibility.jq:278-281) requires every dep to string-equal 'DONE_VERIFIED'; plain DONE is explicitly insufficient and a dep found in no lane resolves MISSING. Nothing anywhere asserts that qa_verified_at and status agree, so a partially-applied QA closeout leaves a row that LOOKS finished to every human reader and reads as unfinished to every picker. MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-23: 3 of the 15 rows in done[] carry a qa_verified_at stamp while status=DONE — TASK-COWORK-CATCHUP-2 (qa 2026-07-28T20:35:33Z), FACTORY-APP-split-assembleBriefing (qa 2026-07-28T20:17:55Z), TASK_RUNIDLE-1-AUDIT (qa 2026-08-08T23:10:08Z). Two of the three are load-bearing: CATCHUP-2 was the SOLE unsatisfied dep of TASK-COWORK-CATCHUP-3/4/5, which cascade to 6/7/8/9/10 — nine rows dammed 26 days; TASK_RUNIDLE-1-AUDIT is the sole dep of TASK_RUNIDLE-2-REDESIGN and TASK_RUNIDLE-3-STALENESS, which cascade to TASK_RUNIDLE-4-TEST and -5-VERIFY — four rows dammed 15 days and still dammed right now. po ratified CATCHUP-2 to DONE_VERIFIED this tick after RAW-verifying all 4 commits in its QA record are real ancestors of HEAD. po deliberately did NOT ratify the other two: FACTORY-APP-split-assembleBriefing and TASK_RUNIDLE-1-AUDIT have commit=none and no review_note, so their evidence is materially weaker and they need real verification, not a status flip.
acceptance: AC-1: Identify the writer that lands qa_verified_at/qa_verified_by without advancing status, and fix it so the two are written in the same transform. Note CATCHUP-2's updated_at (2026-07-28T20:39:16Z) is 3m43s AFTER its qa_verified_at — a LATER write touched the row and still did not advance status, so this is a partial application, not an interrupted one. Find that second writer.

AC-2: A guard that fails loud on any row where qa_verified_at is set and status is not in TERMINAL_SET — wired into orch-apply.sh alongside the existing lane-coherence checks, so the desync cannot be reintroduced silently.

AC-3: TASK_RUNIDLE-1-AUDIT is genuinely verified by qa (not status-flipped on trust — it has commit=none and no review_note) and, if it passes, advanced to DONE_VERIFIED, unblocking TASK_RUNIDLE-2/3 and thence 4/5. Same for FACTORY-APP-split-assembleBriefing, which blocks nothing and is therefore lower priority.

AC-4: A one-shot audit reporting every row in ANY lane whose qa_verified_at/status disagree, run once and attached to the fix — the 3 found today were found in done[] only; the same scan must cover review[], qa[] and in_progress[].
non_goals: Do NOT mass-flip the remaining two rows to DONE_VERIFIED to clear the count. The whole failure class is a status field asserting more than the evidence supports; curing it by asserting harder would be the same defect.
Do not change deps_satisfied()'s strictness — requiring DONE_VERIFIED rather than DONE is correct and is not the bug.

backlog.po_fold_20260824T2048Z:
[po/triage 2026-08-24T20:48Z — FOLD, Pipeline-A cowork-fire envelope 42ac5efee2a8 (20:21:34Z tick). NEW CONSEQUENCE, not a new count: this residue is silently pinning the adaptive-cadence controller's input.]

RE-MEASURED AT SOURCE THIS TICK, not taken from the envelope: `ls docs/signals/*.json | wc -l` = 59; excluding cowork-team-* = 38; `ls docs/signals/price_anomaly_*.json | wc -l` = 22 (this row's title says 21 — it has grown by one). Oldest is docs/signals/price_anomaly_20260702T1607.json, mtime 2 jul 18:09, i.e. 53 days, against this row's recorded 52.

THE CONSEQUENCE, which this row does not currently state and which raises it above hygiene. apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/tools/system/emitPressureStateTool.ts defines signal_backlog as the count of docs/signals/*.json EXCLUDING cowork-team-* (computeSignalBacklogFn over signalsDir). Measured live: 59 files minus 21 cowork-team-* = 38, an exact match with the value the cowork dispatcher reported in its own envelope. signal_backlog feeds signal_backlog_tier, whose thresholds are 0=low / 3=medium / 10=high. With 22 permanently-undrained price_anomaly_* files (plus the sibling residue tracked in CLEAN-SIGNALS-INBOX-COWORK-DRIFT-WINDOW-RESIDUE and CLEAN-SIGNALS-STRANDED-STATE-SWEEP-FILES-PERMANENT-DRAIN-LITTER) the floor alone is more than double the "high" threshold. signal_backlog_tier is therefore PINNED HIGH PERMANENTLY, by dead files, regardless of actual live pressure.

WHY THAT MATTERS BEYOND DISK HYGIENE: signal_backlog_tier is an INPUT to the adaptive cadence system. A control input that cannot vary is not a control input — the fleet's pressure-adaptive behaviour is running open-loop on this dimension and has been for the ~53 days this residue has existed. Nothing alerts on it, because from the controller's point of view the reading is perfectly valid. This is the same failure shape as a probe that returns a constant: it never fails, it just stops carrying information.

SCOPE ADDITION FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: the age ceiling this row asks for is still the right fix, but add an assertion that after the purge signal_backlog reflects only drainable, live signals — i.e. verify the TIER MOVES, not just that files were deleted. A purge that removes the files without re-measuring the tier would close this row while leaving the actual defect (a pinned controller input) unproven either way.

PRIORITY NOTE: currently P2. PO is not re-prioritising it unilaterally from a triage fold, but records that the justification for P2 was disk hygiene, and the justification now includes a stuck fleet-wide control input. Worth re-ranking when next touched.

backlog.note: FOUND BY PO 2026-08-23 while dispositioning TASK-COWORK-CATCHUP-3. This is a gap in the architect brief docs/architecture-briefs/2026-08-23-cowork-slot-durability-layer-inventory-and-miss-detection.md itself, not in any row it minted. MEASURED, NOT INFERRED: grepped the whole repo for catchup_raw / catchup_eligible / catchup-check across *.sh *.js *.md *.ts. Every hit is a PRODUCER, a spec, or a doc. docs/agents/cowork-team/flow/catchup-check.md does not exist (brief S4 says so and ls confirms). cowork-tick-preflight.sh Step 6.5 and cowork-guaranteed-slot-firer.sh were never wired (they were CATCHUP-4 and CATCHUP-5, both BLOCKED by po this tick). There is no consumer of catchup_eligible anywhere in the codebase. THE GAP: brief item 4 (TASK-COWORK-CATCHUP-SCOPE-PREDICATE) replaces cowork-catchup-predicate.js:209 'if (!sl.guaranteed) continue;' with a catchup_scope check and sets it true for refine-bctc-*/bctc-analyst-*, on the correct reasoning that data-refinement jobs have no publish-date semantics so a late run is a correct run. Brief item 3 (TASK-COWORK-SCHEDULE-ONMISS-AND-SCOPE) adds on_miss: 'catchup' | 'skip_and_record'. Both are policy declarations. Neither mints an actuator, and the brief's AC-3 asserts only that the predicate's OUTPUT is right — 'the live matcher's catchup_raw contains the refine-bctc-* / bctc-analyst-* slots with catchup_eligible:true when late' — never that anything fires. So on the day item 4 ships, the system will correctly compute that refine-bctc-slot-1 is catch-up-eligible, declare on_miss:'catchup' for it, and then do nothing, forever, silently. WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: that is precisely the failure this whole cluster exists to fix. TASK-COWORK-CATCHUP-2 shipped catchup_raw on 2026-07-28 and PO's own note on CATCHUP-3 dated 2026-08-06 records the cost — 'catchup_raw has been correctly computed since CATCHUP-2 shipped and is consumed by NOTHING' — with a live example of a recoverable missed chef-morning dish that nothing recovered. If no actuator exists, the widening does not fix the symptom that raised the row. ARCHITECT DECIDES WHICH: (i) name a minimal actuator and scope it — plausibly a narrow extension of TASK-COWORK-CATCHUP-4/5 restricted to catchup_scope slots, with no publish-date dishes and no FR-5 miss-record layer (that is now TASK-COWORK-MISSED-FIRE-AUDIT's job), which is why those two rows are BLOCKED-pending-re-spec rather than cancelled; or (ii) rule explicitly that catchup_scope is diagnostic-only, feeding TASK-COWORK-MISSED-FIRE-AUDIT's counts and nothing else, and amend the brief to say so — a legitimate answer, but it must be WRITTEN DOWN, because on_miss:'catchup' as a config value that fires nothing is a false promise of exactly the kind brief S3 blames for 'guaranteed' predicting nothing. Do not let this be settled by silence. CONSTRAINT IF (i): brief R2 — every guaranteed-slot flow already has a published-marker task_claim gate (FR-P2-7); reuse it, never add a second competing dedup. And brief R5 — the eligible branch of this predicate has never executed in production, so any actuator's tests must cover it end-to-end.

backlog.note: LIVE INCIDENT, 2026-08-23, full causal chain measured. 10:17Z a po session correctly ratified TASK-COWORK-CATCHUP-2 DONE -> DONE_VERIFIED (it already carried qa_verified_at=2026-07-28T20:35:33Z; only .status had lagged). That correctly flipped deps_satisfied false->true for TASK-COWORK-CATCHUP-3/4/5. 10:24:37Z the dev-team tick's Ready-Lane Consumer claimed TASK-COWORK-CATCHUP-3 and pinned .head to it with next_agent=developer. Every field RLC evaluated was accurate: status READY, deps satisfied, not supervised, not plan_only, not an epic wrapper, inline next_agent=developer, priority P0. RLC did nothing wrong. But that row's own status_note, written earlier the same day, read 'CONTRADICTED 2026-08-23 by architect brief ... Brief says do NOT schedule this as the fix. Needs PO disposition (cancel vs rescope) - pm did not cancel unilaterally.' The disposition existed, was correct, and was structurally invisible. Only the router declining to spawn developer stopped a developer from building a deliverable measured to recover zero slots. ROOT CAUSE: there is no machine-readable way to say 'do not dispatch this, a human/PO decision is pending or has been made'. status BLOCKED is the closest primitive but it overloads 'waiting on a dependency' with 'ruled out on the merits', and pm deliberately declined to use it here precisely because cancelling unilaterally was not pm's call. So the only place left to put the ruling was prose. THIS IS A KNOWN FAMILY, NOT A ONE-OFF: the same shape already produced the PROSE-SEQUENCING and DETAIL-DEFERRED gates, and the same underlying pathology (a decision recorded in prose that no predicate reads) is separately tracked as FIX-ARCHITECTHANDOFF-DEAD-FIELD-ZERO-READERS-STRANDS-EVERY-ARCHITECT-BRIEF, where grep found the architect_handoff field has zero readers fleet-wide and only the jq that writes it. The correct fix is a machine-readable disposition flag honoured by all four gates, NOT another hand-correction. DESIGN INPUT, ALREADY EXERCISED THIS TICK: po stamped disposition / disposition_reason_code / do_not_reopen / superseded_by_brief / superseded_by_rows onto the cancelled TASK-COWORK-CATCHUP-3 (now in archive[]) as a straw-man shape. Treat those as a proposal to critique, not a standard — nothing reads them yet, which is exactly the dead-field trap this row exists to close. Whatever shape is chosen must be READ by scripts/devteam-backlog-claim-ready-lane-consumer.jq and the BOUNDED-1/SLS/DRS predicates in scripts/lib/devteam-eligibility.jq, and the gate must be proven by executing the predicates against a fixture, never by reading them (cf. feedback_flow_doc_veto_manufactures_pass_read_spec_before_blaming_script). SCOPE NOTE: a 'pending PO disposition' state is worth distinguishing from a 'ruled out' state — the first should park a row and surface it in PO's own tick, the second should refuse dispatch permanently. CATCHUP-3 spent hours in the first state with no surfacing mechanism at all, which is why a dev-team tick found it before PO did.

backlog.desc: ROOT CAUSE READ AT SOURCE 2026-08-23T11:57Z, not inferred. scripts/agents-flow/notebook-auto-prune.sh emit_dropped_newest_dated_section_signal() (~line 358-386) builds the signal JSON with a bare `cat > "$sig_file" <<EOF` heredoc and interpolates FOUR shell variables directly into JSON *numeric* slots with no quoting and no numeric coercion: $drop_line, $SECTION_COUNT, $NON_SENTINEL_SECTION_COUNT, $SENTINEL_SECTION_COUNT. When any of them holds a multi-line or non-numeric value the emitted file is invalid JSON. LIVE PROOF, two files, both still on disk: docs/signals/notebook-prune-dropped-newest-docs-agent-memory-notebooks-dev-mcp-server-md-2026-08-22T232534Z.json and ...232535Z.json. Both render `"sentinel_section_count": 0` followed on the NEXT LINE by a stray `0,` — i.e. $SENTINEL_SECTION_COUNT contained the two-line value '0\n0'. jq reports 'Expected separator between values at line 14'. Every drain pass skips them; this tick was the 5th consecutive skip. They will never self-drain and will never stop being retried. SECOND, COMPOUNDING DEFECT: the emitter never validates its own output — no `jq . "$sig_file"` after the write, and the heredoc is `|| true`, so a malformed or failed write is indistinguishable from success. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN TWO STRAY FILES: this emitter exists solely to satisfy AC-6 of FIX-NOTEBOOK-AUTOPRUNE-ROLLING-SECTIONS-BYTE-COUNTED-BUT-UNDROPPABLE, whose stated purpose is 'the drop is NEVER silent' after occurrences 1/3/5 were caught only by luck. An unparseable signal is functionally identical to no signal, so on this path the guarantee is inverted while appearing to hold — and it leaves permanent undrainable litter as the only trace.

backlog.title: depends_on/depends/blocked_by accept a free-form prose sentence as a dependency id — the whole sentence becomes ONE dep id that resolves MISSING forever, and Stage 1g reports it as merely NON-FATAL, so 2 live rows sat permanently undispatchable and read as legitimately blocked from every angle
backlog.status_note: ROOT CAUSE: as_dep_array (scripts/lib/devteam-eligibility.jq:133-137) normalizes a bare string to a 1-element array — correct for a single id, catastrophic for a sentence. The two failure modes are indistinguishable on the board: a prose-glued dep looks exactly like a real block. MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-23T12:3xZ across all 7 lanes: 212 dep ids on 127 rows, exactly 3 contain whitespace, and whitespace is a perfect discriminator (zero false positives on the other 209). AC1: TaskSchema must reject any depends_on/depends/blocked_by element matching /\s/ — a dep id never contains whitespace. AC2: promote that specific class from Stage 1g NON-FATAL to a Stage 1 FATAL abort in scripts/orch-validate.mjs; genuine MISSING-but-well-formed ids stay NON-FATAL (they are a legitimate transient state — 12 such rows live today). backlog.title: fb-market-poster WEEKLY_PREDICTION (Sunday) has been 100% suppressed for 6 consecutive Sundays: the weekend publish-once marker keys on PERIOD_SAT (Saturday date) shared by BOTH modes, so any Saturday WEEKLY_RECAP publish deterministically blocks Sunday's separate deliverable. The shared key is an unauthorized deviation from this gate's own approved fix_spec, which specified VN_DATE.
backlog.root_cause: SPEC DEVIATION, not a design tradeoff. The originating row FIX-FB-WEEKEND-DEDUP-GATE (archive/backlog-detail.json, created 2026-06-30T17:28:32Z by po, sprint FB-POSTER-LAUNCHD-FIRER, owner cowork-refactory-expert) approved this fix_spec verbatim: "claim task_claim(task_id='published:fb-weekend:'+VN_DATE, ...)" with verification_gate "a second weekend firing IN THE SAME VN-DATE no-ops". Its root_cause names the threat as the launchd firer and the cowork */15 dispatcher double-firing the SAME day. The implementation (commit 11e10fd20, 2026-06-30) instead shipped PERIOD_SAT = (VN_DOW==0 ? VN_DATE-1d : VN_DATE), widening the dedup period from ONE day to TWO, and wrote the justifying prose into the flow docs as if it were the requirement: weekly-recap.md:44, weekly-prediction.md:47, daily.md:81 all assert "Both Saturday and Sunday of the same weekend share a single dedup key based on the Saturday date. This prevents double-posting across Sat/Sun." That prose is the defect self-documenting; it was never an approved product intent. The originating row never left REVIEW and its QA gate FB-LAUNCHD-QA-FIRE-VERIFY-DEDUP is still BACKLOG, so the deviation was never caught.
backlog.evidence: PO read the source and the archive rather than trusting the reporter. (1) The two modes are non-substitutable BY WRITTEN CONTRACT: weekly-recap.md:8 states "EXPLICITLY NO prediction for the coming week. NO 'Du doan' section." Saturday's post therefore cannot carry Sunday's deliverable; suppressing Sunday deletes the content outright, it does not merge it. (2) main.md declares a 3-mode agent (DAILY Mon-Fri / WEEKLY_RECAP Sat / WEEKLY_PREDICTION Sun) with a VN_DOW MODE ROUTER; weekly-prediction.md is a ~200L sub-flow with its own TNB 6-layer walk, T-45 gate, two-bucket conviction list, its own privacy gate STEP 4d and its own digest-predict portfolio-thesis extraction filter. (3) The catch-up hypothesis is REFUTED BY CONFIG: cowork-schedule.json ._dish_type_catchup_config.fb_weekly_post.catchup_max_lateness_minutes = 120. A Sunday fire is ~24h after Saturday's, far outside a 2h catch-up window, so the Sunday cron leg cannot be a catch-up for a missed Saturday - it is a scheduled second deliverable. (4) Historical record: Sundays 2026-06-07 / 06-14 / 06-21 / 06-28 / 07-12 all published genuine 'Du doan tuan toi' posts, and the notebook at commit 3e08bf39d logs BOTH '2026-07-11 (Saturday WEEKLY_RECAP) Status: published' AND '2026-07-12 (Sunday WEEKLY_PREDICTION) Status: published' as two normal successful cycles in the SAME weekend. (5) Since 2026-07-12: SIX consecutive Sundays with zero post - 07-19, 07-26, 08-02, 08-09, 08-16, 08-23 - while Saturdays published on five of those six weekends (07-18, 07-25, 08-08, 08-15, 08-22; the 08-01/08-02 weekend lost both legs to the known host-suspension gap). (6) Live today 2026-08-23: published:fb-weekend:2026-08-22 held by session 2855be92-98b3-449d-a570-d23b79fc1742, claimed 2026-08-22T13:33:44Z, ttl 100800s, expires 2026-08-23T17:33:44Z - still live across today's cowork dispatcher fire at 13:18:35Z and across the router's 13:35Z manual dispatch attempt. Sunday's own STEP 0a computes MARKER_KEY = published:fb-weekend:2026-08-22, an EXACT match, so the agent self-exits no-op before any data gathering.
backlog.fix_spec: Revert to the approved spec: MARKER_KEY = "published:fb-weekend:" + VN_DATE in BOTH weekly-recap.md STEP 0a and weekly-prediction.md STEP 0a. VERIFIED SITE LIST (line numbers live-checked 2026-08-23T13:47Z, re-grep before editing): PERIOD_SAT is derived at weekly-recap.md:47 and weekly-prediction.md:50, consumed in MARKER_KEY at recap:48 / prediction:51, echoed in the telegram + EXIT strings at recap:63,65 and prediction:66,68, AND referenced again in each sub-flow's Phase-2 claim section at recap:218 / prediction:274 — that last pair is where the marker is actually CLAIMED and is easy to miss when editing only STEP 0a. Delete the derivation and all three copies of the justifying prose (recap:44, prediction:47, daily.md:81) — do not preserve them as historical note, they read as normative and that is exactly how they caused this. NOTE the target shape already exists and is correct one file away: daily.md:57 is `MARKER_KEY = "published:fb-daily:" + VN_DATE`, and the approved fix_spec said to mirror it verbatim ("Mirror main.md STEP 0a EXACTLY (same kind, same ttl, same VN-DATE derivation)"). This is a REVERT TO AN ALREADY-APPROVED SPEC, not a new design: it needs no agents-architect ruling and must NOT wait on the P0 sibling.
backlog.acceptance: AC-1 Sunday WEEKLY_PREDICTION runs to completion and writes docs/social/fb-post-<Sunday VN date>.md on a weekend whose Saturday WEEKLY_RECAP already published. AC-2 no regression of the guard the gate was actually built for: a SECOND fire on the SAME VN date (launchd firer + cowork dispatcher overlap) still no-ops via the exact-match marker. AC-3 the agent-side STEP 0a comparison stays EXACT-match on task_id (it already is) - do not convert it to a prefix match, that is the sibling row's surface and would re-import its defect. AC-4 the three prose copies asserting the shared Sat/Sun key are gone; grep for 'share a single dedup key' across docs/agents/fb-market-poster/ returns 0. AC-5 cowork-schedule.json .slots[fb-weekend].publish_date_basis = 'vn_date_saturday_anchor' is corrected to a per-VN-date basis - it is a THIRD site of the same conflation and would keep the wrong publish date on the Sunday file. ROUTING NOTE for AC-5: that file's own ._maintained_by reads 'agent-father (via architect brief only)', so this AC may need the brief route rather than a direct edit; agent-father escalates rather than editing in place if that constraint still binds. AC-6 the router's Step 2.4 prefix probe key shape 'published:' + slot_id + ':' still matches the new key - VN_DATE keys preserve it, per-mode keys such as published:fb-weekend-recap: would NOT and would silently blind the collision guard; that is why the per-mode axis is rejected here.
backlog.po_ruling_20260823T1340Z: RULING: Sunday WEEKLY_PREDICTION IS A REAL DELIVERABLE. The router surfaced this as a genuine tension between the MODE ROUTER and the 'intentional shared key' prose and asked PO to rule. The MODE ROUTER, the two-day cron, the two sub-flows and the two distinct post titles are all authorized and correct; the PERIOD_SAT key and its three prose copies are the deviation. THIS row is the AGENT's own STEP 0a EXACT-match self-gate against a CURRENT-period marker, and it kills the CRON path - the path that actually fires every Sunday. None of that row's three ratified axes (A exact-period-key, B TTL<=cadence, C stale-owner presence check) repairs this one: A leaves Sat and Sun sharing the identical key so it is a no-op here; B and C would unblock Sunday only incidentally and only when the Saturday holder session happens to be dead. Folding would bury an S-sized revert inside a P0 carrying 6 ACs, 3 rejected axes and a standing PO rescope ruling. The two are cross-linked and SHOULD be reviewed by the same reader, but they ship independently and in either order. Sequencing consequence worth stating: once this row lands the VN_DATE key, fb-weekend joins the exact class the P0 row describes (28h TTL over a 24h key period), so the P0 fix becomes the follow-on for fb-weekend MANUAL dispatch - it is not a prerequisite.

backlog.title: Add a --destamp <slot_id> <prior_value> mode to scripts/agents-flow/cowork-write-last-fired.js so rolling a slot's last_fired BACK stops being a hand-edit of docs/data/cowork-schedule.json
backlog.note:
MINTED by po 2026-08-23T14:10Z, endorsed by qa in the 2026-08-23 review-lane drain and not minted there (scripts/ is outside agent-father's commit_zone).

TODAY: the script is forward-only by contract. Its header states 'Monotonic forward-only: a slot last_fired never decreases (sibling-fresher-stamp guard)' and it reads slot ids off process.argv.slice(2) with no flags at all. That guard is correct for the Step 5b hot path it was written for. But reverting a bad stamp - which happens whenever a dispatcher fires against a slot it should not have, or a test/dry-run leaks a real stamp - therefore has NO tool, and is done by hand-editing docs/data/cowork-schedule.json each time.

WHY THAT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING MERELY TEDIOUS: the script's own header documents two production corruptions caused by hand-rolled inline implementations of this exact write, both silent (a jq needle-binding bug that clobbered sibling slots, and a zsh word-splitting bug that wrote an unchanged file and reported write-OK). Hand-editing the schedule to roll a stamp back is the same hazard on the same file, just in the other direction, and it is currently the only available method.

ACCEPTANCE:
  1. New mode: `node scripts/agents-flow/cowork-write-last-fired.js --destamp <slot_id> <prior_value>`. Exactly one slot per invocation - no multi-slot destamp, because a batched rollback is precisely the shape of the jq needle-binding corruption the header warns about.
  2. <prior_value> must be ISO8601 UTC matching the existing FIRED_AT regex, or a literal `null` to clear the stamp entirely.
  3. The forward-only monotonic guard is BYPASSED for --destamp and for nothing else. Default argv-only invocation keeps its current behaviour byte-for-byte.
  4. Refuse loudly (exit 2, the script's existing caller-error code) on: unknown slot_id, missing <prior_value>, a value that is neither valid ISO8601 nor null, or --destamp combined with positional slot ids.
  5. Same atomic tmp+rename write path and same JSON stdout envelope {ok, error, fired_at, updated} as the forward path - do not add a second write implementation.
  6. A destamp is a corrective action, so it must be visible: print the prior value it overwrote to stdout, not just the new one.
  7. Update the owning flow doc docs/agents/cowork-team/flow/last-fired.md with the new mode and an explicit note that it is for corrections only, never for the Step 5b hot path.
  8. Test both directions, including the guard: a forward stamp on a slot with a fresher sibling stamp must still be refused AFTER this change.

backlog.title: Signal type namespace is OPEN but signal-type-coverage-guard enforces a hand-maintained CLOSED allowlist — 5th CI red of this shape
backlog.status_note:
ROOT CAUSE of a recurring CI red, filed by po 2026-08-23T14:42Z after closing the 5th instance. Design question, plan_only — architect rules, does not implement.

THE SHAPE: any producer may emit a docs/signals/*.json with an arbitrary `type` string (open namespace, no registry, no producer-side validation). scripts/audits/guard-signal-type-coverage.sh then fails CI if a type present in dev_team_idle_chain.pending_triage_inbox[] has no matching row in the Pipeline-A table of docs/agents/po/flow/triage-signals.md (closed allowlist, hand-maintained, in a PO flow doc). So every NEW producer type reds main exactly once, costs one hand-minted FIX row, one agent-father dispatch, and one table-row edit. This is not a bug in any single producer; it is a missing contract between the producer side and the guard.

EVIDENCE OF RECURRENCE (5 rows, all identical in shape, all minted by the guard itself): flow_actuator_fix, system-issue, sprint_registry_unresolved_journal_ids, notebook_prune_dropped_newest_dated_section (all four now satisfied and archived by po 2026-08-23), plus auto-push-abort (live, currently reddening main — FIX-SIGNAL-TYPE-ROUTING-GAP-auto-push-abort). Prior analysis: project_signalrow_type_open_namespace_vs_closed_allowlist_20260813 already recorded 4x redispatch to architect without a design landing.

SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFECT IN THE SAME GUARD — the measurement is queue-shaped, not coverage-shaped. The guard's input is the CONTENTS of pending_triage_inbox[], but PO's Step 0-SIG owns an unconditional CLEAR of that same inbox as its last action every cycle (docs/agents/po/flow/triage-signals.md, FIX-TRIAGE-INBOX-CLEAR-OWNERSHIP-PO-SELF-READ). Therefore PO doing its job turns the guard green with the routing table unchanged, and the gap silently persists until the next envelope of that type arrives. That is the mechanism behind feedback_devteam_drain_step_can_itself_turn_signal_type_guard_red (recorded there as CI-green/local-red divergence; the inverse — coverage-red masked as green — is the same root and is worse, because nothing reports it). A coverage guard must measure the doc against a type REGISTRY, never against whatever happens to be sitting in a transient queue.

DIRECTIONS TO EVALUATE (architect picks, do not treat as a spec): (1) a committed signal-type registry (docs/data/signal-type-registry.json) that producers validate against at emit time and the guard reads as its input instead of the inbox — closes both defects at once; (2) keep the open namespace but make an unknown type a non-fatal WARN plus an auto-minted row, so a new producer never reds main; (3) generate the Pipeline-A table from the registry so the doc cannot drift. Also settle the ownership question: the allowlist currently lives in a PO flow doc, which makes every occurrence agent-father-dispatched (agent-father fails is_dev_role, so these rows are never auto-dispatchable — a structural cost of the current placement).

DELIVERABLE: architecture brief with a rows-to-mint section. Do not implement from this row.
backlog.po_evidence_20260825T1230Z: 6th INSTANCE, and this one isolates the producer. Measured live at 2026-08-25T12:40Z by hand-replaying the guard's read-only extractor against the Pipeline-A type column of docs/agents/po/flow/triage-signals.md (28 routed types) — the mutating script itself was deliberately NOT run, per FIX-GUARD-SIGNAL-TYPE-COVERAGE-CHECK-FLAG-MISLEADING-NOT-DRYRUN. Inbox depth 29, 15 distinct types, 7 UNROUTED: root-cause-confirmed, root-cause-corrected, root-cause-mechanism-found, wiring-gap-measured, flow-wiring-gap-controlled, cowork-tick-telemetry, notebook_undroppable_remainder_over_cap_breach. THE FINDING: SIX of those seven come from ONE producer, cowork-team, and every one is a fresh type minted for a single report — root-cause-confirmed / root-cause-corrected / root-cause-mechanism-found are three type names for THREE CONSECUTIVE REVISIONS OF THE SAME INVESTIGATION (07:42Z / 07:58Z / 12:15Z, all on the cycle-snapshot key derivation), not three kinds of signal. That is the open-namespace failure in its purest observable form: the producer is naming the CONTENT, not the KIND, so a closed allowlist can never converge no matter how many table rows agent-father adds. The 7th (notebook_undroppable_remainder_over_cap_breach) is the ordinary rename case and is already separately filed as FIX-SIGNAL-TYPE-ROUTING-GAP-notebook-undroppable-remainder-over-cap-breach. All 12 envelopes carrying these 7 types were HELD BACK from this tick's inbox CLEAR so the CI guard stays honestly red — note they were fully TRIAGED (folded/minted) first, so the hold-back costs nothing but inbox depth.

[ops 2026-08-23T14:58Z] BLOCKED ON ROOT CREDENTIALS — NOT APPLIED. (Lane status left TODO because the validator only permits READY|TODO in ready[]; the real state is blocked, described here.)
AC-1 DONE (schedule derived from data, not guessed). Union of the 8 guaranteed:true slots in docs/data/cowork-schedule.json, read via jq, verbatim cron -> local clock:
  05:15 Mon-Fri (chef-morning) | 08:45 Mon-Fri (chef-eod) | 09:15 Mon-Fri (fb-daily) | 13:13 Sat+Sun (fb-weekend) | 13:47 Sun (digest-sunday) | 17:30 DAILY (digest-daily) | 19:45 DAILY (chef-evening) | 20:13 DAILY (tnb-audit)

Nothing in the ops tool grant can apply this; it needs a human at the keyboard or an authorised sudoers entry.
EXACT COMMAND TO RUN (derived, ready to paste):
  sudo pmset repeat wakeorpoweron MTWRFSU 05:10:00
AC-3 REVERT COMMAND: sudo pmset repeat cancel
AC-2 VERIFY AFTER APPLYING: pmset -g sched   (must list a "Repeating power events" wake line; it is EMPTY right now — captured as the pre-state baseline at 2026-08-23T14:05Z, output was zero lines).
*** AC-1 vs AC-2 DESIGN CONFLICT FOUND — the task as written cannot be fully satisfied, flagging instead of quietly shipping a partial. *** `pmset repeat` accepts exactly ONE repeating wake event (one time + one day-set). It therefore CANNOT cover a union of 8 distinct times; AC-1 asks for the union, AC-2 asks for a single repeat entry. 05:10:00 is the defensible choice (5 min before the EARLIEST slot 05:15) but it only guarantees wakefulness for that first slot. backlog.title: QA-Drain head-decoupled call site ends its orch-apply pipe with `|| true` and has no retry, so a genuine CAS exit-2 abort is discarded and the tick degrades to a silent no-op
backlog.desc: VERIFIED AT SOURCE by po 2026-08-24: docs/agents/dev-team/flow/main.md § Review-Lane QA-Drain — Head-Decoupled Invocation (jump:qa-drain-headdecoupled) runs `jq ... -f "$PROJECT_ROOT/scripts/devteam-review-claim-qa-drain.jq" docs/data/orch/orch-state.json | bash "$PROJECT_ROOT/scripts/orch-apply.sh" || true` and then reads picked_batch back from the live file. orch-apply.sh documents exit 2 as 'CAS mtime mismatch — concurrent writer detected; caller should retry' (scripts/orch-apply.sh:68) and its own header says the caller should retry — but `|| true` discards that exit status entirely and there is no retry at this site. Today the bug is mostly latent because the CAS window itself is too narrow to fire (see FIX-ORCHAPPLY-CAS-BASELINE-CAPTURED-AFTER-CALLER-JQ-READ); the moment that row lands and CAS starts firing correctly, this line becomes an active silent-drop: the abort is swallowed, picked_batch comes back empty, and the tick produces a no-op indistinguishable from 'nothing eligible'. Raised by dev-team as ROOT CAUSE 2 of the 2026-08-23T21:37Z incident CORRECTION — 'real, separate, same line'. Deliberately NOT dep-gated on the orch-apply row: dropping `|| true` and adding retry-on-exit-2 is independently correct today.
backlog.generic_mandate: Handle exit 2 explicitly at this call site: retry-on-exit-2 with a bounded budget, and log loudly when the budget is exhausted. Do not blanket-remove `|| true` from every pipe in the file without checking each site's own semantics — audit the sibling sites and state the verdict per site.
ac: AC-1 The qa-drain-headdecoupled orch-apply pipe no longer swallows a nonzero exit. Exit 2 triggers a bounded retry; a non-2 nonzero exit is logged, never silently ignored.

AC-3 Audit the sibling `|| true` orch-apply pipes in this same file (at minimum § Review-Lane SECONDARY-Drain's own pipe) and record a per-site verdict — fix or justified-as-is. Do not silently generalize.
AC-4 NEGATIVE CONTROL: a normal exit-0 tick behaves exactly as today, no extra spawn and no extra board write.

(1) TIER-1, _t1_latest_notebook_ts() at :217-238: the loop flushes the PREVIOUS section's timestamp into last_ts on each '## c' heading and keeps whichever tier-1 section came LAST IN FILE ORDER. backlog.status_note:
ARM A (router, 2026-08-26T07:05Z) — CAUSE LOCATED + a SECOND, SHARPER CONSEQUENCE than the V1-join one this row's title records. All facts below RAW-verified by direct jq/sed reads of the live files this cycle, never from an agent return.

CAUSE. `docs/agents/system-auditor/flow/main.md:57-59` is the flow's ONLY mandated invocation of the durability sweep, and it passes ONLY `--project-root`:
  DURABILITY_SWEEP_TRACE=$(bash scripts/auditor-durability-sweep.sh --project-root "$PROJECT_ROOT" 2>&1)
It never passes `--cycle-tag`. `scripts/auditor-durability-sweep.sh` DOES accept the flag (arg-parse :134) and forwards it to all three of its emit call sites (:274, :321, :374) as `${CYCLE_TAG:+--cycle-tag "$CYCLE_TAG"}` — a conditional expansion that SILENTLY OMITS the flag when CYCLE_TAG is empty rather than erroring. Net effect: every signal the durability sweep has ever emitted carries audit_cycle_tag:null BY CONSTRUCTION, on every cycle, since that script shipped.

WHY THIS SITE AND NOT THE OTHERS (this is a retrofit-then-regress gap, not an oversight in the original fix). main.md's own header changelog records FIX-AUDIT-OUTPUT-CONTRACT-SIGNALQUEUE-ROWS-WRITTEN-SELFREPORT-MISMATCH (2026-08-05, +5L) retrofitting `--cycle-tag "$FIRE_TASK_ID"` to "all 5 emit-audit-signal.sh/audit-output-contract.sh call sites in this file". The durability-sweep call site was added LATER — 2026-08-15, FIX-AUDITOR-DURABILITY-STEP0B-DETECTION redispatch 2 — and was never brought under that convention. Any future emit call site added to this flow will regress the same way; nothing enforces the convention.

SECOND CONSEQUENCE — a SHIPPED GUARD IS SILENTLY INERT. `scripts/emit-audit-signal.sh` carries a cycle-scoped idempotency short-circuit, `_e3_already_emitted_this_cycle "$DEDUP_KEY" "$CYCLE_TAG"` (run_emit_signal, ~:805-813), shipped as FIX-AUDITOR-B12-DOUBLE-INVOKE-EMIT-MARKER-LOSS expressly so a same-cycle repeat produces "ZERO new agent_signals rows and ZERO new signal_queue rows" (that script's own header, :73-77). It matches on the PAIR (dedup_key, cycle_tag). With cycle_tag empty it can never match, so the guard is a structural NO-OP for every durability-sweep emit — and nothing prints a marker saying the guard was disabled.

OBSERVED LIVE, 2026-08-26, DATA-tier fire 06:56:04Z. That cycle double-invoked its battery, so the durability sweep ran twice and wrote TWO signal_queue rows where the guard should have allowed one:
  sys-20260826T065952-3c3e  ts=2026-08-26T06:59:52Z
  sys-20260826T070016-7c23  ts=2026-08-26T07:00:16Z
Identical type=auditor_cycle_missing, identical dedup_key=auditor-cycle-missing:tier2:2026-08-26T04:00Z, identical summary, both severity=WARN status=NEW to=po, both audit_cycle_tag:null. Both still live in .signal_queue.rows[] as of this write — deliberately NOT deleted here (detection-only; the duplicate is the evidence).

NARRATION TRAP — record this, it will mislead the next reader. The second invocation printed `[emit-signal] SKIP-dedup dedup_key=... last_sent=2026-08-26T06:59:52Z id=sys-20260826T070016-7c23`, and the auditor read that as "the duplicate was suppressed". It was NOT. SKIP-dedup gates E-2 (send_telegram) ONLY — emit-audit-signal.sh:79 ("success, dedup-skip (Telegram gated)") and :103-104 ("the 7-day LEDGER gates E-2 ONLY") both say so — the E-3 signal_queue row IS written on that path by design, and the marker even prints the NEW row's id, which reads exactly like a reference to the pre-existing one. The marker that would have meant real suppression is SKIP-duplicate-invocation, which never printed. Any consumer treating SKIP-dedup as "no row written" will under-count signal_queue writes.

AC-(a) the durability-sweep call site in main.md passes `--cycle-tag "$FIRE_TASK_ID"` like the other 5; after the change a durability-sweep-emitted row carries a NON-NULL audit_cycle_tag.
AC-(b) a cycle invoking auditor-durability-sweep.sh twice with the same dedup_key yields EXACTLY ONE signal_queue row, the second invocation printing SKIP-duplicate-invocation.
AC-(c) decide whether emit-audit-signal.sh should fail loud (or synthesize a per-process cycle id) when --cycle-tag is absent instead of silently degrading its own anti-double-invoke guard to a no-op. An empty cycle_tag currently disables a shipped guard with no marker recording that it happened — the same invisibility class this row's parent fix was written to close.

--- ARM B (2026-08-26T07:26:04Z DATA cycle) — THIRD consequence of the null tag: it destroys the ability to tell a DELIBERATE re-fire from a DEFECTIVE duplicate ---

ARM A named two consequences of main.md:57-59 omitting --cycle-tag (broken V1 join; inert B12
guard). This cycle exposed a third, and it cost a near-miss false filing by the router.

LIVE DATA. dedup_key "auditor-cycle-missing:tier2:2026-08-26T04:00Z" now has THREE signal_queue
rows, ALL with audit_cycle_tag=null:
  sys-20260826T065952-3c3e  06:59:52Z  READ
  sys-20260826T070016-7c23  07:00:16Z  READ
  sys-20260826T072829-0660  07:28:29Z  NEW
Rows 1+2 are 24s apart = the SAME-cycle double-invoke (the real defect, ARM A).
Row 3 is a DIFFERENT cycle, 28 min later, and is CORRECT — emit-audit-signal.sh:104-115 declares
the cross-cycle re-fire deliberate: "E-1 and E-3 ALWAYS fire regardless of ledger state ... a
persisting finding must keep landing a fresh row every cycle even while its Telegram stays muted",
and _e3_already_emitted_this_cycle "never suppresses a legitimate cross-cycle re-fire".

THE COST. With audit_cycle_tag populated, these three rows separate mechanically: two share a tag
(duplicate), one differs (legitimate). With the tag null on all three, the ONLY discriminator left
is hand-correlating ts against known fire ticks. The router did exactly that, initially misread the
triple as an unguarded-dedup defect spanning 9 keys, and was one step from filing against
FIX-EMITSIGNAL-DEDUPKEY-GRAMMAR-UNVALIDATED-CALLER-FREETEXT-DEFEATS-7D-WINDOW. Reading the spec
header stopped it. A future reader without that reflex files the false row.

SCOPE. 37 of 75 live signal_queue rows carry audit_cycle_tag=null; 38 carry a tag. Nine distinct
dedup_keys hold 2-3 rows each. For every null-tagged group, deliberate-vs-duplicate is currently
unresolvable from the data alone.

AC-(d) ADD: once --cycle-tag is passed at every call site, add a one-line note to the emit-signal
header stating that audit_cycle_tag is the discriminator between a deliberate cross-cycle re-fire
and a same-cycle duplicate — the two are indistinguishable without it, and that ambiguity has
already produced one near-miss false finding (2026-08-26T07:26Z router cycle).

backlog.title: narrativeTruthProbeAdapters foreign-flow probe emits two 'Insufficient foreign flow data...' notes that match NONE of the 10 tool_null_markers, so classifyVerdict grades an honest NULL as NON_NULL and the gate emits a spurious narrative_contradiction against the agent
backlog.root_cause: TWO probe branches compose an honest-gap note whose wording is not in the SSOT marker list, and the classifier has no other way to recognise a gap. narrativeTruthProbeAdapters.ts:107 returns `Insufficient foreign flow data for ${ticker}: only ${history.length} row(s) found.` (the 1-row branch) and :114 returns `Insufficient foreign flow data for ${ticker}: analysis returned null.` (the analyzeForeignFlow-returned-null branch). docs/data/claim-tool-map.json .tool_null_markers holds exactly 10 entries: khong du du lieu / khong co du lieu / chua co du lieu / khong tim thay du lieu / not found in database / period(s) not found / insufficient data / no data available / not enough data / en attente. The nearest miss is 'insufficient data', which is NOT a substring of 'Insufficient foreign flow data' — the words 'foreign flow' sit between them. verdictClassifier.ts classifyVerdict() flattens the probe response to text and returns NULL only on empty text or a case-insensitive substring hit against that list; with no hit it falls through to NON_NULL, which the gate reads as 'the tool returned real data' and therefore as a contradiction of the agent's absence claim. The defect is a WORDING/SSOT coupling, not a logic error in either component taken alone.
backlog.evidence: (1) SOURCE, re-read this tick, not taken from the dispatch: the two offending template literals are at narrativeTruthProbeAdapters.ts:107 and :114 — the dispatch named only :107, so the row is one site wider than reported. (2) NEGATIVE CONTROLS IN THE SAME FILE PROVE THIS IS A PER-STRING GAP AND NOT A BROKEN CLASSIFIER: the same function's :101 branch returns 'No data available for ${ticker}: foreign investor volume has not been collected yet.' which DOES contain marker 8 ('no data available'), and :171 returns 'Period(s) not found in database for ${ticker}: ...' which contains markers 6 and 5. Two of four honest-gap messages in this file are covered and two are not. (3) LIVE, THROUGH THE DEPLOYED CONTAINER, not a fixture — PO called mcp__gateway__call_tool(server=vn-market, tool=narrative_truth_gate) this tick. Covered branch: post_body 'TNH chua co du lieu khoi ngoai.' -> GATE_VERDICT: PASS, '[PASS] dimension=foreign_flow tool=get_foreign_flow — honest no-data confirmed: "No data available for TNH: foreign investor volume has not been collected yet."'. The gate is deployed, reachable and behaving correctly on the branch whose wording happens to be covered — which is exactly why the uncovered branches will fail silently in production rather than loudly in CI. (4) INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED BEFORE PO SAW IT, and this is the reason the row exists: the T8 DoD-harness developer hit it and wrote it down in docs/agent-memory/notebooks/dev-mcp-server.md:61 — 'verified empirically that its message ("Insufficient foreign flow data for X: only N row(s) found") does not contain any tool_null_markers substring (case-insensitive) and would misclassify NON_NULL/FAIL, the exact false-positive DoD (c) exists to rule out. Flagging this as a real latent defect in the already-shipped T3 probe adapter, not fixed here (test-only row).' That developer routed AROUND the branch to keep T8 green, so CCATO-MCP-T8-DOD-HARNESS is DONE_VERIFIED and CI is green WITH THE DEFECT STILL PRESENT — the finding lived only in notebook prose and was on no board lane anywhere until this row.
ac: AC-1 PICK THE FIX SIDE DELIBERATELY AND SAY WHY. Two shapes are available and they are not equivalent. (A) Add a marker to docs/data/claim-tool-map.json .tool_null_markers that covers both messages (e.g. 'insufficient foreign flow data', or relax to 'insufficient') — cheap, but 'insufficient' alone is broad enough to swallow a genuine sentence from a real tool payload and would create the inverse false-NEGATIVE, so a widened marker MUST come with a negative control proving it does not. (B) Change the two probe messages to use wording already in the SSOT list (e.g. 'Insufficient data for ${ticker}: only N row(s) found.'), which keeps the marker list narrow. Prefer (B) unless a reason to prefer (A) is stated. Do NOT do both blindly.
AC-2 FIX BOTH SITES. :107 and :114 are the same defect; fixing only the one the original report named leaves the analyzeForeignFlow-returned-null path still emitting false contradictions.

AC-3 SWEEP THE WHOLE ADAPTER SURFACE, DO NOT SPOT-FIX. Enumerate EVERY honest-gap message any probe adapter can emit (all `raw: { note: ... }` template literals in apps/mcp-server/src/infrastructure/probes/), and assert each one classifies as NULL. Four exist today, two pass and two fail; a fix validated on the two known offenders and not on the full set is the shape recorded in feedback_fleetwide_gate_validated_on_one_file_optout_allowlist.

AC-4 ADD A STANDING REGRESSION TEST THAT FAILS WHEN A NEW UNCOVERED MESSAGE IS ADDED. The durable property is 'every honest-gap note a probe adapter can produce classifies as NULL against the live docs/data/claim-tool-map.json'. Read the marker list from the SSOT file at runtime; do NOT hardcode the 10 strings. This is the only AC that stops the same defect being reintroduced by the next probe adapter.

AC-5 NEGATIVE CONTROL, MANDATORY. A genuine NON_NULL foreign-flow payload (real numeric net-buy/sell data) must still classify NON_NULL and still FAIL an absence claim. A fix that turns the gate permanently permissive on the foreign_flow dimension is strictly worse than the false positive it removes.

AC-6 CLOSE THE T8 ROUTE-AROUND. docs/agent-memory/notebooks/dev-mcp-server.md:61 records that T8's DoD (c) deliberately used compare_financials against an empty table instead of foreign_flow's 1-row branch, precisely to avoid this bug. Once fixed, DoD (c) should be able to use the foreign_flow 1-row branch. Either re-point it or state in the RETURN why not — otherwise the harness stays permanently blind to the branch this row fixes.

backlog.title: commit-sweep-guard exits at pre-commit:721 for every pathspec-SCOPED commit, so its absorb detector never inspects them — a peer write that lands in the read-to-`git add` gap on a multi-writer file (coverage-state.json) is committed silently under an unrelated message; the one SCOPED-mode detector that does run is blind by construction to this case
backlog.created_by: po (triage Step 0-SIG 2026-08-24T2030Z, Pipeline-A bug-escalation envelope ac698731b5a9 from cowork-team/router, self-observed)
backlog.root_cause: TWO layers, both verified by reading scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit this tick rather than by trusting the escalation. LAYER 1 — THE ABSORB DETECTOR IS BARE-ONLY BY CONSTRUCTION. The hook classifies the commit at :705-707 from the lock file git took (index/index.lock -> BARE, next-index-<pid>.lock -> SCOPED, else UNKNOWN). Line 721 is a bare `[ "$mode" = "SCOPED" ] && exit 0`. EVERYTHING that builds the '[sweep-guard] BARE commit about to absorb N staged file(s)' finding — the `git diff --cached --name-only` read at :743, the per-session warn ledger, the escalation threshold, the signal write at :880 — lives BELOW that line and is unreachable for any commit carrying an explicit trailing pathspec. LAYER 2 — THE ONE SCOPED-MODE DETECTOR CANNOT SEE THIS CASE. :717 runs _detect_samefile_pathspec_only_divergence for SCOPED commits, which compares the SHARED index's staged blob for each path against the scratch-index blob about to land, and warns when they differ. In the observed incident the committer had already run `git add` on the shared file, so the peer's content was in BOTH blobs: index blob == landing blob, zero divergence, detector correctly silent. It detects 'staged subset differs from what lands'; it is structurally blind to 'both already contain a peer write the committer never read'. So the escalation's own summary ('the guard does not look at pathspec commits at all') is half right and the correction matters for scoping: a SCOPED-mode hook slot ALREADY EXISTS and is already wired — the fix is a second detector in that slot, not new plumbing. UNDERLYING MECHANISM, which is the part that generalises: an explicit trailing pathspec bounds WHICH FILES a commit touches, never WHOSE CONTENT within them. `git add <path>` stages the file as of add-time, not as of the last time the committer read it. On a file with concurrent writers, the read-to-add window is a live absorb window.
backlog.evidence: SELF-OBSERVED BY THE REPORTER ON ITS OWN COMMIT, then independently re-verified by PO in git this tick. (1) Commit bf85211c3 — PO ran `git log -1` and `git show --numstat`. Its message describes landing 'real KBC/NVL/PDR stamps' (three tickers, written 20:07:23Z). Its actual diff to docs/data/coverage-state.json is 38 insertions / 38 deletions; `git show bf85211c3 -- docs/data/coverage-state.json | grep -c '^+'` = 39. The reporter attributes the surplus to a news-scout 34-ticker write at 20:08:49Z landing inside its window. The commit message and the commit contents disagree by an order of magnitude, and nothing warned. (2) THE TIMING, as measured by the reporter: a pre-commit `git diff --stat` showed 5 insertions / 5 deletions; the `git add` twenty seconds later staged 76 changed lines. The peer's full write landed in that 20-second gap. (3) THE GUARD'S OWN BEHAVIOUR IN THE SAME WINDOW IS THE CONTROL, and it is what makes this a mechanism finding rather than an anecdote: docs/signals/commit-sweep-guard-2026-08-24T200746Z-44631.json exists — actor ca9c65e5, BARE commit, 1 staged file (apps/frontend/.dockerignore), mode=warn. The guard fired, minutes apart, on a ONE-FILE BARE commit while staying silent on a 37-stamp SCOPED absorb. That envelope reached this same PO inbox this tick (565615a826ec) and was dispositioned to pendingObservations per triage-signals.md. (4) NO DATA WAS LOST OR CORRUPTED in this instance — the 34 absorbed stamps were real, correct and needed committing. That is the point: the same mechanism would just as readily absorb a peer's half-written or wrong value under an unrelated message, and the commit log would still read as if it had not.
ac: AC-1 ADD A SCOPED-MODE ABSORB DETECTOR IN THE SLOT THAT ALREADY EXISTS. :717 already calls a SCOPED-only detector before the :721 exit. Add a second call there. Do NOT move or delete the :721 exit — the BARE path's ledger/escalation machinery below it is per-session-budgeted and must not start counting SCOPED commits, or every correctly-pathspec'd commit in the fleet starts consuming the BARE budget.

AC-2 DECLARE THE MULTI-WRITER SET EXPLICITLY, IN DATA, NOT IN THE HOOK. Minimum members from live observation: docs/data/coverage-state.json (market-watcher + news-scout + alert-commander all observed writing it), docs/data/orch/orch-state.json, docs/data/cowork-schedule.json. Put the list where it can be extended without editing the hook — docs/data/system-map.json is the standing SSOT for structural data and the fleet rule is never to hardcode it.

AC-3 WARN ONLY, NEVER BLOCK, ON FIRST SHIP. Same discipline as every other detector in this hook (mode=warn default, GIT_*_MODE=reject only after re-validation). A hard block here would stall every agent that legitimately commits coverage-state.json.

AC-4 THE CHEAPER INTERIM IS A SEPARATE ROW AND MUST LAND FIRST — DO NOT IMPLEMENT IT HERE. The escalation's other proposal, a compare-and-swap helper for coverage-state.json mirroring scripts/orch-apply.sh's CAS contract, has been folded onto backlog[] FIX-COVERAGE-STATE-CROSS-AGENT-LOST-UPDATE (see its po_fold_20260824T2030Z). That fix prevents the absorb; this row only detects it. Sequence: CAS helper, then this detector, and only then any widening of agent commit pathspecs.

AC-5 SEQUENCING WARNING, RAISED BY THE REPORTER AND ENDORSED. There is a separate open intent (the RULE 2.5 coverage-state durable fix) to widen agent trailing pathspecs to INCLUDE docs/data/coverage-state.json. POSITIVE: a SCOPED commit on a declared multi-writer file where a simulated peer write was `git add`ed in the read-to-add gap must WARN. backlog.router_evidence_20260826T1300Z:
[router 2026-08-26T13:00Z] FRESH FULLY-TRACED INSTANCE, on docs/data/orch/orch-state.json — a materially larger surface than the coverage-state.json case in this row title.

WHAT HAPPENED: router commit 796d1c78e, message "chore(tasks): widen mktemp-suffix row to orch-cold-evict.sh sibling sites", was pathspec-SCOPED on BOTH halves (git add -- docs/data/orch/orch-state.json && git commit ... -- docs/data/orch/orch-state.json). It silently absorbed a concurrently-running qa session entire lane-move of TASK-COWORK-CATCHUP-9 (qa[] -> done_verified[], status QA -> DONE_VERIFIED) AND that session .head reset to idle. Reproduce: `git show 796d1c78e -- docs/data/orch/orch-state.json | grep -c TASK-COWORK-CATCHUP-9` returns 6. The commit message mentions none of it. The router had, one commit earlier (62e16dfb0), explicitly written the multi-writer caveat into its own message and still could not prevent this.

DETECTED BY THE VICTIM, NOT THE GUARD — which is this row precise claim. The qa session self-reported that its orch-state write had landed inside a peer commit and that no separate commit was possible. commit-sweep-guard emitted nothing, consistent with pre-commit:721 exiting for pathspec-scoped commits. Sibling row FIX-COMMIT-SWEEP-VICTIM-SELF-DETECT covers the victim-side path this incident actually relied on.

AGGRAVATING FACTOR UNIQUE TO THIS FILE — read before scoping a fix. CLAUDE.md mandates the write path `jq <transform> docs/data/orch/orch-state.json | bash scripts/orch-apply.sh`, i.e. EVERY writer re-serializes the WHOLE ~4.4MB document. The absorbed content is therefore not a stray hunk that a smarter diff could isolate: it is structurally guaranteed that any commit of this file carries every peer write landed since the committer own read. Explicit pathspec is powerless by construction — it bounds WHICH FILES, never WHOSE CONTENT. A fix that only teaches the guard to inspect pathspec commits will therefore fire on essentially EVERY orch-state.json commit fleet-wide unless it also distinguishes intended-vs-absorbed content, which for a whole-document rewrite requires the caller to declare what it meant to change.

FREQUENCY: third observed instance in ~48h. The other two: (1) a developer uncommitted cowork-schedule.json edit absorbed by a cowork-team tick commit d6144f64c, 2026-08-26; (2) the qa case above. Both were surfaced only because the victim happened to notice and say so.

backlog.title: Layer-B 'Dự kiến lần tới' is inert '—' on 23/23 CLI-session cron rows while Layer-A computes the same field on 89/89 from cron_expr alone — a pure, telemetry-free projection is withheld by a literal-null type, not by technical impossibility
backlog.desc: USER-RE-REPORTED 2026-08-24 (verbatim: 'i dont see status is update'). Second report of the same section: 'Cron phiên làm việc (23)' on http://localhost:3001/dashboard/orchestration. The FIRST report (2026-08-23) named THREE inert columns; the row that shipped for it — FIX-DASH-CRON-LAYERB-NEVERFIRED-FALSE-LABEL (DONE_VERIFIED, qa APPROVED 2026-08-24T19:53:58Z, commit 4b4bfea7a, now cold-evicted to docs/data/orch/archive/2026-08.json) — fixed COLUMN 1 ONLY ('Lần chạy gần nhất' → 'Không theo dõi'). Columns 2 and 3 were left inert. That row's own '=== EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE ===' clause says so verbatim ('Building real Layer-B fire telemetry ... If dev-frontend judges it warranted, file a SPIKE — do not attempt it here'); no follow-up was ever filed. This row is that missing follow-up, narrowed to COLUMN 2 only. Column 3 ('Trạng thái') was triaged in the same pass and RULED A DELIBERATE NO-OP — see '=== COLUMN 3 ===' below. === LIVE EVIDENCE (probed 2026-08-24T21:19:30Z, GET http://localhost:3001/api/cron-status) === Layer-A: 89 rows, expected_next_fire populated on 89/89. Layer-B: 23 rows, expected_next_fire null on 23/23 — one single distinct field shape across the whole set (jq group_by: {enf:null, st:'SESSION_SCOPED', elf:null} × 23). Zero variance, i.e. constant by construction, not a data-availability accident. All 23 Layer-B rows DO carry a non-empty cron_expr (23/23 verified) — that is already how the adjacent 'Lịch dự kiến' column renders 'daily 14:23 UTC', 'Monday/Thursday 19:30 UTC' etc. via buildHumanSchedule(cron_expr). === WHY THIS IS A GAP AND NOT A DELIBERATE HONESTY GUARD === apps/mcp-server/src/application/cron/cronStatusCompute.ts's computeExpectedFires(cronExpr, nowMs) is a PURE function of (cron expression, clock). Read it: it constructs CronExpressionParser.parse(cronExpr, {tz:'UTC'}) and calls .next(). It touches NO database, NO cron_job_runs, NO telemetry, NO session. It is the sole producer of Layer-A's expected_next_fire. So the projection Layer-B is missing needs exactly ZERO of the runtime-fire infrastructure that Layer-B legitimately lacks. What withholds it is a TYPE, not a capability: apps/mcp-server/src/infrastructure/cron/layerBCronRegistry.ts declares 'interface CronStatusRowB { ... expected_next_fire: null; ... }' — the LITERAL type null, not 'string | null' — and buildRow() hardcodes it. apps/frontend/app/routes/dashboard.orchestration.tsx normalizeCronRowB() (~L182-197) re-hardcodes the same. Render (~L460-464): 'row.expected_next_fire == null ? — : '. === HARD TRAP — READ THIS BEFORE WRITING ANY CODE === A session-scoped cron fires ONLY IF a live CLI session happens to be open at that instant. Therefore a BARE next-fire timestamp asserts a positive fact that may well be false. That is the EXACT defect class just fixed on column 1, and it must not be reintroduced one cell to the right. The harm class of the CURRENT bug is INFORMATION ABSENCE (honest but empty); the harm class of a careless fix is FALSE ASSERTION (actively misleading) — strictly worse. A fix that trades the first for the second is a REGRESSION and must be rejected at QA. This is not hypothetical on this feature. The provenance chain for the column-1 bug: docs/handoffs/BA-DASH-CRON-RECHECK-TABLE.md:364 carried the qualifier '(Layer-A, never fired)'; docs/architecture-briefs/2026-07-02-DASH-CRON-RECHECK-TABLE.md:127 DROPPED it; the implementer then built the unqualified version. A prose-only qualifier has ALREADY been lost between spec → brief → implementation on this exact table. Hence AC-2 below is a hard, testable acceptance criterion, not advice. === ACCEPTANCE === AC-1 (PRIMARY): for layer === 'cli-session' rows the 'Dự kiến lần tới' cell renders a next-occurrence derived from that row's cron_expr, instead of the current constant '—'. AC-2 (HARD GUARD — non-negotiable, blocks AC-1): the cell MUST NOT render a bare ClientTimestamp. The rendered value MUST carry an explicit conditional qualifier meaning 'only if a session is live' (PO-ruled Vietnamese copy direction: a schedule-derived time plus a 'nếu có phiên' / equivalent qualifier). The qualifier MUST be in the SAME always-visible cell — NOT tooltip-only, NOT title-attribute-only. Rationale: the shipped sibling's AC-3 had to make exactly this correction for column 1 because tooltip-only copy is invisible to both the user and every test. AC-3: the qualifier copy is a NAMED EXPORTED CONSTANT (same shape as the existing CRON_STATUS_LABELS / CRON_LAYER_B_LAST_FIRE_LABEL exports), never an inline JSX string literal. Rationale: the column-1 bug survived every test precisely because the offending string was an inline literal no test could reference. AC-4 (GUARD, must not regress the shipped sibling's AC-4): normalizeCronRowB MUST still force-null the OBSERVED-telemetry fields last_fire, last_status and expected_last_fire. Those are genuinely unknowable for Layer-B and force-nulling them is CORRECT. Do not 'fix' the normalizer wholesale. If the chosen design carries the projection through the DTO, prefer a SEMANTICALLY DISTINCT field name (e.g. projected_next_fire) over relaxing expected_next_fire, so the shipped AC-4 guard survives verbatim and the new field cannot be mistaken for telemetry. Architect's call — see AC-8. AC-5 (SCOPE FENCE): expected_last_fire stays OUT of scope and stays null. 'When it should last have fired' implies for a session cron 'and it did', which is the false-assertion trap again. Only the FORWARD projection is in scope. Do not widen. AC-6 (clock): the projection is computed against the SERVER clock, never the browser clock (BA NFR-2, which pins expected-fire computation to the server clock for Layer-A). Note the Remix loader at apps/frontend/app/routes/dashboard.orchestration.tsx:308 already runs server-side, so a loader-side computation satisfies this; a component-render-time Date.now() would NOT. AC-7 (test): a layer-aware assertion in apps/frontend/app/__tests__/TASK-DASH-CRON-2-cron-recheck-table.test.ts — a Layer-B row asserts BOTH (i) a schedule-derived value is present AND (ii) the qualifier constant is present, and (iii) explicitly asserts the cell is not a bare timestamp. A Layer-A row still renders its unqualified ClientTimestamp unchanged. Full frontend suite green against the known baseline (2188 pass / 2 fail — the 2 pre-existing QUE_DESCRIPTIONS/Kinh-Dich schema fails are unrelated, zero import overlap, per the sibling row's QA record). AC-8 (DESIGN CALL — why this row routes to architect, not straight to a developer): there is a real fork and PO deliberately does NOT pick it. The price_anomaly emitter is still live (newest file dated today), so the floor rises.

backlog.title: One dev-team tick can spawn TWO concurrent po agents: Review-Lane SECONDARY-Drain's resolver defaults to "po", and its task:<row-id> lock does not guard Step 1's task:po-triage-<date> lock
backlog.desc:
SOURCE: recurring-bug signal from dev-team, envelope 622c03db, to=architect, priority=HIGH, createdAt 2026-08-24T22:52:13Z. Landed in .dev_team_idle_chain.pending_triage_inbox and triaged by PO at 2026-08-24T23:50Z.

MECHANISM (PO VERIFIED AT SOURCE, not relayed): docs/agents/dev-team/flow/main.md:982 documents resolved_secondary_dispatch_target($detail_items) (scripts/lib/devteam-eligibility.jq) as: effective next_agent if present-non-empty AND not "dev-team", ELSE "po". PO read that line directly this tick and confirms the "po" default verbatim, including the deliberate design note explaining why "po" and not "architect" was chosen. Same section states SECONDARY-Drain ALWAYS falls through to Step 1 - PO Triage regardless of outcome and NEVER jumps to end. Step 1 then claims task:po-triage-<YYYYMMDD> and spawns po. So on any tick where SECONDARY-Drain's resolver defaults to po, ONE tick issues TWO po spawns under two lock keys that do not guard each other: task:<row-id> vs task:po-triage-<date>. Step 1's S3 outer_claim is the flow's only PO dedup guard and it is structurally blind to the SECONDARY-Drain spawn that just happened in the same tick.

OBSERVED (from the signal, PO did NOT re-verify the 22:37Z tick transcript): tick cron:dev-team:2026-08-24T22:37Z. SECONDARY-Drain picked review[] row FIX-CHEF-BIZCTX-GATHER-TO-CONVICTION-WIRING (status=REVIEW, next_agent=null) -> resolver default po -> spawned. Step 1 was then reachable: task:po-triage-20260824 was verified UNHELD at 22:52Z, so its S3 claim would have succeeded and spawned a second concurrent po. The second spawn was suppressed by an out-of-band intent:po:triage busy-guard (CLAUDE.md PRE-CLAIM Phase B) that is NOT part of this flow.

BLAST RADIUS: two concurrent PO sessions both writing docs/data/orch/orch-state.json. PO's triage-signals.md Step 0-SIG performs the pending_triage_inbox CLEAR (subtractive, declared via ORCH_APPLY_DECLARED_INBOX_TRIAGED). Two concurrent CLEARs over the same envelope set is a lost-update / double-triage hazard on a drain-to-zero queue. PO owns that CLEAR unconditionally on every invocation path (FIX-TRIAGE-INBOX-CLEAR-OWNERSHIP-PO-SELF-READ), so there is no second party that would notice the loss.

FREQUENCY: every tick where SECONDARY-Drain picks a status=REVIEW row whose next_agent is null/empty/dev-team. The signal reports 4 of 15 then-eligible review[] rows had next_agent=null. PO measured review[] at 24 rows this tick but did not re-derive the eligible subset. Routine path, not an edge case.

WHY P1 AND NOT P0 (stated so the next reader does not re-litigate it): the hazard is latent, not an active outage. In the one observed occurrence the second spawn never happened because the router's Phase B busy-guard caught it. P0 in this backlog is also already 8-deep in the DRS-stranded-off-allowlist class, and DRS's tiebreak is array index rather than age, so a fresh P0 appended here would rank last in its own band and would not actually move sooner than a P1. Re-price up if a double-spawn is ever observed reaching two live PO sessions.

backlog.status_note:
ROOT CAUSE behind signal envelope 6c7d4f0b (auditor_cycle_missing, tier-2, WARN, sys-20260825T023823-10cf). The missed window is the symptom; this asymmetry is the cause. PO verified every item below by reading the live artifacts 2026-08-25T02:5xZ:

(1) The SAME Tier-2 run reported '0 anomalies, verdict=CLEAN, notebook append skipped' while its own notebook section docs/agent-memory/notebooks/system-auditor.md § c1013 (2026-08-25T02:39Z) records verbatim 'Anomalies: 1 new' and 'Status: DEGRADED', and it DID write signal row sys-20260825T023823-10cf (confirmed present in .signal_queue.rows[], status READ, dedup_key auditor-cycle-missing:tier2:2026-08-25T00:00Z). The run's self-reported verdict contradicts its own three durable artifacts.
(2) It then stamped docs/data/auditor-tier2-last-healthy.json to 2026-08-25T02:40:07Z — on the cycle it had just recorded DEGRADED.
(3) THE ASYMMETRY, verified by file shape: tier-1's heartbeat carries per-check evidence — {"last_healthy_at":"2026-08-24T16:25:27Z","checks":{docker_ps:PASS,health_3000:PASS,health_3001:PASS,disk:PASS,mem_creep:PASS,launchd_agents:PASS}} — because it is written by the probe's ALL_GREEN branch. Tier-2 and Tier-3 carry ONLY {"last_healthy_at": ...} with no checks object, because the AGENT writes them with no green gate at all.
'last_healthy_at' is supposed to mean 'the last time every check was green'. On tiers 2 and 3 it currently means 'the last time the agent finished', which is a liveness stamp wearing a health stamp's name. Any consumer that treats it as health — including the cycle-missing detector that produced this very signal — is reading a value that cannot go stale while the agent keeps running, no matter how red the cycle is.

backlog.title: scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh mutates its spawn-debounce ledger on EVERY invocation — a second run in the same tick silently downgrades SPAWN to DEBOUNCED and suppresses a legitimate audit
backlog.status_note:
Filed from inbox envelope 7926f1f5 (from dev-team router, type recurring-bug, priority high, observed 2026-08-25T01:26:00Z). Self-observed by the reporter, with a live in-tick reproduction, and the reporter ran its own subject dedup before filing. PO re-ran the dedup across all TEN lanes and confirms no covering row.

DEFECT: _spawn_debounce_decision() (approx :910) performs a read-modify-write of docs/data/auditor-tier1-spawn-debounce.json on every call (ledger mutation approx :931-940 — last_spawn_at, spawn_count+1, window_expires_at), and is invoked unconditionally at approx :1084. The entrypoint is therefore not idempotent. LIVE REPRO, 2026-08-25T01:00Z tick, same signature launchd_agents:com.vn-market.fleet-push: run 1 at 01:21:47Z -> SPAWN, ledger stamped last_spawn_at=01:21:47Z spawn_count=8 window_expires_at=02:21:47Z; run 2 at 01:23:02Z, same tick, same signature -> DEBOUNCED. Downgrade is one-directional (SPAWN->DEBOUNCED, never the reverse) so a careless re-run can only ever SUPPRESS a real audit, never cause a spurious one. Both runs emit well-formed JSON; nothing marks the second as a re-derivation. That is the severity: the decision is not missing, it is silently WRONG, and the cron prompt's deliberate fail-open clause for a missing/unparseable spawn_decision does not fire because nothing is missing.

CONTRIBUTING FACTOR: one entrypoint conflates emitting a health verdict (idempotent, safe to call for debugging/shape-checking/piping to jq) with consuming a rate-limit token (single-shot). Anyone treating it as the former corrupts the latter. Today the only thing standing between a re-run and a suppressed audit is prose in a cron prompt.

REMEDY, in the reporter's order of preference: (a) --decide flag so the ledger write happens only under --decide, making the bare invocation a pure read; (b) callers READ docs/data/auditor-tier1-last-trigger.json, which the probe already writes with the full verdict, instead of re-invoking; (c) key the ledger entry on (signature, fire_tick) so a same-tick second run is a no-op rather than a downgrade. (c) is most robust — it fixes the hazard for callers who never read the docs. Prefer (c), optionally with (a).

HARD CONSTRAINT carried from the reporter, do not violate: this row is about the probe entrypoint contract ONLY. Do NOT address it by re-arming com.vn-market.fleet-push and do NOT add or retarget an ack-ledger entry for it — both are explicitly FORBIDDEN by ready[] row FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-PROBE-SCORES-DELIBERATELY-DISABLED-LAUNCHD-JOB-AS-DEGRADED. That row owns the fleet-push FALSE POSITIVE that merely generated the signature; different defect, same script, and it is currently dispatch_lane=null so it is unpickable. FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-SIDECAR-FILES-HAVE-NO-COMMITTER-AT-ALL owns the fact that this exact ledger file is perpetually uncommitted (same file, different defect). FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-SPAWN-DEBOUNCE-2-FLOWDOC-CRON-PROMPT (DONE_VERIFIED) is the row that put the 'read spawn_decision, do not re-derive' instruction into the cron prompt — this finding is precisely that the prose instruction is not enforcement.

SELF-DISCLOSURE from the reporter, preserved: the router itself caused the double-invocation, by re-running the probe for clean JSON after a tail filter truncated the first output. That tick was NOT suppressed — run 1's SPAWN was correctly treated as authoritative and system-auditor was spawned. Filed so the next caller is not so lucky.

backlog.title: spawn-fanout.md:191 load-average parse truncates to the integer part under a comma-decimal locale (2.48 -> 2), and the remedy the reporter proposes (LC_ALL=C) produces a WORSE malformed value — PO reproduced both
backlog.status_note:
Reported by the cowork-team dispatcher in two consecutive fire envelopes (01ba03d4 01:36:50Z, d9e0fe31 02:07:40Z) with no board row, so it keeps being re-reported. PO reproduced it live on this host 2026-08-25T02:5xZ and ALSO falsified the proposed remedy — do not apply the reporter's fix as written.

DOC LITERAL, docs/agents/cowork-team/flow/spawn-fanout.md:191 (Step 5.1 DEGRADED gate):
  uptime | awk -F'load average' '{print $2}' | awk -F',' '{gsub(/[^0-9.]/,"",$1); print $1}'

MEASURED, same shell, back to back:
  as written                  -> 1        (真 load 1.65; splits on this host's comma DECIMAL separator and keeps the integer part)
  with LC_ALL=C prefix        -> 1.652.893.70   (MALFORMED)
Why the proposed fix is worse: under LC_ALL=C uptime prints '1.65 2.89 3.70' — period decimals, SPACE separated. -F',' then finds no comma, $1 becomes the whole three-number string, and gsub strips the spaces, concatenating all three load averages into one garbage token. The reporter's own framing (harmless at load 2.48 vs threshold 24, latent at 24.9 -> 24 passing <=24) is right about the DEFECT and wrong about the REMEDY: it converts a conservative under-read into a value that will not compare numerically at all.

ALSO CORRECT THE CITED PRECEDENT: the envelopes cite 'scripts/verify-a30-mcp-memory-reclamation.sh already carries the LC_ALL=C pin'. That path does not exist (the script is scripts/audits/verify-a30-mcp-memory-reclamation.sh) and grep -rl LC_ALL scripts/ does not list it either — LC_ALL appears in scripts/agents-flow/cron-marker-liveness-probe.sh, scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh, scripts/audits/mock-guard.sh and scripts/audits/commit-convention-audit.sh. Whoever takes this must not copy a pin from a file that has none.

AC: pin the locale AND fix the field split together so the extractor returns a well-formed float under both locales — e.g. LC_ALL=C uptime | sed -E 's/.*load average[s]?: //' | awk '{print $1}' — and add a two-case regression (comma-decimal locale, period-decimal locale) asserting a numeric result and a correct >24 DEGRADED trip at 24.9. Fix the doc literal at :191; any script copying it must be fixed in the same pass.

[po/triage 2026-08-26T03:48Z] FOLD +6 consecutive confirmations, no re-mint, no priority change. All six cowork-fire envelopes in this tick's inbox self-report the defect in carried_defects, each naming spawn-fanout.md Step 5.1's own LOAD_1MIN expression (uptime | awk -F',') truncating the true load to its integer part on this locale-comma host: 4.50->4 (02:21Z), 9.32->9 (02:36Z), 5,28->5 (02:53Z), 3,76->3 (03:08Z), 3,47->3 (03:20Z), 3,18->3 (03:36Z). Every envelope independently states the defect is IN THE SPEC, not a caller improvisation, and that it is currently NON-BINDING because the threshold is 24 (12 cores x factor 2) -- no verdict has been affected. Priority deliberately left at P3: this is a latent correctness bug that only becomes a real comparison error if a future threshold is set near an integer boundary. Recorded so the count is not lost, not to escalate.
backlog.po_occurrence_6_20260825: OCCURRENCE 6, reported in the 2026-08-25T08:08Z cowork tick telemetry: uptime yielded the comma-decimal '1,90' through the flow's parse. Verdict unaffected THIS tick only because 1.90 vs threshold 24 fails open — the truncation is silent whenever the load is genuinely near threshold, which is exactly when it matters.
