backlog.title: DATA-tier `verdict` label is an unbound free-judgment escape hatch around the mandatory dedup+signal actuator — db-integrity-history-append.sh:74 gates BOTH on verdict=="REAL", so any BY-DESIGN/NOISE/CLEAN label silently skips dedup AND the signal write with no trace of the bypass
backlog.status_note:
CONFIRMED IN CODE (po read the file this tick): scripts/db-integrity-history-append.sh:74 is `if [ "$verdict" = "REAL" ] && [ -n "$table" ] && ...` — the entire block that (a) runs scripts/db-integrity-dedup-check.sh and (b) calls the E3 emit actuator sits INSIDE that guard. `verdict` is a free-text string written by the emitting agent with no allowlist, no schema, and no evidence binding. Any label other than the literal REAL therefore skips dedup-check AND the signal_queue write, and the finding lands in db-integrity-history.json with signal_id absent/null. Nothing anywhere records that a bypass happened, so the bypass is invisible to every downstream audit. LIVE INSTANCE (07:00:48Z sweep 2026-08-25): 336 arithmetically-impossible OHLC rows in daily_ohlcv (H>=max(O,C) / L<=min(O,C), 20 distinct dates) labelled BY-DESIGN, signal_id=null. PRIOR ART, DO-NOT-FOLD: FIX-AUDITOR-EMIT-SEVERITY-LABEL-FLAT-ESCALATION-BYPASS-NEVER-FIRES is the same family (hand-authored label unbound to evidence) but is about the SEVERITY field defeating the escalation ladder; this is the VERDICT field defeating the dedup+signal actuator outright — different field, different actuator, do not merge. NOT the same as FIX-DBINTEGRITY-SIGNAL-PAYLOADREF-WHOLE-ACCUMULATOR (same script, hardcoded --payload-ref, different line, different defect). AC-1: a non-REAL verdict must still run dedup-check and must still leave a durable trace (either a signal row with the verdict carried, or a BYPASSED entry in db-integrity-history.json with the label + author + reason) — silence is never a valid outcome. AC-2: `verdict` becomes a closed enum validated at write time; an unrecognised value fails loud rather than silently taking the skip path. AC-3: replay the 07:00:48Z BY-DESIGN finding against the fixed script and show the trace exists. AC-4: no change to the REAL path's existing behaviour.

==== LIVE INSTANCE 2 — the CLEAN label, and an unbound THRESHOLD behind it (2026-08-26T10:23:03Z) ====
ROUTER-VERIFIED ON DISK. This row's AC-2 ("verdict becomes a closed enum validated at write
time") just acquired a second, larger live instance, and a second dimension.

(a) A NEW verdict value entered the trail this cycle: CLEAN. It was introduced by a
    router spawn-prompt arm (R-13) requiring one findings[] entry per watched table so that
    an OMISSION can no longer masquerade as health. Correct in itself — but CLEAN is not in
    any allowlist, because there is no allowlist. The 10:23:03Z entry carries 8 CLEAN + 3
    BY-DESIGN = 11 non-REAL labels, every one of which takes the
    `if [ "$verdict" = "REAL" ] && ...` silent-skip at db-integrity-history-append.sh:74:
    no dedup-check, no signal write, signal_id null, no trace that a skip occurred.
    Before this arm the trail averaged ~4 findings/cycle; it now carries 17. The population
    of unbound labels per cycle roughly TRIPLED. AC-2 was already P1; it is now on the
    critical path of a second row (FIX-DBINTEGRITY-HISTORY-FINDINGS-MEMBERSHIP-...), whose
    AC-(c) should not ship ahead of this one.

(b) NEW DIMENSION — the verdict is unbound, and so is the THRESHOLD it is computed from.
    Two of this cycle's CLEAN labels are factually wrong:
      fred_series_daily   MAX(fetched_at)=2026-08-23 12:13:02 -> true age 70.2h at scan
      macro_indicators    MAX(fetched_at)=2026-08-24 12:13:00 -> true age 46.2h at scan
    Both details justify CLEAN with an explicit "under 48h stale threshold". Router dumped
    every stale_threshold_hours in docs/data/system-map.json: 0.5, 2, 3, 24, 26, 72, 168,
    720, 840. THERE IS NO 48. The SSOT is 24h for fred / fred-effr-iorb /
    fred-ism-subcomponents, 24h for trading-economics, 24h for sbv. Under the real
    threshold fred is 2.9x over and macro 1.9x over — both STALE, both recorded CLEAN.
    The fred detail additionally asserts "same fetch batch as macro_indicators" and reuses
    macro's 46.1h age; the two fetched_at values are 24h apart, so both the batch claim and
    the age are wrong. A closed enum on `verdict` would NOT have caught either: CLEAN would
    be a legal member. The label was well-formed and the arithmetic behind it was invented.
    => AC-2 should extend: for any finding whose class is freshness/staleness, the actuator
       must derive the verdict itself from docs/data/system-map.json stale_threshold_hours
       for the feeding source, and the finding must carry {source_id, threshold_h,
       observed_age_h} all machine-computed. A hand-supplied threshold in prose fails loud.
    Same family as this row's existing PRIOR-ART note (hand-authored label unbound to
    evidence) — but one level deeper: here the EVIDENCE ITSELF is hand-authored.

(c) The emitting agent self-flagged the fred misclassification unprompted, after RECORD had
    written, and correctly declined to re-run RECORD. Fail-loud worked. It still got the
    number wrong (reported 46.1h vs the true 70.2h) and missed macro_indicators entirely —
    it self-flagged the conclusion while still carrying the corrupted premise. Do not let a
    self-flag be read as a compensating control for AC-2.

(d) Verdict drift on FROZEN data — fred_series_daily, MAX(fetched_at) pinned at
    2026-08-23 12:13:02 across all four cycles that recorded it:
      06:58:59Z BY-DESIGN/INFO/CORRECT -> 07:00:10Z BY-DESIGN/INFO/CORRECT
      -> 09:35:19Z REAL/MED/STALE      -> 10:23:03Z CLEAN/-/NONE

backlog.status_note: OBSERVED LIVE 2026-08-25T05:13:35Z (tick 05:07Z). Rotation selected step1_triage (oldest stamp, 01:16:34Z); the stamp was advanced to 05:09Z immediately, per spec (unconditional, before dispatch). Control flow then reached Review-Lane QA-Drain Head-Decoupled, which claimed a row, dispatched qa, and executed its documented `JUMP TO end`. PO triage never ran. step1_triage went from oldest stamp to newest having done no work; pending_triage_inbox was 40 deep at the time, including the P0 resolver hot/cold divergence escalation drained that same tick. STRUCTURAL ASYMMETRY — step1_triage is the ONLY one of the 6 rotation candidates exposed: the other 5 bodies all sit BEFORE the Session Gate (main.md:930) so they execute before any head-decoupled lane can jump to end, whereas step1_triage has no body at the rotation site at all and its actual dispatch stays at ~:1139 (it needs pendingSignals/reports gathered upstream and must stay reachable from Step 0b busy-tick bypass paths). That places it downstream of ILC (:936) and QA-Drain-HD (:1076), both of which JUMP TO end on a successful dispatch. WHY THE SPEC DOES NOT COVER IT: the no-same-tick-cascade rationale at :573 addresses $SELECTED's OWN gate/promote/claim being a genuine no-op — there the burned turn is intentional. It does not contemplate $SELECTED being PREEMPTED by a different unconditional lane after its stamp was already consumed. The stamp-before-dispatch choice is separately well-argued (single call site vs five duplicated writes); the defect is the interaction, not either decision alone. FREQUENCY: not rare — review[] is chronically non-empty (26 rows now), so QA-Drain-HD has work on most ticks; any tick where step1_triage wins rotation AND QA-Drain-HD or ILC dispatches burns the triage turn, and deferral is up to 6 idle ticks (~3h at the 7,37 cadence). DECISION REQUIRED (next_agent=architect, do not silently pick one): (i) a preempting head-decoupled dispatch rolls back / does not consume $SELECTED's rotation stamp — rolling back ONLY in the preemption case leaves existing no-op-turn semantics untouched; or (ii) exempt step1_triage from ILC/QA-Drain-HD's JUMP TO end, since it neither writes .head nor competes for the WIP slot, and avoiding a same-tick cascade among DISPATCHING lanes is the stated reason for that jump — PO triage is not one. AC-1: whichever is chosen, add a regression assertion to scripts/audits/devteam-dispatch-gate-satisfiability.sh: when $SELECTED == step1_triage and QA-Drain-HD dispatches, PO triage must still be reachable OR the stamp must not have advanced. backlog.title: CCATO narrative-contradiction gate probes the tool at AUDIT time, not at CLAIM time — the identical (agent, claim, ticker, tool, cycle) tuple produced returned_value in {"not found in database", 60, 61, 62.1} across 6 emissions, so the same claim is scored both true and fabricated
backlog.status_note: MEASURED FROM THE LIVE INBOX (po, 2026-08-25): 12 chef narrative_contradiction envelopes, 6 distinct envelope_ids, ALL carrying the identical tuple agent_id=chef / claim='VNM khong co du lieu ky thuat phien nay.' / tool=get_technical_indicators / ticker=VNM / probe_ticker=VNM / cycle=2026-08-24 / gate_version=1. Their returned_value differs: 'not found in database' (2 envelopes) and 62.1 / 61 / 60 (4 envelopes). The 'not found in database' emissions PROVE the claim was true at some probe instant; the numeric ones prove the indicator was populated at a later probe instant. Same claim, same cycle, opposite verdicts — the gate as built cannot falsify anything, it reports the state of the pipeline at whatever moment the audit happened to run. Per docs/agents/po/flow/triage-signals.md's narrative_contradiction row this whole cluster is ONE dedup unit (ticker,tool,cycle) and the pipeline-lag reading disposes of the data half as transient; what is NOT disposed of is that the gate emits a fabrication verdict on a claim its own probe elsewhere confirms. AC-1: the probe value used for adjudication must be the one observable at CLAIM time (snapshot the tool result into the claim record when the narrative is composed), or the verdict must be explicitly downgraded to INCONCLUSIVE when the probe instant differs materially from the claim instant. AC-2: a re-probe that contradicts an earlier re-probe for the same tuple must never silently overwrite it — record both and refuse a fabrication verdict. backlog.root_cause: docs/agents/dev-team/flow/main.md:136 assumes .git is a directory inside a linked worktree. backlog.title: news-scout's producer cadence (4h) is DOUBLE the agent_signals TTL (2h), so alert-commander-market is structurally blind to news-scout on roughly a third of its 28 weekday fires — the bus is empty by construction, not by failure
backlog.root_cause: MEASURED END-TO-END by the cowork dispatcher on the 2026-08-25T12:00Z tick, not inferred. agent_signals is a rolling 2h TTL window, not an accumulating log: signal 11340 created ~08:08:08Z carries expiry 2026-08-25 10:08:08, same for 11341. The producer news-scout runs slots news-scout-offhours (cron '0 */4 * * *') and news-scout-sentiment (cron '30 1 * * 1-5'). The consumer alert-commander-market runs cron '*/15 2-8 * * 1-5' = 28 fires per weekday, each querying a 2h window. A 4h producer cadence against a 2h consumer window means that for every producer period there is a ~2h stretch in which NO news-scout signal can be in the window, so a consumer fire in that stretch sees an empty bus and cannot distinguish it from 'no news'. This retro-explains an empty-bus cycle observed 15 minutes before the measurement.

When `self._ocr_backend is not None` — which is the live configuration for every backend value of OCR_TEXT_BACKEND — the code calls `self._ocr_backend.recognize_text(crop)` on the whole cropped table region and appends exactly ONE cell: `{bbox: [x0, y0, x1, y1], text: cell_text, score: cell_score}`. The `else` branch — the backward-compatible path taken only when no backend is injected — calls `paddle_table.ocr(crop, cls=False)` and iterates the per-line results, which is where the structure used to come from. So the pluggable-backend refactor silently traded table structure for backend pluggability, and _assemble_unit_markdown / _cells_to_row_bands downstream receive one band per region regardless of how many rows the table actually has. PO re-derived this at source 2026-08-25.

backlog.title: A-30 mem_creep has no ephemeral-container discriminator and its spawn debounce is keyed on container NAME, so every `docker compose run --rm` container is a brand-new key and therefore a guaranteed first-sighting SPAWN — 3 distinct throwaway names paged the auditor in 13 minutes
backlog.root_cause: The tier-1 spawn debounce ledger (docs/data/auditor-tier1-spawn-debounce.json) records first_seen_at/spawn_count per container NAME. Names produced by `docker compose run --rm` are generated per invocation and never repeat, so their key cardinality is unbounded and the debounce can never suppress them by construction: N throwaway containers produce N first-sightings and N spawns. A-30 additionally has no predicate distinguishing a long-lived service container (where rising RSS over time IS the signal) from a short-lived batch container (where high RSS is the expected shape of the job and says nothing about a leak).

(AC-2) DO NOT 'fix' this by resetting spawn_count/first_seen_at or GC-ing the debounce ledger: that regresses QA-verified AC-4 and is test-locked at auditor-tier1-probe.test.sh T-DEBOUNCE-3. backlog.title: Every CADRAT-3 Pre-Check gate asks 'did an in-scope file change in git diff HEAD~3..HEAD' — a COMMIT-count window, not a time window. backlog.title: GENERALISED: a ROW-scoped dispatch claim key does not guard a second instance of the SAME agent on a DIFFERENT row — every dispatch site claims task:<row-id> and none also claims the agent-scoped guard for its resolved target, so N sites can run N copies of one agent against one board
backlog.root_cause: Two orthogonal things are being guarded with one key. `task:<row.id>` guards THE ROW (nobody else works this row). What actually needs guarding at spawn time is THE AGENT INSTANCE (nobody else runs a second copy of this agent against the shared board). Because the row key is the only key any dispatch site claims, two different rows resolving to the SAME next_agent both claim successfully and both spawn. The guard is strictly narrower than the condition it exists to prevent, and every dispatch site re-derives its own key by hand, so a new site inherits the bug by default.

A site that hand-builds a key string is the defect; the review must show zero remaining hand-built agent keys. (AC-2) Every spawn site claims BOTH keys: the row-scoped key AND the agent-scoped guard for its RESOLVED target (effective_next_agent / resolved_dispatch_lane, never the raw field — a stale dispatch_lane has already caused this class of bug once, see feedback_drs_claim_script_trusts_stale_dispatch_lane_field). A design that serialises all dispatch behind one global lock is a rejection.

backlog.title: ADJUDICATION NEEDED (architect, not implementation): effective_next_agent/effective_owner's board-wins branch in scripts/lib/devteam-eligibility.jq is structurally unreachable whenever the backlog-detail item has a null updated_at, so the stale archived value always wins - 10 live rows mis-route today and 72 of 104 detail items are latently in the same class
backlog.status_note:
ROUTED BY PO, NOT DECIDED BY PO. This row asks architect to CHOOSE A DIRECTION; it is deliberately not a build ticket and carries no implementation AC. Source: dev-team signal rtr-20260825T2258-effnextagentnullts (to=architect, WARN, 2026-08-25T22:58:14Z), drained to PO's Step 0-SIG inbox at 23:16:56Z because the dev-team drain routes every envelope to PO regardless of its own `to` field (that drain defect is separately tracked by FIX-DEVTEAM-DRAIN-ROUTES-NON-PO-ENVELOPES-TO-PO-STEP0SIG).

(1) MECHANISM - PO RE-DERIVED IT FROM THE SOURCE, NOT FROM THE SIGNAL PROSE. scripts/lib/devteam-eligibility.jq defines effective_next_agent (and its identical twin effective_owner) with the guard `if ($board_ts != null) and ($detail_ts != null) and ($board_ts > $detail_ts) then $board_na else $raw_detail_na end`. parse_ts returns null for absent/non-string/empty/unparseable input by design. Therefore when the detail item has no updated_at, $detail_ts is null, the conjunct is false, and control falls to $raw_detail_na - the archived value - NO MATTER HOW RECENT THE BOARD ROW IS. The board branch cannot be reached on those rows at all. This is not a data-hygiene nit: it silently reverts the outcome the recency-compare was shipped to produce.

(2) THE SIGNAL'S CORRECTION IS UPHELD. The RESIDUAL noted on review row FIX-DRS-CLAIM-TRUSTS-CACHED-DISPATCH-LANE-NOT-EFFECTIVE-NEXT-AGENT (live at task_board.review[29], status REVIEW, next_agent=qa - id verified by path resolution, not by grep) attributed the residual to 'a board edit without an updated_at bump'. That attribution is FALSIFIED: every one of the 10 divergent rows below carries a perfectly good board updated_at. The missing timestamp is on the DETAIL side.

(3) PO'S OWN MEASUREMENTS, taken 2026-08-25T23:29Z against live docs/data/orch/orch-state.json + docs/data/orch/archive/backlog-detail.json. These differ slightly from the signal's numbers (it said 11 live / 73 of 105); PO could not reproduce 11 or 73 and reports what it actually measured. Detail items total 476, of which 434 have null-or-absent updated_at. backlog.title: signal-type-coverage-guard CI job structurally cannot observe most Pipeline-A misses; the disjoint per-pipeline rule-set design needs a broader bridge sweep
backlog.desc: Two related findings surfaced while closing FIX-PO-TRIAGE-SIGNALS-AGENT-FLOW-DEFECT-TYPE-UNROUTED (2026-08-26). (1) CI-BLIND: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s signal-type-coverage-guard job runs on `actions/checkout@v4` — a git-committed snapshot. `.dev_team_idle_chain.pending_triage_inbox[]` (Pipeline A) is drained to empty, unconditionally, by PO in the SAME tick it is triaged, before that tick's own commit — so a genuinely new Pipeline-A-only type will almost never be caught by the CI job; every historical self-filed `signal-type-registry-gap:*` row that names a Pipeline-A type (evidence: system_issue, auditor_cycle_missing, signal_feedback, bug, flow_defect, telemetry, 4x cowork_*, container_capacity_pressure, launchd_tracking_gap, memory_loop_breach, memory_pressure_transient — 15 live rows as of 2026-08-26, dedup_key prefix signal-type-registry-gap:) was produced by a manual/local run against a live mid-cycle file, never by CI. (2) BROAD BRIDGE GAP: several of those 15 stale rows are for types that ALREADY have a Pipeline-B routing row (auditor_cycle_missing, signal_feedback) — i.e. the guard's deliberately-disjoint per-pipeline rule-set design (each pipeline's live inbox is checked ONLY against that pipeline's own tagged rows) means ANY Pipeline-B-covered type that later also arrives via Pipeline A needs its own explicit bridge row (the `system-issue`/`audit-handoff` pattern, now also applied to `flow-defect`/`detector_defect`/`audit_finding`/`preserved_bug_no_tracking_row`/`tooling_defect`) — this is easy to forget per-type and has already recurred at least twice.
ac: AC-1 Decide and implement a fix for the CI-blind finding — options include: (a) a pre-drain fail-loud check inside PO's own Step 0-SIG, run against the LIVE filesystem before the durable-inbox CLEAR, so a genuinely new Pipeline-A type is caught before it is drained away rather than relying on a lucky CI-commit race; or (b) explicitly document in the guard's own header that Pipeline-A CI coverage is best-effort/near-vacuous by construction, so nobody relies on a CI green as proof Pipeline-A is covered.

AC-2 Consider whether the guard's disjoint-per-pipeline design should instead treat any type with a Pipeline-B rule as automatically satisfying Pipeline-A too (the disposition logic in triage-signals.md does not actually depend on which pipeline the envelope arrived via) — or keep requiring explicit per-type bridge rows but add a lint/reminder so a new Pipeline-B row is flagged if the SAME type is ever later observed on Pipeline A without a bridge.

AC-3 (secondary, not blocking) sweep the 15 live signal-type-registry-gap:* backlog rows named above: verify which are now redundant with existing table coverage (close as DONE, same pattern this row's own closure just used for flow_defect/preserved_bug_no_tracking_row) vs genuinely still open (leave/promote).

backlog.title: system-auditor AUDIT_TIER=DATA writes LLM-NARRATED numbers into its durable trail instead of computed ones, and they are wrong in a severity-REDUCING direction -- elapsed-age deltas understated 15.6x and 2.8x in records that state the correct raw timestamp in the same sentence, plus a dedup_skipped counter emitted as 0 while the same return's own history entry records 3 and its prose says 2
backlog.status_note:
MINTED by po triage 2026-08-26T03:48Z from two router detector_defect envelopes, 8dbffd56a (WARN) and d7a5e9153 (WARN). Filed as ONE row with TWO arms because both are the same failure mode -- a number that a model NARRATED being written into the durable audit trail in place of a number that was MEASURED -- and both are fixed by the same shape.
ARM A -- ELAPSED-TIME DELTAS, WRONG IN A SEVERITY-REDUCING DIRECTION. Scan 2026-08-26T03:30:22Z: the signal_outcomes detail says 'no outcome checks in 2+ days' when the real age is 31.14 days (15.6x understated); the macro_indicators detail says 'approximately 14+ hours old' when the real age is 39.3 hours (2.8x understated). BOTH details state the CORRECT raw timestamp and then contradict it in the same sentence, so each record falsifies itself on its face and is checkable with no external data. The direction matters more than the magnitude: every error so far makes a finding look FRESHER, i.e. less severe, than it is -- a 31-day stall narrated as '2+ days' will not be prioritised as a stall.
ARM B -- DEDUP_SKIPPED COUNTER. The [OUTPUT-CONTRACT] emission on the 2026-08-26T02:30:33Z run reported dedup_skipped=0 while that same return's OWN history entry records 3 findings with dedup_check.already_open=true and its OWN prose narration says 2 -- THREE different values for one quantity inside a single return. Not a one-off: the prior DATA entry (scan_ts 2026-08-25T22:35:28Z) likewise records 2 already_open findings against an emitted 0.
WHY ARM B IS LOAD-BEARING AND NOT COSMETIC: dedup_skipped is the only number that makes suppression VISIBLE in the trail. Reporting 0 while 3 findings were suppressed is exactly what let the two confirmed false-suppression incidents tracked on FIX-DEDUPCHECK-MATCHEDTASKID-UNANCHORED-SUBSTRING-MISLABEL (macro_indicators, and signal_outcomes -> ALPHA-S5-TRUTH-LEDGER-BACKTEST) stay invisible. Fixing the matcher there without fixing the counter here leaves the next false suppression equally unobservable.
AC: (1) every numeric field in a DATA-tier durable record is COMPUTED from the raw timestamp/count it cites, never authored in prose -- ages derived by arithmetic on the stated timestamp; (2) a pre-write self-consistency assert fails loud when an emitted counter disagrees with the count of records it summarises (this run would have failed on 0 vs 3); (3) replay the 2026-08-26T03:30:22Z and 2026-08-25T22:35:28Z entries and show corrected values; (4) NEGATIVE CONTROL -- a fixture whose narrated and measured values agree must still PASS, proving the assert is not vacuous.
NOT A DUPLICATE OF FIX-AUDIT-OUTPUT-CONTRACT-V4-V5-DEDUPSKIP-DENOMINATOR-FALSE-VIOLATION: that row is about V4/V5 COMPARING a NEW-only anomaly tally against an ALL-emissions signals_posted counter (a comparison-denominator defect that yields false VIOLATION reports). This row is about the dedup_skipped VALUE ITSELF being emitted as 0 when the emitter's own records say 3 -- an upstream producer defect. Same accounting seam, different half; the V4/V5 comparison cannot be made correct while one of its inputs is fabricated. Cross-reference, do not merge.
ALSO DISTINCT FROM: FIX-AUDITOR-DATATIER-CRONJOBRUNS-ADHOC-COUNT-NONDETERMINISTIC (hand-authored query per run) and FIX-AUDITOR-DATATIER-REINVOKES-STATEFUL-PREGATE-SELF-DEFEATS-ROUTER-SPAWN (stateful probe re-invocation).

MECHANISM A = AutoFallbackOcrBackend (infrastructure/ocr_backends.py:540), per table REGION, ink-coverage discriminator, gated by OCR_TEXT_BACKEND=auto -- DEAD, correctly killed by AC-0 and not reopened here. backlog.why_it_is_not_mechanism_A: Its discriminator does NOT inherit the structural falsification that killed mechanism A. Mechanism A was killed partly because recall-adjusted ink coverage divides by ALL crop foreground and so conflates missed text with non-text ink the engine correctly skipped -- an issuer-styling variable orthogonal to read quality. A raw character count under 30 on a whole page has no such confound: a page that yields under 30 characters is a total miss by construction. That does not make the discriminator correct, but it does mean mechanism A's verdict transfers to it neither as evidence nor as precedent, and it must be judged on its own measurements.

backlog.title: Decision-journal cap-roll is a lost-update race: concurrent agents each compute the SAME next continuation filename and create it with a whole-file Write(), so the later writer silently clobbers the earlier one's entry
backlog.status_note: Two qa sessions hit this within 60 seconds on 2026-08-26 against sprint-COWORK-GUARANTEED-SLOT-CATCHUP-qa-31.md; the entry was recovered ONLY because the second agent happened to notice, i.e. detection is currently luck. Mechanism: .claude/skills/decision-journal/SKILL.md § Cap Check rolls forward by computing `<base>-<n+1>.md` from the highest existing suffix, then creates it with a whole-file Write — a read-compute-write with no exclusivity, so two agents that read the same highest suffix both target the same new path and the second Write wins outright (not an append merge). The blast radius is already large: 31 continuation files exist for this one sprint's qa journal alone. RELATED, DISTINCT, do not fold: FIX-DECISION-JOURNAL-RESOLVE-PATH-IGNORES-ROLLFORWARD-CHAIN (ready[], path-resolution, not concurrency); GUARD-NOTEBOOK-CONCURRENT-EDIT-COLLISION-DATA-LOSS (notebooks + Edit collision, different primitive); FIX-DECISION-JOURNAL-BYTECAP-NO-ACTUATOR (when the roll fires, not how). AC-1 the roll-forward acquires exclusivity before it writes — O_EXCL create / mkdir-lock / claim key — and on collision RE-RESOLVES to the next free suffix instead of overwriting. AC-2 an append to an EXISTING continuation file never truncates it (no whole-file Write on a path that already exists). AC-3 a two-writer regression harness reproduces the clobber BEFORE the fix (entry A provably lost) and shows both entries surviving AFTER, on a throwaway fixture, touching no live journal.

backlog.title: cowork-match-slots finish() discards both mutexes exact dropped[] lists and builds due_reasons/cadence_minutes PRE-mutex while slots[] is POST-mutex, so a by-design supersede drop is indistinguishable from a silent slot loss - already caused one false mechanism diagnosis in a live cowork-team envelope
backlog.verification_gate: Execute scripts/agents-flow/cowork-match-slots.js against a fixture tick where market-watcher-eod and market-watcher-offhours are both due: assert the emitted meta names the dropped slot_id AND the superseding slot_id, and assert a negative-control tick with no supersede pair emits them empty. Prove by executing the script, never by reading it.
backlog.status_note: MINTED by PO triage 2026-08-26T17:54Z from cowork-fire envelope 8591ee13c5e5 (16:07:55Z tick). READ THIS FIRST: THE ORIGINATING ENVELOPE'S OWN MECHANISM HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED. It reported market-watcher-offhours present in due_reasons and cadence_minutes but absent from slots[] and absent from BOTH suppressed_cadence[] and downgraded[], hypothesised "one-slot-per-agent dedup", and flagged it as contradicting main.md OQ-2 (collision guard is WARNING only) and R3 (multi-slot allowed). It also correctly and honestly recorded that it could NOT locate the implementing line. PO located it. THE DROP WAS BY DESIGN AND CORRECT: docs/data/cowork-schedule.json declares market-watcher-eod (cron '0 16 * * 1-5', guaranteed:false) with supersedes:["market-watcher-offhours"]; at the 16:00Z tick both were due (offhours cron '0 */4 * * *'), and scripts/agents-flow/cowork-supersede-mutex.js applySupersedeMutex() dropped the declared victim exactly as specified. The owning brief is docs/architecture-briefs/2026-08-14-market-watcher-eod-offhours-notebook-collision.md (S3b/S3c) -- a deliberate 2026-08-14 design for slot pairs that cannot use the guaranteed-boolean tie-break, which post-dates and supersedes OQ-2/R3 for this one declared pair. NO due fire was lost and nothing about the matcher's dispatch behaviour needs changing. THE REAL DEFECT IS TELEMETRY, and it lives in scripts/agents-flow/cowork-match-slots.js finish() (L305-320). Three parts. (1) BOTH applyChefMutex and applySupersedeMutex already return an exact {dropped:[...]} array naming precisely which slot_ids they removed; finish() assigns only the chef_mutex_applied and supersede_mutex_applied BOOLEANS into meta and discards both dropped[] lists. The information needed to explain the drop is computed on every tick and then thrown away. (2) due_reasons and cadence_minutes are built at L419-423 from downgradeResult.matches, which is PRE-mutex, while finish() returns supersedeResult.matches, which is POST-mutex. The two therefore disagree by construction whenever either mutex fires, and that unexplained disagreement is the only residual trace a consumer ever sees. (3) Last mile: the cowork-fire envelope producer emits chef_mutex_applied but not supersede_mutex_applied, even though cowork-match-slots.js L540 already writes supersede_mutex_applied to stdout -- so the single field that would have identified the cause was available and not propagated. COST, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED: the 16:07Z cowork-team tick spent a full tick's analysis on this, correctly ruled out cron, boundary-dedup, cadence-policy and trigger_prompt/flow_path divergence causes by direct measurement, and still landed on a wrong mechanism plus a false "contradicts documented intent" escalation -- because the correct explanation was computed and discarded. A by-design supersede drop is currently indistinguishable from a silent slot loss, which is exactly the class of thing cowork telemetry exists to tell apart. AC: (1) meta carries a mutex_dropped[] (or per-mutex dropped lists) naming each dropped slot_id AND the superseding slot_id that caused it; (2) due_reasons/cadence_minutes are either rebuilt post-mutex or their divergence from slots[] is explicitly reconciled in the emitted meta; (3) supersede_mutex_applied is propagated into the cowork-fire envelope alongside chef_mutex_applied; (4) regression: a fixture tick with market-watcher-eod and market-watcher-offhours both due asserts the drop and its reason appear in telemetry, and a negative-control tick with no supersede pair asserts the fields are empty. HARD CONSTRAINT ON THE FIX: do NOT weaken, disable or make conditional the supersede mutex itself. It is correct, it is opt-in by schedule declaration, and it exists to close a real notebook collision.

  ACB ACV BDI CTG D2D DHG DLC GAS GVR HCM HSG HVN JSH MBB MWG NKG POW PPC REE SIS TCH VDC VNH VPB
That list includes ACB, CTG, MBB and VPB — four of Vietnam's largest listed banks — plus GAS, MWG, HVN, ACV, REE, POW, GVR, HCM. This is not a long tail of illiquid names; it is a 41% hole containing several of the highest-impact tickers on the exchange.

WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC — THE STALE FILE HAS LIVE CONSUMERS, VERIFIED AT SOURCE:
  1. CLAUDE.md instructs EVERY agent: "All structural data (services, agents, zones, channels, sources, watchlist) lives in docs/data/system-map.json. Query with jq — never hardcode values." An agent that obeys this instruction correctly gets 33 active tickers and silently under-covers 24. The project's own canonical anti-hardcode rule currently routes agents to the WRONG roster.
  2. .claude/skills/system-map-query/SKILL.md:106-115 is the canonical query pattern and ships four worked examples all reading `.project.watchlist[]` — the documented-correct way to get the watchlist returns 33.
  3. docs/agents/fb-market-poster/flow/main.md:200 derives its ticker set from `.project.watchlist[] | select(.active==true)` — a PUBLIC-FACING publisher operating on 33 of 58.
  4. apps/frontend/app/domain/market.ts:293 `WATCHLIST_STOCKS` is a COMPILE-TIME constant that mirrors this file (its own docstring says so: "Canonical watchlist — mirrors docs/data/system-map.json project.watchlist"), embedded at build time, never read from FS at runtime. po confirmed ACB/CTG/MBB/VPB/GAS/MWG appear NOWHERE in that file. The dashboard therefore cannot show four of the largest banks in the market.

PRIOR ART — THIS EXACT DIVERGENCE HAS ALREADY CAUSED A MISSED DETECTION ONCE. docs/spikes/SPIKE_1946-crisis-detection-plx-gap.md diagnosed a crisis-detection MISS whose root cause it names as "a watchlist divergence": PLX was absent from `.project.watchlist[]` while present elsewhere. Treat that spike as the impact precedent when sizing this: the demonstrated consequence is a missed market event, not an inaccurate document.

REMEDY — DIRECTION OPEN, ba/architect own HOW. po did NOT choose, but flags the trap: a one-time hand-sync of 24 rows fixes today and guarantees the same drift returns, exactly as it did after SPIKE_1946. Candidates: (i) GENERATE `.project.watchlist` from the `watchlist` table so the file is derived and cannot drift, with the frontend constant regenerated from it in the same step; (ii) keep the file authored but add a CI/audit check asserting `.project.watchlist` set-equals the runtime `get_watchlist` set, failing loud on divergence; (iii) delete `.project.watchlist` outright and repoint CLAUDE.md, the system-map-query skill, fb-market-poster's flow and the frontend at the runtime tool — smallest surface, but the frontend needs a build-time or runtime fetch it does not have today, so cost is real. ACCEPTANCE (all RAW):
  1. `jq '[.project.watchlist[].ticker] | length' docs/data/system-map.json` set-equals the runtime `get_watchlist` roster — assert SET EQUALITY, not the number 58. A count check passes on the wrong 58 tickers; the ticker sets must match exactly, both directions.

Expect the served page's own "N mã" label to read one less than the roster size while any ticker carries active:false (today: 34 roster, 33 rendered, VEA inactive) — that is correct behaviour, not a divergence. RETIRED: the prior form "ACB, CTG, MBB, VPB specifically present".   3. NEGATIVE CONTROL, the criterion separating a real fix from a re-sync: add a ticker to the runtime watchlist, then demonstrate the divergence is CAUGHT — by regeneration, by a failing audit, or by a loud warning. A remedy that only reconciles today's 24 leaves the drift mechanism armed and SPIKE_1946 will recur a third time.

MINTED 2026-07-25T16:49:30Z by po from a coordinator finding during refine-worker verification. The reporter explicitly asked PO to settle the period-provenance question before sizing, and correctly declined to size it themselves. SETTLED BELOW AT SOURCE.

THE DECISIVE QUESTION WAS POSED AS A BINARY. THE ANSWER IS NEITHER, AND THAT IS WORSE THAN EITHER BRANCH.
The reporter asked: do financial_reports.period_year / period_quarter derive FROM the filename (severe) or from parsed content (cosmetic)? Traced end to end, they derive from NEITHER — and neither does the filename. Both come from the SAME caller-supplied ingest key, so they are structurally incapable of disagreeing with each other, and neither is ever compared to the document.
  - apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/routes/bctcVpsIngestHandler.ts:183-184 — periodYear/periodQuarter are read out of multipart form fields: fields.get("period_year"), fields.get("period_quarter"). Purely caller-supplied by the VPS pusher.
  - :194-201 — the ONLY validation is on SHAPE: year rejected unless 2000..2099, quarter rejected unless in {Q1,Q2,Q3,Q4}. The pair (2025, Q4) is perfectly well-formed and passes. Nothing checks correspondence to the PDF.
  - :224 — normaliseFilename(sourceUrl || actionCode+".pdf", actionCode, periodYear, periodQuarter). THE FILENAME IS DERIVED FROM THE PERIOD KEY, not the reverse.
  - apps/mcp-server/src/application/usecases/bctc/resolvePdfText.ts:45-61 — canonical = ACTIONCODE_YEAR_QUARTER.pdf; the source URL's own basename is used ONLY if it ends in .pdf AND already contains the action code. "DPM_2025_Q4.pdf" is exactly the canonical form, so it is a RENDERING of the stored key.
  - apps/mcp-server/src/application/usecases/parseBctcReport.ts:77-82 — ParseBctcReportParams.period is a PARAMETER of type FiscalPeriod. The parser is TOLD the period; it never reads it out of rawText.
  - :465-470 — $periodYear: report.period.year, $periodQuarter: report.period.quarter, $sortKey: report.period.sortKey written straight through to the INSERT at :354.

done_verified.po_correction_20260826T0650Z:
ROUTER FINDINGS 1 AND 2 ARE BOTH FALSIFIED. PO re-derived from the same container logs, read-only, no container touched.

The router reported 86x 503 + 45x 202 on /pek-extract and concluded (F1) a 66% failure rate caused by semaphore contention, and (F2) that the VN market-hours prohibition was breached 86 times and is enforced only in agent docs. PO ran the status-by-hour histogram the router did not run (docker logs -t, bucketed by UTC hour):
  00Z: 2 x 202   01Z: 43 x 202   02Z: 40 x 503   03Z: 17 x 503   04Z: 16 x 503   05Z: 11 x 503   06Z: 2 x 503
The partition is EXACT and admits no other reading: every one of the 45 successes is outside the block window, every one of the 86 503s is inside it. 45 + 86 = 131 = the router's own totals.

F2 is INVERTED, not merely wrong. The prohibition IS enforced in code: apps/pdf-extractor/interface/routes_pek.py:62 runs a Layer-2 guard calling is_vn_market_open_utc() BEFORE any model check or adapter call and raises 503 with detail.error=market_open; the primitive is apps/pdf-extractor/domain/primitives/market_hours/primitive.py and is unit-tested at apps/pdf-extractor/__tests__/test_market_hours_guard.py. There were ZERO breaches. The 86 attempts were all correctly REFUSED. What is true and much smaller: the CALLER (mcp-server) has no client-side market-hours gate and ignores the retry_after it is handed, so it burns 86 pointless round-trips per session. That is AC-4 here, at P3 weight, not a P0.

F1 collapses with it: the 86 503s are the guard, not the semaphore, so there is no 66% failure rate. The off-window success rate is 45/45 at the HTTP layer. The semaphore failure is real but it is a different, later failure — it happens AFTER the 202, in the background task.

DOC DRIFT FOUND IN PASSING (fold into AC-5): routes_pek.py:41 and interface/schemas.py:80 both document the block window as 02:00-08:59 UTC, while the executing code and its own error message at :72 say 02:00-07:59. One of those is a lie to every reader. Today's traffic cannot discriminate (no 07Z or 08Z calls yet).

ready.actual_mechanism: The mutex serialises COMMITTERS, but PO and every other board writer are not committers — they are WRITERS, and they go through scripts/orch-apply.sh, which PO verified contains NO task_claim and NO commit-mutex participation whatsoever (grep for commit-mutex/task_claim/git in that file returns nothing). So the write path and the commit path are on two different locks, which is to say on no shared lock at all. The evictor claims the mutex, reads a file a peer is actively editing outside that mutex, runs its transform, and then git add at line 415 stages the ENTIRE current file content — eviction delta and peer WIP indistinguishably fused — and commits it under a cold-evict message. The peer WIP is captured not because the commit was sloppy about paths but because it was correct about paths and the harm lives inside one of them.

DESIGN COMPLETE (architect, brownfield, no BA/PM relay — direct PO-mint FIX row). Zone: cross-service/ (scripts/) confirmed via docs/data/system-map.json .project.zones[id=cross-service].specialist=developer + zone-detect Tier-2 ("root/scripts/ -> developer"). BUILD-STANDARD: not-applicable (bug-fix/refactor, no new primitives, no new service/feature).

ROOT CAUSE (source-verified, scripts/orch-apply.sh read in full): Stage 0/1 (orch-validate.mjs, schema+coherence) and Stage 2 (orch-conservation-check.mjs, whole-board magnitude + signal-row-identity) both legitimately PASS on a byte-identical-for-the-target-row candidate — neither stage's job is to know what any individual caller INTENDED to change. CAS-mtime cannot fire either: this incident's staleness predates orch-apply.sh's own process lifetime (jq read the ALREADY-current live file after pm's commit landed, so select() legitimately matched 0 rows within in_progress[] — no write raced DURING the pipe's run). Distinct root cause from the CAS-mtime class, same shape already named in dev-standards.md's row-identity guard writeup ("stale relative to live BEFORE its own process started").

KEY BROWNFIELD FINDING: scripts/orch-stamp-updated-at.mjs (Stage 1.5) ALREADY computes, per row id, `changed = !liveRow || !deepEqual(omit(candidateRow,'updated_at'), omit(liveRow,'updated_at'))` for every row in the candidate (source: flattenRows()/deepEqual()/omitField(), lines ~150-257) — exactly the primitive needed to detect "selector missed its target." Nothing currently consumes that per-id result beyond the stamp-or-not decision. Fix reuses this machinery instead of duplicating it (HARD CONSTRAINT in orch-apply.sh's own header: never duplicate validation logic).

FIX SHAPE — chosen: (a) opt-in per-id companion assertion, env-var-plumbed exactly like the existing ORCH_APPLY_ALLOW_SHRINK / ORCH_APPLY_DECLARED_SIGNAL_EVICTIONS precedent (inherited via subprocess env, zero new orch-apply.sh plumbing). REJECTED alternatives, both named in the board row's own note, both source-checked before rejecting:
  - (b) escalate "stamped 0 row(s)" to a loud warning — REJECTED: dev-standards.md's own "Routed writers" list (signal-dashboard WRITE/PRUNE, fail-loud-protocol.md head-reset, any head-only write) shows MANY legitimate call sites touch zero task_board rows every single cycle — that IS their normal successful outcome. Blind escalation manufactures a false-positive storm on the majority of routine writes, not a targeted fix.
  - (c) jq-transform-string parsing — REJECTED: fragile against arbitrary jq syntax (nested selects, alternate predicates, first()/limit()), reverse-engineers intent from source text instead of trusting a structural caller-supplied fact. Opt-in declarative env var matches the file's own existing idiom.

MECHANISM (scripts/orch-stamp-updated-at.mjs, extend the existing stamping loop — do not add a new script/stage):
1. New env var `ORCH_APPLY_EXPECT_MUTATED_IDS=<comma-separated task ids>` — optional, read directly from process.env (no CLI-arg change, mirrors ORCH_APPLY_ALLOW_SHRINK's "no special plumbing" note).
2. In the existing `for (const [id, candidateRow] of candidateRows)` loop, additionally push `id` into a `changedIds` Set whenever `changed` is true (already computed — one extra Set.add per iteration).
3. After both stamping passes (rows + head), BEFORE `writeFileSync`: if the env var is non-empty, for each declared id check `changedIds.has(id)`. This single predicate unifies all 3 failure shapes with zero extra branching: (i) id present in both live+candidate with identical content [[exact PO incident — row relocated to another lane, content byte-identical]]; (ii) id present in live only [row removed from candidate entirely]; (iii) id present in neither [typo / already-evicted] — none of these ever enter changedIds, since the loop only adds ids where `changed===true`.
4. Any unsatisfied id -> print every failing id to stderr, `process.exit(4)` BEFORE the write (TMP stays at its pre-stamp, already-schema-valid state; orch-apply.sh's cleanup trap removes it since the rename never happens — live file untouched, per the file's own "Live file is SACRED" hard constraint).
5. scripts/orch-apply.sh Stage 1.5 error-handling: one new branch — `stamp_exit -eq 4` -> propagate a NEW distinct exit code 4 (documented in the top-of-file EXIT CODES comment + new ORCH_APPLY_EXPECT_MUTATED_IDS env-var doc block, styled like the existing ORCH_APPLY_ALLOW_SHRINK block) instead of collapsing into the current generic `exit 1`. Rationale for a distinct code: remediation is "re-read live file, recompute filter, retry" — identical to exit 2's CAS-mtime remediation, NOT exit 1's "malformed candidate, retry fails the same way." Lets any retry-wrapper safely auto-retry on {2,4} but never blindly retry on 1.
REGRESSION SAFETY: exit 4 only fires when the new opt-in var is set. None of the ~290 existing orch-apply.sh call sites set it today -> zero behavior change for all of them, verified by design (additive-only code path).

COMPANION FIX — docs/agents/po/flow/main.md AC-3 (explicitly required by the board row): current AC-3 only checks file-PRESENCE in HEAD (`git show --stat $SHA | grep -q orch-state.json`) — provably insufficient, it passed on this exact incident because OTHER rows changed in the same commit. Two-layer rewrite: (1) PRIMARY — mandate that any po-authored orch-apply.sh pipe targeting a specific row/id (not a full-lane rebuild, not head-only) MUST set `ORCH_APPLY_EXPECT_MUTATED_IDS=<id[,id...]>`, catching the failure BEFORE any commit exists. (2) belt-and-suspenders — extend AC-3's post-commit self-verification to re-read the SPECIFIC target row from the just-committed HEAD (`git show $SHA:docs/data/orch/orch-state.json | jq --arg id "$TARGET_ID" '.. | objects | select(.id?==$id)'`) and assert the intended field(s) are actually present, not merely that the file is in HEAD. This generalizes the rule already adopted fleet-wide in docs/protocols/fail-loud-protocol.md's Analysis-Only Exit Guard ("re-read the persistence layer before claiming it — never trust the write call's own exit code") from file-level to row-level.

TEST COVERAGE (extend scripts/test/orch-apply-wrapper-tests.sh, new "EXPECT-MUTATED-IDS TESTS (FIX-ORCHAPPLY-SELECTOR-MISS-SILENT-NOOP)" section after the existing UPDATED_AT STAMPING TESTS section, same pass/fail/assert_real_live_unchanged harness + fixture idiom as STAMP-*/ROW-DROP-*):
  - EXPECT-MUTATED-SATISFIED: declared id's row content genuinely changed -> exit 0.
  - EXPECT-MUTATED-UNSATISFIED-SELECTOR-MISS: fixture reproduces the LIVE incident shape verbatim (candidate's select() targets a lane the row has already left in the live file) -> exit 4, assert_real_live_unchanged. This case IS the board row's own AC ("replay this exact race on a fixture... prove the wrapper fails loud instead of returning OK").
  - EXPECT-MUTATED-ROW-ABSENT: declared id in neither live nor candidate -> exit 4.
  - EXPECT-MUTATED-UNSET-NOOP: env var NOT set, genuine no-op candidate -> exit 0 unchanged (regression proof for the ~290 default callers).
  - EXPECT-MUTATED-MULTI-PARTIAL: 2 declared ids, only 1 satisfied -> exit 4, message names exactly the unsatisfied one.

RISK FLAGS: (1) Opt-in-only — callers who never set the var get zero new protection; residual adoption gap, mitigated by making it MANDATORY in po/flow/main.md (the flow that hit this) and documented as the standard idiom in dev-standards.md for any future row-targeted mutation, but NOT retrofitted across all ~290 existing ad-hoc jq callers in this task (separate, larger hardening effort — flagging as a natural follow-up, same spirit as the already-planned scripts/audits/po-mint-orchapply-actuator-verify.sh named on this same AC-3 block: a lint pass could grep for `select(.id==` row-targeted filters missing a sibling ORCH_APPLY_EXPECT_MUTATED_IDS= at the same call site). (2) New exit-code-4 contract surface — verified additive/zero-regression per above. (3) No DDD/domain-layer risk — pure infra wrapper-script change, no apps/*/src touched.

  - scripts/orch-apply.sh — Stage 1.5 exit-4 branch; top-of-file EXIT CODES + new env-var doc block.
  - scripts/test/orch-apply-wrapper-tests.sh — new EXPECT-MUTATED-IDS TESTS section (5 cases above).

orch-row-prose-ceiling-check aborts on a 21-byte numeric occurrence_count increment, so every over-ceiling row is permanently unbumpable and recurrence tracking silently stops
ready.status_note:
REPRODUCED LIVE TWICE THIS TICK, exact bytes captured. PO attempted to record that FIX-NOTEBOOK-AUTOPRUNE-ROLLING-SECTIONS-BYTE-COUNTED-BUT-UNDROPPABLE had recurred 4 more times, by incrementing ONLY its numeric occurrence_count field (5 -> 9). No prose was added. scripts/orch-apply.sh aborted:

  [orch-row-prose-ceiling-check] ABORTED — 1 row(s) with net new inline growth past ORCH_ROW_PROSE_CEILING_BYTES=12000:
    id=FIX-NOTEBOOK-AUTOPRUNE-ROLLING-SECTIONS-BYTE-COUNTED-BUT-UNDROPPABLE live=24298B -> candidate=24319B

21 bytes, entirely digits. Stage 0/1 validation PASSED and orch-conservation-check PASSED; only the prose ceiling refused, and it refused the whole write (live file untouched).

THE DEFECT: the check measures NET ROW BYTE GROWTH but is named and reasoned about as a PROSE ceiling. For a row already above the ceiling the predicate degenerates to 'no growth of any kind, ever' — which forbids the one class of update that is unambiguously bounded, non-prose, and exactly what an over-documented row most needs: incrementing its own recurrence counter. Consequence is silent and compounding: the more a defect recurs, the more prose its row accumulates, the sooner it crosses 12000B, and from that moment onward its occurrence_count FREEZES. Every downstream consumer that ranks or prioritises by occurrence_count then reads a stale low number for precisely the worst-offending rows — an inverted-priority failure. This is not hypothetical: FIX-NOTEBOOK-AUTOPRUNE-ROLLING-SECTIONS-BYTE-COUNTED-BUT-UNDROPPABLE is stuck at 5 while PO measured occurrences 6-9 this tick alone, and FIX-PO-TRIAGE-SIGNALS-AGENT-FLOW-DEFECT-TYPE-UNROUTED (34589B) is equally frozen.

NOT A DUPLICATE of the SPIKE-BCTC-EXTRACTION-DORMANT-MASS-ENRICHFAIL-FLOOD blocker (telegram report 4911). That report describes the same check blocking a large PROSE write (the po_goahead_* stamp on a 34725B row) — the check behaving as designed on the case it was built for. This row is the case it was NOT built for: a zero-prose numeric field. Same check, different and clearly unintended branch.

WHY detail_ref IS NOT THE ANSWER HERE (pre-empting the check's own suggested fix, which says 'route this row's new/updated prose through its detail_ref cold store'): occurrence_count is not prose and does not belong in a cold detail store. It is a hot, queryable ranking field — moving it cold would break every jq that reads it off the lane row, which is the whole point of it being inline. Running scripts/orch-backlog-stub.sh to cold-migrate a row purely to permit a counter increment is disproportionate and would itself rewrite the row.

PROPOSED FIX (small, surgical): exempt a small allowlist of bounded NON-PROSE scalar fields from the growth predicate — occurrence_count, updated_at, and any other numeric/ISO-timestamp scalar. Compute the ceiling over PROSE fields only (status_note, title, description, and the detail blobs), which is what the check's own name, message and remediation text all already assume. Explicitly do NOT add a bypass env var — the check is right to have none, and this fix removes the need for one.

AC: on a fixture row whose status_note alone exceeds 12000B, (a) incrementing occurrence_count by 1 LANDS; (b) appending 1 byte to status_note still ABORTS with the existing message. Both assertions required — (b) proves the fix did not defeat the check.

PREMISE CORRECTION — READ THIS BEFORE TOUCHING ANYTHING. The escalation that produced this row asserted that the 2026-07-07 brief section 3.8 ordered a Tier-1 loaded-assertion that 'was never shipped'. That is FALSE and PO verified it at source. Check 6, _check_launchd_agents() at scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh:583-687, IS shipped. It reads every launchd/*.plist's own <key>Label</key> off the file (no hardcoded label list), requires an EXACT field-3 label match in `launchctl list` AND field-2 status == 0, and honors an ack ledger with a tracked_by-liveness resolution against orch-state. It has been hardened twice since: FIX-LAUNCHD-PROBE-PRESENCE-ONLY-FALSE-GREEN (2026-07-23, presence -> presence+exit-status) and FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-PROBE-ACKED-LAUNCHD-DEATH-SUPPRESSION (2026-07-23). The 2026-07-01 -> 07-04 silent-unload class that motivated section 3.8 IS covered. Do not re-implement it. Architect's own brief section 8 R6 says only 'it is loaded today'; 'never shipped' was added in relay.

THE ACTUAL RESIDUAL DEFECT — different failure mode, and the one that cost 4 days. Check 6 asserts LOADEDNESS. Loadedness is INVARIANT under host Standby. Live right now: `launchctl list` prints `-\t0\tcom.vn-market.cowork-guaranteed-slot-firer` — PID '-', status 0 — which is byte-identical to what it printed throughout the 96.5h continuous Standby of 2026-08-18T12:00Z -> 2026-08-22T12:35Z (confirmed in `pmset -g log`, cited in docs/architecture-briefs/2026-08-23-cowork-slot-durability-layer-inventory-and-miss-detection.md section 3). Check 6 was therefore ALL_GREEN for the whole of a total Layer-C firing outage. launchd StartInterval does not replay intervals missed across sleep, so the job is awake-scoped, not host-scoped.

NO FALLBACK ORACLE EXISTS EITHER — verified, do not reach for the log. log() is defined at scripts/agents-flow/cowork-guaranteed-slot-firer.sh:97 and is called only from inside the fire path (invocation + error sites). On a no-match tick the script exits with zero log output BY DESIGN, and per the plist's own header most of the ~96 daily ticks are no-match. So log silence is the expected steady state and cannot discriminate 'ticking, nothing due' from 'asleep, not ticking'. Log mtime is currently 2026-08-22T20:32:48Z and that is a perfectly healthy reading. There is presently NO observable anywhere in the system that distinguishes those two states.

THIRD CO-DEPENDENCY: the Tier-1 probe is itself cron/session-scoped, so during the same Standby it did not run at all. A self-check whose own liveness depends on the liveness it polices cannot close this class on its own — whatever heartbeat is written must be evaluable retroactively from its timestamp, not only live.

DESIGN IS FORCED, NOT OPEN (this is why the row goes straight to developer, no architect hop): write an unconditional per-tick heartbeat from the firer BEFORE the match gate — cheapest correct form is a timestamp file written on entry, ~0 cost on the ~90% no-match ticks — and add a Tier-1 freshness assertion on it at roughly 2x the 900s cadence, mirroring the existing 2x-cadence freshness convention already used for the probe's own heartbeat (auditor-tier1-probe.sh header, 'Freshness threshold = 2x each tier's own cron cadence'). Retroactive-evaluable by construction. Do NOT build a second miss detector.

ANTI-DUPLICATION FENCE — MANDATORY READ BEFORE IMPLEMENTING. docs/architecture-briefs/2026-08-23-cowork-slot-durability-layer-inventory-and-miss-detection.md section 6 change #1 (Layer C calls cowork-write-last-fired.js) and change #2 (new scripts/agents-flow/cowork-missed-fire-audit.js) are being decomposed by pm RIGHT NOW under FIX-COWORK-DAILY-SLOT-SILENT-SKIP-NO-CATCHUP-CATCHUPRAW-SCOPED-TO-GUARANTEED-ONLY. Those build a per-SLOT missed-fire detector. THIS row is per-PROCESS tick liveness — a different observable at a different layer, and it still fires when no guaranteed slot happened to be due. Read section 6 #1/#2 and section 8 R3 (alarm volume) first. If after reading you conclude the two genuinely collapse into one mechanism, CLOSE THIS ROW AS A DUPLICATE and say so — do not build a second detector alongside theirs.

SEQUENCING: no hard depends_on, but do not land before brief change #1, or a heartbeat and a last_fired writer land in the same file in two uncoordinated diffs.

A file that fails it is skipped by the drain loop's 'SKIP non-signal shape' guard, which means it is NEVER enveloped, NEVER appended to .dev_team_idle_chain.pending_triage_inbox, NEVER moved to docs/signals/processed/, NEVER fingerprinted, NEVER DB-inserted, and NEVER pruned — the 7-day prune in section 0a-2 only walks processed/. Oldest currently stuck: docs/signals/cowork-signal-2026-07-29T0722Z-chef-intraday-tokenbudget-marker-leak.json, 25 days.

CONCRETE COST, PROVEN THIS TICK. docs/signals/cowork-team-2026-07-30T001827Z-alertcmd-session-id-gap.json carried two recommendations. Both have since shipped — SESSION_ID_LINE on 2026-07-31 (spawn-fanout.md:292) and the >=2-DISTINCT-marker threshold on 2026-08-23 (spawn-fanout.md:460-472, commit b545a69cc) — and the signal was never drained on either occasion, because it is one of the 50. Both fixes reached production by a route that bypassed the inbox entirely. A signal whose asks are fully satisfied and whose file is still sitting unread in the inbox 24 days later is proof the inbox is not a queue, it is a write-only directory.

WRITER SIDE. The dominant emitter is cowork-team, writing a bare finding object — {event, discovered_during, evidence, recommendation, action_taken_by_dispatcher, ts} — with no envelope at all. Note the writer is not obviously wrong: docs/agents/po/flow/main.md's own 'Signal write rule' specifies only the FILENAME contract and says nothing about a required body envelope, so the envelope requirement is enforced by a reader-side predicate that no writer-side doc states. That asymmetry is the root cause, not a careless emitter.

DISTINCT FROM THE KNOWN TYPE-NAMESPACE ROW. project_signalrow_type_open_namespace_vs_closed_allowlist_20260813 and docs/architecture-briefs/2026-08-23-signal-type-registry-open-namespace-vs-closed-allowlist.md are about a type VALUE that no routing row matches, inside an otherwise valid envelope. This is envelope ABSENCE — the file never reaches the type table at all. Different layer, different fix.

DECISION FOR ARCHITECT (three options, they are not exclusive): (i) enforce the envelope at write time and state the body contract in the writer-side docs, so a bare finding cannot be emitted; (ii) widen the reader to synthesize an envelope from filename + mtime; (iii) at minimum, make non-drainable LOUD — any file in docs/signals/ older than a declared age that is neither drainable nor a sanctioned by-path family must raise an escalation that names it, instead of being counted as litter forever.

DO NOT BLANKET-WIDEN THE READER. BY_PATH_CONSUMER_FAMILIES at scripts/agents-flow/drain-signals.js:102 already establishes that some non-envelope files in this directory are LEGITIMATE by-path dish inputs (price_anomaly_*, glob-read by chef) that must never be drained, and the script's own comment records that this family has been misdiagnosed as stuck inbox litter FOUR times already. ready.title: SQLite corruption (5th recurrence): systemic root-cause fix required — bind-mounted market.db loses advisory-lock enforcement across Docker Desktop host/container boundary
ready.subject: Docker Desktop bind-mount locking defect causing recurring SQLite corruption on market.db (04-25, 07-13, 07-30, 08-06, 08-26)
ready.description: Recurring corruption on live named-volume market.db (Docker Desktop shared volume via bind-mount). Root cause: virtiofs/FUSE bridge does not reliably honor POSIX advisory locks (fcntl) when SQLite file is accessed concurrently from both host-side scripts (bun:sqlite) and container-side connections (mcp-server long-lived pooled connections). Results in page reuse, rowid ordering defects, index orphaning. Affects intraday_foreign_flow_5m, pdf_extracted_text, agent_signals tables — each incident requires whole-DB restore from backup. 5 occurrences in ~4 months (04-25, 07-13, 07-30, 08-06, 08-26) with 20h-200h data loss per incident — pattern indicates structural defect, not transient failure. Repeated recovery (stop-backup-restore-restart cycle) is cost-justified short-term, but systemic fix required to prevent recurrence. Investigation scope: (1) move market.db to named-volume exclusive-to-container mount (no host-side access), or (2) implement host-side write-serialization gate for PDF extraction/migration scripts to prevent concurrent access, or (3) upgrade Docker Desktop hypervisor/virtiofs layer if update available (low confidence this will be effective alone).

(i) architect ran 2026-08-26T00:37Z to 01:00Z = 1,369,909 ms (~22m50s); its task_release at return reported ok:true released:0, i.e. the lock was ALREADY GONE — an unguarded window of roughly 12m50s. THIS IS A SIBLING, NOT A DUPLICATE, of FIX-DEVTEAM-RESUME-KEY-TTL-3600-LAPSES-UNDER-LIVE-AGENT-REOPENING-DOUBLE-SPAWN-WINDOW (currently review[]): that defect is the identical shape and its fix shipped as ecb825731, but it heartbeats task:<row-id> and does not touch the intent:<agent>:<key> namespace at all — which is precisely the namespace CARD.md itself calls the hard gate. The sibling work demonstrated that an unbounded keepalive inverts the guard the other way, because then a dead agent key never expires and blocks every future spawn. Any bound must live OUTSIDE the renewed lock. Preferred direction: heartbeat the intent key while the spawned agent is provably live, with an externally-held bound. ready.reproduced_at_source: REPRODUCED LIVE by PO 2026-08-26T08:2xZ against the 9-envelope inbox, exact command: `jq -r '.dev_team_idle_chain.pending_triage_inbox[] | "\(.type) :: \(.payload.title // \"-\")"' docs/data/orch/orch-state.json`. Result: 6 of 9 rows printed to stdout, then `jq: error (at ...:25022): Cannot index string with string "title"`, exit 5. Envelopes [6][7][8] never printed. The `// "-"` alternative operator does NOT save it — the error is a type error on the index operation itself, raised before the alternative is evaluated. WHY THIS IS DANGEROUS RATHER THAN MERELY UNTIDY: the error goes to stderr while the PARTIAL result goes to stdout with a non-zero exit, so any caller that pipes stdout and does not check $? sees a plausible, well-formed, SHORT inbox and no indication anything was dropped. Ordering is arbitrary (envelope arrival order), so a string payload at index 0 hides ALL nine. This tick it hid 3 of 9, one of which was the bug-escalation itself. Confirmed to have actually happened this tick: the router's first listing of the inbox stopped at [5] for exactly this reason.

review.po_evidence_and_priority_20260729T1140: PRIORITY P3 -> P2 (PO decision 2026-07-29T11:40Z) ON NEW MEASURED EVIDENCE, and this row is now coupled to the memory problem rather than being a tidy-up. WHY THIS IS NO LONGER COSMETIC: 785 MiB on disk EXCEEDS the 768 MiB memory cap, so no read workload can ever have its working set resident, and every hybrid /search fans out across 3137 fragments plus the index set. Fragment count is therefore a direct multiplier on read cost and on cgroup-charged page cache — the thing that has rag-service pinned at 94-98% of its cap. This row and FIX-RAG-SERVICE-CLEAN-EXIT-RESTART-LOOP are the same failure viewed from two ends: the compaction failure-path counter defect that row fixes is WHY 3137 fragments accumulated, and the fragment count is WHY reads are expensive.
